scores.rationale: A deep functional bench presents on every call and internal promotions are visible (Siddharth Gupta GM to VP Marketing, Jayaraman GM to VP), though the CEO was hired externally and a CMO was brought in from outside.
scores.quote: MR. SIDDHARTH GUPTA – VICE PRESIDENT, MARKETING

scores.rationale: Management quantifies self-inflicted and external shortfalls without spin — naming the GST de-stocking hit, admitting cake and modern-trade dairy underperformance, and detailing the West Asia supply disruption and required price increases.
scores.quote: we need to meet our own expectations on an overall level on cake

scores.rationale: Profit growth far outpaced revenue (PAT +23% on 4.1% sales in Q2; +21% on 7.1% in Q4), which reflects commodity deflation and cost programmes as much as management skill, so results should not be read as pure execution quality.
scores.quote: net sales grew by 4.1%, operating profit grew by 23%

scores.rationale: Britannia holds mind-space monopoly-like positions in specific brand niches (Good Day, Marie Gold, Little Hearts, 50-50, NutriChoice) that management describes as leadership to be nurtured, but the biscuit category overall is contested.
scores.quote: obviously media and consumer awareness interventions to strengthen the leadership that we enjoy in these brands

scores.rationale: Regional strength exists (dominance ambitions region by region) but there are no switching costs in biscuits — consumers and modern trade shift on price, and regional competitors are actively taking share.
scores.quote: making sure that we are price competitive in each of the regions with the key players, so that we continue to dominate the regions that we operate in

scores.rationale: The structure is fragmenting rather than consolidating, with numerous small and regional entrants attracted by the profit pool and national players resorting to discounts, so it is not a stable oligopoly.
scores.quote: as the profit pool of the industry becomes larger, there are very small players and regional players coming into this industry

scores.rationale: New regional entrants are appearing and pricing rationality is breaking down in modern trade, which is severe enough that the new CEO made fighting regional competition one of five stated strategic priorities.
scores.quote: We've also put a section on focused intervention to fight regional competitors. We all know that regional competition has come up, and they are doing their best and some of them are also doing well

scores.rationale: The unorganised/non-compliant trade is a genuine donor pool under GST 2.0, and Britannia notes it is outgrowing other organised national players, though the regional insurgents are gaining rather than donating.
scores.quote: while market share has remained flattish from a Nielsen perspective, I think other players in the industry have not grown as fast as us

scores.rationale: Britannia is a large, heavily covered listed FMCG leader in a category attracting increasing competitive and capital interest — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: as the profit pool of the industry becomes larger, there are very small players and regional players coming into this industry

scores.rationale: Strong brand equity supports premiumisation (Good Day Crafted, Pure Magic with Harry Potter licensing, celebrity endorsements) and healthy gross margins, but pricing power is constrained — management must stay price-competitive regionally and added grammage rather than holding price.
scores.quote: Good Day Crafted, which are premium cookies, which are getting a lot of focus in modern trade and larger GT, which is also doing very well

scores.rationale: Trust and quality reassurance are central to the positioning — nutrition claims (no maida, no palm oil, no added sugar, DHA-enriched) and the Nutrition Foundation work — though for a low-ticket consumer staple price remains a live consideration.
scores.quote: It's got 100% millets, no maida, no palm oil, and no added sugar

scores.rationale: Distribution reach and channel intimacy are the company's core strength — rural distributors upgraded to full-scale, RTM high-potential outlet focus, and best-in-class e-commerce/quick-commerce salience at an adjusted 12%+ of sales.
scores.quote: our e-commerce contribution is upwards of 12%, which is best in class

scores.rationale: As a retail-facing business Britannia correctly leads with intangibles — brands, celebrity campaigns, licensed characters and taste innovation — matching benefit type to a consumer customer base.
scores.quote: We tied up Gukesh for Milk Bikis, and that advertising is on air

scores.rationale: Product-formulation capability is evident (millet cookies, DHA fortification, cheese-dipped crackers) but this is recipe and manufacturing know-how, not a deep or defensible multi-product technology edge.
scores.quote: this is enriched with DHA, which is a good ingredient for kids to grow up with the right thinking abilities

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network dynamic is described anywhere in the last-12-months calls.

Distribution is the clearest durable moat — a rural-to-urban direct network being continuously deepened, dedicated channel structures, and disproportionate quick-commerce share that new regional entrants cannot replicate at scale.
scores.quote: we are looking at taking our rural distributors to be full-scale distributors, which is helping us... better extraction from the existing distribution infrastructure that we've created

scores.rationale: Growth investment is visible in technology and co-location capacity expansion, which is now a named revenue driver, but no capex quantum or incremental ROIC is disclosed on any of the four calls.
scores.quote: Our technology capabilities and expansion of co-location services are also delivering greater values to clients.

scores.rationale: Spend is channelled into large-scale investor education and brand campaigns (16,663 programs covering 8.5 lakh investors in FY26, Nivesh Mitra app, SEBI vs Scam) that build franchise equity, though much of it is IPF/regulatory-driven rather than discretionary brand capex.
scores.quote: BSE conducted 16,663 investor awareness programs, covering over 8.5 lakh investors in FY26

scores.rationale: No R&D spend, pipeline or efficiency metric is discussed in any of the four calls; product innovation is mentioned only in passing for the index business.
No acquisitions were announced or discussed in the last twelve months; the only subsidiary action was a rebranding of a wholly-owned entity, which is not an M&A datapoint.
scores.quote: we have rebranded our wholly owned subsidiary, Asia Index Private Limited to BSE Index Services Private Limited

scores.rationale: FY26 dividend of Rs 10/share (Rs 412 crores, +30%, +67% ex the prior-year 150th-anniversary special) is a coherent, growing policy, but it is only ~16% of Rs 2,497 crores PAT and there is no buyback discipline to judge.
scores.quote: recommended a dividend of Rs. 10 per equity share... The total payout for the year would be Rs. 412 crores, which is an increase of 30% from last year

scores.rationale: Classic asset-light exchange economics with extreme operating leverage — FY26 revenue +59% against opex +20%, EBITDA margin to 64% from 51% — protected by a SEBI-licensed franchise.
scores.quote: Operating expenses increased by 20% to Rs. 1,755 crores from Rs. 1,458 crores... margins expanding to 64% from 51%

scores.rationale: BSE remains the challenger with clear runway and is visibly capturing share — index derivatives average daily premium turnover up ~118% to Rs 19,523 crores, 255 new listings and first globally for IPO listings in FY26.
scores.quote: average daily premium turnover reaching a record of Rs. 19,523 crores compared to Rs. 8,978 crores in FY25, translating into a robust year-on-year growth of approximately 118%

scores.rationale: The business is essentially all-India; the only international thrust cited is index licensing to foreign clients, with no country entries, offshore volumes or execution track record given.
scores.quote: We are actively expanding our customer base by catering to insurance companies, market-linked debenture issuers, and foreign clients

scores.rationale: Growth is overwhelmingly volume-led — derivatives premium turnover +118% driving transaction charges +87% while cash ADTV stayed at 'long-term normalized levels' — with no evidence of price realisation increases.
scores.quote: While cash market volumes remained at long-term normalized levels throughout the year, FY26 marked a milestone with BSE recording its highest ever ADTV of Rs. 7,950 crores.

scores.rationale: BSE is riding near a cyclical peak rather than a trough — 13 consecutive record-revenue quarters, record IPO fundraising and record SIP flows — so the cyclical setup is unfavourable, not early-cycle.
scores.quote: BSE delivered its 13th consecutive quarter of record revenues

scores.rationale: The end market is in genuine secular expansion — investor accounts past 25 crores (+3.53 crores in one year), SIP flows at a record Rs 3.5 lakh crores and DII deployment of ~Rs 8.5 lakh crores in FY26.
scores.quote: Over the past year alone, BSE has added 3.53 crores new investor accounts... SIP flows reached a record Rs. 3.5 lakh crores for the year

scores.rationale: Purely organic growth with no M&A or leverage, tight cost control (opex +20% on revenue +59%) and a self-imposed capped SGF contribution policy that trades reported profit for risk coverage.
scores.quote: BSE introduced policy to contribute 5% of transaction-related revenue to the core SGF on a monthly basis with a cap to ensure financial prudence while maintaining adequate risk coverage

scores.rationale: Ramamurthy's third full year shows sustained execution of a multi-year plan — Sensex derivatives revival, SME platform scaling from 600 to 700 listings in 179 days — plus tenacity on structural asks like the Common Contract Note.
scores.quote: Common Contract Note has been successfully implemented in India with effect from 27 June 2025, a long-standing request of BSE

scores.rationale: Management is institutional rather than celebrity-driven, but prepared remarks lean heavily on promotional and political framing (congratulating the PM and FM, 'Viksit Bharat', 'The Power of Vibrance') rather than plain substance.
scores.quote: I take this opportunity to congratulate Honourable Prime Minister Narendra Modi ji for successful agreement of the trade deal with the United States.

scores.rationale: A dedicated Chief of Staff and HR Strategy role now appears on the call, but the CIO/CTO and chair seats visibly rotate across the four calls and no talent-pipeline programme is described.
scores.quote: Dr. Vivek Jain - Chief of Staff and HR Strategy

scores.rationale: Disclosure is granular and volunteers unflattering line items — treasury income declines, weak cash volumes, and the Rs 22 crore employee cost hit from the new Labour Codes — though the overall tone is promotional and no mistakes are owned.
scores.quote: employee expenses for the period increased by Rs. 22 crores primarily attributable to the enactment of Government of India's new Labor Codes

scores.rationale: The spectacular optics (PAT +176% in Q3, +88% for FY26) rest heavily on a derivatives volume boom and a favourable regulatory/flow environment, so results materially overstate demonstrable management skill.
scores.quote: net profit attributable to the shareholders of the company has demonstrated a significant acceleration, more than doubling to Rs. 602 crores from Rs. 220 crores, representing a robust year-on-year growth of 176%

scores.rationale: BSE owns the Sensex franchise and a de-facto monopoly position in the SME listing niche (700 companies, Rs 1.8 lakh crores market cap), which functions as a mini-monopoly in issuers' and investors' minds.
scores.quote: BSE's SME platform achieved a significant milestone with the successful listing of its 700th SME company on February 1, 2026.

scores.rationale: Index licensing creates real switching costs — Rs 2.54 lakh crores of passive AUM is contractually tracked to BSE indices — and co-location tenants face relocation friction, though trading itself is order-routed and low-friction.
scores.quote: passive products tracking our indices have accumulated Rs. 2.54 lakh crores in asset under management

scores.rationale: The structure is a duopoly with a far larger rival rather than the stable multi-player oligopoly the framework prefers, and large broker/HFT customers retain routing leverage over the exchange.
scores.quote: revenue growth in Q1 FY'26 was led by strong volumes in our Sensex derivatives product as we expanded our client base

scores.rationale: Entry requires a SEBI licence and clearing infrastructure so no new entrants appear anywhere in the calls, and pricing is regulator-supervised rather than discount-war driven — but regulatory dependence cuts both ways, with fees and clearing costs at ~53% of opex.
scores.quote: 53% of the total operating expenses are attributable to regulatory fees and clearing and settlement expenses

scores.rationale: BSE is the share-taker rather than the beneficiary of weak rivals — its gains come at the expense of a dominant, well-run incumbent, not a donating laggard, and no weak competitor is identified in the calls.
scores.quote: In August 2025, BSE saw listing of NSDL on BSE

scores.rationale: BSE is the opposite of under-the-radar — a 150-year-old listed national institution with quarterly analyst calls, heavy media coverage and intense regulatory and investor scrutiny.
scores.quote: celebration of BSE's 150th anniversary

scores.rationale: The BSE/Sensex name carries genuine brand equity that management explicitly monetises, and margins are high (FY26 EBITDA 64%, PAT margin 49%), though pricing is regulator-constrained rather than freely brand-led.
scores.quote: This reflects the deep trust, faith and respect the BSE brand inspires globally

scores.rationale: Customers buy settlement certainty through ICCL, and BSE voluntarily over-funds the Core SGF to Rs 1,202 crores to maintain 'adequate risk coverage', showing trust — not price — is the product.
scores.quote: As of Jan 2026, BSE's core SGF balance stood at Rs. 1,202 crores

scores.rationale: Reach and accessibility are strong — 25 crore registered investor accounts, 10 states with over 1 crore each, plus a mutual fund distribution platform and co-location for latency-sensitive clients.
scores.quote: The total number of investor accounts registered on BSE has now crossed 25 crores, reflecting the continued deepening of retail participation

scores.rationale: The benefit mix is reasonably matched — brand and education for the retail base, and reliability plus licensing/co-location lock-in for corporate issuers, brokers and index licensees.
scores.quote: averaged daily volumes across our cash market, derivatives market, and Mutual Fund Distribution platforms remained very robust

scores.rationale: Technology is credited with revenue growth via co-location and platform capability, but there is no R&D intensity, no multi-product tech differentiation claimed, and the CIO/CTO seat changed hands within the window.
scores.quote: co-location services, which continued to develop rapidly

scores.rationale: Exchange liquidity is a genuine two-sided network and BSE's derivatives book is compounding on it (premium ADTV +118%, wider client base), but its network remains the smaller of the two national pools.
scores.quote: This sustained expansion reflects deeper market participation

scores.rationale: Reach across the member/distributor network, the mutual fund distribution platform and 25 crore investor accounts spanning 10 large states is hard to replicate, though it does not exceed the incumbent rival's reach.
scores.quote: with 10 states each contributing more than 1 crore registered investors, underscoring the broad-based expansion

scores.rationale: Investment is in AI platforms, leaders and sales capacity rather than physical growth capex, and with FY26 revenue down 1.2% there is no evidence yet of incremental returns.
scores.quote: We've made significant investments in our AI platforms, and we have won some marquee deals around our AI push.

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend in any of the four calls.
Proprietary AI investment (Cogito platform, agentic AI) is visibly converting into marquee wins including displacing a global Tier 1 incumbent, though no R&D spend or efficiency metric is disclosed.
scores.quote: we are deploying our AI-powered solutions, including our Cogito platform, which is designed to accelerate enterprise software development

scores.rationale: No acquisitions mentioned across the last-12-month calls.
Cash balances are reported as rising but no dividend or buyback policy is discussed in the excerpts.
scores.quote: Cash and cash equivalents at the end of Q3 increased to Rs. 2,491 crore, up 6% quarter-on-quarter

scores.rationale: The business is asset-light with best-in-class working capital (DSO 54 days), but the excerpts show no protecting moat — revenue is eroding on ramp-downs and client insourcing.
scores.quote: our DSO has improved quarter-on-quarter and now stands at 54 days, which you would agree is amongst the best in our industry

scores.rationale: Despite ample runway as a mid-tier vendor, the year's evidence is share loss — project completions, ramp-downs and customer insourcing drove FY26 revenue down 1.2% in rupee terms.
scores.quote: our Manufacturing vertical, which is our largest vertical, has registered a very soft performance due to project completions, ramp downs, as well as insourcing

scores.rationale: New Americas CEO and added US/Europe sales capacity signal geographic intent, but no executed expansion results are shown within the window.
scores.quote: we've completed hiring of multiple additional sales talent across both the U.S. as well as Europe geos

scores.rationale: There is no growth to attribute; realized pricing is deflationary as AI productivity gains are passed to clients, and mix shift (fixed-price/offshore, pruning tail accounts) lifted margin while shrinking revenue.
scores.quote: upfront productivity benefits that we had to pass on because of AI deals that we have won

scores.rationale: IT services spending is clearly in a trough, but management explicitly sees no identifiable upturn yet.
scores.quote: we have not seen any material change in the demand environment... discretionary spending therefore remains constrained

scores.rationale: Enterprise AI adoption is a secular tailwind the company is chasing, but its actual end-market exposure (manufacturing-led clients) is contracting and AI is compressing its own revenue.
scores.quote: our exposure is higher to manufacturing-led customers across both Manufacturing and Life Sciences & Services verticals

scores.rationale: Fully organic, no M&A, large net cash and rising collections, with counter-cyclical hiring and a willingness to exit unprofitable revenue.
scores.quote: some bold decisions that we took of walking away from several non-profitable revenue streams

scores.rationale: Management articulates a long-term 'AI First' pivot and keeps investing through the downturn, but repeatedly guided to sequential growth that did not materialise (Q4 revenue fell 3.7% in dollar terms).
scores.quote: We expect that there will be sequential growth in the remaining two quarters of the year

scores.rationale: Calls are plain, numbers-first and free of self-promotion, with the promoter chair absent from the calls entirely.
scores.quote: our performance during the quarter and year under review reflects a very soft demand environment

scores.rationale: Nearly every senior seat was filled externally from Tier 1 firms while the CFO and COO departed for 'personal reasons', pointing to a thin internal pipeline rather than systematic talent development.
scores.quote: These leaders that we have added have all come in from Tier 1 companies

scores.rationale: Management consistently strips out one-offs and FX to give steady-state margins, explains the US federal tax provision in detail, and openly owns the revenue miss.
scores.quote: FY '26 has been somewhat unprecedented, where we fell short of our own expectations on the revenue front while improving margins significantly

scores.rationale: The headline 333bps FY26 margin expansion is not taken at face value because management itself attributes chunks to one-offs and FX, leaving a steady-state ~15% — results are separable from skill.
scores.quote: the steady-state EBITDA margin without these one-offs and exchange gains would have been closer to 13.5%

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like hold on customers; work is being completed, ramped down or taken in-house by clients.
scores.quote: we were witnessing some ramp downs as well as some insourcing amongst a few of our customers

scores.rationale: Switching costs run against as well as for the company — it displaced a Tier 1 incumbent on a core banking platform, showing incumbency does not protect anyone here.
scores.quote: replacing a global Tier 1 firm as an incumbent partner

scores.rationale: Customers hold clear negotiating power, extracting productivity give-backs and lengthening decision cycles in a fragmented vendor market.
scores.quote: customers have been holding back on discretionary spend and are pushing for productivity benefits

scores.rationale: Barriers are low and pricing is not rational — the company both wins by displacing incumbents and loses work to insourcing and cost optimisation.
scores.quote: customers are still focused on cost optimization, cutting back on discretionary spending

scores.rationale: One Tier 1 displacement shows share is takeable, but with its own revenue eroding Birlasoft looks as much a donator as a taker this year.
scores.quote: We have also been winning against some of the largest players in the industry.

scores.rationale: This is a listed mid-cap in India's most heavily analysed and capital-attracting sector, not an ignored niche.
scores.quote: all the conversations on deals are being led with our AI capabilities

scores.rationale: No image- or taste-based pricing power; margin gains came from cost and mix while revenue pricing was given away to clients.
scores.quote: upfront productivity benefits that we had to pass on because of AI deals

scores.rationale: Some trust-based wins on domain expertise and a production agentic-AI deployment delivering measured client value, offset by account-specific issues and ramp-downs.
scores.quote: The customer's business teams are already seeing a tremendous amount of business value in terms of efficiency gains and accuracy

scores.rationale: Management's own remedy — a 30-40% increase in sales headcount — is an admission that current coverage and customer intimacy are inadequate.
scores.quote: By the middle of FY '27, I reckon that our sales team strength would have gone up by 30% to 40% on a year-on-year basis.

scores.rationale: The customer base is corporate, where the required lock-in is absent — clients are insourcing and optimising spend rather than being held by switching costs.
scores.quote: Customers continue to focus on optimizing their spends

scores.rationale: Cogito and agentic-AI assets give a credible but shallow and recent edge; capability is being bought in via hires rather than compounded from deep proprietary R&D.
scores.quote: we will continue to make investments that are necessary to build a differentiated value proposition in the marketplace

scores.rationale: The calls are silent on any two-sided or self-reinforcing network dynamic.
Distribution is a stated weakness under repair, with sales capacity and geo leadership being built from scratch rather than being an unmatched asset.
scores.quote: we are also making significant efforts to further strengthen our sales team and expect to see a substantial increase in that

scores.rationale: Capex is clearly growth- and backward-integration-led (sole capacity FY25, upper capacity at Paonta Sahib and Pant Nagar, Haridwar/Ganaur) with output set to double by FY27 and return ratios still healthy (ROCE 22.4%), though near-term depreciation compressed PAT margins.
scores.quote: commenced commercial production of premium uppers at our Pant Nagar facility in January 2026

scores.rationale: Sustained A&P (Siddhant Chaturvedi 'Aye Bro, Capsule Pro', Kriti Sanon 'You Go, Girl', new logo/brand identity) is traceable to measurable mix gains — women+kids mix rose from 18.7% to ~22% and women's from 14.2% to 16.2%.
scores.quote: the campaign resonated strongly with our female consumers, resulting in an improvement in the women's category mix

scores.rationale: No formal R&D line, but design-led product development is productive — ~250 new SKUs in FY26 on an 80-100 day time-to-market, with sneakers doubling in volume every quarter for a year.
scores.quote: Our accelerated time to market of 80-100 days enabled by a fully integrated manufacturing ecosystem

scores.rationale: No acquisitions discussed in any of the four calls; growth is entirely organic capacity and category expansion.
No dividend, buyback or distribution policy was discussed in the last-12-month calls.

Asset-light hybrid model (60+ external fabricators, in-house assembly) delivers ROCE 22.4% / ROE 18.1% with working capital improving to 82 days, though the moat protecting these returns is brand/distribution rather than structural.
scores.quote: Return on Capital Employed at 22.4% and Return on Equity at 18.1%

scores.rationale: Runway is real (large unorganized base) and share capture is visible — touchpoints expanded from ~20,000 to ~29,000 and north-region mix rose from 40% to 47% on state-specific distribution strategies.
scores.quote: the number of touchpoints for you have increased from 20,000 -29,000 odd

scores.rationale: Expansion is intra-India deepening (state-specific distribution strategies, north region mix up) with no evidence of exports or new international geographies in the window.
scores.quote: it is almost like a state-specific strategy that has been formulated

scores.rationale: Growth is decisively ASP/mix-led — FY26 revenue +11.4% on ASP +7%, premium >INR1,500 saliency up from 45.2% to 57.2%, and Q1 revenue grew despite an 11.6% volume decline purely on ASP +14.7%.
scores.quote: our volume declined by 11.6%, however, the impact was largely offset through higher ASP, higher margin product mix

scores.rationale: The company entered the window at a demand trough (muted Q1, online de-growth) and the GST rationalisation plus festive recovery drove an identifiable upturn through Q2-Q4.
scores.quote: The recent reductions in GST rates are expected to spur demand

scores.rationale: End market benefits from secular premiumisation and formalisation of Indian footwear, with the company extending into athleisure apparel to widen its addressable market.
scores.quote: we have strategically ventured into Athleisure apparel in January 2026. This expansion not only broadens our addressable market

scores.rationale: Purely organic growth, no M&A, working capital days improved to 82 while expanding capacity, and retail expansion was deliberately restrained in favour of profitability; only mild working-capital borrowing was flagged.
scores.quote: While we prioritize profitability over aggressive retail expansion this year, our exclusive brand outlet network remains steady at 300 stores

scores.rationale: Multi-year backward integration into soles then premium uppers, plus a stated ambition to become an India lifestyle brand, shows a consistent long-term plan executed through a disruptive transition year.
scores.quote: aligns perfectly with campus' long-term vision of becoming one of India's prominent lifestyle brands

scores.rationale: Management communication is factual and executive-led rather than celebrity-driven, but the brand strategy is heavily publicity-oriented (film-star ambassadors, logo relaunch) and calls carry promotional framing.
scores.quote: we are thrilled to announce that actor Kriti Sanon is the new face of our women's category

scores.rationale: Some broadening of the leadership bench is visible (CBO/COO Uplaksh Tewary joining calls alongside CEO and CFO from Q3), but no systematic talent development or succession pipeline is discussed.
scores.quote: management team is represented by Mr. Nikhil Aggarwal – Whole-Time Director and CEO; Mr. Sanjay Chhabra - CFO and Mr. Uplaksh Tewary - CBO

scores.rationale: Management owned the self-inflicted Q1 disruption and quantified optical distortions (INR 8 crore freight reclassification cutting reported growth ~2%, e-com accounting change), while declining to give guidance it could not stand behind.
scores.quote: there is never honestly a good time to make this transition

scores.rationale: Stripping the halo, a meaningful part of FY26's improvement came from external tailwinds — GST rationalisation, festive timing shifts and accounting reclassifications — rather than demonstrated durable skill, and Q1 showed execution risk in their own warehouse/SAP transition.
scores.quote: The robust demand during the festive season coupled with the positive impact of GST rationalization has further accelerated our performance

scores.rationale: Branded mass-market footwear offers no monopoly-like hold on the customer's mind or aftermarket; the company competes on price-value against domestic and global brands, and had to cut prices with everyone else.
scores.quote: Like everybody else, we have also taken a cut on pricing to reflect the GST benefit

scores.rationale: Consumer footwear carries no switching costs or captive aftermarket — repurchase is discretionary and channel-driven across distribution, LFS and multiple marketplaces.
scores.quote: we have made a lot of improvements in our revenue mix with Amazon, Snapdeal, as well as our own brand.com

scores.rationale: The market is fragmented with a large unorganized segment and powerful e-commerce gatekeepers (Flipkart, Myntra) able to unilaterally change commercial terms, indicating weak industry structure rather than a stable oligopoly.
scores.quote: change in accounting policy by our e-com portals Flipkart and Myntra resulting in a lower revenue and lower trade or commission cost

scores.rationale: BIS quality control and in-house integration create a modest regulatory barrier, but pricing is not insulated — GST-led MRP corrections and 'selective price corrections' show competitive price-setting rather than rational pricing power.
scores.quote: our manufacturing ecosystem is not only compliant but also strategically independent within a BIS-regulated environment

scores.rationale: The GST cut eroded the price advantage of unorganized players, creating an explicit pool of weak competitors to take volume from, which management is sizing capacity against.
scores.quote: the price advantage that unorganized players sort of used to enjoy has sort of significantly reduced now

scores.rationale: This is a high-visibility, heavily advertised listed consumer brand in a category crowded with well-capitalised domestic and global competitors — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: marking Campus' evolution into a culture-led brand spanning fashion, sports and everyday lifestyle

scores.rationale: Brand-led premiumisation supports gross margin expansion to 53.5% and consumer acceptance of higher price points, but positioning is explicitly 'affordable/value-for-money' rather than true pricing power.
scores.quote: Our gross margins were at 53.5% in FY26 versus 52.3% in FY25

scores.rationale: Management claims family-wide trust, but the purchase driver described throughout is design, style and price accessibility rather than reliability for which price is secondary.
scores.quote: reinforcing Campus as a trusted brand for the entire family

scores.rationale: Wide and deepening access — ~29,000 touchpoints, 300 EBOs, all major marketplaces plus own site — reinforced by direct retailer/distributor intimacy through annual meets that feed product insight back.
scores.quote: The event was attended by 150 retailers thereby enhancing our consumer engagement, bolstering our distribution network

scores.rationale: Customer base is retail consumer and the benefit stack is correctly matched to it — celebrity-led brand building, design refresh and premium SKUs rather than TCO arguments.
scores.quote: This campaign showcases the versatility of our flagship Air Capsule Pro collection

scores.rationale: Despite framing the portfolio as technology-anchored, there is no disclosed R&D intensity or proprietary technical edge — the advantage described is supply-chain speed and design, both replicable.
scores.quote: With a product portfolio anchored in technology, design responsiveness and evolving lifestyle needs

scores.rationale: No two-sided network exists in the model; scale benefits described are procurement and manufacturing throughput, not self-reinforcing user network effects.
scores.quote: we can easily go up to 200,000 pairs a day

scores.rationale: Distribution is the company's clearest edge — distribution channel grew 20% in Q2 and drove FY26 growth, supported by state-specific go-to-market, 60+ fabricators and a debottlenecked central warehouse doubling throughput.
scores.quote: Our results reflect the strength of our distribution-led strategy

scores.rationale: Investment is directed at growth platforms — a new core 'architecture program', payment gateway build-out, WealthServ and non-MF business lines — with EBITDA margin still climbing to 46.5%, though capex quantum and incremental ROIC are never disclosed.
scores.quote: MF yields held quite well. And with all the operational efficiency, automation, the new platform program, what we call the architecture program

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend in any of the four calls; only unpaid recognition/awards for Bima Central are mentioned.

A sustained product-build culture has yielded new revenue-bearing products — payment gateway, Bima Central, WealthServ, SIF and GIFT City servicing — with the PG business scaling within a year of launch.
scores.quote: from a product development culture that the moment that we started almost 5, 6 years back to deeply build a product and a tinkering culture

scores.rationale: The only deal in the window is a small, complementary slump sale of NSE/DotEx's KRA business — no infrastructure, leases or headcount taken on, immediately revenue-accretive, and integration was completed within two quarters.
scores.quote: This is largely, the inventory of CAMS goes up... It does not bring in, brings in very marginal costs

scores.rationale: Dividends, buybacks or any distribution policy are not discussed in the available excerpts.

An asset-light processing platform absorbed 6x the historical onboarding workload and the NSE KRA book with marginal incremental cost, while EBITDA margin climbed from ~43.5% to 46.5% behind a 68% share moat.
scores.quote: Percentage EBITDA climbed back to just in excess of 46%, about 46.5%

scores.rationale: Real applied-AI depth is emerging (matchmaking agents, pricing agents, image-recognition condition assessment) but it is recent and not yet proven to be defensible or revenue-material.
scores.quote: what we're able to do today with photographic image recognition, we're able to judge condition

scores.rationale: Genuine two-sided marketplaces with 150 million yearly users and 85 million MAUs arriving 95% organically, where added buyers and sellers directly improve matchmaking for the other side.
scores.quote: CarWale, BikeWale, OLX, all our 3 consumer platforms get more than 150 million yearly active users, which is unique by itself

scores.rationale: The combination of 500+ physical auction/abSure locations and a 1.9 million vehicles-a-year auction run rate is a physical service reach no pure-digital rival can match.
scores.quote: Vehicles auctioned at a rate of 1.9 million vehicles a year.

scores.rationale: No capex figures are disclosed, but management describes growth-oriented investment in localised manufacturing of industrial products and supply-chain localisation rather than pure maintenance spend.
scores.quote: We brought our globally acclaimed metalworking fluids Hysol MB 50 and Hysol 20 XBB range to the Indian market through local production

scores.rationale: Sustained, large-scale A&P (SRK-led Activ/Garmi Mein Bhi 3X campaign, Power1 and EDGE racing platforms) reached 300mn+ consumers and coincided with 12 straight quarters of volume-led growth, so the spend is visibly converting to sales.
scores.quote: Our brand building initiatives reached an unprecedented scale, touching 300-plus million consumers and trade professionals

scores.rationale: Consistent new-product output — ~20 localised launches in FY25, first-to-market API SQ MAGNATEC, India's first RRBO-based engine oil, EV fluids from the local technology centre — though R&D intensity is modest and leans on parent technology.
scores.quote: launched new products and localized close to 20 products across automotive, industrial and our specialty range

scores.rationale: No acquisitions were announced or discussed in any of the four calls; only non-equity MoUs with VinFast, Triumph and HPCL, which are not M&A.

A coherent, consistent dividend policy (₹3.50 interim plus ₹5.25 final = ₹8.75 for FY25) explicitly balanced against reinvestment, but there is no buyback and hence no valuation-sensitive repurchase discipline to credit.
scores.quote: total dividend for the year to INR8.75 per share. This reflects our commitment to consistent shareholder returns while ensuring that we retain flexibility to invest

scores.rationale: The blending-and-distribution model is asset-light with tightly managed working capital and robust cash conversion on ₹5,722cr revenue, protected by brand and distribution, though no asset-turn metric is given on the calls.
scores.quote: We managed costs and working capital tightly, which supported profitability even in a high-growth environment

scores.rationale: Share is being gained and management claims No.1 position in key categories, but at 20%+ overall share in a leadership position the incremental runway is more limited than the framework's ideal challenger.
scores.quote: gained market share in our core automotive lubricants business

scores.rationale: Expansion is domestic-geographic (rural/Bharat, sub-20,000-population villages, 40,000 rural outlets, 700 Rural Service Express) and is executing well, but there is no international expansion given the parent's global structure.
scores.quote: we focused on expanding our reach directly into villages that have a population below 20,000

scores.rationale: Growth is explicitly volume-led with FY25 volume up 8% against revenue up only 7%, implying negative net price/mix, the opposite of the pricing-and-mix-led growth the framework rewards.
scores.quote: For the full year, volume grew 8% year-on-year... revenue from operations grew 7% year-on-year to INR5,722 crores

scores.rationale: The company is not positioned near a cycle bottom; it is entering a rising input-cost cycle from Middle East conflict, crude and currency, which is a headwind rather than an identifiable upturn ahead.
scores.quote: we saw the early signs of external headwinds driven by the conflict in the Middle East

scores.rationale: Management points to low per-capita vehicle penetration and government-led manufacturing as structural supports, but the lubricant end market faces eventual EV-driven erosion that they can only partly hedge with EV fluids and services.
scores.quote: low per capita penetration of cars and bikes should continue to support the core lubricant demand

scores.rationale: Organic-only growth, no acquisitions, a debt-free/strong balance sheet and explicitly disciplined capital deployment, though the calls show no evidence of counter-cyclical investment.
scores.quote: Our capital allocation approach remains consistent, disciplined deployment, strong cash generation and a continued focus on shareholder returns

scores.rationale: Strategy (Bharat/rural, industrial, services) has been executed consistently for multiple years and survived leadership change, but the MD exited mid-window leaving an interim CEO, and independence is clouded by a pending parent-level ownership transaction.
scores.quote: on discussions around shareholder development at parent level... the deal is subject to closure after various approvals

scores.rationale: Management commentary is process-and-metrics led with no personality cult; the celebrity presence is in brand campaigns, not in the executives themselves.
scores.quote: stay close to customers, make smart choices and deliver with discipline

scores.rationale: Capability development is mentioned and the interim CEO was promoted internally, but the CFO was hired externally from P&G and the MD seat turned over again within the window, so the internal pipeline is not demonstrated.
scores.quote: She is our CFO, who has been on Board for over a week now, and she comes to us with over 17 years of experience at P&G India

scores.rationale: They disclose unfavourable facts plainly — PAT below prior-year Q4 due to Labour Code charges, persistent competitive intensity, forex and feedstock pressure — though no explicit ownership of a strategic mistake appears.
scores.quote: PAT was down from INR271 crores in quarter 4 '24, though, which was impacted by onetime Labour Code-related changes

scores.rationale: Steady results owe substantially to an inherited global brand, an entrenched distribution base and a benign category rather than clearly separable current-management skill, and the leadership churn makes attribution to the present team unsafe.
scores.quote: the deep trust that customers repos in Castrol brand

scores.rationale: Castrol occupies a strong position in the aftermarket mechanic's mind — a million mechanics on its Fast Scan app acting as advocates — which is a mind-share near-monopoly in the influencer channel, if not in the category.
scores.quote: the flagship mechanic Connect app called Fast Scan, which is being used by over 1 million mechanics in India

scores.rationale: There are mild lock-ins via OEM co-engineering, chemical management services contracts and branded workshops, but consumer switching costs in retail lubricants are low and no regional monopoly exists.
scores.quote: We take end-to-end responsibility across the chemical life cycle, delivering efficiency, compliance and value to our customers

scores.rationale: Castrol leads with only ~20% share against PSU oil marketers and multiple global brands, and management repeatedly flags competitive intensity, so this is a fragmented market rather than a stable oligopoly.
scores.quote: Our overall market share stands at over 20%

scores.rationale: Management names competitive intensity as a persistent condition across all four calls, and revenue growing slower than volume points to price/mix give-back rather than rational pricing.
scores.quote: As competitive intensity continues, raw material movement and currency volatility persisted through the year

scores.rationale: Repeated share gains in core automotive and 13% industrial growth in a market with weaker PSU and regional lubricant players indicates identifiable donors of share.
scores.quote: All of this has translated into continued market share gain, reinforces that our strategy is delivering as planned

scores.rationale: Castrol is a heavily advertised, widely covered listed leader currently at the centre of a global parent-level ownership transaction — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: Our brand building initiatives reached an unprecedented scale, touching 300-plus million consumers

scores.rationale: Brand image supports premium mix (premium portfolio grew double digit in both volume and value) and ~23.5% EBITDA margin, but overall realisation lagged volume, so pricing power is real yet not fully exercised.
scores.quote: our premium brands portfolio delivered a double-digit volume growth and value growth during the quarter

scores.rationale: The proposition sold is protection and reliability — guaranteed 3X protection claims, OEM co-engineering approvals, and supply continuity positioned as the priority in a disrupted environment — with trust ahead of price.
scores.quote: our priority, first and foremost, is to be a reliable partner during times of uncertainty

scores.rationale: Accessibility is best-in-class and still widening: 150,000-160,000 retail outlets, 40,000 rural outlets, 700 Rural Service Express kiosks, 800 auto-service centres and direct digital intimacy with a million mechanics.
scores.quote: Castrol India's products are now available through over 150,000 retail outlets across the country

scores.rationale: The benefit type is well matched to each customer — image and protection claims for retail bikers/car owners, and TCO, compliance and end-to-end chemical management lock-in for industrial B2B accounts.
scores.quote: industrial, where we have now seen consistent growth for 9 quarters and Q2 growth in industrial being at 13%

scores.rationale: There is genuine formulation capability — first-mover on API SQ, India's first RRBO-based engine oil, localised EV transmission and thermal fluids — but the depth derives largely from the global parent and R&D intensity is not high.
scores.quote: we shall be leveraging our technology center to formulate EV transmission and thermal fluids suited for India's environment

scores.rationale: There is a partial two-sided effect: the mechanic app and workshop base make Castrol more attractive to OEMs, and VinFast's choice to plug into that network validates it, but the loop is not strongly self-reinforcing.
scores.quote: VinFast will leverage Castrol's workshop network, select Castrol auto service outlets, to provide aftersales service

scores.rationale: The reach — 150,000+ outlets, 40,000 rural points, 800 Castrol Auto Service centres across 300 cities, 34,000 bike workshops and 13,000 multi-brand workshops — is a service-and-availability advantage rivals cannot replicate quickly.
scores.quote: 800 Castrol Auto Services at the end of March. We now tapped 34,000 independent bike workshops

scores.rationale: Growth investment is claimed in AI and an edge data centre but the calls give no capex figures or incremental ROIC to judge it against maintenance spend.
scores.quote: building a sovereign, compliant, and scalable foundation through our edge data center

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend in any of the four calls.
A steady stream of new product launches (PayCentral.AI, Agent OS, CommerceAI, VLLMs) but no R&D spend disclosure and no evidence any of it has converted into paying customers or revenue.
scores.quote: launch of PayCentral.AI. It is India's first agentic payment platform built on Google's agent payment protocol

scores.rationale: Deals in the window are the opposite of small complementary bolt-ons: an INR 800 crore related-party transfer of the e-commerce business to 80%-owned Rediff, plus stakes in Online PSB Loans and NBFC Ratnaafin, moving into lending far from the payments core.
scores.quote: Board has approved a strategic transfer of the e-commerce platform infrastructure business to Rediff.com for INR 800 crores

scores.rationale: The company raised equity via a rights issue during the window and no buyback, dividend or distribution policy is mentioned at all.
scores.quote: I want to express our deepest gratitude to all our investors for the successful rights issue

scores.rationale: The payments model is inherently asset-light, but management concedes a competitive pricing environment and de-emphasises take rates, so the protecting moat the parameter requires is not evidenced.
scores.quote: prioritizing volume-led growth and absolute profitability over headline take rates

scores.rationale: Clear runway (not dominant) with evidence of active share capture through merchant onboarding, cooperative-bank tie-ups and Bharat Connect/Bajaj Finance integrations.
scores.quote: we continue to see robust merchant onboarding and TPV growth supported by favorable card mix and a vertical expansion

scores.rationale: UAE and Saudi operations are described as scaling with real volume, Oman is launching with multiple banks and GIFT City/IFSCA approvals are in hand, though the US ambition is still only stated intent.
scores.quote: our operations in UAE and Saudi Arabia are scaling rapidly, processing billions of dirhams annually with Oman set to launch next

scores.rationale: Management explicitly chooses volume over price and accepts take-rate compression, with only a partial offset from a favourable credit-card and large-ticket mix.
scores.quote: we are concisely prioritizing volume-led growth and absolute profitability over headline take rates

scores.rationale: No cyclical positioning is discussed; digital payments is not framed as a cycle with an identifiable trough.
The end market — India's digital payments and cross-border commerce infrastructure — is in genuine secular expansion, and the company's TPV and regulatory footprint track that expansion.
scores.quote: As India's digital economy gains momentum, Infibeam isn't just participating. We are building the roads, the rails and the engines

scores.rationale: Within twelve months management raised rights-issue capital, restructured the group, renamed the company, and pushed into AI content streaming, a consumer UPI app, NBFC stakes and lending — the antithesis of organic focus and no-big-M&A discipline.
scores.quote: One of our major strategic priorities going forward is embedded finance and lending

scores.rationale: One genuine multi-year promise was delivered (the $1bn run-rate target set in 2023 hit roughly on time), but the strategic identity is re-articulated almost every quarter, which undercuts tenacity on a single vision.
scores.quote: we had suggested by March 2026, we expect to hit $1 billion on an annual revenue run rate basis... we were able to achieve nearly that run rate

scores.rationale: Management renamed the listed company to AvenuesAI and leans on superlative claims ('world's first', 'global first', 'India's first'), the opposite of low-profile substance.
scores.quote: creating the world's first agentic payment framework

scores.rationale: No discussion of talent development, succession or internal leadership pipeline in any of the four calls.
Commentary is dominated by abstract flywheel and convergence narrative with no acknowledgement of any mistake or shortfall; the one candid note is passing reference to pricing competition.
scores.quote: This is not just about optimizing what we have. It's about designing the infrastructure for tomorrow.

scores.rationale: Record results are attributed to the company's architecture and flywheel rather than to the underlying digital-payments tailwind, making it hard to separate skill from market growth.
scores.quote: our best-ever performance with record revenues and profits, the highest in our history

scores.rationale: CCAvenue holds a trusted brand position in merchant minds but competes directly on price, so there is no monopoly-like hold on the customer or an aftermarket.
scores.quote: one of the India's most trusted payment gateways

scores.rationale: Switching-cost lock-in is asserted as a future outcome of ecosystem integration rather than demonstrated with retention or churn evidence today.
scores.quote: The switching cost moved beyond just contractual dependency and they become operationally existential

scores.rationale: Indian payment aggregation is a crowded, price-competitive field where merchants clearly hold negotiating power, as shown by management's retreat on take rates.
scores.quote: delivering stronger cash flows and operating leverage even in a competitive pricing environment

scores.rationale: The full RBI/IFSCA licence stack is a real regulatory barrier, but it is offset by an admittedly competitive pricing environment that signals irrational discounting among incumbents.
scores.quote: Completing a full regulatory stack, acquiring, issuing and billing, making us one of the few Indian fintechs with end-to-end authorization

scores.rationale: No competitor is identified as weak or losing share; competition is only referenced generically as pricing pressure.
The company deliberately maximised visibility by rebranding around the most capital-attracting theme available rather than staying in an ignored niche.
scores.quote: we completed our corporate rebranding to AvenuesAI Limited. This is not a cosmetic change.

scores.rationale: This is B2B payment plumbing with no image- or taste-driven pricing power, and management is conceding price to hold volume.
scores.quote: maintaining discipline on take rates

scores.rationale: The core customer proposition is regulatory certainty and reliability — the full RBI acquiring/issuing/billing licence stack and bank-grade integrations are what merchants are buying.
scores.quote: offering deep integrations, regulatory credibility and a strong merchant partnership across sectors

scores.rationale: Distribution reach and direct merchant intimacy are evident through cooperative-bank channels, net-banking integrations and vertical-by-vertical onboarding.
scores.quote: CCAvenue also integrated its net banking platform with TJSB Sahakari Bank, India's fourth-largest urban co-operative bank

scores.rationale: The corporate side is correctly matched on reliability and compliance, but the new B2C push into a UPI app and AI content streaming targets retail customers with no established brand intangible.
scores.quote: we also transitioned into becoming a hybrid B2B and B2C organization

scores.rationale: Extensive AI capability claims across payments, agents and orchestration, but no R&D intensity figures, no customer wins attributed to the technology, and no demonstrated superior customer outcome.
scores.quote: Phronetic.AI, our AI arm focusing on building advanced reasoning models, VLLMs and Agentic AI platforms

scores.rationale: A closed-loop learning flywheel between consumers, merchants and data is described in detail, but presented as a design intent rather than with any metric showing it strengthening with scale.
scores.quote: this quarter, for the first time, we are seeing the flywheel move as one system

scores.rationale: Reach across enterprise merchants, SMEs, cooperative banking networks, net-banking rails and now offline POS gives a distribution footprint that is hard to replicate quickly in a service-critical category.
scores.quote: We also received the RBI authorization for off-line payment aggregation, extending our presence across physical merchants locations through POS-based networks

scores.rationale: Management says existing capacity suffices for the next two years with no committed growth capex, only vague talk of a possible freeze-dried tie-up, so growth capex is currently paused in favour of deleveraging.
scores.quote: on a largely on a long-term basis for the next 2 years, we are good as far as capacity is concerned

scores.rationale: A&P is not quantified but management cites measurable brand-equity gains (awareness, conversion) alongside 40-50% branded growth and Continental reaching #3 nationally, indicating spend is converting into equity.
scores.quote: there has been a pretty good equity building on the brand also. We are seeing in our equity scores also. There's quite a good uptick in the awareness levels and the conversion ratio

scores.rationale: No discussion of R&D spend or new-product pipeline in any of the four calls.
No acquisitions completed or announced in the window; only a hypothetical 'strategic tie-up' for freeze-dried capacity was floated without detail.
scores.quote: we could look at not necessarily a capacity expansion, but maybe a strategic tie-up

scores.rationale: Only a routine INR2.75 interim dividend was declared with no buyback or articulated distribution policy, cash instead going to debt reduction.
scores.quote: the company has declared an interim dividend of INR2.75 per equity share for FY25-26

scores.rationale: The business is capital-intensive (large plants, INR1,268 crore debt) but asset turn improved sharply in FY26 as revenue grew 43% on existing capacity and working capital days fell 80 days to 166, lifting cash flow to INR858 crores.
scores.quote: Working capital days have actually come down by 80 days to 166 days

scores.rationale: Continental moved to #3 in India with double-digit share in modern trade and e-commerce and #2 in AP/Telangana, off a small base with clear runway against two entrenched leaders.
scores.quote: Continental as a brand is well established as the number 3 player in the country. And in some regions and platforms, we are also the number 2 player

scores.rationale: Expansion is real and multi-pronged — manufacturing flexibility across India and Vietnam let it sidestep US tariffs, while domestically it is pushing beyond the South into West and Northeast via modern trade and e-commerce.
scores.quote: it's not going to impact much of the trade and especially for us because we had the flexibility to supply from Vietnam

scores.rationale: Management explicitly disclaims pricing as a growth driver because it runs a cost-plus model where realisations merely track green coffee, so growth is volume-led (18-20%) with per-kilo EBITDA roughly flat and down sequentially in Q4.
scores.quote: it's actually not right to look at the price growth because that is determined on the green coffee prices considering we do cost-plus model

scores.rationale: Green coffee has come off its peak to INR3,300-3,800 with good Brazil supply, and stabilising prices are pulling back long-term contracts that had lapsed during the volatile period — a favourable turn from the trough of customer hesitancy.
scores.quote: last year, when the prices are so choppy, our volume growth were in the range of 10% to 15%, which goes to now 15% to 20%, considering long-term contracts have started to seep in

scores.rationale: Management observes coffee demand stayed robust through extreme price inflation — the hallmark of secular, not cyclical, end-market growth — alongside a structurally under-penetrated Indian coffee market.
scores.quote: considering the demand has always been robust, the supply fluctuations have led to these kind of price volatility

scores.rationale: FY26 saw debt cut from a INR1,950 crore peak to INR1,268 crores (net INR963 crores by June) with D/E from 0.92 to 0.5, achieved organically with no equity dilution, no asset sales and no pause in growth.
scores.quote: All this happened without dilution of equity, without sale of any non-core assets or without pausing the growth

scores.rationale: The chairman explicitly frames CCL as a year-on-year, 30-year capacity-building story and refuses to be judged quarterly, and the promised deleveraging plan was executed as communicated.
scores.quote: we maintain CCL, it's a year-on-year company. Don't look at quarter-to-quarter. See it's been 30 years now

scores.rationale: Calls are hosted by small-house brokers, opening remarks are plain numbers without promotional framing, and management repeatedly damps down excitement rather than amplifying it.
scores.quote: I don't think so that there's much to read into that

scores.rationale: No discussion of talent development, succession or leadership pipeline in the four calls.

Management refuses to upgrade guidance despite beating it, admits the sequential EBITDA-per-kilo decline, concedes the FX margin exposure, and states plainly that lower US tariffs give no advantage since the earlier tariffs caused no harm.
scores.quote: even if the lowering of tariff also is not going to help us... it's not going to give us undue advantage now also

scores.rationale: Headline 43% revenue growth is largely green-coffee price pass-through in a cost-plus model, but stripping that out still leaves genuine skill — 18-20% volume growth, improved annual EBITDA per kilo and a self-funded INR750 crore debt reduction.
scores.quote: since our top line is a function of green coffee prices, the revenue growth stands at 13.76%

scores.rationale: As a private-label/contract instant-coffee supplier CCL is one of several global sources, and in branded India it is the #3 challenger, not a monopoly in any customer's mind.
scores.quote: Continental as a brand is well established as the number 3 player in the country

scores.rationale: Long-term contracts with customised blends returning as prices stabilise imply real switching friction, though management never claims lock-in and admits customers go wait-and-watch when prices move.
scores.quote: the long-term contracts obviously start coming in. And this is evident in our volume growth also

scores.rationale: Indian branded coffee is a stable three-player structure, but CCL's larger B2B business sells to sophisticated global retailers on a cost-plus basis, meaning the paying customer retains full negotiating power over the margin.
scores.quote: we do cost-plus model

scores.rationale: Domestic branded competition is turning irrational, with rivals pushing hard on price in response to CCL's share gains and pricing now varying by channel, day and month.
scores.quote: considering the way we have gained market share, a lot of players are kind of pushing very hard on the pricing front as well

scores.rationale: CCL is taking share in AP/Telangana from an established MNC incumbent, indicating a donator exists, though the players it is displacing are large and well-capitalised rather than weak.
scores.quote: if you were to take the states of AP and Telangana, where we are very strong, we are #2 player now

scores.rationale: Management is understated but the stock is covered by mainstream brokerages including Nuvama, Motilal Oswal and Systematix, so it is not off the radar of capital.
scores.quote: the line of Abneesh Roy from Nuvama

scores.rationale: The core business is explicitly cost-plus with EBITDA measured per kilo rather than as a margin, so there is no image-based pricing power; the brand equity being built in India is a small and recent exception.
scores.quote: our business works on per kilo EBITDA where there is no contraction

scores.rationale: In the most volatile green-coffee market in decades CCL's customers returned to long-term contracts specifically because it could assure supply and stable delivery, including rerouting through Vietnam around US tariffs.
scores.quote: the more stable they are, they are more assured they are. So the long-term contracts obviously start coming in

scores.rationale: Domestically CCL is executing an aggressive distribution build, with strong general-trade reach in the South and channel shares in modern trade and e-commerce exceeding its overall market share.
scores.quote: our channel shares in e-com and modern trade are much better than our overall market shares

scores.rationale: The match is coherent on both sides — corporate B2B customers are served with reliability, supply flexibility and long-term contracts, while Indian retail consumers are addressed via brand equity building and distribution.
scores.quote: There is consistent market share gains across geographies and platforms

scores.rationale: No R&D intensity, product technology or process-differentiation claims made in any of the four calls.
Nothing in the calls describes any two-sided or self-reinforcing network dynamic.

Manufacturing and supply reach across India and Vietnam let CCL serve global customers through tariff disruption, and Indian distribution is expanding, but management describes distribution in the North and West as still under-penetrated.
scores.quote: other markets like the Northeast and the West, where our distribution may not be so penetrated as it is in South

scores.rationale: Technology capex is high and rising and framed as capacity ahead of demand, but the incremental return this year is negative — 9M consolidated income rose only 3% (INR970cr vs INR944cr) while PAT fell to INR375cr from INR426cr.
scores.quote: your technology costs have increased by around 4x since FY '23, whereas during the same period, volume increase has been somewhere around 1.82x

scores.rationale: Sustained brand/trust-building spend through investor education (100mn YouTube views, 12-language IPF microsite, Amar Chitra Katha comic, SEBI vs SCAM), though it is largely IPF/regulator-linked outreach rather than sales-driving A&P.
scores.quote: we recently crossed a milestone of 100 million YouTube channel views on the CDSL account

scores.rationale: New product launches (nomination Phase 2, portability, Form 121, proxy-advisory in MyEasi) are regulator-mooted rather than outputs of a proprietary R&D engine, and no R&D efficiency evidence is given.
scores.quote: There are newer products also which have been coming into play, which the regulator keeps on kind of doing some time-to-time.

scores.rationale: No acquisition was discussed in any of the four calls; expansion was organic (new IFSC unit under CVL), leaving nothing to score.
The only dividend discussed is an intra-group receipt from the subsidiary; no buyback, payout policy or valuation-linked distribution reasoning appears in the window.
scores.quote: our reported profit had included a significant contribution from dividend received from our subsidiary

scores.rationale: The depository model remains asset-light with a regulatory duopoly moat and ~80% share, but management is explicitly turning it more capital-intensive by pre-building capacity, which pressures asset turn.
scores.quote: as we grow in business, it's like -- as I've said many times, it's like similar to basically an infrastructure company

scores.rationale: Clear evidence of continued share capture (79% to 80%+, with 85-90% incremental share and 2.7cr accounts opened in FY26), but the runway is limited because CDSL is already dominant in retail demat.
scores.quote: maintaining our 80% plus market share with a consistently incremental market share of 85% to 90%

scores.rationale: A credible but small first step outside the domestic market via SEBI no-objection for a CVL KRA unit at GIFT IFSC; no revenue contribution yet and no other geography.
scores.quote: received SEBI's no objection to set up a separate business unit at GIFT IFSC, proposed to be registered with IFSCA as the first KYC Registration agency

scores.rationale: Growth is account-volume driven while price-sensitive lines shrink — ADT fell 18% YoY in Q2 and 8.3% in Q3, annual issuer charges were flat sequentially despite more issuers, and CVL revenue fell to INR132cr from INR189cr on 9M.
scores.quote: we have seen strong growth Y-o-Y, but on a sequential basis, it has been almost flat. This is despite sequential strong growth in terms of the number of issuers

scores.rationale: The transaction cycle is clearly in a downturn (ADT down 8-18% YoY, activity 'moderated from last year's highs') but management identifies no upturn and flags added geopolitical uncertainty, so the bottom is not established.
scores.quote: the quarter has been one of steady participation and continued broad-based growth, even as market activity moderated from last year's highs

scores.rationale: The end market is in secular expansion — industry demat accounts went from ~20cr to 22.4cr within the four calls, with SEBI survey evidence of a large untapped participant pool.
scores.quote: we have crossed 22.4 crores demat accounts as a depository industry

scores.rationale: Purely organic expansion, no acquisitions or leverage discussed, and counter-cyclical investment in technology and capacity precisely while market volumes were falling.
scores.quote: that says the capacity building process so that as the surge in case if it happens like we have seen in 2020, '21, it becomes seamless for the market

scores.rationale: Consistent, repeated long-horizon framing across all four calls with refusal to give guidance, though the agenda is heavily set by SEBI rather than independently chosen.
scores.quote: Our intent is to build a more long-term resilient infrastructure institution as I have been saying in all my past investor calls.

scores.rationale: Every call opens with an extended recitation of awards, and the CEO personally highlighted a 'India's Best CEO of 2026' accolade in a quarter when consolidated profit had fallen.
scores.quote: Business Today recognized me... in the Market Infrastructure Institutions category as India's Best CEO of 2026

scores.rationale: Hiring is described structurally across SEBI's three verticals and the subsidiary CEO bench (Alvares, Shetty, Srivastava) is stable across the window, but no systematic talent-development or succession process is evidenced.
scores.quote: we need the people to get recruited in all these three verticals at the paramount form

scores.rationale: The CFO proactively flagged that prior-period profits were flattered by INR47.5cr and INR62cr of intra-group dividends, aiding fair comparison, though management declines to break out IPO versus corporate-action income.
scores.quote: In comparison, the profit reported for September 2025 quarter has entirely been generated from our core operations

scores.rationale: The narrative leans heavily on awards and recognitions while the underlying delivery weakened (9M PAT down to INR375cr from INR426cr, CVL PAT down to INR42cr from INR91cr), so results reflect a structural duopoly position more than demonstrated managerial skill.
scores.quote: Profit after tax was INR42 crores as compared to INR91 crores 9FY25

scores.rationale: CDSL holds a monopoly-like position in retail demat (80% share, 85-90% incremental) and CVL is the first and largest KRA, though pricing is regulator-set rather than owner-set.
scores.quote: CDSL Ventures, our wholly owned subsidiary and the first and largest KYC registration agency

scores.rationale: Investor accounts and issuer ISINs are sticky annuity relationships, but management is itself automating demat account portability, which mechanically lowers switching costs.
scores.quote: we also executed the next phase of the Demat account portability cum closure automating investor transfer

scores.rationale: A stable regulated duopoly with NSDL where end investors and issuers have no negotiating power, but tariffs are set by SEBI, capping the benefit of that structure.
scores.quote: both the depositories have collaborated to introduce a new feature in the respective investor apps

scores.rationale: Depository entry is effectively closed by SEBI's MII regulations and pricing is administered rather than competed away, though the adjacent KRA business has just seen a new entrant in KFintech.
scores.quote: if you are referring to KFintech, they have just started operation. And we have not really seen any impact as on date.

scores.rationale: NSDL is a clear share donator in retail demat — CDSL's incremental account share of 85-90% far exceeds its 80% installed base, so the gap keeps widening.
scores.quote: CDSL saw more than 2.7 crores accounts opened this financial year, bringing our total to 18.01 crores demat accounts

scores.rationale: The opposite of obscure — a listed MII with quarterly broker-hosted calls, a stream of global awards, SEBI-chairperson-attended launches and dense analyst coverage.
scores.quote: The event was graced by eminent leaders, including the honourable SEBI Chairman

scores.rationale: Trust is the stated proposition and gross margins are structurally high, but there is no pricing power from image — tariffs are regulated and the KYC arm's revenue fell sharply under competitive and CKYC pressure.
scores.quote: revenue from operations was INR132 crores compared to INR189 crores in the 9MFY'25

scores.rationale: The entire proposition is certainty and reliability — uninterrupted operations, peak-volume readiness and security — with price never the discussed variable.
scores.quote: In such periods, the role of trusted market infrastructure becomes even more important.

scores.rationale: Continual accessibility improvements (MyEasi app, nomination Phase 2, portability, Form 15G/15H acceptance, ease of integration) serve investors directly, though the customer relationship is intermediated by DPs.
scores.quote: Our focus remains on strengthening the underlying value proposition of the platform through technology, service standards, ease of integration, and trust.

scores.rationale: The benefit mix is well matched — reliability and integration lock-in for corporate customers (DPs, issuers) and access/education/convenience for the retail investor base.
scores.quote: our responsibility is to make access, education and protection move together as a single unit

scores.rationale: Technology spend is large and rising but is described as capacity, infrastructure, security and network upkeep across four standard layers, not a differentiated multi-product technology edge.
scores.quote: on all the four components of infrastructure, application, security and network is where we are continuously innovating

scores.rationale: A real but modest two-sided effect — DP preference feeds investor accounts which feeds incremental share of 85-90% — though issuers must connect to both depositories regardless, limiting self-reinforcement.
scores.quote: supported by the continuous trust of investors and depository participants on our platform

scores.rationale: The DP reach is the decisive advantage NSDL cannot match, converting into 65-75 lakh new accounts per quarter and 2.7cr for the full year at 80%+ share.
scores.quote: CDSL saw more than 75-+ lakh accounts opened during this quarter, bringing our total to 17.27 crores

scores.rationale: Sustained ~Rs1,000 crore annual capex on capacity expansion plus CAMSO upstream calender/mixer equipment while running at 80-85% utilisation indicates genuine growth (not just maintenance) capex, though incremental ROIC is not disclosed.
scores.quote: Overall capacity utilization is around 80% to 85%. Expansion projects are progressing as per plan, and we expect total CAPEX for the financial year to be around Rs. 1,000 crores

scores.rationale: A&P is increasingly digital and measurably converting — premium lead-generated sales doubled, brand sentiment up 46% and a top-10 Brand Finance ranking — suggesting spend that builds equity and sells product.
scores.quote: Our premium sales through lead generation grew 2x in quarter 1 while overall 4-wheeler sale through lead generation grew 32%

scores.rationale: R&D consistently yields commercialised new products across the window — bio-based SecuraDrive CIRCL, RockRad premium TBR, run-flat/Z-rated 21-inch, and 130+ new off-highway SKUs in FY26 — plus repeated OEM nominations.
scores.quote: About 130-plus new off-highway SKUs were launched, which gives robustness to our product portfolio

scores.rationale: CAMSO is the opposite of a small simple bolt-on: a multi-year (4-6 quarter) carve-out from Michelin at ~50% utilisation, with $80m of Sri Lanka debt, transition costs and FX losses that cut consolidated Q1 PAT to INR4 crores versus INR98 crores standalone.
scores.quote: higher costs in our CAMSO business arising from initial investments in new warehouses, new offices, start-up costs, new hirings there without commensurate growth in revenue

scores.rationale: No discussion of dividends, buybacks or any distribution policy in the last four calls.

Tyre manufacturing here is structurally asset-heavy — Rs1,000 crore annual capex, owned plants at Halol/Chennai/Ambernath/Sri Lanka and new upstream calender and mixer lines being erected — so this is not an asset-light model.
scores.quote: it will come to our hands only when we erect the upstream equipment of calender and mixture

scores.rationale: Clear evidence of share capture from a non-dominant base — FY26 replacement share up ~0.5% in PCUV and TBR and ~1% in motorcycle — though OEM share slipped slightly in Q4 and EV OEM share drifted from 30% to 25%.
scores.quote: In PC UV about 0.5% up; in motorcycle, about 1% up... in truck bus radial also about 0.5% up in replacement

scores.rationale: International is the standout: growth of high-teens to 30% every quarter, saliency up from ~19% to ~23%, and permanent localised entities set up in Germany, UK, France and Poland, sustained despite US tariffs and Middle East disruption.
scores.quote: We have set up overseas entities and branches in Germany, U.K., France and Poland to build a more permanent localized presence

scores.rationale: Growth is explicitly volume-led rather than price/mix-led, and pricing action is reactive cost pass-through taken with a lag after a 15-16% raw material spike crushed Q1 EBITDA to 9.1%.
scores.quote: 2/3rd of the stand-alone revenue growth came from volumes

scores.rationale: The company sits at a visible margin trough — Q1 FY27 gross margin down 575bps and EBITDA at 9.1% on a raw-material spike — with 7-8% replacement price hikes already taken and more planned, a recognisable setup for recovery ahead.
scores.quote: Q1 standalone gross margin witnessed a contraction of 575 basis points Q-o-Q... we have been taking price increase right through April, May and June

scores.rationale: Management frames a multi-year but modest secular runway — healthy single-digit industry growth through FY31 aided by GST formalisation, EV adoption and premiumisation — real but not explosive expansion.
scores.quote: supportive tax policies, increasing EV adoption and ongoing premiumization trends are likely to position the tire industry for a healthy single-digit growth through FY '31

scores.rationale: Capex guidance is held steady and consistent, but the period is defined by a large, complex, debt-funded acquisition whose Sri Lanka capital structure is now being reworked to cut interest and FX risk — the opposite of organic focus with prudent leverage.
scores.quote: nearly INR48 crores impact from depreciation in Sri Lankan Rupees, LKR, on the $80 million denominated debt... We are about to change the capital structure

scores.rationale: The same four strategic pillars — electrification, international, premiumisation, digital/AI — are reported against in every call with quantified progress, and the CAMSO integration is being executed to a stated multi-year plan rather than abandoned when costs bit.
scores.quote: the CAMSO business is in transition and will continue to be in transition for at least 4 more quarters. At the outset, we had said 4 to 6 quarters, so 2 quarters have gone

scores.rationale: Calls are run by the MD and CFO in a plain operational register, but each quarter also foregrounds awards and rankings (EcoVadis Gold, India Green Manufacturing gold medal, Vault Circle, Brand Finance top 10), which is mild self-promotion rather than pure substance.
scores.quote: We achieved EcoVadis Gold rating, which places us in the Top-5 percentile of the companies globally

scores.rationale: Only thin people-related disclosure — a rising employee happiness score and CAMSO sales hiring — with nothing on systematic talent development or an internal leadership pipeline.
scores.quote: employee happiness score to move up to 87% from 85% previous year

scores.rationale: Consistently candid across all four calls: quantified bad news is volunteered up front, including September replacement de-growth, a 575bps gross margin collapse, sub-scale CAMSO utilisation, Sri Lanka cyclone and competition, and specific market-share losses.
