scores.quote: there was some marginal drop in share in scooter and in passenger, which is much less than 1%

scores.rationale: Strong headline growth is substantially macro- and base-driven — GST reform, softening rubber, and repeatedly acknowledged low bases — and management itself flags this, so results should not be read as pure managerial skill.
scores.quote: In PCUV, we had a low base effect. So growth was optically very high in OEMs

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like position in the customer's mind: CEAT is one of several Indian tyre makers fighting for OEM fitments and dealer shelf, with share measured in fractions of a percent and Asian competitors pressuring price in Europe.
scores.quote: despite uncertainty surrounding the U.S. trade agreement and pricing pressure from Asian competitors, particularly in European market

scores.rationale: There is a quasi-regional stronghold in Sri Lanka with market leadership across categories, and OEM fitments create some replacement pull-through, but the Sri Lanka position is now under active competitive attack rather than protected.
scores.quote: local competition further intensified, particularly in 2-wheeler and PCR categories. Focus here is to hold on to our already high market shares

scores.rationale: The Indian tyre market behaves as a stable oligopoly — CEAT can push 7-8% replacement price increases through in a single quarter and expects OEM increases on a scheduled lag, which implies limited end-customer negotiating power.
scores.quote: About 7% to 8% in replacement, about 3% to 4% in OE and about 4% to 5% in IB has already been taken

scores.rationale: Capital intensity and OEM homologation are real barriers and industry-wide price hikes have stuck, but rationality is imperfect — Asian competitor price pressure in Europe and intensifying competition in Sri Lanka are both cited.
scores.quote: pricing pressure from Asian competitors, particularly in European market

scores.rationale: There are identifiable donors: incumbent OEM fitments being displaced in higher rim sizes, and global suppliers ceding ground as India becomes an accepted alternate sourcing base for CV, OHT and PCUV tyres.
scores.quote: India is emerging as an alternate and credible sourcing base for these tires on the back of improved brand credibility with global OEMs

scores.rationale: This is a heavily covered large-cap — four consecutive calls hosted by different brokerages (Emkay, Equirus, JM Financial, Nirmal Bang) with dense analyst participation — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: welcome you all to Q1 FY '27 Earnings Conference Call of CEAT Tyres

scores.rationale: Some brand-based pricing power is emerging (premium 17-inch+ replacement volumes doubling, top-10 brand ranking, 40-42% gross margin band), but it was insufficient to hold margins through the Q1 raw-material spike, so demand is not price-indifferent.
scores.quote: Overall sales volume of premium tyres, which is 17-inch plus rim size tyre grew by 100% in replacement

scores.rationale: OEM customers buy validated reliability — CEAT is nominated onto new EV and premium launches and sells premium TBR on lower total cost of ownership rather than sticker price.
scores.quote: we have launched a couple of absolutely top-of-the-line premium products, which gives a lower TCO to our customers

scores.rationale: Access is being deepened on both ends — direct customer relationships taken over from Michelin plus localised European branches, and a digital/agentic front end converting leads at 32-100%+ growth.
scores.quote: about 60% of the customers have transited to CEAT by end of Q1, and we expect to complete the customer transition by end of Q2

scores.rationale: The benefit mix is correctly matched to customer type: brand, sentiment and premium imagery for retail replacement buyers, and TCO plus OEM homologation lock-in for corporate/fleet customers.
scores.quote: In truck bus radial also, we have started premiumizing... which gives a lower TCO to our customers

scores.rationale: There is a credible innovation cadence (bio-based concept tyre, run-flat, Z-rated 21-inch, EV-specific sizes) but no deep proprietary edge — CEAT still buys semi-finished compound from Michelin for its premium OHT line and will not control that value chain until FY28.
scores.quote: we will continue to buy semi-finished goods from Michelin till we set up our upstream equipments

scores.rationale: Nothing in the business model as described is self-reinforcing with scale — it is manufacturing sold through dealers and OEMs, where each additional customer confers no benefit on the next.
scores.quote: On the procurement front... we will continue to buy semi-finished goods from Michelin

scores.rationale: Distribution reach is a genuine and widening asset — leading Indian exporter of passenger car tyres, own branches now in four European markets, and direct takeover of the CAMSO customer base — though it is not unmatched versus larger domestic peers.
scores.quote: if we measure the share of Indian exports brand-wise, then CEAT is a leading exporter of passenger car tyres out of India

scores.rationale: FY26 capex of ~INR219 crores went mainly into growth assets (Falna glassware plant, Rajasthan integrated steel-bottle lines) with only some maintenance capex, but incremental ROIC is so far weak — glassware is only at breakeven at 60% utilisation and steel lines commissioned late.
scores.quote: Capex incurred during the year stood at around INR219 crores, which mainly includes investment for the setting of manufacturing line for steel bottle as well as other select consumerware product, writing instrument and some portion spent for the maintenance capex

scores.rationale: The only A&P-type spend discussed was reactive discounting and trade schemes to defend volumes in a weak demand environment, which compressed margins rather than building brand equity.
scores.quote: demand has been slow, and that is why sales promotion activities have increased in terms of schemes and some discounts

scores.rationale: No formal R&D line is disclosed, but a steady cadence of new product launches (mechanical pencils, arts stationery, licensed kids' products, premium pens) demonstrably drove the writing instruments turnaround from -10% to double-digit growth.
scores.quote: revenues from newly launched products, particularly in the premium pens category

scores.rationale: The Cello writing-instruments trademark deal is a complementary, capital-light bolt-on (brand leased from promoter entity CPIW rather than bought by the listed company) that began contributing in Q4 and drove 64% segment growth, though the related-party structure and unproven post-deal margin temper the score.
scores.quote: One of the subsidies of Cello World Limited has entered into an agreement to lease the trademark for Cello brand for stationery and writing instruments from CPIW

scores.rationale: No discussion of dividends, buybacks or any distribution policy appears in any of the four calls.

The business is actively becoming more asset-heavy — a new glassware plant and a fully integrated steel-bottle plant absorbing INR219 crores of capex while revenue grew only 8.8% — so asset turn is falling, and management itself flags working-capital/inventory discipline as a corrective priority.
scores.quote: Operating profits remain under pressure owing to higher costs associated with new glassware plant and steel bottle manufacturing unit

scores.rationale: Management claims share gains in glassware via import substitution against Chinese imports and is adding the Cello pens brand to a fragmented stationery market, but the core consumerware categories were flat-to-declining, so the evidence is partial.
scores.quote: Despite active dumping pressure from Chinese suppliers, we have successfully scaled up production and gained market share

scores.rationale: Exports are a small and volatile share (8.4% falling to 6.7%, then 7.6%), with a writing-instruments export slowdown early in the year and a pickup by Q4 — no articulated international expansion strategy.
scores.quote: Writing instruments continued to face challenges in terms of export demand slowdown

scores.rationale: Management explicitly could not take price in FY26 despite energy and wage inflation, and the premiumisation mix shift is still only 7-8% of sales, so growth came from new capacity/brand addition rather than price or mix.
scores.quote: we are not able to increase prices from last year because of the environment

scores.rationale: FY26 was described as a trough — 'a phase of temporary consolidation' with subdued consumer demand, stockouts and weak polymer prices — with capacity now in place and management guiding to a significantly better FY27, though they concede Q1 FY27 still looks challenging.
scores.quote: financial year 26 represented a phase of temporary consolidation... we expect financial year to be a significantly better year, though challenges do seem looming in the first quarter

scores.rationale: Consumerware/hydration and the shift to organised, branded houseware plus import substitution from China are genuine secular drivers, but the calls repeatedly describe soft, cyclical consumer demand rather than a permanently expanding market.
scores.quote: Strategically, our focus remains on import substitution in categories such as tumblers and storage

scores.rationale: The balance sheet is effectively debt-free with a net cash position and capex was funded internally while continuing to invest counter-cyclically through a weak demand year, though the brand deal routed through a promoter entity is a governance blemish.
scores.quote: Debt-to-equity ratio stands at 0.01%

scores.rationale: Management is willing to absorb near-term losses for long-term positioning, explicitly framing glassware as a strategic build rather than a profit play while persisting through Chinese dumping.
scores.quote: glassware remains a long-term strategic growth business rather than a near-term profit maximization opportunity

scores.rationale: Calls are consistently run by the JMD and CFO with plain operational detail and no celebrity positioning or promotional flourish; the Chairman is never a presence on the calls.
scores.quote: I would invite a lot of investors to see this plant because it's very well done

scores.rationale: No discussion of talent development, succession or leadership pipeline in any of the four calls beyond the gratuity provisioning under new labour codes.

Management volunteers unflattering specifics — glassware losses, a 40% QoQ steel decline from stockouts, inability to raise prices, a weak December — and answers analyst pushback on margin misses directly, though it leans on 'temporary blip' framing and declines to disclose sub-segment revenues.
scores.quote: It increased costs, and we have not been able to pass that in the market. That is our major reason for this quarter

scores.rationale: Stripping out the narrative, FY26 results were mediocre — 8.8% revenue growth, EBITDA margin down to 22.7% and 20.9% in Q4, with growth largely attributable to an acquired brand and new capacity rather than demonstrated operating skill.
scores.quote: Financial year 26 was marked by multiple headwinds and evolving market conditions across industries and segments

scores.rationale: Cello has strong consumer recall in pens and houseware but faces open competition in every category, with no aftermarket or service annuity; the brand recall is real but not monopoly-like.
scores.quote: The Cello brand continues to enjoy a strong consumer recall and trust in the writing instruments segment

scores.rationale: These are low-ticket consumer products with essentially zero switching costs — the customer can substitute a Chinese import or a rival brand at the shelf, as the dumping pressure demonstrates.
scores.quote: the category continues to face some pressure due to increased dumping from China

scores.rationale: Categories are crowded and fragmented with importers, OEMs and organised rivals, and the company's inability to pass through cost inflation shows the end customer and channel hold the negotiating power.
scores.quote: we have not been able to raise prices

scores.rationale: Chinese dumping is a persistent entrant pressure forcing management to seek regulatory protection, and discounting/scheme intensity rose during the demand slowdown — the opposite of pricing rationality.
scores.quote: We are actively engaging with relevant authorities to seek some protection against these dumping -- against this dumping happening from -- mainly from China

scores.rationale: BIC's exit from the Indian pens business handed Cello the chance to reclaim its own brand, and unorganised/OEM steelware suppliers are a source of share as the new integrated plant replaces bought-out product.
scores.quote: Recently, they exited this business in India and the promoter group of Cello World Limited found an opportunity to get the brand back into our hold

scores.rationale: This is a listed, analyst-covered consumer brand with quarterly ICICI/Monarch-hosted calls competing in visible, capital-attracting categories — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: on behalf of ICICI Securities, we welcome you all to Q4 FY26 and FY26 Results Conference Call

scores.rationale: Gross margin is high (54% in Q1, 49.8% for FY26) and the brand carries premium positioning, but the margin eroded through the year and management could not translate brand equity into price increases.
scores.quote: we have achieved the highest ever gross profit margin at 54%, reflecting our manufacturing excellence, strong positioning as a premium brand

scores.rationale: Quality claims are made — products priced at par with imports on quality grounds — but reliability failed the customer this year through repeated stockouts in insulated steel and electric kitchenware.
scores.quote: we faced stockouts in insulated steel products, which led to an approximate 40% quarter-on-quarter decline in steel revenues

scores.rationale: Distribution breadth is the standout asset — general trade at ~75% of sales alongside a fast-scaling e-commerce/quick-commerce channel now near 17% of revenue at comparable profitability, deliberately built as an omnichannel reach advantage.
scores.quote: These channels now account for nearly 17% of our overall revenue with profitability broadly in line with other business segments

scores.rationale: The customer base is overwhelmingly retail and the company matches it with brand, premiumisation and channel reach, though the intangible pull is not yet strong enough to sustain pricing.
scores.quote: premiumization is another aspect that we are continuously working on. We have kind of increased the mix to about 7% to 8%

scores.rationale: No technology edge is claimed; the advantages cited are manufacturing scale, backward integration and cost optimisation such as solar power, not proprietary technology or R&D intensity.
scores.quote: We are also undertaking solar-based cost optimization initiatives at the plant

scores.rationale: No network-effect dynamic is present or discussed anywhere in the calls.

An established general-trade network plus manufacturing infrastructure is explicitly the asset management intends to leverage to monetise the reacquired Cello brand — a reach a returning or new entrant cannot replicate quickly.
scores.quote: leveraging our established manufacturing and distribution infrastructure to unlock the full potential of the business

scores.rationale: Capex is discussed only as fungible plant-and-machinery to support order execution, with no quantified growth capex programme or incremental ROIC disclosure.
scores.quote: You require more resources for the plant and machinery, which we have or if we do not have, we can hire, we can buy.

scores.rationale: No A&P spend or brand-building discussion in any of the four calls.
No R&D spend or programme mentioned; new techniques like precast are client-driven adoption, not disclosed R&D.
The company made no acquisitions in the window; the only ownership event is that it is itself now promoter-controlled, which the framework does not measure here.
No buyback, dividend policy or distribution discussion in the excerpts.

Roughly INR10,061 crores of revenue on a conservatively financed balance sheet (net debt/equity down 0.34x to 0.18x) indicates decent asset turn, but an L1-tendered EPC business has no protecting moat around it.
scores.quote: Conservatively financed with a debt-equity ratio is 0.18%

scores.rationale: Order intake stepped up from a historical ~INR7,000 crores per year to INR19,000 crores including L1, lifting work in hand to INR29,000 crores — clear share capture in a large fragmented market.
scores.quote: Put together INR19,000 crores job we have secured, which is normally used to be around INR7,000 crores in previous years. So phenomenal jump in work secured.

scores.rationale: Overseas execution is real and progressing — Colombo ~80% done, Bangladesh 42% with payments received, and a new Ruwais/Abu Dhabi port order being mobilised — though it remains a modest slice of revenue.
scores.quote: We have started a few new jobs. One is in Abu Dhabi for ADNOC... Other international job at Colombo is almost completed.

scores.rationale: FY26 revenue grew only 9% while margin gains came from execution discipline, completed projects and one-off claim realisations rather than pricing power, and management guided margins back down to 10.5%.
scores.quote: The project has been executed on time, within the budgeted cost and cost monitoring done properly... and a few of the claims which was pending from the client that has been realized.

scores.rationale: The company sits in an ongoing Indian infra capex upcycle with an INR70,000 crores bid pipeline of big-ticket jobs ahead, but this is mid-cycle strength rather than a bottom-of-cycle entry point.
scores.quote: We can see that there are at least INR70,000 crores of job in pipeline... And each job will be INR5,000 crores to INR10,000 crores.

scores.rationale: End markets — metros, ports, airports, large-diameter tunnels and a newly entered data-centre vertical — are in structural expansion backed by government infra spend.
scores.quote: There is new segment as we have launched, data centers have already started, secured a job and started working in job. There is huge prospect in data center business.

scores.rationale: Growth is entirely organic with prudent leverage falling to 0.18x and a credit rating upgrade to A+, though the promoter is visibly pushing for aggressive order growth rather than counter-cyclical restraint.
scores.quote: I'm also very happy to say that our credit rating has been increased from A to A+ during this last quarter

scores.rationale: Operational tenacity is evident on hard jobs (Chennai Metro TBM breakthrough, Sivok Rangpo, 300-tonne piles in Bangladesh), but management explicitly frames strategy as promoter-directed rather than independent.
scores.quote: there are a lot of pressure from the promoter as well to secure more and more job

scores.rationale: Calls are plain, project-by-project and engineering-led with no self-promotion, and the MD routinely defers financial detail to the accounts team.
scores.quote: The numbers are all known, so I don't want to repeat

scores.rationale: Resource depth is asserted rather than demonstrated, and the accounts head deputising for an absent CFO in Q4 shows some bench but follows notable CFO/Chairman turnover across FY24–FY26.
scores.quote: we have our teams, resources available to execute those jobs

scores.rationale: Management volunteered the Vadhvan stall and order-timing lag as the reason revenue missed, quantified the shortfall, and explicitly refused to let analysts extrapolate the 15.1% Q4 margin, guiding back to 10.5%.
scores.quote: Vadhvan Port not staring, I mean, initiated has really impacted our revenue. Otherwise, we would have been very happy to report around 18% to 20% revenue more

scores.rationale: Headline PAT growth of 60% flatters underlying skill because it leans on realised legacy claims and completed-project write-backs, and management itself walks the run-rate margin back to ~10.5%.
scores.quote: But on annual basis, we should take 10.5% to 11% kind of EBITDA margin, excluding other income. / Yes, yes, yes.

scores.rationale: Every project is won through open competitive tendering with L1 pricing, and there is no aftermarket or services annuity in the excerpts.
scores.quote: L1 position, we are in Pune Metro, we are L1, INR1,700 crores.

scores.rationale: No switching costs or captive positions — work is re-tendered project by project, and even a secured order like Vadhvan can stall entirely outside the company's control.
scores.quote: it is not very sure how Vadhvan will take place, because it's totally not in our control

scores.rationale: Marine and large-tunnel work is a genuinely limited market with few qualified players, but government and port clients retain full negotiating power through L1 bidding.
scores.quote: Marine is a limited market, as you know.

scores.rationale: Prequalification requirements on INR5,000–10,000 crores big-ticket jobs limit the bidder set, and clients now offer better payment terms and more balanced contracts rather than a discounting spiral.
scores.quote: the payments from the customers, in particularly government customers are very good. Gone are the days when we have to wait for a long time. And the contractual terms and conditions are also getting more level

scores.rationale: The calls never discuss competitors' weakness or from whom share is being taken.
This is an INR10,000 crores listed Adani-group contractor running broker-hosted quarterly calls with analyst coverage — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: we have crossed the INR10,000 crores limit in terms of revenue first time in our company history

scores.rationale: EBITDA margins of 10–12% and PAT near 5–6% are contractor-level economics with no image- or taste-driven pricing power.
scores.quote: for a construction company, purely 5% PAT, I think, is quite good compared to any standard

scores.rationale: Clients buy proven execution certainty on technically hard work — TBM breakthroughs in bad geology, 300-tonne piles, and signature deliveries that earned client appreciation.
scores.quote: CMRL Chennai Metro, which have started, it was a very tough job. Considering the geology, we could overcome those challenges

scores.rationale: No discussion of distribution reach, accessibility or a sales force in an EPC tendering model.

Customers are corporate and government buyers where reliability matters and repeat orders recur (Navy's Project Varsha, group ports, metros), but wins still come through price-led tendering rather than switching-cost lock-in.
scores.quote: We are L1 in a Project Varsha for Indian Navy, also close to INR1,000 crores

scores.rationale: Demonstrated multi-discipline engineering capability — tunnelling, deep marine piling, precast — extends into new verticals, but it is applied know-how rather than a disclosed R&D-intensive product edge.
scores.quote: the size of the pile, we deal with around 50, 60 tonne weight, but there the pile weight is 300 tonnes... The first time we are doing such a big pile, but it's being done very nicely.

scores.rationale: A project-based EPC contractor has no two-sided network; nothing in the calls suggests scale creates self-reinforcing demand.
Pan-India plus Gulf/South Asia execution footprint gives reach across segments, but plant and manpower are hireable and the company itself says machinery can simply be bought or rented.
scores.quote: You require more resources for the plant and machinery, which we have or if we do not have, we can hire, we can buy.

scores.rationale: Clear growth-oriented investment — new GIFT City IFSC branch, planned corporate/mid-corporate branches, customer acquisition centres at 35 places and 9 government business centres, plus technology upgradation — but incremental returns are still unproven with ROA only ~0.9-1.0% and cost-to-income above 55%.
scores.quote: Central Bank of India had opened one new branch at GIFT City, Gandhinagar... We have planned to open more corporate finance branch and mid-corporate branch

scores.rationale: No A&P spend is disclosed; promotional effort shows up as branch-level outreach programmes and named deposit products (Cent Queen INR1,457 crore, Salary Cent Prestige INR787 crore) rather than brand-building expenditure judged like capex.
scores.quote: we started outreach program at more than 100 plus places. We got very good business leads also

scores.rationale: No R&D spend or new-product development pipeline is discussed in any of the four calls; technology is described as adoption of existing platforms, not research.
No acquisitions, divestments or inorganic activity are mentioned across the last-12-month calls.
A regular, modest dividend policy exists (12%, INR1.20/share for FY26, paid partly as 2% quarterly interims) but there is no buyback and no valuation-linked distribution discipline described.
scores.quote: Total dividend declared is at the rate of 12%, INR1.20 per equity share for FY 2025-26, and it includes all the interim dividend declared and paid at the rate 2% quarterly

scores.rationale: A balance-sheet-heavy PSU bank with INR8.33 lakh crore of business generating ROA of only ~0.89-1.01% and NIM around 3%, i.e. low asset productivity with no protecting moat.
scores.quote: ROA improved to 0.89% from 0.86%. ROE improved to 13%

scores.rationale: Advances grew 28.58% YoY in Q1 FY27 and total business 18.29%, far ahead of system credit growth, from a small base — a moderator explicitly noted the bank is at the high end versus other PSU banks — though durability of the corporate-led surge is untested.
scores.quote: gross global advance increased by 28.58% to 3,54,348 crores

scores.rationale: Credible but early expansion: a new GIFT City IFSC unit to build overseas business, 159 NRI desks, a centralized forex cell, and an explicit plan to grow gold loans in South India where the bank is under-present.
scores.quote: a platform we are going to leverage for our overseas business... still a lot of scope is available in terms of our presence in South India

scores.rationale: Growth is overwhelmingly volume-led while pricing deteriorated — yield on advances fell 78bps YoY to 8.15% and NIM compressed to 2.89-2.96% before only partially recovering to 3.06% on falling deposit costs, not on pricing power.
scores.quote: there is a reduction in yield on advances by 78 basis points year-on-year, that is 8.15%

scores.rationale: The bank appears past the trough of the rate/margin cycle — NIM bottomed at 2.89% in Q2 FY26 and recovered to 3.06% as cost of deposits fell 33bps to 4.60% and stabilised, with CD ratio rising from 64% to 74%.
scores.quote: Cost of deposit improved to 4.60% that is 33 basis point improvement registered. So, cost of deposit has stabilized

scores.rationale: End markets cited — retail, agriculture, MSME/micro enterprises, gold loans, SHG, plus renewable energy, data centres and HAM road projects on the corporate side — are in secular expansion in India, with RAM growing 21.38%.
scores.quote: major areas on corporate side is renewable energy, data centres and some projects in HAM, good opportunities we are observing

scores.rationale: Growth is entirely organic with no M&A, funded without expensive bulk money — management explicitly refused CDs and high-rate deposits — and capital is comfortable at CRAR 18.28% with Tier 1 of 16.54%.
scores.quote: we didn't go for any CD or also did not give any higher interest rate to mobilize resources

scores.rationale: The MD who joined 30 September 2025 laid out a vision in his first call and visibly executed it — outreach programmes from November, weekly credit committees, fortnightly board committees, new verticals — meeting 11 of 14 guidance parameters, though the track record is under one year.
scores.quote: in 11 parts, we have achieved whatever market guidance we have given, we have achieved

scores.rationale: Communication is plain, numbers-first and mission-framed with no personality promotion; calls are hosted by mid-tier brokers and the tone is that of career PSU bankers rather than celebrity management.
scores.quote: an organization of 114-plus years of its existence, serving nation in true sense that is Bharat

scores.rationale: Systematic capability building is visible — 1,000 credit officers in specialised training joining October 2026, 300 marketing officers hired and being posted, dedicated gold loan and SHG verticals reporting to EDs, and business per employee up from INR21.31 crore to INR23.89 crore.
scores.quote: our 1,000 credit officers who were undergoing specialized training for credit, they are going to join us in the first week of October 2026

scores.rationale: Management proactively names its misses rather than burying them — flagging cost-to-income as a 'major area of concern', listing the three guidance parameters it failed, and explaining the QoQ operating profit drop by naming treasury income falling from INR300 crore to INR9 crore and write-off recoveries from INR1,062 crore to INR352 crore.
scores.quote: Only CASA, NIM, and cost-to-income, these parts we actually could not achieve

scores.rationale: Headline profit growth owes much to non-repeatable items rather than demonstrated skill — provisions fell 54% YoY, write-off recoveries swung violently quarter to quarter, and FY26 saw a one-time INR632 crore DTA hit — so results cannot yet be separated cleanly from cycle and low-base effects.
scores.quote: provisions as of September'25 is Rs. 573 crores only, reduced from June'25 which was Rs.1,135 crores

scores.rationale: Nothing monopoly-like is evident — the bank competes in commoditised deposit and credit markets, admits it must benchmark its products against industry standards, and is a price-taker on yields.
scores.quote: Though it is here, but we are revisiting, benchmarking those products with the industry-based standard

scores.rationale: A genuine regional stickiness exists in rural/semi-urban India where 65% of the 4,605 branches sit and 65% of branches carry over 50% CASA, producing customer inertia and cheap sticky deposits.
scores.quote: our 65% branches are having more than 50% CASA ratio. And now also, 47% is one of the highest CASA numbers

scores.rationale: Indian banking is a fragmented market of large PSU banks, private banks, SFBs and NBFCs; the bank is a small share-taker with no pricing structure to defend, evidenced by yields falling 78bps while it chases growth.
scores.quote: you are on the high end of growth in the current quarter where PSU banks and the established results are

scores.rationale: Licensing is a real entry barrier and management showed pricing rationality by refusing to pay up for deposits, but asset-side pricing is clearly competitive with yield on advances falling 41bps then 78bps YoY.
scores.quote: Yield on Advances, due to obvious reason, it got reduced to 8.36%

scores.rationale: The bank is plainly growing faster than the PSU peer group, but no weak competitor is identified as the source of share, and management attributes the corporate surge to its own low base rather than rival retreat.
scores.quote: As base was very low that's why the growth number is visible to us

scores.rationale: It is a listed, analyst-covered PSU bank with quarterly calls, though coverage is thin and hosted by smaller brokers — neither genuinely under-the-radar nor crowded.

A 114-year brand generates real customer trust that translates into a 46.6-47.3% CASA ratio and 18%+ term deposit growth without paying above-market rates, though there is no evidence of pricing power on the asset side.
scores.quote: It shows our presence and trust of our customers in our brand value

scores.rationale: The proposition is explicitly safety and reliability — a sovereign-owned bank marketing 'safe and resilient' banking with 96% PCR and CRAR of 18.28% — and depositors accept sub-market rates for it.
scores.quote: giving them superior banking experience which is safe and resilient

scores.rationale: Accessibility is a genuine strength — 22,346 touch points, 4,605 branches with 65% rural/semi-urban, 3,820 ATMs, 13,890 BC outlets, 83 lakh mobile users and a feet-on-street model — though management admits digital adoption still lags the capability built.
scores.quote: pan-India presence with 22,346 Touch Points with 4,605 branches... 3,820 ATMs, 13,890 BC outlets and 30 BC MaXX Centres

scores.rationale: The retail/rural book (RAM at 68% of credit) is well matched to convenience and assurance benefits, but the fast-growing corporate book (up 46.5% YoY to INR1,12,770 crore) is won on price with no switching-cost lock-in described.
scores.quote: Corporate Credit as of June '25 was 76,966 crores and it has grown to 1,12,770 crores registering growth of 46.52%

scores.rationale: Technology is a catch-up and adoption story rather than an edge — management concedes the challenge is raising adoption of platforms already built, and cites standard tools (tablets at branches, bots, alerts) available to every peer.
scores.quote: Now, challenge is to bring improvement in adoption level

scores.rationale: Nothing in the business model is self-reinforcing with scale — deposit and lending relationships are bilateral, and growth is driven by outreach campaigns and hired officers, not by any two-sided network.

Physical reach into rural India is the bank's most defensible asset — 65% of branches in rural/semi-urban centres delivering 58% priority-sector lending against a 40% mandate and 15% micro-enterprise share against a 7.5% threshold — though other PSU banks have comparable networks.
scores.quote: These 65% RUSU Branches contributed in our achievement of priority sector targets of 58% against the mandated threshold of 40%

scores.rationale: Large, clearly growth-oriented capex across FY26 (new Tamil Nadu particle board plant, Badvel MDF ramp, plywood expansions at Kandla/Guwahati/Joka, Hoshiarpur and Chennai lines, plus an announced INR 1,100 cr UP project) with returns still only recovering (ROCE 12.5%→14.6%), so incremental ROIC is improving but not yet high.
scores.quote: on the UP capex, which you have announced for INR 1,100 crores... All these expansions are being done with a view of where we want to reach in 5 years

scores.rationale: Management deliberately absorbed a margin hit for higher A&P in Q1 FY26 and reiterated brand-building commitment each quarter, with plywood subsequently posting record volumes and 15-16% EBITDA margins, suggesting the spend is productive.
scores.quote: This marginal decline is largely due to higher advertising and promotional spend we undertook during the quarter to support our growth initiative.

scores.rationale: No discussion of R&D spend, new-product pipeline or innovation output in any of the four calls beyond generic references to technology upgrades.
No acquisitions were made or discussed in the last twelve months; the only new business (Century Ports) is an organic greenfield/rejuvenation project, not a bolt-on.
Buybacks, dividend policy and payout discipline are never discussed; the only reference to shareholder return is a generic statement about strategy.
scores.quote: keeping shareholder return at the core of our strategy

scores.rationale: Working capital discipline is genuinely improving (standalone cycle 76→63 days) but the business is getting more asset-heavy through MDF/particle board/port capex, and management itself frames the task as sweating assets already built rather than running asset-light.
scores.quote: we continue to sweat the substantial assets that have been created over the last 3 years

scores.rationale: Management explicitly prioritises share gain over margin in MDF while BIS and import curbs squeeze unorganised and imported supply, and delivery backs it — record plywood volumes, 25.5% MDF and 38.2% particle board FY26 revenue growth against a soft macro.
scores.quote: right now, our focus is going to be on market share gains... we are trying to gain a foothold as the market leader

scores.rationale: Credible and executing domestic geographic build-out (South MDF network deepening, Tamil Nadu particle board, Hoshiarpur, Chennai, planned UP cluster) plus improving laminate exports, though international brand expansion remains secondary.
scores.quote: As we are aging more in the South, we are continuously expanding our network

scores.rationale: Growth is predominantly volume and utilisation led, with mix/realisation contributing meaningfully only in laminates and pricing used defensively to pass through chemical and resin inflation rather than to lead growth.
scores.quote: This growth was driven by higher volume and improved capacity utilization across plants

scores.rationale: The wood-panel cycle is turning up from a trough — MDF oversupply absorbing as industry utilisation rises, laminates turning around after 1-2 subdued years, particle board moving from loss to 7.2% quarterly EBITDA — so the company sits early in an identifiable upturn rather than at the peak.
scores.quote: we are reaching a stage where capacity utilization has begun to improve right across the industry

scores.rationale: End market has durable secular drivers repeatedly evidenced and monetised: urbanisation, rising incomes, affordable housing, and a regulatory-driven (BIS) shift from unorganised to branded product.
scores.quote: The ongoing formalization of the sector aided by BIS implementation and stricter environmental regulations is anticipated to benefit organized players

scores.rationale: Expansion is entirely organic and largely internally funded (H1 operating cash flow INR 269.4 cr vs negative INR 2.73 cr prior year) with visible working-capital discipline, though the INR 1,100 cr UP programme and the unrelated port diversification add balance-sheet ambition.
scores.quote: Cash flows from operations have improved to INR 269.4 crores in H1 against negative INR 2.73 crores in FY '24-'25, enabling us to fund CapEx requirement and largely through internal accruals.

scores.rationale: A stated multi-year destination (INR 12,000 cr by FY31, ~18% CAGR) is being backed by capacity built to a five-year plan, and the year's delivery matched guidance (19.2% revenue growth, EBITDA margin 11.1%→13.0%) including the patiently executed laminates turnaround.
scores.quote: our long-term growth ambition is INR 12,000 crores by FY '31. So that includes an annualised CAGR of 18% plus

scores.rationale: Calls are run in a plain operational register by the promoter family alongside segment CEOs, with no celebrity framing or grandstanding, and management declines to speculate publicly ahead of decisions.
scores.quote: Look, all options are open on the table. It's a bit too early to comment.

scores.rationale: A professionalised bench sits under the promoter family — dedicated CEOs for MDF/particle board and laminates and a newly added COO for plywood who answer analysts directly — indicating real delegation rather than founder-only control.
scores.quote: MR. NAVARUN SEN – COO, PLYBOARDS BUSINESS; MR. SUMANT WATTAS – CEO, MDF & PARTICLE BOARD BUSINESS

scores.rationale: Management volunteers unflattering facts — MDF industry oversupply, particle board margin pressure and ramp-up losses, laminates having been subdued for years, and the Q4 stocking-ahead-of-price-hike effect that flattered growth.
scores.quote: it's a mix of, I would say, a little bit of year-end stocking, but also a lot of fundamentals playing out

scores.rationale: FY26's strong optics (PAT +44%, ROE 10.6%→15.2%) are substantially attributable to newly commissioned capacity ramping and regulatory/import tailwinds plus a cyclical recovery, so results should not be read straight through as managerial skill.
scores.quote: This uptick is primarily driven by the positive contribution from our Badvel plant, which was an early ramp-up phase during the same period last year.

scores.rationale: Century has genuine top-of-mind brand recall in branded plywood but competes in fragmented, substitutable categories with no aftermarket or services annuity described.
scores.quote: the business benefits from strong brand recall and enhanced manufacturing scale

scores.rationale: No switching costs or captive aftermarket exist for panel products; the only quasi-regional edge cited is plant proximity/cost advantage in the South and Tamil Nadu, which rivals can replicate.
scores.quote: with the launch of our new facility, which offers a cost advantage, we anticipate an improvement in margins going forward

scores.rationale: MDF is concentrated among a handful of players but is not a stable oligopoly given fresh line additions and lingering oversupply, while plywood remains highly fragmented with a large unorganised tail.
scores.quote: there is still some oversupply in the market. A lot of capacities have come up and 3 multi-daylight lines have started

scores.rationale: New capacity entered the market over the year and pricing remains challenged in particle board, indicating weak entry barriers and imperfect pricing rationality, only partly offset by BIS-driven quality barriers.
scores.quote: Margins remain under pressure, primarily due to elevated timber costs and ongoing pricing challenges.

scores.rationale: A large unorganised segment plus imports being curbed by BIS provide an ample pool of weak competitors from whom Century is visibly capturing volume.
scores.quote: this is a time period with BIS coming in, with the imports being curb where we can expand substantially

scores.rationale: This is a widely covered listed building-materials name with quarterly calls attended by multiple institutional brokers, and the segment is attracting heavy competing capital — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: A lot of capacities have come up

scores.rationale: Brand strength supports category-leading plywood margins (15.2% FY26, 16.1% in Q4) and allowed calibrated price action to absorb chemical/resin inflation, though the panel category is not a true image-driven premium product.
scores.quote: the company was able to effectively manage the challenges through operational efficiencies, strategic sourcing initiatives, improved product mix and calibrated pricing excellence

scores.rationale: Demand is described as shifting to branded, certified, quality-assured product as buyers pay for reliability over price, which is precisely the assurance benefit Century's brand and BIS compliance deliver.
scores.quote: the shift towards branded and organized products. As consumer awareness around quality, sustainability and aesthetics increase

scores.rationale: Distribution reach is repeatedly cited as a direct growth driver and management works the secondary influencer channel of carpenters and retailers directly, indicating real customer intimacy.
scores.quote: we are continuously expanding our network and also working on the secondary, which is the carpenters and retailers

scores.rationale: The customer base is retail/home-builder mediated by carpenters, and the benefits offered — brand recall, aesthetics, certified quality, dealer reach — are the right intangible-plus-availability match for that customer, though there is no corporate lock-in leg.
scores.quote: the growing preference for branded and premium products

scores.rationale: Nothing in the year's commentary points to proprietary technology; capability is framed as standard capacity lines and process/cost optimisation, with technology mentioned only as generic upgrade spend.
scores.quote: We remain committed to investments in brand building, technology upgrades and distribution expansion

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network is described anywhere in the four calls.

Expanded distribution reach is named as a driver of record plywood and MDF quarters and is being deepened into the secondary carpenter/retailer layer across a pan-India plant footprint, a real but not yet demonstrably unmatchable advantage.
scores.quote: This performance was supported by healthy volume growth and improved distribution reach.

scores.rationale: Only growth capex disclosed in the window is a token faucetware debottlenecking of ~Rs 5 crore to lift output from 4.3 to 5 lakh pieces/month, plus selective internalisation of sanitaryware — capital-light and incremental, not a high, rising growth-capex programme.
scores.quote: capacity expansion to increase the production capacity to 5 lakh pieces per month with minimal capex outlay of approximately INR 5 crore

scores.rationale: A&P is rising (Rs 49 crore in FY26, guided higher in FY27, new brand ambassador) but it visibly depressed Q3 margins while the brands it funds are still pre-revenue, so brand-equity payoff is asserted rather than demonstrated within the year.
scores.quote: our marketing and publicity spends stood approximately at INR 49 crore, and we expect this to increase in FY27

scores.rationale: No R&D line is disclosed, but the innovation engine is producing measurable commercial output — a third of sales from recent launches, plus eight Senator sanitaryware ranges, nine faucetware collections and a new wellness range.
scores.quote: new product launches contributed about 33% of the overall sales

scores.rationale: No acquisitions in the window; instead the company exited two non-core LLPs to simplify the structure — good housekeeping, but it gives no evidence of bolt-on M&A skill either way.
scores.quote: we completed the exit from two of our LLPs; Race Polymer Arts LLP and Packcart Packaging LLP... Cera does not have any subsidiaries

scores.rationale: No discussion of dividends, buybacks or distribution policy in any of the four calls.

The asset base is being sweated hard — faucetware ran above nameplate at 102% utilisation and the next capacity step costs only ~Rs 5 crore — though sanitaryware at 82% and collapsing margins temper the return side.
scores.quote: capacity utilization stood at 102% for Faucetware and 82% for Sanitaryware

scores.rationale: CERA is picking up volume while unorganised Morbi capacity is gas-constrained, and Polipluz is a purpose-built vehicle to attack an unorganised pool the company sizes at ~Rs 9,000 crore.
scores.quote: we have been able to effectively service demand... in a market where several players have faced disruptions

scores.rationale: Expansion is domestic-only but deliberate and reportedly productive — a named focus-market list (Northeast, WB, Bihar, TN, MP, Odisha and others) that management credits with a meaningful share of FY26 growth; no export/premium-brand-travelling evidence.
scores.quote: Continuous efforts undertaken across these regions... have contributed meaningfully to the growth achieved by the Company

scores.rationale: Growth is volume/recovery-led, not price- or mix-led: prices were held flat until a purely defensive March 2026 hike to recover brass costs, while trade discounts rose and EBITDA margin fell from 17.5% to 10.2% at its trough.
scores.quote: Prices remained unchanged during the period... we have recently announced a calibrated price increase

scores.rationale: The company sits right at a cycle inflection — H1 FY26 flat-to-negative retail demand followed by +11.1% in Q3 and +11.4% in Q4, with a residential up-cycle and rural recovery cited as the drivers.
scores.quote: revenues growing in double digits at 11.4%... reinforces our confidence that demand conditions are gradually improving

scores.rationale: The end market has genuine secular support — formalisation of a large unorganised pool, urban redevelopment, housing and sanitation programmes, and premiumisation of bathrooms — even if near-term demand is uneven.
scores.quote: Structural factors such as improving housing quality, urban redevelopment, rising consumer aspiration and increasing formalization

scores.rationale: Growth is organic and self-funded, non-core LLPs were divested, store rollout was deliberately throttled to protect unit economics, and the balance sheet is described as carrying ample growth capital with no leverage concerns raised.
scores.quote: While the balance sheet provides ample growth capital, the company remains committed to disciplined execution

scores.rationale: Management kept funding Senator, Polipluz and the dealer management system through the downturn, accepting visible margin drag rather than cutting investment to protect quarterly optics.
scores.quote: These initiatives are currently in the investment and brand-building phase... we expect the outcomes to play out progressively over time

scores.rationale: All four calls are run by the CFO and VP Finance with no promoter/chairman appearance or personality-led messaging; the celebrity element is an external brand ambassador for the product, not management.
scores.quote: the management team comprising Mr. Vikas Kothari - CFO; and Mr. Deepak Chaudhary - VP, Finance and Investor Relations

scores.rationale: New capability is being bought in rather than grown — experienced professionals hired across sales, BD and brand activation for Senator/Polipluz — against a five-year record of heavy senior churn (MD, multiple chairmen and the CFO all exiting).
scores.quote: bringing on board experienced professionals across sales, business development and brand activation

scores.rationale: Margin misses are explained with specific, unflattering attribution (trade discounts, brass, publicity phasing, pre-operating costs) and weak demand is named plainly, though slipped targets — 40 Senator stores vs the 45–50 promised, 1,120 Polipluz dealers vs 2,000 by March 2026 — are rolled into FY27 without explicit acknowledgement of the miss.
scores.quote: This decline was primarily driven by an increase in trade discounts and elevated brass input costs

scores.rationale: The strategic narrative (brand architecture, segmentation, DMS) has been consistent for four quarters while the measurable result deteriorated — EBITDA margin 17.5% to 10.2% — and the Q3/Q4 revenue rebound coincides with a sector-wide cycle turn and rivals' gas disruption, so skill is not yet separable from environment.
scores.quote: The improvement reflects a gradual revival in the market conditions as well as the company's improved market traction

scores.rationale: CERA has real brand recall and is a preferred B2B partner, but nothing monopoly-like in the customer's mind — it competes on trade discounts and describes its strength as being in the mass and mid-segments.
scores.quote: the core Cera brand... where we have established scale, distribution reach, and strong brand recall

scores.rationale: Lock-in is at the channel rather than customer level — DMS integration with 200+ dealers and a 28,000-retailer loyalty scheme create some stickiness, but sanitaryware buyers face no switching costs and there is no captive aftermarket.
scores.quote: retailer loyalty program with over 28,000 enrolled retailers

scores.rationale: The structure is not a tight oligopoly — a large unorganised segment (Morbi, plus a ~Rs 9,000 crore deep-value pool) coexists with several branded players, and rising trade discounts show the channel and end customer retain negotiating power.
scores.quote: targeting an approximately Rs. 9,000 crore market currently dominated by the unorganized players

scores.rationale: Pricing behaviour is not rational — discounts rose enough to be a named margin driver for two consecutive quarters and price increases were purely cost-recovery, constrained by the need to stay 'competitive'; the main real barrier is CERA's subsidised GAIL gas, not industry structure.
scores.quote: continued trade discounts... keeping in mind both margin protection and market competitiveness

scores.rationale: There is an unusually clear donor pool — gas-starved unorganised Morbi producers unable to supply, plus the unorganised deep-value segment Polipluz was created to convert.
scores.quote: the industry has been witnessing disruptions in parts of the unorganized sector, particularly in Morbi, due to gas availability challenges

scores.rationale: Not an ignored niche — this is a covered listed player in a contested building-materials category actively raising its profile with campaigns and a brand ambassador, but neither is it a capital-magnet hot sector.
scores.quote: the introduction of a new brand ambassador, which we expect to announce in the near term

scores.rationale: Image-based pricing power is weak — despite 43% premium-mix and the Senator luxury push, the company could not price ahead of cost, leaned on discounts, and let margin fall to 10.2%.
scores.quote: margins remaining below our normal range, largely on account of higher input costs as well as on account of continued trade discounts

scores.rationale: Reliability is CERA's clearest customer proposition — it held supply and serviced demand while competitors were disrupted, and wins large projects on execution reliability rather than price.
scores.quote: our strong brand equity, execution reliability and long-standing relationships with developers continue to enable participation in larger and more complex projects

scores.rationale: Access and channel intimacy are being deliberately deepened — a 70-member Polipluz field force with hardware-store reach, 50+ dedicated luxury sales professionals, 40 Senator flagships and a DMS giving real-time secondary-sales visibility.
scores.quote: The DMS gives us better visibility into secondary sales, dealer-wise inventory and retail coverage

scores.rationale: Benefit type is matched to customer type with discipline — aspirational/image brands (Senator, Cera Luxe, Polipluz) for retail tiers, and reliability plus institutional catalogues and pricing for the 39%-of-revenue project business.
scores.quote: We have also introduced a dedicated institutional catalog and pricing to address project-led premium demand

scores.rationale: No technology edge is claimed — differentiation is design- and trend-led rather than proprietary, with no R&D intensity, patents or technical superiority discussed across four calls.
scores.quote: our new designs are developed through regular market feedback and are 'designed to trend'

scores.rationale: The business has no self-reinforcing two-sided network; the closest analogue is a one-way plumber/retailer loyalty scheme that buys influence rather than compounding with scale.
scores.quote: we have also extended our popular StarPlumber loyalty program to this new channel

scores.rationale: Reach is broad and being systematically extended — 28,000 loyalty retailers, 200+ DMS-integrated dealers, 102 Polipluz distributors and 1,120 dealers built in one year, 40 Senator flagships, and named focus-state build-outs — though it is a strong rather than unmatchable network.
scores.quote: we have onboarded 102 distributors and 1,120 dealers during FY26, with a target to expand the network to 200 distributors and 2,000 dealers

scores.rationale: Branch build-out is clearly growth (not maintenance) capex — 318 net branch additions in FY26 — and incremental returns are rising, with gold-loan AUM/branch up from INR11.1cr to INR17cr and 90% of branches above breakeven.
scores.quote: total branch network expanded to 1,429 locations in Q4 FY '26 with a net addition of 98 branches during the quarter and 318 branches during the year

scores.rationale: No A&P spend, brand-building budget or marketing efficiency was discussed in any of the four calls; only incidental references to branch-led 'brand visibility'.

Not classic R&D, but sustained technology investment (gen AI, data science, AI-enabled tools) is yielding measurable output — cost-to-income fell from 65% in Q1 FY25 to 46% in Q1 FY26 and gold-loan TAT is under 30 minutes.
scores.quote: invest in next-generation technologies, including generative AI and data science capabilities, which continue to play an instrumental role in sharpening our underwriting, risk management and customer engagement

scores.rationale: No acquisitions were announced or discussed across the last four calls; growth was entirely organic branch and geography addition.

The year's capital action ran the other way — a INR2,000 crore equity dilution via QIP plus INR400 crore public NCD issue — with no buyback, dividend or stated distribution policy mentioned despite near-doubling of profit.
scores.quote: We successfully completed a Qualified Institutions Placement, raising INR2,000 crores in primary equity capital.

scores.rationale: A lending balance sheet is structurally asset-heavy, but capital efficiency is improving at the margin through co-lending (23.5% of AUM) and fee income at 28.5% of net total income, which partially offsets.
scores.quote: co-lending AUM surged 93% year-on-year to INR7,138 crores, now accounting for almost 23.5% of total AUM

scores.rationale: A small base against a very large Indian retail credit market, with AUM compounding 42%→40%→47%→60% year-on-year and disbursements up 116% in Q4 — multiples of system credit growth, so share is being captured with runway left.
scores.quote: consolidated AUM stood at INR36,623 crores, reflecting a robust 60% year-on-year growth

scores.rationale: Methodical, well-executed entry into Bihar, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Odisha across the year, with the discipline of consolidating productivity before the next wave and 90% of gold branches above breakeven.
scores.quote: net addition of 89 new branches, mainly 36 in Telangana, 18 in Andhra Pradesh, 8 in Karnataka and 20 in Odisha

scores.rationale: Growth is overwhelmingly volume/branch-led while blended yield actually drifted down through the year (16.9%→16.5%→16.4%→16.3%); mix shifts to gold and self-employed housing only cushioned rather than drove it.
scores.quote: blended yields and spreads on net advances remained healthy in the quarter at 16.3% and 7.1%

scores.rationale: The funding cycle is a tailwind (falling cost of funds lifting spreads), but the gold-loan engine is riding elevated and volatile gold prices, which is closer to a cycle peak than a bottom.
scores.quote: Considering the volatility in gold loan prices, we maintained conservative loan-to-value ratios on new disbursements

scores.rationale: End markets — affordable housing, small-ticket secured MSME/Micro LAP and formalising retail credit — are in secular expansion, reinforced by policy support such as PMAY.
scores.quote: rising urbanization, income formalization, and housing upgrades are driving demand for secured credit. Further, Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana subsidy scheme is also fuelling the growth

scores.rationale: Purely organic growth with no M&A, a 100% secured book, conservative LTVs and equity raised ahead of leverage — though the sheer pace (60% AUM, 116% disbursement growth) is aggressive rather than counter-cyclical.
scores.quote: These ratings reflect company's diversified and 100% secured lending portfolio, with strong asset quality, robust capitalization and focus on prudent lending and risk management processes.

scores.rationale: Promoter-MD Rajesh Sharma has run a consistent multi-year build of a pan-India, multi-vertical secured lender, sequencing the first QIP in over a decade, a maiden public NCD and maiden global ratings within one year.
scores.quote: This was a landmark event for the Capri Global marking our first QIP in over a decade.

scores.rationale: Calls are operationally detailed rather than personality-driven, but the commentary leans promotional ('impressive', 'highest ever', 'delighted', 'landmark'), so there is no clear evidence of deliberate low-profile restraint.
scores.quote: delivering highest ever quarterly profit of INR283 crores, a 59% increase year-on-year

scores.rationale: Senior bench was strengthened, but through lateral hires (CEO Monu Ratra, ED Fixed Income Ajay Manglunia) rather than an evidenced internal pipeline; the only talent metric given is productivity, not development.
scores.quote: We strengthened our leadership team by the appointment of Mr. Monu Ratra as CEO of the company.

scores.rationale: Management voluntarily stripped out a one-off gain to give the clean underlying number and disclosed segment NPAs plainly, which is more candid than the headline-only norm.
scores.quote: we had onetime benefit of the INR15 crores in the operating expenses due to the reversal of provisions on account of change in the perquisite policy. Adjusted for that, our cost-to-income ratio would have been 49%

scores.rationale: The spectacular optics (profit nearly doubling to INR949 crore) are hard to separate from two strong exogenous tailwinds — a gold price surge driving 111% gold-loan growth and a falling rate cycle cutting funding cost — so results currently flatter underlying skill.
scores.quote: Gold loans grew an impressive 111% year-on-year

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like hold on the customer's mind or an aftermarket; it competes head-on with banks and established gold/housing/MSME lenders in commoditised secured credit, with no evidence of pricing autonomy.
scores.quote: expanding distribution reach improving customer on-boarding

scores.rationale: Switching costs in secured retail lending are minimal — a gold or LAP borrower can refinance elsewhere — and the only stickiness cited is 55% repeat borrowing, which is habit rather than lock-in.
scores.quote: high customer stickiness driven by repeat borrowers of 55%

scores.rationale: The markets served (gold, affordable housing, MSME LAP, construction finance) are fragmented and contested by banks, large NBFCs and fintechs; the customer has ample alternatives, and CGCL itself must partner with 12 banks and 18 insurers to distribute.
scores.quote: deep relationship across 12 partner banks and financial distribution

scores.rationale: Regulatory capital gives a mild barrier, but the segments are crowded and CGCL's own blended yield ground down each quarter of FY26 from 16.9% to 16.3% even as it entered new states — evidence of competitive rather than rational pricing.
scores.quote: Our yields and spreads on net advances remained healthy in the quarter at 16.9% and 7.2%

scores.rationale: Bank co-lending partners effectively hand over origination economics and CGCL is walking into under-penetrated states where incumbents are weak, though no specific retreating competitor was named.
scores.quote: we marked our entry in high potential new geographies of Orissa, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Karnataka

scores.rationale: It was a niche mid-cap, but the last twelve months moved it firmly onto the radar — a INR2,000 crore QIP with foreign institutional participation and maiden Fitch and Moody's ratings.
scores.quote: secured credit rating from 2 leading global rating agencies, long-term issuer default rating of BB- with a stable outlook by Fitch Ratings and Ba3 Corporate Family Ratings with a stable outlook by Moody's

scores.rationale: Borrowers are underserved credit seekers choosing on availability, rate and turnaround, not image or taste; the high 16%+ yield is risk pricing rather than brand-derived pricing power.
scores.quote: improving credit access for underserved customer segment

scores.rationale: In gold loans the customer is literally entrusting their gold, and management leans on security and trust — AI-enabled vault security, 10 lakh customers served, 55%+ repeat — as the reason for share gain.
scores.quote: led by healthy customer demand and trust

scores.rationale: The proposition is essentially convenience: 1,429 branches placed close to borrowers, a fully digitised journey with sub-30-minute turnaround, and a large direct sales force of 13,000+ employees.
scores.quote: a fully digitized loan journey offering TAT of less than 30 minutes

scores.rationale: The customer base is retail/self-employed (6.9 lakh customers) and the benefit offered — proximity, speed, secured small-ticket credit — is matched to it, though it is convenience rather than an intangible or lock-in benefit.
scores.quote: Our growth remains granular, diversified and retail led with our customer base now exceeding 6.9 lakhs

scores.rationale: Technology is a real operating advantage — AI underwriting, digital journeys and AI-enabled security drove cost-to-income from 65% to 46% and AUM per gold employee from INR1.6cr to INR3.1cr — but it is applied efficiency, not proprietary multi-product deep tech.
scores.quote: employee productivity from INR1.6 crores AUM per employee earlier to INR3.1 crores now

scores.rationale: Growth is branch-and-feet-on-street led with no two-sided platform dynamic; each new customer adds nothing to the value proposition for the next, so scale brings operating leverage, not network effects.
scores.quote: supported by a widening distribution network and growing customer base

scores.rationale: Distribution is the strongest structural asset — 1,429 branches, co-lending with banks at 23.5% of AUM, car loan origination via 12 banks and 18 insurer tie-ups — but it is a reach rivals like the established gold lenders can and do match.
scores.quote: Our branch network expanded to 1,138 locations in Q1 FY '26 with a net addition of 27 branches

scores.rationale: Large, clearly growth-oriented capex — the INR 7,584 cr CG Semi OSAT project (G1 live, G2 at 14.5m chips/day under construction) plus a fresh INR 748 cr greenfield switchgear expansion — alongside standalone ROCE of 22-35%, indicating high incremental returns on the core.
scores.quote: the Board of Directors today approved another greenfield expansion for Switchgear business for an investment of INR 748 crores, net of taxes

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or brand-promotion spend in any of the four calls.

R&D is referenced only indirectly through KAVACH design, the 'Innovate to Value' (I2V) cost-engineering programme and semiconductor technology hiring, with no disclosure of R&D spend or a track record of new-product yield.
scores.quote: we are working aggressively on the I2V piece, which is Innovate to Value

scores.rationale: Mixed record: G.G. Tronics is a working bolt-on winning INR 148 cr KAVACH orders, but the Axiro/Renesas RF semiconductor acquisition is currently margin-dilutive rather than accretive (INR 38-41 cr drag per quarter, ~110-130 bps).
scores.quote: total semiconductor segment impact of INR38 crores, which is 110 basis points

scores.rationale: The only capital-markets action in the window is dilution, not distribution — a INR 3,000 cr QIP raised at elevated valuations — with no buyback, dividend or stated distribution policy discussed.
scores.quote: CG launched and successfully completed QIP of equity shares and raised about INR 3,000 crores

scores.rationale: Standalone ROCE of 22-35% with free cash flow at 119% of PAT and operating cash flow at 165% of PAT shows asset-efficient core operations, though the heavy semiconductor build is pulling consolidated ROCE down to 20%.
scores.quote: Free cash flow generated for the quarter was INR 339 crores, which is about 119% of PAT and return on capital employed annualized for the quarter was 35%

scores.rationale: Motors grew 8% against a flat-to-negative IEEMA market, implying share capture, but management concedes ~40% LT motor share already, limiting further runway in that line.
scores.quote: if you are getting 8% up, which means you are either eating through the market share or putting across the value proposition in front of the customers

scores.rationale: Credible export push — the largest order in company history, a $99m direct US transformer export for a hyperscale data centre, plus export intent behind the new switchgear plant — tempered by a conscious slowdown in some export geographies on tariffs.
scores.quote: CG secured one large order of INR900 crores, which was about $99 million of power transformer export orders from Tallgrass in U.S.

scores.rationale: Power Systems growth is explicitly price-realisation and leverage led (281 bps FY26 PBIT margin expansion), but Industrials shows the opposite — commodity inflation that could not be passed on and competitive railway pricing.
scores.quote: 281 basis points of margin expansion and underpinned by the efficient order execution and strong operating leverage

scores.rationale: The power/T&D cycle is clearly in upswing rather than near a bottom (backlog +91% y/y, four quarters of margin expansion), while the industrial/motors cycle appears to be turning up off a trough — a mixed cyclical position, not an early-cycle entry point.
scores.quote: It was negative, if you look at the data. It has crossed the bridge of being flat or a little better than that.

scores.rationale: End markets are in secular expansion — grid build-out and 765 kV transmission, hyperscale data centres, railway safety (KAVACH) and India's semiconductor localisation push under ISM.
scores.quote: It's a large-scale data center project in the United States... power transformers specifically engineered to meet the stringent reliability, efficiency and uptime requirements of hyperscale data center applications

scores.rationale: Growth is largely organic and funded by equity plus government incentives (INR 3,501 cr central and ~INR 1,400 cr Gujarat support) rather than leverage, though the scale of the semiconductor diversification away from the core electricals business is a meaningful departure from bolt-on discipline.
scores.quote: Total project cost of INR 7,584 crores, the central government assistance of INR 3,501 crores

scores.rationale: Management is executing multi-year programmes — the two-phase semiconductor plant to FY29, the CGX/CG Edge operational transformation, and a patient KAVACH commissioning ramp — accepting near-term margin dilution for later payoff.
scores.quote: reflecting operating discipline and strategic focus using our CG edge as a tool

scores.rationale: Commentary is business-focused and the wide bench of segment VPs answers directly, but the tone leans promotional ('outstanding', 'record', 'all-time high' repeated each quarter), so neither notably low-profile nor celebrity-driven.
scores.quote: I'm very pleased to share with you all that we have delivered outstanding set of numbers

scores.rationale: Deliberate, disclosed investment in senior and technical talent for the semiconductor businesses, and an orderly internal handover in the Railway leadership between Q2 and Q3 calls.
scores.quote: partially offset by the strategic investment in increasing our talent pool of the senior personnel and technology people in CG Semi as well as in Axiro

scores.rationale: Consistently specific about shortfalls — railway project deferments, inability to fully pass on commodity inflation, competitive railway pricing, and a quantified semiconductor drag — including correcting an order-intake number to a like-for-like decline.
scores.quote: if I offset it with one large order, which we had in the Q2 of last year, the actual order intake was about 13% up year-over-year. But if we look apple-to-apple here, it was -10%.

scores.rationale: Headline results are strong but the gains are concentrated in Power Systems riding a favourable T&D cycle, while the Industrial segment — the part more dependent on management execution — saw FY26 PBIT margin fall from 12.1% to 9.9%, so skill and cycle cannot be cleanly separated.
scores.quote: PBIT was at INR613 crores which is 9.9% of the sales as against INR707 crores, 12.1% in the previous year

scores.rationale: Strong mindshare positions — ~40% LT motor share and a leading position in railway propulsion and KAVACH — but nothing approaching monopoly, and no captive aftermarket/services economics are described.
scores.quote: I understand we already have a 40% market share there

scores.rationale: Heavy qualification and approval barriers create switching friction — PowerGrid 765 kV package awards, RDSO-type railway propulsion approvals and KAVACH passenger trials — though these are shared with a handful of approved vendors.
scores.quote: we are almost reaching that stage to start executing it now, because the whole process is in process and all the test results have happened. Passenger trials are in progress right now.

scores.rationale: Indian transformers/switchgear behaves as a tight oligopoly where suppliers hold pricing power against utilities and developers, evidenced by sustained price-led margin expansion, but the railway segment shows the customer (Indian Railways) dictating pricing.
scores.quote: Margins were higher year-over-year on account of better price realization, driven by robust underlying demand

scores.rationale: Pricing rationality is holding in Power Systems with four consecutive quarters of realisation-driven margin expansion, offset by explicit 'competitive pricing' pressure in railways.
scores.quote: Margin deviation is due to the mix change and the competitive pricing in railways business

scores.rationale: Outgrowing a flat-to-negative motors market implies weaker competitors are ceding share, though no specific donating competitor is named in the calls.
scores.quote: We are doing much better than the market. If you look at the market IEEMA data, the market was a little better than what it was previous quarter. From negative zone, it has come to flat.

scores.rationale: The opposite of under-the-radar — calls are hosted by IIFL with broad analyst participation, and a INR 3,000 cr QIP was oversubscribed more than 3x by Indian and global marquee investors.
scores.quote: It was oversubscribed by more than 3x and saw the participation from Indian and global marquee investors.

scores.rationale: Demand is robust but pricing rests on capacity tightness and specification, not image or taste, and gross margins in Industrials were repeatedly compressed by commodity inflation that could not be passed through.
scores.quote: lower gross margin in motors due to significant commodity inflation that could not be passed on entirely to the market

scores.rationale: Core value proposition is certainty and reliability — hyperscale data-centre transformers sold on uptime and efficiency specifications, and KAVACH sold on collision avoidance and on-time commissioning rather than price.
scores.quote: power transformers specifically engineered to meet the stringent reliability, efficiency and uptime requirements of hyperscale data center applications

scores.rationale: No discussion of distribution reach, channel intimacy or sales-force strength in these four calls.

Customer base is overwhelmingly corporate/institutional (PowerGrid, Indian Railways, Techno Electric, US data-centre developers) and the value proposition offered matches it — reliability, on-time execution and approved-vendor lock-in rather than brand appeal.
scores.quote: CG got a large order for supply and servicing of 765 kV transformer package from Power Grid Corporation, valuing approximately INR 641 crores

scores.rationale: A genuine multi-product technical footprint — 765 kV transformers, railway propulsion, KAVACH, European drives and automation, and RF semiconductors via Axiro — but no disclosed R&D intensity and the semiconductor capability is bought-in and still loss-making.
scores.quote: houses our Radio Frequency Semiconductor Components business acquired by us from Renesas

scores.rationale: No two-sided network or self-reinforcing scale dynamic is described anywhere in the calls.
Distribution and service reach are not discussed in the excerpts, and the consumer products head did not speak in any of the four calls.

Large, clearly growth-oriented capex across Delhi airport Taj, CIGNUS II, Hyatt Airoli, a greenfield Ritz-Carlton and the Udaipur buy, taking keys from 3,389 operating to a >5,000 target with management asserting high long-term returns.
scores.quote: Chalet now has 3,389 operating keys with a pipeline of approximately 1,655 keys across 7 assets

scores.rationale: A&P is visible and appears effective — the Athiva launch plus targeted marketing at Khandala delivered sold-out days and ADR above INR15,000 in the first full quarter — but spend levels and efficiency are never quantified.
scores.quote: We did multiple marketing activities during this period to create market awareness, and this was all exceptionally well received.

scores.rationale: No R&D discussion in any of the four calls; not a meaningful line item for a hotel owner.

The Udaipur deal is small, simple and complementary (INR1,710mn for a 144-key resort on 8.2 acres), but the acquiree is not already strong — it needs significant rebuild — and no timelines, capex or post-deal margin evidence exists yet.
scores.quote: We intend to significantly upgrade the infrastructure and rooms before we rebuild and relaunch the property

scores.rationale: A maiden interim dividend was declared in Q2 FY26 alongside heavy reinvestment, which is a coherent start, but there is no buyback record or articulated long-run distribution policy to judge.
scores.quote: We have also announced our maiden interim dividend this quarter

scores.rationale: The business model is deliberately asset-heavy — management explicitly contrasts owning real assets against asset-light peers — so asset turn is structurally low even if the locations are moat-like.
scores.quote: our differentiated business model anchored in asset ownership... in a landscape increasingly crowded by asset-light players

scores.rationale: Chalet is a small owner in a fragmented Indian market with clear runway (keys heading from 3,389 to 5,000+) and showed micro-market share capture in MMR against a weak Mumbai market.
scores.quote: MMR also delivered high single-digit RevPAR growth... beating the larger market comfortably on RevPAR growth

scores.rationale: Credible domestic geographic broadening into Udaipur, Hyderabad ultra-luxury, Delhi airport, Airoli and Goa reduces MMR concentration, though execution slipped on Delhi and it is India-only, not an internationally travelling brand.
scores.quote: We completed the acquisition of Udaipur Resort, marking our entry into this fast-growing and deep leisure market

scores.rationale: Growth is unambiguously rate- and mix-led every quarter — ADR up 17%, 16% and 16% with occupancy down 4.4pp, 2.3pp and 7.7pp — plus upselling via F&B refurbishment and upper-upscale/ultra-luxury repositioning.
scores.quote: ADR improved 17% year-on-year to INR12,207... Overall occupancy stood at 66%, down 4.4% points

scores.rationale: The hotel cycle is clearly past its trough — several years of ADR-led upcycle already banked and Q4 FY26 RevPAR down 3% — so the company is mid-cycle rather than positioned near a bottom, even if supply still lags demand.
scores.quote: RevPAR declined 3% year-on-year in quarter 4, largely driven by a 7.7 percentage point drop in occupancy

scores.rationale: Management makes a well-evidenced secular case — rising incomes, experience-led spending, INR12 lakh crore infra push, MICE/weddings and a persistent supply-demand gap — and the FY26 numbers (ex-resi revenue +18%) corroborate it.
scores.quote: Travel and tourism is rapidly moving from being a discretionary spend to a way of life.

scores.rationale: Growth is predominantly organic and self-funded with a repeatedly emphasised strong balance sheet and only one small acquisition, though the simultaneous multi-project pipeline is capital-hungry and leverage detail is thin in these excerpts.
scores.quote: We continue to focus on disciplined execution, operational excellence and prudent capital allocation
