scores.quote: we have also strategically revisited our sales promotion schemes in response to the current market dynamics

scores.rationale: The Indian PV market is a crowded multi-player contest with heightened price pressure and retail buyers who freely shop across brands, not a stable oligopoly with a powerless end customer.
scores.quote: in a highly competitive landscape, with heightened price pressures

scores.rationale: Competition is explicitly described as increasing and the company had to revisit promotional schemes to stay competitive, indicating discount-led rivalry rather than pricing rationality.
scores.quote: Despite increased competition, the Hyundai CRETA continues to lead from the front

scores.rationale: The only ceding segment identified is declining hatchbacks, an industry-wide mix shift rather than named weak rivals donating share; competition is characterised as intensifying.
scores.quote: Hatchback continued to witness decline in line with industry trend

scores.rationale: This is the opposite of obscure — India's largest-ever IPO, MSCI and Nifty Next 50 inclusion, and quarterly calls hosted by major brokerages.
scores.quote: HMIL was the only large cap from India to be included in this Global Index

scores.rationale: There is real aspirational brand pull — premiumisation via ADAS/sunroof, 1.1 million sunroof-equipped cars sold — but demand proved far from steady in FY26 and promotional support was needed.
scores.quote: The doubling of ADAS variant contribution and increasing popularity of sunroof-equipped models reflects the rising aspirations of our customers

scores.rationale: Trust and safety are central to the proposition — a 5-star Bharat NCAP rating for the new Venue and a three-decade 'trusted household brand' positioning — though in mass-market autos price remains a live purchase factor.
scores.quote: the all-new Venue has secured 5-star safety rating under Bharat NCAP testing

scores.rationale: Deliberate accessibility investment in white-space rural markets through outlet additions across both sales and service has produced record rural penetration.
scores.quote: our highest-ever rural penetration of 23%

scores.rationale: The customer base is retail and the benefit stack is correctly matched to it — brand legacy, design, features and safety ratings rather than TCO contracts.
scores.quote: offering products that are future-ready, feature-rich, and engineered for India

scores.rationale: There is a multi-powertrain technology spread (ICE, CNG dual-cylinder, EV, planned hybrids, hydrogen R&D) marketed as a customer benefit, but the underlying platforms come from the parent rather than a proprietary local edge.
scores.quote: we shall be introducing new ecofriendly powertrains like Hybrids

scores.rationale: Nothing in the business model is self-reinforcing across users — car sales are one-off transactions, and the calls describe scale in manufacturing and distribution terms only.
scores.quote: HMI's positioning as manufacturing hub for emerging markets

scores.rationale: A deep, still-expanding sales and service footprint reaching into rural white spaces is a genuine reach advantage in a market where after-sales service matters, though the clear leader in Indian PV distribution is a rival.
scores.quote: we continue to unlock white spaces by expanding our network through strategic outlet additions

scores.rationale: No capex line is disclosed, but the company is visibly funding growth infrastructure — GIFT City retail FME branch, a DIFC Dubai office with a dedicated team, and a proprietary AI stack — while operating expenses actually fell y-o-y and ROE ran 85–88%, implying very high incremental returns on what it does spend.
scores.quote: We have established a retail FME branch presence in GIFT City ... we have established our office in DIFC in Dubai with a dedicated team in place.

scores.rationale: Advertising and promotion spend is never quantified or discussed in any of the three calls; only a Chief Marketing and Digital Business Officer's presence is noted.

There is no formal R&D line, but the technology/AI build-out is producing measurable output and a steady product cadence — four iSIF strategies launched within two quarters plus the GIFT City inbound fund — though the payback is still unproven.
scores.quote: a customer can use our natural language search engine on our website, which has already processed over 5 million queries ... 60% of our customer queries over email are replied using AI

scores.rationale: The ICICI Venture AIF transfer is exactly the bolt-on profile the framework favours — small relative to a INR11 lakh crore MF book, complementary rather than overlapping — but it is intra-group and post-deal margin benefit is not yet demonstrated (alternates are only 8.5% of net revenue).
scores.quote: the product bouquet that we get from Venture is totally complementary to what we already have in the alternate

scores.rationale: A consistent, generous dividend policy (INR14.85 interim plus INR12.4 final) matches an asset-light business with no reinvestment need, but there is no buyback and, as a recent listing, no track record of repurchasing at low valuations.
scores.quote: the Board of Directors have declared a final dividend of INR12.4 per share

scores.rationale: Near-zero capital intensity produces an 85.8% FY26 ROE with an operating margin that expanded from 35.9 to 37.6 bps, and the moat protecting it is real — largest market share in active and equity schemes.
scores.quote: The return on equity for the year ended March 2026 is at 85.8%

scores.rationale: Clear evidence of active share capture — equity share rose from 13.8% to 14.2%, net flow share exceeds AUM share, and it took seven of every ten new industry customers — but as the #2 AMC and #1 in equity it is already large, so the runway is narrower than an insurgent's.
scores.quote: in this quarter, we added every seven of 10 new customers from the industry

scores.rationale: Two credible offshore beachheads opened and moved to execution within the year — GIFT City launched its first fund (Smart Navigator) and DIFC Dubai is staffed and approved — but contribution is immaterial so far and 'gaining traction' is unquantified.
scores.quote: we had launched our first offering in GIFT City, the ICICI Prudential Smart Navigator Fund ... it is encouraging to see that the fund is gaining traction

scores.rationale: Growth is overwhelmingly volume/AUM-led, not price- or mix-led: equity margin slipped from 67 to 66 bps, gross yield was flat at ~52 bps all year, and the fastest-growing segment is passives at 10–12 bps, which dilutes mix.
scores.quote: our margins on an annualized basis stands at 66 basis points for equity ... 12 basis points for passives

scores.rationale: The cycle turned within the window — Nifty fell 14.5% to 22,331 by March 2026 and then small-caps rebounded 24% in Q1 FY27 — so the company is past the trough rather than positioned near the bottom of an identifiable upturn.
scores.quote: Nifty 50 decreased by 14.5% from the levels of 26,130 ... small-caps outperformed with a return of 24%

scores.rationale: The end market is in genuine secular expansion — industry AUM tripled in five years to INR83 lakh crore, unique investors grew 12–13% y-o-y to 62 million, and monthly SIP flows held above INR31,000 crore through a 14.5% market drawdown.
scores.quote: Monthly SIP inflow remained largely stable throughout Q1 Financial Year 27, despite volatile market conditions, demonstrating the resilience and stickiness of the retail investor participation

scores.rationale: Growth is essentially organic with only one small complementary intra-group acquisition, no debt is mentioned, and cost discipline held through the downturn quarter with operating expenses down 3.5% y-o-y while revenue grew 19.5%.
scores.quote: Operating expenses amounted to INR3.89 billion, which is a decrease by 3.5% year-on-year

scores.rationale: The CEO repeatedly refuses to manage to short-horizon expectations on the new SIF business and frames it on a multi-year performance basis, and management concedes the category needs years of investor education to scale.
scores.quote: This -- one should see this as a long-term, this one. I am not looking at it as a short-term 1 or 2 years. Let us show performance for 2, 3 years first

scores.rationale: In its first three calls as a listed company management stayed factual and target-free, declining to publicise fundraising numbers for its new product rather than seizing the visibility.
scores.quote: We are not putting any number out as to what is the number that we are going to raise from it.

scores.rationale: The only people disclosure in the window is a newly granted ESOP/ESU pool vesting over three years and headcount rising 3,522 to 3,585 — alignment and retention machinery, but nothing on a systematic development or internal leadership pipeline.
scores.quote: The ESOP and ESU grants will vest in the next 3 years from the date of the grant with pre-identified vesting ratios.

scores.rationale: Management pre-announces bad news with precision — quantifying the ESOP P&L drag year by year for FY27–FY29 before it hits, explaining the negative other income as mark-to-market, and openly calling its new SIF category early-stage rather than overselling it.
scores.quote: The approximate debit to the P&L for FY27 will be INR640 million to INR680 million. For FY28 will be INR360 million to INR400 million

scores.rationale: The headline 86% ROE and 30% profit growth are substantially a function of an asset-light regulated structure riding a market that tripled industry AUM in five years, and earnings visibly swing on mark-to-market rather than operating skill — PAT fell 16.8% q-o-q on that alone, so results should not be read as pure management quality.
scores.quote: Profit after tax stood at INR7.63 billion, which is up by 10.4% year-on-year and decreased by 16.8% quarter-on-quarter

scores.rationale: A 26.6–26.7% share of equity-oriented hybrids — roughly double its share in any other category and the largest in the industry — is a genuine category-level mind-share position, though not a monopoly across the wider fund business.
scores.quote: the largest market share of 26.7% as of March 31st, 2026

scores.rationale: Switching costs exist only in the soft form of SIP inertia and capital-gains friction — flows stayed sticky through the drawdown — but investors can redeem freely and 29.5% of equity AUM is direct, so there is no captive aftermarket or regional lock-in.
scores.quote: Monthly SIP inflow remained largely stable throughout Q1 Financial Year 27, despite volatile market conditions

scores.rationale: Indian asset management is a concentrated top-tier oligopoly in which this firm holds the #2 overall and #1 active/equity position against a fragmented retail base with no negotiating power — but SEBI, not the industry, sets the TER ceiling, capping how much that structure is worth.
scores.quote: maintaining our position as the second largest AMC with a market share of 13.4%

scores.rationale: Regulatory licensing limits entry and the latest TER change passed through harmlessly, but pricing rationality is weak at the margin — the fastest-growing segment (passives, +25–48% y-o-y) earns only 10–12 bps, which is a de facto fee war.
scores.quote: There is no negative impact on account of changes in the TER regulations.

scores.rationale: Weaker rivals are visibly donating share: the company grew equity AUM 27.2% y-o-y in a quarter the industry shrank, and outgrew industry equity by 3.6 points the following quarter.
scores.quote: This reflects an increase of 27.2% year-on-year ... This quarter stands in contrast to the industry, which has experienced a decline.

scores.rationale: The opposite of an ignored niche — a freshly listed, second-largest AMC in the most capital-attracting sector in India, holding earnings and media calls and reporting an 86% ROE that is highly visible to competitors and capital alike.
scores.quote: A warm welcome to our first earnings conference call as a listed company.

scores.rationale: The brand supports pricing that has not been discounted to buy share — equity yield held at 66–67 bps across all three quarters while equity share rose to 14% — evidence that customers are not choosing on price alone.
scores.quote: For FY 2026, our margins stand at 67 basis points for equity

scores.rationale: Management explicitly sells reliability rather than peak returns, framing the franchise around risk-calibrated performance, and cites customer experience over 3–5 year holding periods as the reason flows persist.
scores.quote: These market positions serve as a testament to our ongoing commitment to achieving risk-adjusted returns for our customers.

scores.rationale: Accessibility is a genuine strength — 95.7% of purchase transactions are digital, an AI natural-language layer and hyper-personalised distributor portal are live, and the distributor relationships span MFDs, banks and national distributors.
scores.quote: 95.7% of our total mutual fund purchase transactions were executed across digital platforms

scores.rationale: The mix is correctly matched to a retail base — 17.3 million unique customers acquired largely through systematic transactions running ~INR4,900 crore a month, which is the intangible/habit lock-in appropriate to retail rather than a corporate TCO sell.
scores.quote: As of June 30th, 2026, we have a unique customer base of 1.73 crores.

scores.rationale: AI is deployed in production across three pillars — customer search (5 million queries), 60% of email query handling, and an investment-data conversational layer — which is operationally real, but nothing shows this is a defensible edge peers cannot replicate.
scores.quote: In investment management, through a proprietary platform, we are building a conversational layer over our investment data.

scores.rationale: No two-sided network dynamic is described or claimed anywhere in the three calls; scale benefits discussed are distribution and cost, not network.

Reach is the clearest moat — a deliberately diversified channel mix with no single channel dominant, and dependence on the parent bank actually falling from 8.1% to 7.7%, converting into net flow share above AUM share and 70% of all new industry customers.
scores.quote: MFDs accounts for 36.2%, national distributors accounts for 15.9%, ICICI Bank share at 7.7%, other banks contributing 10.7%, and direct representing 29.5%

scores.rationale: Clear growth-oriented physical and digital build-out — 528 branches added in 12 months to 7,511 plus continuous platform development — though opex growth (12-13% YoY) is outpacing core operating profit growth (5-6%), so near-term incremental returns look diluted.
scores.quote: The Bank opened 126 branches during Q4-2026 and 528 branches in the last 12 months and had a network of 7,511 branches and 12,087 ATMs

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend, its quantum, or its returns in any of the four calls.

No R&D line, but a steady cadence of new digital product output (SmartLock, iMobile Global, redesigned InstaBIZ/Corporate Net Banking, online LAS limit enhancement) shows development spend consistently converting into shippable customer products.
scores.quote: We have also launched iMobile Global, a unified banking app for NRI customers. It is currently available in the UK and will soon be expanded to other international geographies.

scores.rationale: No acquisition was announced, discussed, or integrated in the last-12-months window.

A coherent, conservative policy — ₹12/share dividend on FY2026 PAT above ₹50,000 crore with capital deliberately retained (CET-1 16.35% post-dividend) — but no buyback and no valuation-linked repurchase discipline to reward.
scores.quote: The Board has recommended a dividend of ₹12 per share for FY2026... After reckoning the impact of proposed dividend, CET-1 ratio was 16.35%

scores.rationale: A bank is structurally balance-sheet heavy (₹3.4 lakh crore net worth carrying a much larger loan book), so asset turn is inherently low, though a sector-leading 4.32% NIM shows the moat earns a high yield on those assets.
scores.quote: Net interest margin was 4.32% in Q4-2026 compared to 4.30% in Q3-2026

scores.rationale: Total loans grew 15.8% YoY in Q4-2026 and business banking 24.4%, well ahead of system credit growth, and management explicitly frames share gain as the objective — but deposit growth of 11.4% and 7.2-9.5% retail growth show the gain is segment-specific, not broad.
scores.quote: we see many opportunities to drive risk calibrated profitable growth and grow market share across key segments

scores.rationale: Expansion is real but modest and mostly domestic-density plus NRI corridors — 528 new branches, Money2India live in USA/UK/Canada/Europe/UAE and iMobile Global launched in the UK — while the overseas loan book remains just 2.4% of the total.
scores.quote: The overseas loan portfolio was 2.4% of the overall loan book at December 31, 2025

scores.rationale: Growth is volume-led, not price-led: NII grew only 7.7-8.4% YoY against 11.5-15.8% loan growth, meaning spreads compressed and balance-sheet expansion carried the revenue, with mix shifting toward lower-yield mortgages/corporate as high-yield cards shrank.

scores.rationale: Indian credit and financial-services penetration is a genuine secular expansion that management anchors its strategy to, though 11-15% loan growth is solid rather than exceptional secular compounding.
scores.quote: The Indian economy continues to be resilient, supported by a series of structural reforms... We continue to remain focused on our long-term strategy, aligned with India's evolving economic landscape and growth potential

scores.rationale: Textbook stewardship over the window — no M&A, CET-1 held at 16.3-16.5%, ₹13,100 crore of contingency provisions untouched, unsecured cards/personal loans deliberately shrunk while business banking was grown, all under an explicit risk-calibrated framing.

scores.rationale: The identical strategic framework — PBT-ex-treasury, 360-degree customer centricity, ecosystems and micromarkets — is repeated verbatim across all four calls and executed through a rate-compression year without chasing growth, showing consistency, though the window is too short to prove multi-year tenacity.
scores.quote: our strategic focus continues to be on growing profit before tax excluding treasury through the 360-degree customer centric approach and by serving opportunities across ecosystems and micromarkets

scores.rationale: Calls are tightly scripted, numbers-first, delegated to the ED and CFO with no personality-driven narrative or promotional guidance — the MD's remarks run a few minutes and hand off.
scores.quote: Joining us today on this call are Sandeep Batra, Rakesh, Ajay, Anindya and Abhinek.

scores.rationale: Only culture slogans are offered — no discussion of talent development programmes, attrition, or an internal leadership pipeline, so there is directional but not substantive evidence.
scores.quote: The principles of "Fair to Customer, Fair to Bank", "One Bank, One Team" and "Return of Capital" will guide our operations.

scores.rationale: The RBI-directed ₹1,283 crore PSL provision was disclosed unprompted in opening remarks with the cause (facilities non-compliant since 2012 origination), the remedy, the duration of the drag, and both reported and adjusted profit figures — owning an unflattering regulatory finding rather than burying it.

scores.rationale: Stripping the franchise's reputation away, the current-year delivery is mixed — genuine underwriting skill (net NPA 0.33%, 71.9% of corporate book A- and above) but core operating profit up only 5.1% with PAT growth of 6.2% flattered by low provisions rather than operating momentum.
scores.quote: Core operating profit grew by 5.1% year-on-year to ₹18,305 crore in Q4-2026

scores.rationale: ICICI holds a strong brand position but no monopoly-like ownership of the customer's mind in Indian banking, where it competes head-on with HDFC, SBI, Axis and Kotak for the same relationships.
scores.quote: We aim to be the trusted financial services provider of choice for our customers

scores.rationale: Real switching costs exist in the sticky operating-account layer — current accounts, salary relationships and corporate cash management on InstaBIZ/Corporate Net Banking with maker-checker workflows — evidenced by 11.3% average CASA growth despite slower total deposit growth.
scores.quote: On InstaBIZ, role-based dashboards for makers and checkers help speed up transaction approvals and improve traceability.

scores.rationale: The top tier is concentrated, but deposit pricing power sits with the customer — average deposits grew only 8.7-11.4% against faster loan growth and NII lagged, showing the bank must pay up to fund itself.
scores.quote: Average deposits increased by 8.7% year-on-year to ₹15,86,088 crore during Q3-2026

scores.rationale: RBI licensing makes new full-service bank entry near-impossible and ownership is stable, but pricing rationality is imperfect — deposit competition and spread compression drove NII growth below loan growth all year.
scores.quote: Net interest income increased by 7.7% year-on-year to ₹21,932 crore in Q3-2026

scores.rationale: Share is visibly being taken in segments weaker lenders once dominated — business banking grew 22.8-24.4% YoY while the bank simultaneously cut exposure to NBFCs/HFCs from ₹874 billion to ₹791 billion, i.e. lending direct rather than through the donators.
scores.quote: The business banking portfolio grew by 24.4% year-on-year

scores.rationale: The opposite of obscure — an NYSE/SGX/SIX-listed ₹3.4 lakh crore net-worth bank with SEC filings, quarterly media calls and dense analyst coverage.
scores.quote: Copy to- (i) New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) (ii) Singapore Stock Exchange (iii) Japan Securities Dealers Association (iv) SIX Swiss Exchange Ltd

scores.rationale: Brand is explicitly managed as an asset and the sustained 4.30-4.32% NIM — among the best in Indian banking — evidences pricing power, though a bank's intangible pull is weaker than a consumer brand's.
scores.quote: We focus on building a culture where every employee in the Bank serves customers with humility and upholds the values of brand ICICI.

scores.rationale: Safety and trust are the stated centrepiece of the customer proposition — SmartLock one-click freeze, a new authenticated domain, 1600-series verified outbound calling, and 250+ senior-citizen fraud-awareness sessions in a single quarter — customers are buying certainty, not price.
scores.quote: providing them a safe environment is paramount... In Q3 alone, we conducted over 250 awareness programmes in housing societies nationwide, helping them recognise prevalent frauds

scores.rationale: Accessibility is a deliberate, funded priority across physical and digital — 7,511 branches and 12,087 ATMs plus iMobile, InstaBIZ, Money2India and fully online LAS limit enhancement, all organised around a micromarket coverage model.

scores.rationale: Benefits are correctly matched by segment — trust/safety and app convenience for the 41.7% retail book, and workflow lock-in plus credit reliability for corporates (71.9% of the corporate book rated A- and above) — though the retail engine is growing at only 9.5%.
scores.quote: The retail loan portfolio grew by 9.5% year-on-year. Including non-fund outstanding, the retail loan portfolio was 41.7% of the total portfolio.

scores.rationale: A broad, in-house multi-product digital stack (iMobile, iMobile Global, InstaBIZ, Corporate Net Banking, digital lending) delivers a real customer benefit, but the year's disclosures are UI refinements and feature adds rather than a defensible technology edge rivals cannot replicate.

scores.rationale: The ecosystem/micromarket model creates some cross-referral density between corporate clients and their employees/suppliers, but nothing in the calls evidences a self-reinforcing two-sided network that strengthens with scale.

scores.rationale: Reach is the standout durable advantage and it is still widening — 528 branches added in 12 months to 7,511, 12,087 ATMs/CRMs, a micromarket coverage model and cross-border NRI corridors — a footprint that would take a rival a decade and enormous capital to replicate.

scores.rationale: No physical capex disclosure, but management repeatedly cites deliberate growth investment in retail health distribution that translated into 51.1% retail health growth and 2x new indemnity business, implying good incremental returns.

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend in any of the four calls.

scores.rationale: No acquisition activity or M&A commentary appears in the last-12-month excerpts.

Asset turnover/float leverage is not addressed in the excerpts; judging it for an insurer would require balance-sheet detail not present here.

Clear share capture in the segments it targets (retail health 3.3% to 4.1%, overall share 8.1% to 8.3% in Q3, motor beating industry in H2) though full-year GDPI growth of 7.0% still trailed the industry's 9.2%.

scores.rationale: Beyond an 'International' title in the management roster, no geographic expansion strategy or execution is described.

scores.quote: Health continues to be the fastest -growing segment for the GI industry and has contributed 47.3% of the overall insurance premium for Q1FY2027

scores.rationale: Management repeatedly forfeits top-line growth versus the industry to protect underwriting quality, running a 103.4% combined ratio against an industry 117.8%, and provided upfront for the adverse motor TP judgement.

scores.rationale: Calls are consistently data-led and process-oriented, delivered by a stable CEO/CFO pair with segment chiefs, with no promotional or personality-driven framing.
scores.quote: We continue to be focused on delivering profitable growth through disciplined underwriting, prudent risk selection and portfolio diversification

scores.rationale: A deep bench of long-serving segment chiefs was rotated across major portfolios during the year (Singhi from Retail to Corporate, Goradia from Corporate to Retail) and a new Chief Health UW was added, indicating internal succession-building.
scores.quote: Mr. Anand Singhi - Chief - Corporate, International, Banca (KRG) & Government Business, ... Mr. Sandeep Goradia – Chief - Retail, Business Strategy & Solutions Team

scores.rationale: Management openly reports where it lags — GDPI growth below industry in three of four calls, commercial lines growing 5.4% vs 12.2% — and quantifies bad news such as the 12-15% motor TP loss-ratio hit rather than burying it.
scores.quote: In the Commercial lines segment, our growth stood at 5.4% for FY2026 as compared to the industry growth of 12.2% for FY2026.

scores.rationale: The outperformance is attributable to identifiable skill rather than favourable conditions — the gap widened precisely while the industry's combined ratio deteriorated to 117.8% and while the company accepted slower growth.

scores.rationale: Holds leadership in specific niches (Liability, Marine Cargo, Engineering) and a dominant OEM motor position, but these are leadership positions rather than true monopoly-like control.

scores.rationale: The market is fragmented with the leader at only ~8.3% share, and corporate buyers plainly hold the negotiating power given the sharp rate reductions extracted at renewal.
scores.quote: improving its market share from 8.1% for Q3 FY2025 to 8.3% for Q3 FY2026

scores.rationale: Competitors are underwriting at deeply loss-making levels (industry CoR 117.8%, motor 128.0%) while ICICI Lombard writes at 103.4%, giving it a large pool of weakened rivals to take share from as capital erodes.
scores.quote: the industry -combined ratio for the Motor segment deteriorated to 128.0% in FY2026 from 123.7% in FY2025

scores.rationale: This is a heavily covered, capital-attracting sector — GST reform, 100% FDI, a Public Insurance Registry and Ind AS transition all point to intense regulatory and investor attention, not obscurity.

scores.rationale: Some brand pull is evident in retail health growing 51.1% without chasing price, but the product is largely commoditised and the company loses commercial business purely on rate, showing limited image-based pricing power.
scores.quote: Our Retail Health business, continued to demonstrate strong growth of 51.1% for FY2026, significantly outpacing the industry growth of 19.9%

scores.rationale: The corporate proposition is explicitly built on reliability and risk management rather than price, and the sustained claims/underwriting capability is the stated basis of customer value.

scores.rationale: A dedicated Enterprise AI & Technology chief and demonstrably superior risk selection/pricing/claims analytics underpin the widening CoR gap, though no product-level technology depth is quantified.
scores.quote: This sustained outperformance re■ects the effectiveness of our risk selection, pricing and claims management practices

scores.rationale: No two-sided network dynamic is described anywhere in the excerpts.

scores.quote: we have added more than 46,000 agents, 140+ partnerships and 3 bank tie-ups in 9M-FY2026

scores.rationale: No disclosure of advertising or promotion spend or its return in any of the four calls; brand is referenced but never linked to A&P outlay.

Product development is a recurring, disciplined output — three new long-term savings products launched in Q3-FY2026 plus higher sum-assured multiples and rider attachment lifting product-level profitability — functioning as R&D-equivalent for an insurer.

scores.rationale: No acquisitions discussed in the last-12-months calls; the only corporate action is a name change and a promoter-to-investor reclassification, not M&A.

The business is structurally asset-light (distribution and underwriting, ■3.34 trillion AUM against a small balance sheet) with cost-to-premium falling to 13.6% savings and 227%/225% solvency, though moat protection is partial rather than absolute.
scores.quote: savings Cost-to-Premium ratio reduced by 50 basis points year-on-year to 13.6% in Q1-FY2027

scores.quote: Our sum assured market share stood at 11.8%

scores.quote: higher retail protection mix, improvement in product-level profitability through increasing sum-assured multiples, longer tenure policies, and increasing rider attachment

scores.quote: The MFI segment witnessed recovery after an extended period of moderation

scores.rationale: Growth is entirely organic, leverage is minimal (only ■12bn and ■14bn subordinated debt against 225% solvency vs 150% required), and the company kept investing in agency and micro-market branches through a down year rather than cutting.

scores.rationale: Management held to a multi-year cost-alignment programme and agency investment through a weak FY2026, delivering VNB margin expansion to 24.7% and then 26.7%, and frames protection as a multi-decadal build rather than chasing quarterly APE.

scores.rationale: Calls are delivered in a plain, metric-led format by the functional leadership team with no promotional or personality-driven framing, and the promoter reclassification and name change are explained matter-of-factly.

scores.rationale: The CDO succession was internal and pre-announced with the successor introduced on the call — Amish Banker rose from branch operations to COO to Chief Distribution Officer — evidencing a working internal pipeline.

scores.rationale: Management proactively disclosed unfavourable facts — persistency below its own assumptions in specific pockets, declines against high bases, the input-tax-credit hit — with named corrective action rather than deflection.
scores.quote: We have observed some challenges in specific channel and product pockets, where persistency ratios are lower than the initial assumptions. To address this, corrective actions have been initiated

scores.rationale: Weaker players exist to take share from — the company grew retail APE 9.9% and Q1 RWRP 13.4% while the industry grew 2% RWRP in H1-FY2026 — implying share is being ceded by laggards.

scores.rationale: The core product is certainty itself, and the company competes on it explicitly — 99.3% settlement ratio, 1-day turnaround, best-in-class 22% early claims ratio and zero NPAs since inception since inception.

scores.rationale: The benefit mix is well matched — retail buyers get brand trust and claims certainty while group/corporate clients get underwriting discipline and risk-reward selection — with retail protection and group protection both growing strongly.

scores.quote: a part of the tariff impact and the Russia oil-related penalty impact was absorbed to protect customer relationships

scores.rationale: FTAs remove the duty disadvantage against Bangladesh and Pakistan while ICIL holds share and capacity, creating identifiable weaker players to take volume from as UK/EU access opens.

scores.rationale: The opposite of under-the-radar — quarterly IR-advised calls, publicised awards, a globally benchmarked ESG ranking and a heavily promoted consumer brand relaunch.

scores.rationale: Genuine intangible pull exists in the branded slice — Wamsutta's premium positioning and demand said to be performance- rather than price-driven — but the majority core saw down-trading and single-digit-to-low-teens EBITDA margins, so image-based pricing power is not yet in the numbers.
scores.quote: brand-related demand in these categories is driven more by performance than price sensitivity

scores.rationale: Retailers are buying reliability and continuity — sustained orders through a 50% tariff, six straight export awards, and management positioning the company on supply-chain responsiveness rather than price.
scores.quote: positioning Indo Count as a preferred long-term sourcing partner for large global retailers

scores.rationale: Convenience is being built deliberately: three US plants for coastal proximity and responsiveness, a full bed/bath/utility range that raises retailer wallet share, and ~2,000 domestic touch points with 700 counters added in one quarter.
scores.quote: It enables customer proximity, improves responsiveness and gives us clear operational flexibility

scores.rationale: The benefit type is well matched to a corporate customer base — reliability, proximity and end-to-end range for large retailers — while the newer retail-facing D2C brands carry the intangible proposition.
scores.quote: The ability to offer a range of collections across bed, bath, utility bedding, etcetera... enhances the wallet share with our retail partners

scores.rationale: Across four calls the stated advantages are scale, manufacturing footprint, brands and relationships — never technology or R&D intensity — consistent with a low-tech, process-manufacturing business.
A B2B manufacturing and licensed-brand model with no platform or two-sided dynamic; nothing in the calls suggests value that compounds with the number of participants.
Distribution and service reach is the most defensible asset — 50+ countries across five continents, three onshore US plants giving domestic responsiveness rivals lack, and ~2,000 India touch points.
scores.quote: With our presence across 50-plus countries spanning 5 continents

scores.rationale: Only ongoing IT/digital investment is mentioned as a growth-oriented spend with no quantification or incremental ROIC evidence.
scores.quote: there is good investment in IT expenditure so as to improve further our mobile banking and other areas

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend in either call.
No R&D discussion; not applicable and not mentioned.
Activity in the window was divestment of stakes (Ageas Federal life insurance JV) for one-off gains rather than complementary bolt-on acquisitions, so no evidence of value-accretive M&A capability.
scores.quote: a gain of Rs.380 Crores coming from the sale of our stake in Ageas Federal

scores.rationale: No mention of dividends, buybacks or any distribution policy in the calls.
Asset turnover is not a meaningful bank metric and was not discussed; ROA/ROE were given but no asset-turn-plus-moat evidence.
Post-PCA the bank is re-entering segments it had exited and growing advances 17% Y-o-Y, indicating runway to regain share from a low base, though no explicit share data.
scores.quote: all the mid corporates that were there in our book earlier but had to exit during PCA regime as well as also to generate business from erstwhile mid corporates

scores.rationale: No discussion of new geographies or branch/market expansion beyond existing footprint.
NIM expanded sharply to 4.22% core (up ~120bps Y-o-Y) on faster asset repricing plus a 56% CASA mix, so growth is being led by price/mix rather than volume alone.
scores.quote: NIM stands at 4.22%, which is an improvement of 1.2% compared to last year and 50 basis points sequentially

scores.rationale: Management describes the credit cycle turning up after 4-5 years of muted investment, with the bank itself just out of PCA and credit costs at cyclical lows (0.18% for the quarter).
scores.quote: after 4-5 years of muted investment cycle growth, investment cycle is back on the table

scores.rationale: Management cites broad Indian economic expansion and a fast-growing digital transaction base as the structural backdrop, though this is generic sector commentary.
scores.quote: The Indian economy today is witnessing a significant growth across all sectors despite the inflationary hurdles

scores.rationale: Conservative posture is evident — voluntary provisioning well above regulatory requirement, calibrated corporate lending, deliberately not leading on deposit pricing — but ownership/strategy is controlled by GoI/LIC and a pending disinvestment.
scores.quote: additional provision on the restructured assets aggregated amounts to almost 636 Crores... not otherwise required by the regulator

scores.rationale: Key strategic decisions including the disinvestment of the bank sit with DIPAM and government/LIC owners, and management explicitly disclaims knowledge or control of the process.
scores.quote: they are only running the process, I think they will be in a better position to answer this disinvestment question because we are only aware whatever is coming to media

scores.rationale: Calls are plainly factual and CFO-led with minimal self-promotion, though the MD does headline the record profit.
scores.quote: I am conscious that many of you may have to attend to other calls, so I will be quite brief

scores.rationale: Hiring is only now restarting after a four-year PCA freeze, with no evidence of systematic talent development or leadership pipeline.
scores.quote: we have not done any major recruitment for nearly 4 years mainly because we are under PCA

scores.rationale: Management proactively strips out one-offs (Kingfisher/Videocon recovery, IT refund, stake-sale gains) to present comparable core numbers and flags that credit cost is unsustainably low.
scores.quote: it is not likely to remain at this subdued level of 0.18%. But definitely, we are expecting that it will remain at about 1% or lower

scores.rationale: Headline record profits are substantially flattered by non-recurring items — stake sales, income-tax refund interest and provision write-backs — so results overstate underlying operating skill.
scores.quote: If we exclude the gains from strategic sales, the operation profit has shown a growth of 36% year-on-year and a small reduction of 4% from last quarter

scores.rationale: No evidence presented of any monopoly-like niche or captive service position.
The 56% CASA ratio implies some sticky, low-cost deposit relationships, but no discussion of switching costs or a protected franchise.
scores.quote: CASA ratio, we have been able to maintain at 56.19%

scores.rationale: Indian banking is described as highly competitive on deposit pricing with the bank a price-follower responding to peer moves, not a member of a stable pricing oligopoly.
scores.quote: We are strategizing to increase the deposit rate to respond to the market moves made by other banks

scores.rationale: Deposit-rate competition is escalating and lending yields track policy/market rates, indicating price-taking behaviour rather than rational industry pricing; ownership is also unstable pending disinvestment.
scores.quote: We have increased deposits rates, slightly behind the market mainly because we do not want not play a leader function here

scores.rationale: Corporate borrowers are migrating back from the bond and money markets to bank loans as market rates rose faster than MCLR, giving banks share to capture.
scores.quote: there is a lot of borrowing from the bond market and money market has come back to the loan market now

scores.rationale: The bank is a large, heavily-covered listed PSU-legacy institution at the centre of a high-profile government disinvestment, the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: there was news in the media that the government is asking something from RBI which will ease the process

scores.rationale: The bank is a deposit-rate follower rather than leader — implying some franchise stickiness — but no evidence of image-driven pricing power, and yields move with policy rates.
scores.quote: This movement on of about 80 bps is mainly due to the movement in the market rate

scores.rationale: A 56% CASA ratio sustained while paying below-market deposit rates suggests customers value the safety/stability of the franchise over price.
scores.quote: CASA is slightly higher at 56%

scores.rationale: 95% of customer-induced transactions run through digital channels with UPI dominant, indicating strong accessibility, though management admits no DBUs are yet set up.
scores.quote: about 95% of the customers into transactions are now going through the digital channel, out of which UPI has taken the lion's share

scores.rationale: Strategy explicitly tilts toward granular retail (62-68% of book) with calibrated corporate exposure, a sensible match of a low-cost retail deposit franchise to retail lending.
scores.quote: we will continue to pursue a differentiated granular approach to build up more retail business and we will follow a calibrated approach towards the corporate book

scores.rationale: Digital adoption is high and investment is ongoing, but this is table-stakes UPI/mobile infrastructure shared across Indian banking, not a proprietary tech edge.
scores.quote: we have invested and going forward also we will continue to invest in improving the digital footprint

scores.rationale: No evidence of any two-sided or self-reinforcing network discussed.
Branch/distribution reach is never quantified or claimed as an advantage; only digital-channel penetration and priority-sector target achievement are cited.
scores.quote: On priority sector we have achieved all targets. There is no deficit.

scores.rationale: Capex is genuinely growth-oriented (5G launch, ~30,000 new towers over six quarters) but is falling quarter-on-quarter (Rs 42.8bn Q4FY25 → 24.4bn Q1FY26 → 17.5bn Q2FY26) and management itself concedes sector returns sit below cost of capital, with FY26 revenue up only 3.0% and cash EBITDA flat on Rs 16,000 Crore deployed.
scores.quote: the industry's ROCE continues to remain below cost of capital

scores.rationale: A&P shows creative traction (Cannes Lions, London International and Clio awards for Number Rakshak, CSK IPL partnership) and brand awareness is claimed to hold, but it took until Q4FY26 for the subscriber base merely to stop shrinking, so the spend is defending rather than compounding brand equity.
scores.quote: we have been able to stablise our subscriber base at 192.8 million customers vis-à-vis last quarter, a first since the merger

scores.rationale: No R&D spend, programme or pipeline is disclosed in any of the four calls; the AI/ML references (spam engine, AI recharge assistant) are feature deployments, not a described R&D investment.
No acquisitions in the twelve-month window; the only inorganic items are a satellite partnership with AST SpaceMobile and vendor/technology tie-ups, which are not M&A.
scores.quote: we announced a strategic collaboration with AST SpaceMobile

scores.rationale: No dividend or buyback; the period is defined by massive dilution — Rs 614bn of equity raised in FY25 including Rs 369bn of government dues converted at Rs 10/share taking GoI to 49%, plus a further Rs 4,730 Crore promoter infusion committed in FY26.
scores.quote: the Company has raised equity of ~Rs. 614 billion... GoI shareholding increased from 22.6% to 49%

scores.rationale: Extremely asset-heavy — ~527,000 broadband sites, spectrum, and Rs 16,000 Crore of capex over six quarters — supporting only Rs 44,873 Crore of FY26 revenue and Rs 9,217 Crore cash EBITDA, with no moat protecting those assets.
scores.quote: Over the last 6 quarters we have deployed over Rs. 16,000 Crore

scores.rationale: Vi has been the share donor, not the gainer: losses of ~5 million subscribers per quarter as recently as FY25, narrowing to 0.5mn in Q1FY26 and only reaching flat at 192.8mn in Q4FY26 — stabilisation, not capture.
scores.quote: the subscriber decline was restricted to 0.5 million during the quarter i.e. ~90% lower compared to ~5 million each in Q2 and Q3 of last financial year

scores.rationale: There is no new-geography expansion; the footprint work is catch-up coverage inside existing Indian circles (4G population coverage 86% vs peers near 99%, 5G reaching all 17 circles only three years after rivals launched).
scores.quote: improved our 4G population coverage over 86% on pan India basis

scores.rationale: Growth is explicitly price/mix-led rather than volume-led — ARPU Rs 175 → Rs 190 (+8.3% YoY) for a 19th consecutive quarter of increases on a flat subscriber base, driven by 4G/5G mix rising to 66.9% from 63.8%.
scores.quote: The Customer ARPU expansion over the last year has been driven primarily by premiumization

scores.rationale: The company sits at an identifiable trough with visible upturn triggers in the window: AGR dues cut to Rs 64,046 Crore from Rs 87,695 Crore, ICRA upgrade to BBB/Positive, and first post-merger subscriber additions in Feb–Mar 2026.
scores.quote: Our AGR dues have been finalised at Rs 64,046 Crore... a reduction from the earlier frozen figure of Rs 87,695 Crore

scores.rationale: The end market is in secular expansion — data usage per 4G/5G subscriber up 27.2% YoY to 20.2GB and total traffic up over 30%, with broadband penetration still below 65% and rural tele-density near 60% — though management concedes the economics of that volume growth remain unsustainable.
scores.quote: overall broadband penetration still remains below 65% representing a significant opportunity for further growth

scores.rationale: Stewardship is the opposite of prudent leverage and organic self-funding: survival has depended on government conversion of Rs 369bn of dues to equity, a DoT-committee reassessment of AGR liabilities, vendor equity to Nokia and Ericsson, and repeated promoter infusions.
scores.quote: We are deeply grateful to the Government of India for conclusively resolving the AGR matter

scores.rationale: Tenacity is evident in the network rebuild, but independence is structurally absent — the Government holds 49% and the company's cash flows, tariffs and balance sheet outcomes are set by DoT decisions and industry tariff leaders rather than by management.
scores.quote: We are in discussion with the DoT for next steps on this matter.

scores.rationale: The executives themselves present in a low-key, operationally factual style, but the company is anything but under the radar — a politically salient, state-part-owned turnaround with the Aditya Birla Group chairman personally taking the board chair.
scores.quote: Mr. Kumar Mangalam Birla, Chairman of Aditya Birla Group has now taken charge as the Non-Executive Chairman

scores.rationale: The CEO succession was internal and handled smoothly (Kishore stepping up Aug 2025 with a stated employee-first culture), but the CFO was hired externally from Mondelez and the top team has turned over repeatedly, so no settled internal pipeline is demonstrated.
scores.quote: I'm equally delighted to welcome Mr. Tejas Mehta, as our new CFO, who joins us from Mondelēz

scores.rationale: Operating disclosure is specific and includes bad news (subscriber losses quantified, capex and ARPU given precisely), but the calls open with lengthy promotional macro narrative and the excerpts contain no ownership of past strategic mistakes or discussion of the residual funding gap.
scores.quote: the data traffic has grown by 21.4% YoY at overall level

scores.rationale: The visible improvement is largely exogenous — AGR relief, equity conversion by the government, and an industry-wide July 2024 tariff hike — so results should not be read as evidence of managerial skill; execution credit is limited to network rollout.
scores.quote: The private mobile operators hiked tariff in July 2024... leading to improvements in ARPU and revenue

scores.rationale: Vi holds no monopoly-like position in any segment; it is the sub-scale third private operator, launching 5G in 2025 well behind rivals and rebuilding coverage others already have.
scores.quote: our 5G services are now live in over 80 cities across all our 17 circles

scores.rationale: Mobile number portability means near-zero switching costs and no captive aftermarket, which is exactly why the base bled ~5 million subscribers a quarter before the network spend began.
scores.quote: ~5 million each in Q2 and Q3 of last financial year

scores.rationale: The market is a three-private-player oligopoly with high barriers and tariff repair underway, but pricing power is not shared equally — management states ARPU remains among the lowest globally and that incremental data is priced at an unsustainable level.
scores.quote: the ARPU in India remains as one of the lowest globally

scores.rationale: Entry barriers are extreme (spectrum costs, 500,000+ site networks) with no new entrants and increasingly rational pricing evidenced by 19 consecutive quarters of ARPU growth, though management still argues current pricing is below sustainable levels.
scores.quote: further tariff increases are essential

scores.rationale: Vi is itself the share donator in this market, having shed subscribers every quarter post-merger until Q4FY26; the calls show no weak rival from whom it is taking share.
scores.quote: we have registered improvement in subscriber numbers, for the first-time post-merger in the month of February

scores.rationale: This is one of the most closely watched situations in Indian markets — Supreme Court judgements, DoT committees, a 49% government stake and quarterly regulatory headlines — the antithesis of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: The Hon'ble Supreme Court via its judgement dated October 27, 2025 and November 3, 2025

scores.rationale: The brand retains affinity and wins creative awards, but it confers no pricing power — Vi follows industry tariff moves, sits at the lowest global ARPU band, and must give away extra data and validity (130GB Guarantee, 24 extra days) to retain customers.
scores.quote: provides 130 GB of additional data over the year... 2-day extra validity credited on every unlimited voice recharge

scores.rationale: Reliability was Vi's structural weakness — the subscriber exodus was explicitly attributed to network gaps now being fixed — so customers have been buying certainty elsewhere, notwithstanding new trust features like Vi Protect and country-of-origin call display.
scores.quote: consistent and right investment has been key in stemming our subscriber losses

scores.rationale: There is real convenience differentiation (only Indian operator with truly unlimited roaming in 40+ countries across 151 destinations, doorstep SIM delivery, AI recharge assistant, Easy+ app), but distribution and store reach remain sub-scale versus the two larger operators.

scores.rationale: Benefit types are reasonably matched — retail gets brand, OTT bundles and data guarantees, enterprise gets reliability and TCO propositions (CCaaS, IoT, 1.3 Tbps enterprise corridor) — but neither side shows lock-in, and enterprise is a small, contested book.
scores.quote: developing the 'Dedicated Enterprise Corridor', by strengthening the fixed line capabilities with the addition of ~1.3 Tbps network capacity

scores.rationale: No proprietary technology edge — the network is vendor-supplied (Nokia, Ericsson, who were paid in equity), 5G arrived roughly three years after competitors, and the AI features described are commodity operator capabilities.
scores.quote: ~Rs. 25 billion to vendors Nokia and Ericsson

scores.rationale: Telecom scale works against Vi rather than for it: a shrinking-then-flat 192.8mn base against far larger rivals means the scale flywheel compounds for competitors, and no two-sided network dynamic is claimed anywhere in the calls.
scores.quote: we have been able to stablise our subscriber base at 192.8 million customers

scores.rationale: Coverage — the distribution equivalent in telecom — is a deficit not an advantage, with 4G population coverage still only ~86% against the ~99% industry level management itself cites, and the 90% target still unmet.

scores.rationale: Bank equivalent of growth capex — sustained investment in ~1,000+ branches, mobile app, technology stack and analytics that is now converting into 20% loan growth and operating profit up 36% Y-o-Y with cost-to-income falling 310bps.
scores.quote: We put out 1,000 branches... the operating profit of the quarter excluding trading gains has increased by 36% on a Y-o-Y basis

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotion spend, brand campaigns, or their returns in any of the four calls.
No R&D line or technology-spend efficiency discussion; only generic claims of being a 'technology first bank'.
Only the historical 2018 merger is referenced as context; no acquisition activity in the last twelve months is discussed.
No mention of dividends, buybacks or any distribution policy in the window; capital talk is confined to capitalization adequacy.

A bank is inherently balance-sheet-heavy and this one carries a high-cost, still-normalizing funding base at 5.96% cost of funds with a 70.7% cost-to-income ratio, so asset-light economics are absent even as ratios improve.
scores.quote: cost to income ratio excluding trading gains improved by 166 basis points on a sequential basis to 70.7%

scores.rationale: Small base with long runway and demonstrated share capture — customer business up ~20%, loans up 20.6%, deposits up 17.7% and CASA crossing INR1.58 lakh crores, all well above system growth.
scores.quote: we registered a strong growth of 20.6% on a Y-o-Y basis and that book has now crossed INR3 lakh crores

scores.rationale: Branch build-out is domestic and largely complete at ~1,050 branches with NRI banking mentioned only in passing; no credible new geographic expansion narrative in the window.
scores.quote: We in the last five years, seven years we put up over 1,000 branches, cumulatively maybe over 1,050 or 1,060

scores.rationale: Growth is overwhelmingly volume-led (20%+ book growth) with margin gains coming from falling cost of funds rather than pricing power — NIM rose only 5bps adjusted, and the mix is deliberately shifting toward lower-yield mortgages and LAP.
scores.quote: the NIM has shown an improvement of 5 basis points and the adjusted numbers would look like 5.85% going up to 5.90%

scores.rationale: Positioned just past the bottom of the MFI credit cycle with credit costs falling — provisions down 31.1% Y-o-Y, MFI SMA normalized to 0.71% — and management guiding operating profit toward 3.5% of assets from 2%.
scores.quote: we expect this to further go upwards of about 3.5% in due course

scores.rationale: Indian retail credit, cards and wealth are structurally expanding end-markets, evidenced by 4.8 million cards in force, 22% spend growth and wealth AUM up 24% Y-o-Y.
scores.quote: the AUM has now reached almost about INR64,000 crores and it grew at 24% on a Y-o-Y basis

scores.rationale: Organic focus and prudent provisioning (a voluntary INR515 crores contingency buffer) are offsets to a business that has repeatedly needed external capital and has just absorbed a INR590 crore fraud loss revealing control gaps.
scores.quote: we have created a contingency provision of INR515 crores. This is purely I would say voluntary and on a prudent basis

scores.rationale: Seven-year delivery against a stated plan — cost of funds cut from 7.8% to 6.11% to reach parity with mid-tier peers, C/D ratio from 137% to 94%, and first-ever INR1,000 crore quarterly profit — is exactly the long-horizon tenacity the parameter asks for.
scores.quote: we have brought down cost of funds from 7.8%... We have brought it down today to 6.11%

scores.rationale: The CEO's commentary is markedly promotional and self-narrating across calls, and the bank actively courts media and investor attention rather than staying low-profile.
scores.quote: We have spoken to a few media channels who talked to us yesterday.

scores.rationale: The only substantive people evidence in the window is negative — branch employees colluding in a INR590 crore fraud — with management offering culture assertions rather than any talent-pipeline system.
scores.quote: certain employees of this branch, most possibly in connivance with external parties, have fraudulently transferred these amounts

scores.rationale: Management convened an unscheduled investor call within two days of the fraud, quantified the loss precisely, named the cause as employee collusion, and separately strips out one-offs (day count, tax refund, fraud) when reporting margins and opex.
scores.quote: this looks to us on the basis of the work we've done, clearly a case of an employee fraud

scores.rationale: Reported gains lean heavily on external tailwinds — falling rates lowering cost of funds, a INR514.8 crore CGFMU government guarantee claim and INR181 crores of treasury gains from softening G-Secs — so skill is hard to separate from cycle.
scores.quote: we had received a claim of INR514.8 crores under the CGFMU scheme against MFI portfolio

scores.rationale: Indian banking is intensely contested and the bank itself concedes it competes on price-parity with mid-tier peers, having had to pay 7% on savings to attract deposits — the opposite of a monopoly position in the customer's mind.
scores.quote: it's not that we are very proud of raising money at 7% savings account

scores.rationale: No regional monopoly or captive aftermarket; deposits are rate-shopped nationally and the bank has had to reprice buckets explicitly to control who stays.
scores.quote: we have structured this in such a way that large ticket bulk money does not come to the bank

scores.rationale: Indian banking has dozens of scheduled banks plus NBFCs and small finance banks, and the bank sits as a challenger below the large private incumbents rather than in a stable oligopoly.
scores.quote: now we are as competitive as any other good quality mid -tier bank

scores.rationale: Licensing creates real regulatory entry barriers, but deposit-rate competition has been irrational enough that the bank paid 150bps above mid-tier peers for years to fund itself.
scores.quote: we were paying 150 basis points more than mid -tier banks

scores.rationale: The bank is visibly taking share from weaker deposit and MFI-exposed lenders, growing deposits 17.7% and loans 20.6% while the stressed microfinance segment consolidates.
scores.quote: total deposits... the growth was about 17.7% on a Y-o-Y basis

scores.rationale: A listed, heavily analyst-covered bank running a high-profile brand campaign of customer-first positioning and holding ad-hoc media and investor calls is the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: brand positioning, hyper personalization engine , analytics, technology, service center

scores.rationale: Pricing power runs the wrong way — the bank had to overpay depositors and is now migrating loan mix toward 8%-9% mortgages, indicating commoditized, rate-driven demand rather than image-based pricing power.
scores.quote: there is the products which are where we lend at 8% to 9% like mortgages, loan against property

scores.rationale: Management stakes its positioning on trust and customer-first products and cites employee pride in service levels, but the Chandigarh fraud directly undercut the reliability proposition in the same window.
scores.quote: customer service, the customer first being like the almost front and center about what the bank is all about

scores.rationale: Convenience is the actual moat being built — 1,000+ branches, a strong mobile app, hyper-personalization and relationship managers producing 50.8% CASA, the clearest evidence of customer primacy in daily banking.
scores.quote: CASA ratio for the quarter as a result improved by 1% to 50.8%

scores.rationale: The mix is sensibly matched — retail gets convenience and rate-led propositions while corporate and commercial banking grew 30% with trade, FX and transaction fees indicating switching-cost stickiness.
scores.quote: in wholesale, we continue to power up and there the growth was even stronger at 30%

scores.rationale: Technology is a genuine differentiator on the digital side — a self-built stack, hyper-personalization engine and strong mule/AML controls — though the fraud proved the physical channel lags, and no R&D intensity is quantified.
scores.quote: we are a very technology ahead bank or technology first bank and on all fronts like mule and AML etcetera

scores.rationale: No evidence of a two-sided network or self-reinforcing scale dynamic is discussed in any of the four calls.
A 1,000-branch national footprint plus digital reach built from a standing start in seven years is real distribution scale, though it does not yet rival the top private banks' networks.
scores.quote: we put up over 1,000 branches, cumulatively maybe over 1,050 or 1,060

scores.rationale: No capex figures or growth-vs-maintenance investment discussion appear in any of the four calls.
A&P spend is never mentioned in the last-12-months calls.

A dedicated 'New Product Initiatives & Exchange Technology' function plus three years of technology interventions (API bidding/back-office integration, data analytics) and a pipeline of new contracts (carbon credit certificates, VPPA, CfD, REC alignment) shows product development that is converting into new participant classes.
scores.quote: We have done lot of technological interventions and as a result of that we believe that our customer engagement has significantly increased. We have done API integration with our customers

scores.rationale: No acquisitions are discussed in the excerpts.
No buyback or dividend policy discussion appears in the four calls.

Classic asset-light exchange economics — Rs.183.3 crore revenue producing Rs.123.4 crore PAT (67% net margin) in Q2 FY26 — but the protecting moat is under active regulatory attack via market coupling, so it is not a clean +2.
scores.quote: Revenue for the company grew by 9.2%... to Rs. 183.3 crores in Q2 FY '26. Profit after tax increased by 13.9%... to Rs. 123.4 crores

scores.rationale: IEX is already the dominant exchange with little runway left to gain, and management's framing is defensive — hoping to retain share once CERC-mandated market coupling pools the order book.
scores.quote: we should be able to retain significant market share even in the Day-Ahead Market

scores.rationale: The calls describe an India-only national platform with no geographic expansion initiative discussed.
Growth is volume-led with negative price/mix realization — Q2 FY26 volume rose 16.1% while revenue rose only 9.2%, and Q3 volume +12% against revenue +14% still shows no pricing lever being pulled.
scores.quote: IEX recorded electricity trading volume of 35.2 billion units, a Y-o-Y growth of 16.1%. Revenue for the company grew by 9.2% year-on-year

scores.rationale: FY26 demand was cyclically depressed (flat at ~1,709 BUs on a prolonged monsoon and mild summer) with a clear identified upturn already underway in FY27 on a harsh summer.
scores.quote: this year, right from the month of April, the summer has been very harsh and we have had less rain... about 12% increase in peak demand and 8% to 9% increase in energy consumption

scores.rationale: The end market is in permanent secular expansion — per-capita consumption targeted to double by 2030 and quadruple by 2047, capacity to ~950 GW by 2030, plus renewables/storage/carbon markets structurally increasing short-term traded volumes.
scores.quote: targeting per capita electricity consumption of almost about 2,000 units by 2030 and 4,000 units by 2047... CEA projects installed capacity of almost about 950 gigawatt by 2030

scores.rationale: Wholly organic focus across all four calls — growth pursued through new contracts and technology rather than acquisitions, with no leverage or large capital deployment flagged.
scores.quote: We have done lot many customer-centric activities. We have done lot of technological interventions

scores.rationale: Management has tenaciously contested the market-coupling order through APTEL and, despite an adverse February 2026 ruling, continues to engage regulators and pursue legal recourse while building an 18-year customer franchise.
scores.quote: we continue to engage actively with the policy makers and regulators and are also exploring the legal recourse available to us

scores.rationale: Calls are dense, technical and regulation-focused, delivered largely by functional heads (JMD, IR head) rather than built around the CMD's persona.
scores.quote: We will begin with the opening remarks from Ms. Aparna, followed by an interactive Q&A session.

scores.rationale: No discussion of talent development, succession or leadership pipeline in the excerpts.
