scores.rationale: The company is at a cyclical high rather than a bottom — FY26 margins of 29.7% were inflated by Tolvaptan sole-generic exclusivity, and management itself guides FY27 down to ~25% margins on high-single-digit topline.
scores.quote: we expect to grow our top line high-single digits with margins at around 25% in FY27

scores.rationale: End markets are in secular expansion — chronic therapies, GLP-1/obesity (Semaglutide, Bofanglutide partnership), biosimilars aided by FDA easing interchangeability and PBM/CMS prioritisation.
scores.quote: FDA easing the clinical study and interchangeability requirements, as well as PBMs and potentially CMS starting to prioritize biosimilars

scores.rationale: Focus is organic-first with only a small bolt-on acquisition, improving leverage ratios and ROCE ~25%, and no large transformative M&A over the window.
scores.quote: positive results on most key financial metrics, be it growth, gross and operating margins, earnings per share, or leverage ratios

scores.rationale: Fifteen consecutive quarters of YoY growth on a complex-products strategy sustained since FY23, plus a multi-year Brazil turnaround, evidence long-horizon execution and tenacity.
scores.quote: proving that perseverance and disciplined execution deliver results

scores.rationale: Calls are substance-dense — numbers, compliance status, pipeline detail — with no celebrity framing, though this is a large, widely-covered promoter-led listed company rather than a genuinely low-profile one.
scores.quote: we remain grounded in our long-term aspiration to build a company for the future

scores.rationale: Beyond raw sales-force headcount growth, the calls contain no discussion of talent development systems, succession, or internal leadership pipeline.

Management guided 24-25% EBITDA margin and openly acknowledged beating it, disclosed FDA 483s/OAI at Pithampur Unit 2 across successive calls, quantified LOE drag on India growth, and guided FY27 margins down rather than extrapolating the windfall.
scores.quote: we handsomely beat the guidance we set at the beginning of the year... we are on track with our remediation efforts at our Pithampur unit 2 facility

scores.rationale: Record FY26 results are substantially attributable to a one-off Tolvaptan sole-FTF exclusivity windfall rather than repeatable skill, as confirmed by the guided step-down to ~25% margins in FY27 — the headline numbers overstate underlying capability.
scores.quote: Growth was driven by new products such as Tolvaptan where we benefited from being the only generic on the market

scores.rationale: The monopoly-like positions Lupin enjoys — sole FTF on Tolvaptan, CGT exclusivity on Risperdal Consta — are regulatory and time-boxed, not durable ownership of the customer's mind or an aftermarket.
scores.quote: Tolvaptan with sole first to file exclusivity

scores.rationale: Generics carry minimal switching costs — Albuterol and Suprep lost share the moment new entrants arrived, and Lupin itself won India share when Mixtard exited, showing the substitution runs both ways.
scores.quote: additional generic competition in a few key products like Suprep® and Albuterol

scores.rationale: The US generic market is fragmented with powerful buyers (PBMs, distributors) forcing continuous price decline, and India's IPM is a highly crowded branded-generic market.
scores.quote: offset by low single-digit price decline in our base products

scores.rationale: Complex injectables, respiratory and biosimilars carry genuinely high entry barriers (Nanomi platform, biologics facility, FDA inspections), but the plain-generic base repeatedly attracts new entrants and continuous price erosion.
scores.quote: anticipated impact of additional generic competition in Albuterol

scores.rationale: Identifiable weak/exiting competitors to take from — Mixtard's exit in Indian insulin created a diabetes tailwind, and Brazil's near-tripling came from capturing an under-served diabetes market.
scores.quote: With the revival of the Respiratory category and the exit of Mixtard in the insulin market, we see near term tailwinds

scores.rationale: Lupin is a large-cap, heavily analyst-covered Indian pharma company in the most contested categories of the moment (GLP-1s, biosimilars), the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: we became the first Indian company to secure approval for generic Victoza®

scores.rationale: Gross margin of 73.5% and the ability to make a new brand a top-3 branded generic within a month indicate real brand pull in India, though US pricing power is absent.
scores.quote: Gross margins continued upward trajectory during the quarter at 73.5%

scores.rationale: Reliability is central to the pitch and most sites cleared inspections (NAI for Nagpur Unit-1, EIRs for Goa, Aurangabad), but the unresolved OAI at Pithampur Unit 2 running across all four calls undercuts the certainty claim.
scores.quote: we recently received VAI status for our Pithampur Unit 3 respiratory facility and are actively addressing the OAI at Unit 2

scores.rationale: Access is a genuine strength — a ~12,000-strong India field force repeatedly cited as the growth engine, plus proven US specialty distribution capability demonstrated on the Tolvaptan launch.
scores.quote: Our ability to seamlessly launch Tolvaptan through specialty distribution channels stands as a testament to the strong execution and commercial capabilities

scores.rationale: Benefit type is reasonably matched to customer — brand/prescriber intimacy for India's retail-facing branded generics, and complexity/supply reliability for US institutional buyers — but the US side lacks switching-cost lock-in.
scores.quote: supported by a strong sales force of nearly 12,000 people

scores.rationale: Multi-platform technical depth — the proprietary Nanomi long-acting injectable platform delivered its first approval, alongside inhalation, peptides, GLP-1s, iron colloids and biosimilars, on sector-leading R&D intensity.
scores.quote: first product from our proprietary Nanomi long-acting injectable platform

scores.rationale: No two-sided network or self-reinforcing scale dynamic is described anywhere in the calls.

Reach rivals struggle to match — a ~12,000-person India sales force carrying 80+ planned launches, plus built-out US specialty distribution and direct commercial infrastructure across Europe, Brazil, South Africa and Philippines.
scores.quote: the broad reach of our 10,000 plus people sales force

scores.rationale: A large ~INR 1,100 crore growth programme (Lote fluoro-intermediates, Dahej Phases 1-2, Hitachi Energy line, world-scale ethyl acetate) is being executed to plan, but incremental returns are unproven — Lote/Dahej costs are already dragging the P&L while EBITDA falls.
scores.quote: the capex linked to the same can be accommodated in the previously called out INR 1,100 crores

scores.rationale: No mention of advertising or promotional spend in any of the four calls.
New product development is named as a focus area and an alternative product was mapped for the phased-out agro intermediate, but no R&D spend, pipeline size or efficiency evidence is given.
scores.quote: the new growth projects and focusing on the new product development and the cycle

scores.rationale: No acquisitions discussed in the last-12-month calls; growth is entirely organic greenfield capex.
No dividend, buyback or distribution policy discussed in any of the four calls.

The business is capital-heavy and getting heavier — the single largest capex in company history is going in while revenue declined ~9% and EBITDA margin fell to 5.3%, so asset turns and returns are deteriorating.
scores.quote: our Dahej facility, which is the single largest capex that Laxmi has embarked on

scores.rationale: Only ~8-9% share of diketene derivatives with an 18-20% growth history since 2017 leaves real runway, but in this window the company only held share rather than gained it.
scores.quote: market share close to about 8%, 9% in the diketene derivatives space

scores.rationale: The company supplies global customers and won a global OEM contract, but there is no evidence of a deliberate, executed geographic expansion programme in these calls.
scores.quote: deferred deliveries of select products to global customers

scores.rationale: Growth is the opposite of price/mix-led — realisations fell with feedstock, price moderation alone cost ~12% of Specialties revenue, volumes were flat, and management's stated aim is volume-driven growth.
scores.quote: our current focus in the Essentials segment remains achieving volume-driven profitable growth

scores.rationale: The company appears near a cyclical trough with identifiable upturn markers — acetic acid bottomed near $300-320 then reversed upward, global subscale capacity is shutting, China's anti-involution measures and an EU-India FTA are cited as catalysts.
scores.quote: Only in December, we are noticing this trend positively reversing

scores.rationale: Part of the portfolio is levered to secular end-markets — the eco-efficient gas for SF6-free high-voltage switchgear and fluorine intermediates — though the core ethyl acetate/diketene markets are mature and oversupplied.
scores.quote: an eco-efficient gas used in their SF6-free high-voltage switchgear portfolio called EconiQ

scores.rationale: Organic-only growth, debt-to-equity of 0.17 and counter-cyclical investment through a downturn show prudence, tempered by INR 400-500 crore of term loans being drawn as earnings trough.
scores.quote: our debt-to-equity ratio is at 0.17, which is very much robust

scores.rationale: Multi-year projects were guided and then delivered inside the guided band — Lote's first-year ramp was called out as 40-60% of peak and closed at 40-45%, and Dahej Phase 1 got consent-to-operate and began supplying as promised.
scores.quote: we have actually achieved what we had lined up for ourselves into FY '26. We achieved 40% to 45% of the peak revenues

scores.rationale: Commentary is workmanlike and process-focused — feedstocks, turnarounds, self-help measures — with no promotional framing even when announcing a marquee Hitachi Energy contract.
scores.quote: we continue, as I said, on self-help measures... focusing on productivity

scores.rationale: Leadership transitions are planned and announced with named successors and senior hires from Asian Paints/DuPont/BASF, but the pipeline is externally sourced and the CFO seat has churned repeatedly, including an interim promoter-family CFO in Q4.
scores.quote: His successor, we have announced, is Mr. Rajesh Naik

scores.rationale: Declines are decomposed with specific percentages (10% phase-out, 12% price moderation, 5-6% one-time campaign), one-time gains are flagged rather than buried, and an environmental allegation at Lote was addressed head-on — offset slightly by refusing to quantify deferred orders.
scores.quote: there is a price moderation, which is causing 12%... phaseout of agrochemical intermediate, which is around 10%

scores.rationale: There is little halo risk to correct for — results are visibly poor (EBITDA down 33%, margin 5.3%) yet management neither claims credit for external tailwinds nor hides behind them, describing the backdrop plainly as demanding.
scores.quote: the backdrop that we are operating in, in chemicals was demanding and continues to be demanding

scores.rationale: The largest business is commodity ethyl acetate (~80% of Essentials) sold on a published spread, with no evidence of a monopoly-like position in the customer's mind or an aftermarket annuity.
scores.quote: ethyl acetate, which constitutes about 80% of our Essentials basket

scores.rationale: Qualification-based lock-in exists in pockets — a dedicated contracted line for Hitachi Energy's trademarked EconiQ gas — but the bulk of revenue shows no switching costs, as an agro customer's phase-out removed ~10% of Specialties outright.
scores.quote: the contract with Hitachi Energy has been signed

scores.rationale: The end markets are oversupplied and buyers hold the pricing whip — management repeatedly cites global overcapacity and market price moderation flowing straight through to its realisations.
scores.quote: the trajectory continues to be shaped by regional dynamics, given the supply side overcapacities

scores.rationale: Pricing is anything but rational or protected — spreads fell from a 12-year average of ~$220 to ~$120 and prices moderated across every segment, indicating low barriers and capacity-driven competition.
scores.quote: Average over a 12-year period, the spread has been about $220... as we speak now, it is in the $120 range

scores.rationale: Weak competitors are visibly exiting — global shutdowns and restructuring of subscale, non-competitive assets plus China's anti-involution actions create share available to survivors like Laxmi with new capacity coming online.
scores.quote: shutdown and/or restructuring of structurally subscale and non-competitive assets

scores.rationale: The diketene/fluorine niches are genuinely specialised and lightly covered, but the company is listed, hosts quarterly analyst calls and is building world-scale capacity, so it is not meaningfully off the radar.
scores.quote: we have given you some more insights into our investor deck on Slide 17

scores.rationale: There is no image- or taste-based pricing power — realisations track acetic acid and ethanol feedstock, and gross margin compressed from 35.8% to 33.1% year-on-year on mix.
scores.quote: this revenue is impacted by the acetic acid feedstock prices

scores.rationale: During the Q4 feedstock spike some customers explicitly paid up for supply certainty, and Laxmi's procurement strategy kept its assets running reliably — evidence that reliability, not price, is the sale in parts of the book.
scores.quote: willing to pay a certain premium on the supply reliability side

scores.rationale: Management stresses getting close to customers as new capacity lands and is digitising the supply chain, but offers no evidence of superior accessibility or a distinctive sales force.
scores.quote: getting into a hunting mode with close proximity to many of our customers

scores.rationale: The customer base is entirely corporate (pharma, packaging, agro, coatings, Hitachi Energy) which suits a reliability/TCO pitch, but pricing passes through with feedstock rather than being anchored by switching-cost lock-in.
scores.quote: market price moderation across the segment

scores.rationale: Fluorination chemistry at Lote and the ketene/diketene platform are non-trivial capabilities, validated by a global OEM contracting Laxmi for its SF6-free switchgear gas — but R&D intensity is never quantified and the edge covers a minority of revenue.
scores.quote: our fluorine setup. That is also ramping up according to the plans that we had laid out

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network dynamic is described anywhere in the calls.

Distribution is a cost line being optimised rather than an advantage — logistics costs doubled on the Middle East conflict and the supply chain is being redesigned and digitised, with no reach rivals cannot match.
scores.quote: the logistic costs have doubled since this conflict has started

scores.rationale: Board-approved 5-year plan for 1,000 new branches plus 'Project 321' (321 branches in 18 months) sited by external scientific study, funded alongside ROA of 1.86-1.9% and ROE of 23-24.65%, i.e. heavy growth spend at high incremental returns.
scores.quote: this is a 5-year plan to open 1,000 branches in the next five years... In this FY 26, we have taken one big initiative to open 321 branches

scores.rationale: No advertising or promotion spend is discussed in any of the four calls.
No R&D spend or programme is disclosed; only a revamped mobile app and a risk-built profitability dashboard are mentioned, with no efficiency or spend data.
No acquisitions of any kind are mentioned in the last-12-months calls.

A 10% interim dividend was approved in Q3FY26 on record profits, but the only capital-markets action beyond that was a government OFS to meet MPS norms — no buyback or articulated distribution policy.
scores.quote: 10% interim dividend has been approved by our Board today

scores.rationale: Balance-sheet-heavy by nature (INR 5.95-6.5 lakh crore business), but earns an unusually high ROA of 1.86-1.9% off a 52.5% CASA funding base — good returns on assets without an asset-light model or a durable moat.
scores.quote: ROA at 1.9% is, again, an improvement of 10 bps year-on-year

scores.rationale: Advances grew 27% Y-o-Y in Q1FY27 and 22% in FY26 against a much slower system, from a small base among PSU banks, so runway plus demonstrated capture.
scores.quote: Total advances against 18%, we have grown at Y-o-Y 27%, INR65,000 crores of advances have been added

scores.rationale: Expansion beyond its Maharashtra base into scientifically-shortlisted 'potential growth centres' and a GIFT City IBU opened within six months of RBI approval, though the IBU book is still only Rs 100 million against a $1bn aspiration.
scores.quote: we have closed this half year with Rs. 100 million of business in the IBU... maybe it can be a $1 billion book in the next 12 months

scores.rationale: Growth is clearly volume-led — NII rose 14.5% against 27% advance growth and NIM slipped to 3.85% — with only partial mix help from CASA and high-yield gold/vehicle loans.
scores.quote: our NII growth... has lagged our total advances growth of 27% versus NII growth of 14.5%

scores.rationale: Asset quality metrics are at cyclical best levels (GNPA 1.45%, NNPA 0.13%, PCR 98.55%, credit cost falling), which places the bank near the top rather than the bottom of the credit cycle, with rate cuts already compressing NIM.
scores.quote: Gross NPA is maintained at the March level 1.45%... NNPA... maintained at 0.13%. PCR stands at a healthy 98.55%

scores.rationale: Management is deploying into structurally expanding end-markets — renewables, data centres and infrastructure — alongside secular retail credit penetration (home loans +29%, vehicle +56%, gold +53%).
scores.quote: Sectors like green, clean energy, renewable sector, we have funded in a major way... We have done data centers

scores.rationale: Organic-only growth with no M&A, deliberate shedding of high-cost bulk deposits and account-level profitability discipline, tempered by a CD ratio pushed to 85% as deposits lagged credit.
scores.quote: we have not mindlessly grown the top line but have remained conscious about the bottom line

scores.rationale: Multi-year framing — a 5-year branch plan and a 5-year INR1,200-1,500 crore/year write-off recovery plan that has been beaten two years running — though as a 73.6% government-owned bank true independence is limited.
scores.quote: we had planned that annually, we should be recovering between INR1,200 crores to INR1,500 crores for the next 5 years... This year... It is INR1,423 crores

scores.rationale: Commentary is metric-dense rather than personality-driven, but the MD actively markets the stock — touting rating upgrades and FII/DII shareholding gains — and accepts effusive analyst praise without deflecting.
scores.quote: the FII shareholding has gone up from 0.39% in 2023 to 5.8%

scores.rationale: Some organisational building — a new customer-acquisition vertical under a General Manager and branch/zonal-level profitability dashboards — but EDs are government appointments and no systematic talent pipeline is described.
scores.quote: a new business vertical, calling it as new business customer acquisition vertical headed by a lady General Manager

scores.rationale: Publishes 15-19 explicit guidance parameters at each year's start and reports performance against every one, but deflected a direct question on rising cost of deposits into a CASA narrative rather than answering it.
scores.quote: bank has typically shared 18 to 19 parameters for which the guidance was shared at the beginning of the year... we have been able to meet all the guidance

scores.rationale: Headline results are flattered by a benign system-wide credit cycle and large written-off-book recoveries (INR1,423 crore) rather than demonstrably separable managerial skill, and the calls are dominated by analyst adulation.
scores.quote: Compliments to you, sir... for a very, very excellent quarter results-wise

scores.rationale: A mid-sized PSU bank in a commoditised lending market with no described monopoly position in the customer's mind, pricing individually negotiated account by account.
scores.quote: in the individual accounts also when they are negotiating the pricing with the clients

scores.rationale: Some captive stickiness via 52.5% CASA and institutional/government relationships that carry switching friction, but no regional monopoly — current account balances fell sharply in Q1 and bulk deposits are openly rate-shopped.
scores.quote: CASA ratio also was maintained above the 50%. We closed the year with 52.51% CASA

scores.rationale: Indian banking is a fragmented, actively competitive market — management itself describes a deposit war — and customers negotiate both rates and charges.
scores.quote: despite whatever, I should say, challenges, geopolitical uncertainties and a real war for deposit s also

scores.rationale: RBI licensing is a genuine entry barrier and ownership is stable at 73.6% government, but pricing rationality is weak — bulk deposit rates and loan concessions are actively bid.
scores.quote: the bulk high cost is a function of rate of interest that we will decide. And we can easily get that business to enter our system

scores.rationale: Consistent above-system growth (business +19%, advances +27% Y-o-Y) implies share is being taken from slower-growing peers, and management explicitly frames itself as outperforming the industry.
scores.quote: We are consistently outperforming the industry

scores.rationale: The bank has deliberately exited obscurity — courting international ratings and institutional investors, with FII holding up from 0.39% to 5.8% and DII from 0.24% to 6.86% in three years.
scores.quote: we have been very, very particular about our engagements with the investors, both foreign and domestic

scores.rationale: Management asserts brand-based pricing power and clients paying up for service, but the evidence contradicts it — yield on advances flat at ~9.05% and NIM down 10 bps Y-o-Y in a commodity product.
scores.quote: a price which the Bank of Maharashtra brand deserves to charge to the client... clients happily pay a price for the good service

scores.rationale: Depositors accept a below-market 4.52% cost of deposits and 52.5% CASA for sovereign-backed safety, and rating upgrades (S&P BBB-, ICRA/CARE AA+) reinforce trust-over-price positioning.
scores.quote: S&P Global has assigned us a BBB- rating, and which is three notches improvement

scores.rationale: Deliberate convenience investment — 321 new branches, a fully revamped mobile app built around minimum clicks, and a dedicated institutional acquisition sales vertical.
scores.quote: we have revamped the version... able to transact on this mobile application with minimum number of clicks

scores.rationale: The benefit mix is broadly matched — trust/branch convenience and a full product basket for retail (RAM 63% of book), while corporate 37% is served on turnaround time and relationship rather than price alone.
scores.quote: we have a complete basket of products that is taking care of the professionals, the HNIs, the NRIs, the business community

scores.rationale: Only table-stakes digital work is described — a revamped mobile app and an internally built branch profitability dashboard claimed as 'pioneering' — with no R&D intensity or multi-product tech edge.
scores.quote: my risk management has developed a simple profitability dashboard

scores.rationale: Growth is driven by branch openings, verticals and salesforce reach rather than any self-reinforcing two-sided network; nothing in the calls strengthens with scale in that way.

A deliberately built distribution edge — 1,000 branches planned over five years targeted at growth centres, plus twin core and institutional CASA verticals — but not reach that larger PSU rivals cannot match.
scores.quote: there is a core business of CASA, there is an institutional business of CASA and we are trying to address both these components with a different strategy

scores.rationale: The INR852 crore capex plan has largely sat idle for years — only two small projects (cold drawn, ~INR100cr; Telangana finishing line, ~INR184cr budget with only INR90cr of POs issued) have started, and the finishing line only debottlenecks existing unusable capacity rather than adding new capacity.
scores.quote: We had put out the capital expenditure plan of Rs. 852 crores against which we have issued purchase orders for two projects which would be less than Rs. 150 crores

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend in any of the four calls — it is a B2B tender-driven seamless pipe business.

The flagship R&D effort — premium connections — has run over two years with repeated inability to commit to a date, and is a licensed royalty tie-up with a foreign partner rather than in-house development, with a competitor already having launched.
scores.quote: It is a very slow process. It is continuing for more than 2 years now... I cannot give you a definitive date even right now

scores.rationale: Management has repeatedly searched for inorganic opportunities but declined to transact at prices it finds uncomfortable, showing price discipline rather than deal-making for its own sake.
scores.quote: we are still trying for inorganic opportunities, but in our assessment we have not found any opportunity which makes sense

scores.rationale: Despite a treasury that grew from INR2,630cr to over INR3,100cr against a ~INR9,000cr market cap, dividend is merely held flat (payout ~17%) with no buyback even at a very low P/B, and management deflects capital-return questions to prior transcripts.
scores.quote: The rationale for conserving cash has been explained many times on earlier conference calls, and I would urge you to kindly refer to transcripts of those calls.

scores.rationale: This is a heavy, capital-intensive seamless pipe mill with admittedly old plant, ~4.4 lakh tons on 5.5 lakh tons of usable capacity, ~INR1,200-1,450cr quarterly revenue and a huge idle cash pile depressing returns; ROCE cited at only ~16% in a good year.
scores.quote: our plant and machinery is subject to the risk of obsolescence because it is very old plant and machinery

scores.rationale: Volumes have been flat at ~4 lakh tons for three years — share held, not gained — and management explicitly states no deterioration but offers no evidence of capture.
scores.quote: There has been no deterioration compared to last 3 years because we are still on track to manufacture 4 lakh tons

scores.rationale: Exports, notably to the US, have deteriorated on tariffs and have not conclusively recovered; the only geographic project is a domestic Telangana finishing line.
scores.quote: due to the anticipation of the tariff tantrum and the actual tariff tantrum, export orders have not conclusively improved

scores.rationale: Pricing has collapsed — FY25 revenue was flat despite >10% higher dispatches, and FY26 realizations fell further on Chinese dumping, with the only margin 'improvement' in Q3 FY26 being an inventory markdown reversal, not real pricing.
scores.quote: This has been solely due to fall in sales realization on a year-on-year basis.

scores.rationale: The business is clearly in a downcycle (oil and gas capex slowdown, dumping) which could argue for cyclical positioning, but management explicitly refuses to call a bottom and the key antidumping catalyst is unresolved until October 2026.
scores.quote: We do not see any indicators to conclusively say that the slowdown is well past us.

scores.rationale: Management concedes the domestic seamless market grows only 2-3% a year and is capped by Indian oil and gas exploration activity, with industry nameplate capacity (1.9mt) far exceeding actual production (~0.9mt).
scores.quote: Market grows at around 2%, 3% annually, not more than that because the customers to whom we sell are oil and gas players.

scores.rationale: Leverage is prudent (AA+ upgrade, INR3,100cr net treasury) and there is no reckless M&A, but the counter-cyclical investment test fails — capex is being deferred, not accelerated, precisely during the lean period, as a shareholder pointedly noted.
scores.quote: when the lean period is going on, why there is no action on this subject?

scores.rationale: Tenacity is visible in the multi-year premium-connections pursuit and refusal to overpay for acquisitions, but the repeatedly unexecuted INR852cr plan and open-ended timelines undercut evidence of long-term vision actually being executed.
scores.quote: for the last 3 years, we have seen that your capex has been the same, the projected capex, but nothing has been happening on the ground

scores.rationale: Calls are handled entirely by a Deputy General Manager of IR with no promoter or MD appearance across all four quarters, and messaging is plain and unpromotional.
scores.quote: MANAGEMENT: MR. KAUSHAL BENGANI – DEPUTY GENERAL MANAGER, INVESTOR RELATIONS & FINANCE

scores.rationale: No discussion of talent development, succession, or leadership pipeline in any of the four calls.

Management is refreshingly blunt about bad news — flagging in advance that the September quarter would be muted, admitting old plant obsolescence risk, and disclosing the margin uptick was only an inventory reversal — but is evasive or curt on product mix, bid pipeline, and capital allocation rationale.
scores.quote: the increase in margins was on account of reversal of the inventory markdown which was done in the earlier quarter

scores.rationale: Reported PAT is heavily flattered by treasury/other income (INR160cr of other income in Q1 FY26 versus INR165cr of EBITDA; Q3 FY26 boosted by gold and silver gains), so headline profits reflect market luck rather than operating skill.
scores.quote: The highlight for this quarter was the Other Income, which was boosted by improvement in market sentiment and in gold and silver sector

scores.rationale: The company is the domestic seamless market leader with the widest size range and approved-vendor status with PSUs, but this confers no pricing power — imports at 20-25% of the market are setting the price.
scores.quote: We are market leaders, as you rightly pointed out. However, the entire industry is facing the effects of the slowdown

scores.rationale: There is no evident switching-cost lock-in — sales are short-cycle tender orders of three to four months to PSUs like ONGC and Oil India, with customers freely substituting cheap Chinese imports.
scores.quote: the order book that we have is always for a period of three to four months

scores.rationale: Structure is the opposite of a protected oligopoly: severe overcapacity (1.9mt nameplate vs 0.9mt production), unabated Chinese dumping at a quarter of the market, and PSU customers with full tender-based negotiating power.
scores.quote: imports are as high as 20%, 25% of the total domestic industry size, which is impacting the margin of the entire industry

scores.rationale: New domestic players have entered a stagnant market and Chinese imports flood in with an antidumping duty management itself calls ineffective, producing industry-wide price erosion rather than rational pricing.
scores.quote: the present antidumping duty is not so effective right now

scores.rationale: Weak competitors exist and the company has held volumes while the industry struggled, but the price-setting share donator here is Chinese capacity taking share from MSL, not the reverse.
scores.quote: the continuous Chinese dumping has affected margins of the entire domestic industry

scores.rationale: It is a low-profile, unglamorous niche trading at a depressed valuation with sparse analyst coverage, though the obscurity reflects poor economics rather than a protected pocket.
scores.quote: very low P/B ratio in the market... the market still seems a lack of confidence in the management

scores.rationale: There is no brand-driven pricing power whatsoever — realizations are set by commodity pipe prices and imports, and EBITDA fell 41% then 27% sequentially on realization decline alone.
scores.quote: The reason for decline in margin is attributed to fall in realization.

scores.rationale: Approved-vendor status with PSUs and the full size range plus qualified value-added grades (sour service subsea, cylinder, drill pipes) show customers buy qualification and reliability, though this has not protected price.
scores.quote: ensuring that we are a developed source with PSUs

scores.rationale: No discussion of distribution reach, sales force, or customer intimacy in these calls — sales are through PSU tenders.

The customer base is correctly corporate/PSU and served with reliability and qualification credentials, but the required corporate lock-in via switching costs or TCO advantage is absent given short tender cycles and import substitution.
scores.quote: The current order book is at INR1,302 crores, of which 33% comprises ONGC and Oil India orders.

scores.rationale: Technology is a stated weakness, not an edge — the plant is old and at obsolescence risk, and the one premium technology (premium connections) is being licensed from a foreign partner years after a competitor.
scores.quote: We do not manufacture premium connections right now. We have signed a royalty agreement with a foreign partner

scores.rationale: No network effects are relevant to or discussed in this commodity manufacturing business.
Distribution reach and service networks are not discussed in any of the four calls.

Concrete growth investment is underway — full branch redesign, AI-based branch security, paperless digital acquisition and new LOS platforms — though no incremental-ROIC disclosure supports a higher score.
scores.quote: our new branch design is ready... we are getting ready to next year completely transform our branches

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend in any of the four calls.
As a lender there is no R&D line, and the calls discuss only technology/process investment, not R&D productivity.
No new bolt-ons in the window, but the legacy Asirvad microfinance acquisition is the source of consolidated losses, with AUM down 39-56% YoY and a Rs.156 crore quarterly loss.
scores.quote: Loss was INR156 crores in Q3 FY '26 versus INR168 crores in Q2 FY '26

scores.rationale: A consistent but token Rs.0.50 interim dividend each quarter with no buyback or articulated distribution framework.
scores.quote: The Board has declared an interim dividend of INR0.50 for this quarter.

scores.rationale: This is an inherently balance-sheet-heavy lender carrying Rs.63,798 crores of AUM funded by banks, markets and securitization — the opposite of asset-light.
scores.quote: Our consolidated AUM for Q4 '26 was INR63,798 crores, up 22.4% sequentially

scores.rationale: Gold AUM nearly doubled YoY and gold rose to 80% of consolidated AUM from 59%, with 3.58 lakh new customers added in a single quarter, though much of the AUM gain is price rather than share.
scores.quote: Gold loan business constitutes 80% of the consolidated AUM versus 59% in the prior year.

scores.rationale: Purely domestic; co-lending extends reach into new geographies while non-gold businesses had their geographic spread deliberately cut back, netting out to neutral.
scores.quote: Co-lending partnerships have added a further origination channel, extending our reach to geographies where we have limited presence.

scores.rationale: Growth is collateral-price-driven, not pricing or mix — gold tonnage rose just 2.8% YoY while AUM rose 58%, and management introduced competitively priced schemes to attract borrowers.
scores.quote: Consolidated gold tonnage was 58.9 up by 3.2% Q-o-Q and up by 2.8% Y-o-Y

scores.rationale: Mixed cycle position — microfinance is bottoming with early recovery signs, but the gold book is being flattered by elevated gold prices near a cycle high rather than sitting at a trough.
scores.quote: microfinance is still in a recovery phase with a modest AUM expansion and improvements in asset quality

scores.rationale: Management points to structural expansion of formal gold lending and NBFC-led financial inclusion, with industry AUM expected to scale sharply over two years.
scores.quote: Industry-wide gold loan AUM is expected to scale sharply over the next two financial years, driven by elevated gold prices, a rising prevalence of secured credit

scores.rationale: Capital adequacy of 21.3%, no new acquisitions, and a deliberate pullback from weak segments show prudence, though the retrenchment is reactive to credit losses rather than counter-cyclical and PCR is only 27.34%.
scores.quote: Capital adequacy at 21.3%, well above the regulatory requirements.

scores.rationale: The multi-year diversification strategy is being reversed (MSME, vehicle, car and farm-equipment loans scaled down or paused) while the new CEO deferred the strategic roadmap twice, from Q4 FY26 to FY27.
scores.quote: we have as of now significantly scaled down all these businesses... We have additionally paused car loans, new and used and farm equipment loans.

scores.rationale: Calls are businesslike with no self-promotion, but the promoter consolidating Chairman and MD roles after the independent chairman's exit weighs against the low-profile stewardship ideal.
scores.quote: Board at today's meeting decided to appoint Mr. V. P. Nandakumar, MD, as the Chairman with effect from August 28, 2025.

scores.rationale: Extensive HR transformation and a stated focus on internal talent, but a wholesale external import of a new group leadership team, Group CFO and co-CEOs suggests the internal pipeline was inadequate.
scores.quote: We are in the process of onboarding a new group leadership team... we will also be bringing in external talent where required

scores.rationale: The CEO openly names underperformance rather than spinning it and commits to metric-driven disclosure, offset slightly by repeatedly withholding guidance.
scores.quote: As seen from our results, we have to significantly improve on our credit performance and profitability here.

scores.rationale: Headline 99% gold AUM growth flatters management skill — tonnage grew only 2.8% and consolidated FY26 PAT actually fell 17.5%, so the optics are gold-price luck, not execution.
scores.quote: our consolidated PAT before OCI and minority interest was at INR993 crores, down 17.5% year-on-year

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like hold on the customer — management repeatedly describes heightened competition from banks and NBFCs in a commoditised, fully collateralised product.
scores.quote: in spite of heightened competition

scores.rationale: Short-tenure gold loans against a fungible collateral carry effectively zero switching costs, and no captive aftermarket or regional lock-in is claimed anywhere in the calls.
scores.quote: The lending landscape remained competitive with sustained focus on improvements in asset quality

scores.rationale: The gold-loan market includes banks, multiple NBFCs and now co-lending partners, and management describes the environment as competitive and tightly regulated rather than a stable few-player structure.
scores.quote: the lending environment remains competitive and tightly regulated

scores.rationale: RBI's harmonised gold-loan rules explicitly create a level playing field that invites banks in, and the company itself resorted to competitively priced schemes to win borrowers — evidence of price competition, not rational restraint.
scores.quote: we have introduced various gold loan schemes at comprehensive prices to drive our gold loan strategy

scores.rationale: Formalisation of secured credit implies share available from informal lenders, but Manappuram is itself the donator in microfinance, MSME and vehicle finance where it is shrinking.
scores.quote: Microfinance portfolio listed a year-on-year decline of 56%.

scores.rationale: A large listed NBFC with Bain Capital as an investor, brokerage-hosted calls and intense regulatory attention is the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: Manappuram Finance now has started leveraging Bain Capital's extensive expertise in financial services within India

scores.rationale: Management invokes a strong brand, but pricing is set competitively through schemes rather than by image-led pricing power, so brand does not translate into demonstrated price premium.
scores.quote: With our strong brand, extensive distribution network and disciplined execution

scores.rationale: Customers pledging household gold buy custody certainty, and the company invests in rigorous appraisal standards and best-in-class AI branch security to underwrite that trust.
scores.quote: We continue to strengthen our loan-to-value management framework and uphold rigorous gold appraisal standards

scores.rationale: Superior accessibility is real — 85% of the book is sourced through the online gold loan platform, 3.58 lakh new customers were added in one quarter on a 25.9 lakh active base, backed by a dense branch network.
scores.quote: 85% of the loan book now sourced through online gold loan platform

scores.rationale: The customer base is retail bottom-of-pyramid households and small businesses, and the benefit offered — speed, accessibility and custody assurance — is correctly matched to that segment.
scores.quote: mainly to cater to small businesses and individuals at the bottom of the pyramid

scores.rationale: Digital sourcing, analytics and paperless journeys are being built, but the CEO is still reviewing technology architecture and platforms, indicating catch-up rather than a defensible multi-product tech edge.
scores.quote: reviewing our technology, architecture, and platforms

scores.rationale: Nothing in the calls describes any two-sided or self-reinforcing network; gold lending is a bilateral, collateral-based transaction that does not strengthen with scale.
An extensive branch network is treated as the core asset — the CEO plans to launch new products specifically to exploit it, and co-lending extends it further.
scores.quote: study new products that can be launched, taking advantage of the fantastic branch network that the Company has

scores.rationale: In-window growth capex is visible but modestly disclosed — a new biological facility and expanded biological R&D at BSV's Ambernath site, plus EU GMP upgrades at Udaipur and Ambernath — while the D&A step-up (Rs 219-222 cr/qtr vs ~Rs 100 cr) is mostly BSV acquisition amortisation rather than new-plant returns, so incremental ROIC is unproven.
scores.quote: we are also setting up a new biological facility to scale up and de-risk operation s at BSV's Ambernath site and expanding its biological R&D facilities

scores.rationale: Brand-building spend is not disclosed as a line item, but consumer brand equity is clearly compounding — Gas-O-Fast +36%/+33%, Manforce +18%/+14%, OvaNews +36% secondary growth and modern trade/e-commerce up 40-57% — though total OTC revenue still only grew 9% in FY26.
scores.quote: Secondary sales of Gas-O-Fast, Manforce and Ova News grew 33%, 8% and 36%, re spectively, during quarter 3

scores.rationale: R&D intensity rose sharply within the year (1.7-1.9% of sales to 2.9%, guided 2.5-3%) and is already yielding launches that rank #1 in their categories (Crenzlo, Vonalong, HER2-P pertuzumab biosimilar, AdvaUD), though it cost ~80-100 bps of EBITDA margin and the innovation pipeline (GPR-119, AMR molecule) is still early.
scores.quote: R&D expenses increased from 1.9% of sales in quarter 2 FY'25 to 2.9% of sales i n quarter 2 '26, in line with our guidance of 2.5% to 3%

scores.rationale: Bolt-on brand buys look good — Rivotril from Roche this quarter, and Glizid (acquired 2022) now a Rs 200 cr+ family compounding at 30%+ — but the dominant deal, BSV, is the opposite of small-and-simple: it drove a Rs 5,000 cr commercial-paper load, ~Rs 170 cr/qtr finance cost, doubled D&A and coincided with EBITDA margin falling ~120-280 bps y/y.
scores.quote: we acquired the brand, Rivotril, from Roche, a renowned textbook brand of clonazepam

scores.rationale: Distribution is coherent but minimal and subordinated to deleveraging — a token Rs 1/share interim dividend framed as a 30-year milestone gesture, with cash directed to fully retiring Rs 5,000 cr of commercial paper and cutting net debt Rs 488 cr q/q; no buyback at any valuation.
scores.quote: the Company's Board has approved an interim dividend of Rs. 1 per share

scores.rationale: The protecting moat is real (No.1 prescription share) but the balance sheet got heavier, not lighter, in this window — BSV goodwill/intangibles pushed D&A from ~Rs 100 cr to ~Rs 220 cr a quarter against revenue growth decelerating to 11-12%, so asset-light is not the current profile.
scores.quote: depreciation and amortization expenses have increased to INR222 crores as compared to INR100 crores in quarter 2 FY '25, which is primarily driven by depreciation and amortization impact related to BSV assets

scores.rationale: Genuine runway (rank 4 by value with only 4.9% share) and measurable capture in chronic — share up 190 bps to ~39% in FY26, anti-diabetes covered-market rank improved 5th to 4th, 1.6-2.2x IPM outperformance — but offset by acute/GST-driven quarters where secondary sales lagged IPM (6.3% vs 7.2%; 8.7% vs 10.7%).
scores.quote: Our consistent outperformance in anti -diabetic in last couple of quarters have improved our covered market rank from fifth to fourth during the quarter.

scores.rationale: Exports grew 35% in FY26 to Rs 2,061 cr with EU GMP certification at both Udaipur and Ambernath opening semi-regulated markets, but organic export growth was repeatedly described as single-digit and Q4 grew only 4% on geopolitical headwinds — so the expansion is credible but so far consolidation-led.
scores.quote: our export revenue for the quarter grew by 4% year -on-year to INR557 crores, primarily impacted by geopolitical headwinds

scores.rationale: Growth is predominantly price and mix rather than volume — FY26 volume growth was just 2.3% (albeit up from 0.5%) against ~14.4% domestic growth, with Q3 gross margin expansion explicitly attributed to price increases and favourable mix, and chronic mix up 190 bps.
scores.quote: our volume growth has increased to 2.3% in financial year '26 versus 0.5% last year

scores.rationale: The calls describe a company-specific execution trough and recovery (post-GST disruption, workforce churn, corrective actions) rather than an identifiable end-market cycle; Indian pharma demand is not presented as cyclical, so there is no basis to judge cycle positioning.

End markets are secular — IPM growing 7-10% with chronic therapies (cardiac, anti-diabetes, respiratory inhalers, IVF/fertility, biosimilars) structurally outgrowing acute, and management is deliberately reweighting toward specialty chronic — but company growth decelerated to ~11-12% in H2, below its own historical trajectory.
scores.quote: our strategic focus is now increasing towards specialty chronic therapies and R&D -led innovation products

scores.rationale: Within this window stewardship was disciplined — full retirement of Rs 5,000 cr commercial paper, net debt down Rs 488 cr q/q, no new large M&A (only a small Roche brand buy), and continued R&D investment through a weak-margin year — though this is repair work following the leveraged BSV deal.
scores.quote: we have fully retired the commercial papers worth INR5,000 crores with the last tranche worth INR1,500 crores, which has been paid in October 2025

scores.rationale: Promoter-family leadership pushed through a costly multi-quarter reset — margin-dilutive R&D step-up, BSV integration and prescription-portfolio transition, digital rebuild — while explicitly accepting near-term pain for later benefit, which reads as independent and long-term though the payoff is still promised rather than banked.
scores.quote: The corrective actions we have taken are strengthening our foundation, and we expect their impact to become increasingly visible in the coming quarters over the next few years.

scores.rationale: Calls are workmanlike and metric-dense with no personality promotion, and disclosure is delegated across CEO/CFO/IR rather than centred on one figure; the only limelight-seeking note is the publicised OpenAI partnership.
scores.quote: Our partnership with OpenAI marks a new era of digital transformation

scores.rationale: There are genuine talent-system investments (Mankind University, a self-paced AI learning platform; explicit people-centric framing) but they sit against admitted workforce instability requiring 'disruptive changes' and a senior-leadership record of Chairman, MD and CEO-level exits — a pipeline being rebuilt, not yet demonstrated.
scores.quote: the disruptive changes undertaken have led to meaningful improv ement in our workforce stability

scores.rationale: Consistently high candor across all four calls: organic growth is disclosed separately from BSV consolidation every quarter, underperformance versus IPM is stated plainly rather than buried, and margin declines are bridged to specific causes (R&D +100 bps, employee cost +130 bps, GST stockist discounts, slow-moving inventory accruals).
scores.quote: our secondary sales increased by 6.3% year -on-year which was lower as compared to 7.2% IPM growth. We believe GST impact was higher for us as compared to IPM

scores.rationale: Halo risk is low precisely because recent results are unflattering — PAT down 21.3% y/y in Q2, revenue growth decelerating to 11.5-11.8%, headline growth flattered by BSV consolidation — so the skill assessment rests on disclosed operating detail rather than on glowing outcomes, but equally there is no in-window proof of exceptional skill.
scores.quote: The profit after tax for quarter 2 FY '26 has decreased by 21.3% year-on-year

scores.rationale: Several genuine mind-share monopolies exist — No.1 prescription rank for nine consecutive years, Vonoprazan/Vonalong No.1 by both value and volume, Crenzlo No.1 branded generic in cardio, Telmikind at Rs 750 cr+ — but these are brand-level positions inside contestable molecule markets, not structural monopolies.
scores.quote: Vonoprazan which is now the number 1 prescribed brand by both value and volume in its category

scores.rationale: Switching costs are prescriber-habit based rather than contractual, but BSV's specialty niches (Anti-D, Foligraf, HMG in IVF/fertility) are thinly contested and clinically sticky, evidenced by 52% Foligraf and 40% HMG growth and a Phase-3 non-inferiority publication defending the franchise.
scores.quote: BSV domestic specialty business witnessed strong double -digit growth, led by robust growth in mandate brand like Anti-D, Foligraf, HMG

scores.rationale: The Indian pharma market is structurally fragmented, not an oligopoly — Mankind is only 4th by value with a 4.9% share, and it competes molecule-by-molecule against numerous branded-generic players, giving trade channels real leverage as GST-related stockist compensation showed.
scores.quote: Mankind continued to consolidate its rank, 4th by value, with a market share of 4.9%

scores.rationale: Pricing behaviour is rational — price increases contributed to Q3 gross margin expansion to 72.6% and there is no mention of discount wars — but entry barriers in branded generics are moderate at best, and the company had to fund stockist discounts to absorb the GST 2.0 transition.
scores.quote: This increase is a combination of sal es price increase effect, favorable sales mix and release of certain inventory -related accruals

scores.rationale: Weak holders of assets are visibly donating share — Mankind buys under-exploited brands from larger owners and rescales them (Glizid from Panacea now Rs 200 cr+ at 30%+ CAGR; Rivotril from Roche) while outgrowing IPM 1.6-2.2x in anti-diabetes and 1.1-1.2x in cardiac.
scores.quote: One of the chronic brand, Glizid, which we acquired from Panacea in 2022 is now an INR200 crores -plus brand family, growing at a CAGR of 30% +

scores.rationale: This is the opposite of an ignored niche — a large listed company ranked 4th in IPM with heavy analyst coverage, quarterly investor calls, an IR function, and a publicised OpenAI tie-up; competitors and capital watch it closely.
scores.quote: Mankind continued to consolidate its rank, 4th by value

scores.rationale: Gross margin held at ~71-72.6% with successful price increases and strong consumer-brand pull (Gas-O-Fast, Manforce, Preganews, OvaNews compounding at double-to-triple IPM rates), though the positioning is explicitly affordability-led rather than premium image-led.
scores.quote: our purpose -led growth has been rooted in delivering quality and affordable healthcare to all

scores.rationale: Doctors buy reliability rather than price — 15.1% prescription share, 84.1% prescriber penetration and nine straight years at No.1, reinforced by EU GMP certification at Udaipur and Ambernath and BSV's published Phase-3 non-inferiority data.
scores.quote: For the ninth consecutive year, we maintained our lea dership position with ranked number 1 in prescription, supported by 15.1% prescription share and 84.1% prescriber penetration

scores.rationale: Accessibility and field intimacy are the standout strength — dominant presence across Tier 2 to Tier 6 towns (so dominant that GST disruption hit it harder than IPM), PCPM rising to Rs 7.2 lakh, 84%+ prescriber coverage, plus fast-growing modern trade/e-commerce reach up to 13% of OTC.
scores.quote: GST impact was higher for us as compared to IPM due to our stronger presence in Tier 2 to Tier 6 cities

scores.rationale: The benefit-to-customer match is coherent — intangible brand pull for retail OTC consumers (Manforce, Gas-O-Fast, Preganews) and trust/reliability plus detailing intensity for the prescribing doctor, with newly added corporate-hospital penetration as a third channel.
scores.quote: expanding o ur corporate hospital s penetration

scores.rationale: R&D at 2.9% of sales is a real step-up and the pipeline includes differentiated assets (GPR-119, an AMR molecule, IVF recombinant biosimilar, HER2-P pertuzumab), but the business remains branded generics and in-licensed/first-to-market launches rather than a deep multi-product technology edge.
scores.quote: Alongside GPR - 119 for anti -obesity and anti -diabetes , our pipeline includes candidates targeting autoimmune disease, a novel anti-microbial resistance molecule

scores.rationale: No evidence of any two-sided or self-reinforcing network in the four calls; the digital and AI initiatives described are internal productivity tools, not platforms.

Distribution and field reach is the company's hardest-to-replicate asset — No.1 prescription share for nine consecutive years with 84.1% prescriber penetration, No.2 by volume at 6.2% share, and unmatched penetration of Tier 2-6 India, now extended into modern trade, e-commerce and corporate hospitals.
scores.quote: second by volume, with a market share of 6.2%

scores.rationale: A committed INR 460 crore growth capex programme over 2-3 years (new fractionation, CBA facility, 200 tpd refinery, Burkina Faso processing) follows capacity that already lifted revenue 76% at ROCE of 33.6%, so growth spend is large, rising and earning high incremental returns.
scores.quote: committing a capital expenditure of INR 460 crores over the next 2 to 3 years

scores.rationale: No advertising or promotion spend is discussed anywhere in the four calls; the business is B2B ingredient supply.

R&D produced a slate of new products in FY25 (bake-stable, water-cream and premium filling fats, frozen dessert applications) that won new customers and geographies, and the company elevated a VP-R&D to Deputy CEO, though absolute R&D spend is never quantified.
scores.quote: We have developed new products during financial year '25, which includes all-round filling fats, bake stable filling fats, water cream filling fats, frozen dessert applications and premium filling fats for new customers

scores.rationale: No acquisitions were made in the window — expansion is greenfield/organic (land purchase adjacent to Birkoni, new subsidiaries), so there is no M&A record to judge.

Only a token final dividend of 30% of the INR 2 face value was declared with no buyback and no articulated distribution policy, consistent with full reinvestment but offering nothing to score positively.
scores.quote: final dividend of 0.6 paisa per share that is a 30% of face value of INR 2 per share

scores.rationale: The model is capital- and inventory-heavy (INR 549 crore inventory, 125-151 working-capital days, INR 460 crore of plant capex) so asset turn is unremarkable even though ROCE is high at 33.6%.
scores.quote: Our total inventory as on 31st March '25 stands Rs. 549 crores

scores.rationale: Revenue grew 69% then 76% on a small base in a market management calls structurally undersupplied, implying real share capture, but it already claims domestic leadership which limits runway at home.
scores.quote: we operate in a structurally undersupplied and high-growth exotic niche specialty fats and butters market

scores.rationale: Exports are 73% of revenue and the company has stood up subsidiaries in West Africa, UAE and Brazil plus a Burkina Faso processing plant, expanding both sourcing and end-market reach.
scores.quote: we have established strategic global subsidiaries in West Africa, the UAE and Brazil for strengthening our global market presence

scores.rationale: Management attributes FY26 growth to volume plus an improved value-added mix (70-75% of sales), so mix is a genuine contributor but volume from new capacity is the primary driver rather than pricing.
scores.quote: up 76.1% year-on-year driven by volume growth and improved product mix

scores.rationale: The calls never discuss where the business sits in a cocoa or commodity cycle, so no cycle-position judgement is supportable from this evidence.

The end market is described as structurally undersupplied and high-growth, driven by durable secular demand for sustainable, traceable cocoa butter equivalents in chocolate, confectionery and cosmetics.
scores.quote: the demand for sustainable solutions in this niche market is growing rapidly and significantly worldwide

scores.rationale: Expansion is entirely organic with no M&A, the new packing plant and lab were funded from internal accruals, and leverage fell from 0.83:1 to 0.38:1 while working capital days improved from 180 to 125.
scores.quote: we have successfully commissioned a new packing plant with the new laboratory building and other infrastructure, all funded through our internal accruals

scores.rationale: A consistent multi-year backward-integration strategy from tribal seed collection through to fractionation, now extended to Burkina Faso, shows long-term intent, though the promotional framing tempers confidence.
scores.quote: Our backward integration from procurement to research and development to super critical fractionation provides us with unparalleled control over quality, cost, supply stability

scores.rationale: A small-town Chhattisgarh promoter family with a modest public profile, but the calls carry grandiose self-description that cuts against understatement.
scores.quote: We plan to reach to every human on this carth.

scores.rationale: The bench was visibly deepened during the year with two Deputy CEO appointments including an external R&D/business-development scientist, alongside a meaningful INR 15.4 crore ESOP charge, though one appointee is family.
scores.quote: DR. KRISHNADATH BHAGGAN – DEPUTY CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER - BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT & VICE PRESIDENT, R&D

scores.rationale: Guidance was raised transparently in steps (INR 1,050cr to 1,150cr to 1,300cr) and beaten at INR 1,358cr, and the adverse INR 23.3 crore mark-to-market forex provision was disclosed in detail rather than buried.
scores.quote: The cunmilative mark-to-market provision for the financial year stand at INR 23.3 crores

scores.rationale: The extraordinary optics — 76% growth, 27% EBITDA margins, 40% ROE — coincide with a period of record cocoa prices that mechanically pulls demand toward cocoa butter equivalents, and the calls never separate that tailwind from execution, so the assessment is not halo-robust.
scores.quote: the global relevance of our specialty fats and coco butter equivalents and the sustained and growing demand

scores.rationale: The combination of a wild-harvest sal/shea sourcing network reaching tribal collectors and supercritical fractionation gives it a near-unique position for exotic seed butters, which management frames as a defensible moat.
scores.quote: create a defensible competitive moat for Manorama

scores.rationale: Customized, certified formulations qualified into multinational chocolate and cosmetic recipes create real switching costs, evidenced by repeat demand from the same key customers across all four quarters.
scores.quote: focus on customized, high-quality solutions

scores.rationale: Supply is described as structurally short which helps supplier economics, but the customer base is large multinational chocolate and cosmetics companies with substantial negotiating power and the competitive structure is never described.
scores.quote: structurally undersupplied and high-growth exotic niche

scores.rationale: Entry requires a decade-scale rural sourcing network, heavy certification (FSSC 22000, RSPO, Fairtrade, Kosher, Halal, Organic) and solvent fractionation assets, and margins held steady at ~27% across the year with no sign of price competition.
scores.quote: EBITDA INR 367.7 crores with an EBITDA margin of 27.1%

scores.rationale: Competitors are never named or characterised in these calls, so there is no evidence about weak rivals ceding share.
The business is an unglamorous exotic-seed butter processor operating out of Mahasamund, Chhattisgarh in a niche management itself calls exotic, well away from mainstream capital attention.
scores.quote: exotic niche specialty fats and butters market

scores.rationale: Management asserts pricing power and margins are healthy, but this is a B2B ingredient with no consumer brand or taste-driven image, and the value proposition rests on function and certification rather than intangibles.
scores.quote: we aim to strengthen our leadership in specialty fats and butter with pricing power

scores.rationale: Customers buy certainty — full traceability, an unusually long certification stack and integrated control of quality and supply stability — with management positioned explicitly as a trusted partner rather than a low-price option.
scores.quote: This strategic approach positions us as a trusted partner for our customers in the chocolate, confectionery and cosmetic industries

scores.rationale: Deeper customer engagement and customised solutions, backed by on-the-ground subsidiaries in West Africa, UAE, Brazil and Latin America, bring the company physically close to both suppliers and clients.
scores.quote: continuous innovation, capacity expansion, and deeper customer engagement

scores.rationale: The customer base is entirely corporate (chocolate, confectionery, cosmetics multinationals) and the offer is correctly matched to it — reliability, traceability, certification and formulation lock-in rather than consumer image.
scores.quote: consistent demand from leading international clients in the chocolate, confectionery and cosmetic industrial sectors

scores.rationale: Supercritical and solvent fractionation plus an in-house R&D function that keeps releasing new fat formulations gives a real technical edge, though R&D intensity is never quantified and the technology is not proprietary at a patent level.
scores.quote: Our backward integrated model, high-tech R&D, research and development with cutting-edge technology

scores.rationale: No two-sided or self-reinforcing network is described in any of the four calls.
The genuinely hard-to-replicate reach is upstream in seed collection rather than downstream distribution, and no customer-facing distribution or service advantage is evidenced.
scores.quote: Our waste to wealth, sourcing model continues to empower billions of rural and tribal women

scores.rationale: Growth capex has essentially stopped — FY26 net retail area addition was only ~4,200 sq ft on a 1.79 mn sq ft base, with new openings offset by closures of underperforming and experimental formats.
scores.quote: we selectively added new stores while also rationalizing underperforming locations, resulting in a net addition of about 4,200 square feet to our retail area

scores.rationale: A&P is heavy and demonstrably builds brand equity (Karan Johar podcast, 1bn+ view 'Made for Each Other' campaign) but is converting poorly into sales, with FY26 SSG of only 2.7%.
scores.quote: surpassing 1 billion-plus views and becoming the most liked organic branded collaboration on Instagram in India

scores.rationale: No R&D spend or programme is discussed in any of the four calls; design/collection work is described but never framed or quantified as R&D.
No acquisition, divestment or deal of any kind is mentioned across the last-12-month calls.
Buybacks, dividends and distribution policy are entirely absent from the excerpts despite 98% cash conversion.

The franchise-led, asset-light model shows up in near-perfect cash conversion and improving inventory turns alongside 44% EBITDA margins, though revenue per square foot is flat as sales grow only 3.5%.
scores.quote: the Company reported strong cash conversion ratio of approx. 98%

scores.rationale: The company is already the self-described category leader and FY26 SSG of 2.7% with flat store area shows no evidence of active share capture, even if the unorganised wedding-wear market leaves theoretical runway.
scores.quote: Vedant Fashions is India's leading wedding and celebration wear company

scores.rationale: International expansion is token — two stores added in Australia and UAE in Q2 — while the domestic footprint actually contracted from 257 to 252 cities over the year.
scores.quote: We also strengthened our international presence with 2 new stores in Australia and the UAE

scores.rationale: Management explicitly declined to pass through the GST increase from 12% to 18% and is chasing 'more competitive' price points, so pricing is a headwind not a driver; only the Twamev premium mix is positive.
scores.quote: in 90% of our products, GST rates have increased from 12% to 18%. However...we have not increased MRP of all the products

scores.rationale: The business is visibly near a cyclical trough — muted mid-premium sentiment, fewer wedding dates in December and none in January — with management pointing to government measures as an identifiable upturn trigger.
scores.quote: fewer wedding dates in December and no wedding dates in January, coupled with muted consumer sentiment

scores.rationale: Indian weddings are a durable end market and premiumisation is cited as a rising trend, but reported growth of 3.5% revenue and 6.1% retail sales shows no secular expansion in the current window.
scores.quote: Encouraged by the robust traction and rising premiumization trend, we plan to further accelerate and scale this segment faster

scores.rationale: Fully organic, no M&A, deliberate closure of formats that failed, and 98% cash conversion point to prudent stewardship, though 'discipline' here is also partly forced by a weak demand environment.
scores.quote: we pursued a focused and disciplined approach to expansion, prioritizing strategic and sustainable store openings

scores.rationale: Management consistently prioritised long-term retail quality and brand equity over reported numbers, absorbing the GST hit rather than protecting near-term margin.
scores.quote: our focus this year has been on strengthening the quality of retail as foundation for sustained long-term growth

scores.rationale: The calls are functional and promoter-family executives keep a modest personal profile, but the brand strategy is aggressively celebrity-fronted and Q3 was delegated entirely to the CFO and IR head, giving mixed evidence.
scores.quote: MR. RAHUL MURARKA – CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER; MR. NIRAJ SARAF – GENERAL MANAGER FINANCIAL PLANNING AND ANALYSIS

scores.rationale: Retail training is cited in every one of the four calls as a systematic lever alongside KPI management, though there is no evidence on senior leadership pipeline.
scores.quote: our sustained focus on enhancing customer experience, retail training, data driven merchandising

scores.rationale: Management quantified the 15-20 day GST dispatch disruption and the ~6% primary-vs-secondary revenue delta, explained gross margin compression without deflection, and openly admitted failed store concepts.
scores.quote: some of the different kind of concepts we tried in the past two years to three years, which have not worked for us

scores.rationale: The dazzling 65% gross and 44% EBITDA margins are largely a legacy of the franchise model rather than proof of current management skill — beneath them, SSG fell to 2.7% and gross margin slid from 66.9% to 65% over the four calls.
scores.quote: The Company continued to report industry-leading gross margin of 65%

scores.rationale: Manyavar occupies a near-monopoly position in the Indian consumer's mind for branded wedding wear, which management leans on explicitly, though it is a mindshare position without any aftermarket lock-in.
scores.quote: cemented Manyavar's identity as the definitive wedding wear brand

scores.rationale: Wedding wear is an infrequent, discretionary purchase with zero switching costs or captive aftermarket — nothing in the calls points to customer lock-in, and the response to weak demand was competitive pricing rather than captive pricing.
scores.quote: We are taking a lot of initiatives around designs, varieties, price points to be more competitive

scores.rationale: The category is fragmented rather than an oligopoly; management describes industry-wide weakness across the mid-premium segment and is adjusting price points to defend, indicating the end customer holds the power.
scores.quote: consumer sentiments remain weak across the mid premium industry

scores.rationale: Pricing rationality weakened during the window — a full GST increase absorbed rather than passed on, plus a stated push for more competitive price points, amounting to an effective price cut to defend volumes.
scores.quote: we have not increased MRP of all the products...products which are aspirational yet value for money

scores.rationale: No competitor is named or characterised in any of the four calls, so there is no evidence of identifiable weak players to take share from.
This is a widely covered listed company running billion-view celebrity campaigns and a Karan Johar podcast — the opposite of an under-the-radar niche.
scores.quote: the launch of the Manyavar Shaadi Show, a 6-episode YouTube podcast, hosted by renowned celebrity, Karan Johar

scores.rationale: Gross margins of 65-67% confirm real image-based pricing power, but the refusal to pass through a 600bp GST increase shows that power is currently being tested rather than exercised.
scores.quote: The Company continues to report industry leading gross margin of 66.9%

scores.rationale: Customers buy Manyavar for occasion confidence rather than measurable reliability, and the calls provide no evidence that price is secondary to trust — indeed price competitiveness is now an explicit lever.
scores.quote: how we can bring more fresh products for the consumer, how we can improve their consumer experience

scores.rationale: 669 EBOs across 252 cities plus omnichannel integration and auto-replenishment give strong accessibility and in-store intimacy, though the network stopped expanding this year.
scores.quote: EBO network stands at about 1.79 million square feet, spanning across 669 stores in 252 cities and towns globally

scores.rationale: The customer is retail and the benefit offered is correctly intangible/brand-led — a house of brands segmented by occasion and price tier (Manyavar, Mohey, Twamev, Mebaz, Diwas).
scores.quote: reinforcing Vedant Fashions as the definitive house of brands for all wedding and celebration wear needs

scores.rationale: Technology is operational rather than differentiating — data-led merchandising, auto-replenishment and omnichannel systems support execution but no proprietary tech edge or R&D intensity is claimed.
scores.quote: efficient auto-replenishment systems, all anchored by a strong back-end infrastructure

scores.rationale: The described model is single-sided brand retail through franchised EBOs; nothing in the calls indicates a two-sided network that strengthens with scale.
scores.quote: Our robust store network, relevant inventory and designs, multidimensional marketing initiatives

scores.rationale: 1.79 mn sq ft of dedicated wedding-wear EBOs across 252 cities with cross-brand leverage is a reach no rival in the category matches, but it is now static and shrank by five cities during the year.
scores.quote: our strong structural moats, a resilient business model, a disciplined approach, overall giving us significant advantage of cross-brand leverage

scores.rationale: Investment is real but is expensed IP/product development rather than disclosed growth capex, and FY26 incremental returns were poor — revenue rose only from INR463 crores to INR474 crores despite the spend.
scores.quote: the entire year had a muted growth overall from INR463 crores to INR474 crores

scores.rationale: No A&P spend, brand-building budget or marketing efficiency was discussed in any of the four calls; app downloads are cited without any linked promotional spend.
Sustained R&D in HD maps, mGIS and AI has converted into concrete new wins such as the Survey of India geoportal built on the company's own platform, though FY26 revenue conversion was weak.
scores.quote: Owing to the investments MapmyIndia has been making in building its mGIS platform for geospatial systems over the last many years, we've been able to bring that to the fold to enable Survey of India

scores.rationale: The Gtropy bolt-on required founder replacement and gap-fixing rather than being already strong, and the INR25 crores Zepto stake is a non-core financial investment in a customer rather than a complementary operating bolt-on.
scores.quote: we are refocusing the business on the way MapmyIndia has been doing in the enterprise world... as we identify certain gaps in the past; we are addressing those

scores.rationale: A modest final dividend of INR3.50 per share was declared with no buyback and no articulated distribution policy or valuation discipline.
scores.quote: declaring a final dividend for FY26 of INR3.50 per equity share of INR2 each at the rate of 175%

scores.rationale: The business is asset-light IP/software with 44-46% EBITDA margins protected by a proprietary map database, though flat FY26 revenue means turns did not improve.
scores.quote: Q4 FY26 EBITDA margin has expanded 460 bps year-on-year to 44.6%

scores.rationale: Runway remains large versus global map providers and share capture is visible in new logos and order booking of INR600-780 crores plus 10 million app downloads in the year.
scores.quote: The open order book, which was INR1,500 crores at the beginning of the year has increased to INR1,770 crores as of December 31

scores.rationale: The business is effectively India-only; international expansion is mentioned once as a vague future aspiration with no execution evidence.
scores.quote: in a better way today in India, and then of course, over time, out internationally also

scores.rationale: Growth is order-volume led with mix shifting toward lower-margin IoT and hardware-inclusive government contracts rather than price/mix uplift; no pricing power was discussed.
scores.quote: that kind of a business is largely IoT-led... the hardware component might not be more than INR10-15 crores out of total 100 crores

scores.rationale: The government-spend cycle bottomed in Q3 on grant delays and state elections, with a visible upturn already evident in the Q4 inflection.
scores.quote: the fiscal grant to the state for the national flagship projects that we are involved in got delayed this time... We also saw delays in Maharashtra and Bihar as a result of urban state elections

scores.rationale: End markets — national geospatial infrastructure post-2021 liberalization, quick commerce, autonomous driving and fleet IoT — are in secular expansion.
scores.quote: This is a follow-up on the liberalization of the geospatial sector in 2021, when the Honorable Prime Minister said, this is a Class A industry with a lot of geostrategic importance

scores.rationale: Management stays organic, unlevered and kept investing through a weak year, though the minority Zepto stake is a mild deviation from pure operating focus.
scores.quote: when we are making these other investments, we know that there's a huge bump that happens in Q4 that takes care of the year's overall target

scores.rationale: Founder-led with a demonstrated multi-decade pattern of going deep into one sector at a time and indigenizing its stack, but the maintained INR1,000 crores FY28 target after 2% FY26 growth strains credibility.
scores.quote: the company over the course of the last few decades has always found certain sectors where we have gone deep into; automotive being one where we have been deep into since 2007

scores.rationale: Commentary is substance-led on contracts, delivery and platforms with no personality promotion, despite occasional name-dropping of ministerial endorsements.
scores.quote: we would like to communicate that the nature of this business is such that it should be observed more on a yearly basis rather than quarter-on-quarter

scores.rationale: Leadership was visibly broadened beyond the founding family during the year, with a COO and President-Government Business fielding analyst questions from Q3 onward.
scores.quote: FY26 has been a year of consolidation, resilience and strategic execution for the company, marked by meaningful progress across leadership alignment, organizational accountability

scores.rationale: Management openly labelled Q3 weak, volunteered off-cycle order-book disclosure and named the delay causes, though it reaffirmed an FY28 target requiring implausible CAGR without addressing the gap.
scores.quote: I would like to start saying very openly that from many of the investors' perspective, the Q3 has been a weak quarter

scores.rationale: The marquee-win narrative (Survey of India, IOCL, DMRC, Zepto) runs well ahead of delivered results — 5-year PAT CAGR of 11% versus 24% revenue CAGR — so results should not be read as proof of skill.
scores.quote: Our revenue growth CAGR for the 5 years is at 24%... Our PAT growth over the 5 years CAGR is 11%

scores.rationale: It occupies a near-monopoly position as India's indigenous map platform, to the point the national government geospatial layer is being built on its own core platform.
scores.quote: this is a landmark entry into building the government's national geospatial platform based on MapmyIndia's own platform... It is similar to how Aadhaar and UPI were built
