scores.rationale: Low structural entry barriers in digital engineering, and margins depend on internal levers (utilization, offshoring, sub-con rationalization) rather than pricing power, indicating limited industry pricing protection.
scores.quote: expected to get offset through a combination of other margin levers, including offshoring, utilization, sub-con rationalization, SG&A optimization

scores.rationale: Persistent's 17%+ growth against peers growing far slower — including the acquiree's own admitted recent slowdown — implies a pool of weaker vendors from whom share is being taken.
scores.quote: for the last 5 years we are happy to say we are among the top as far as the growth is concerned in our industry.

scores.rationale: An $8.1bn market cap with heavy analyst coverage, investor days and awards programmes is the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: Today, we stand at about $8.1 billion in terms of market cap.

scores.rationale: Management claims strong brand recognition in respective markets, but this is B2B services with no image-driven pricing power and margins sensitive to wage and utilization swings.
scores.quote: The two companies have very strong brand name in respective markets.

scores.rationale: The $650m multi-year award was explicitly won on delivery track record and engineering trust rather than price, the clearest assurance-benefit evidence in the window.
scores.quote: This is a true testimony to the relationship and to what we have delivered for this customer over the years.

scores.rationale: Land-and-expand intimacy is visible in clients migrating up every revenue bucket, and the combination adds 40+ country coverage and European nearshore access to customers.
scores.quote: we will be 46,000+ team members globally spread across 40+ countries.

scores.rationale: An almost entirely corporate/enterprise base served with the right benefit set — reliability, multi-year contracts and switching-cost lock-in — matching framework expectations for B2B.
scores.quote: Top 5 customer revenue growing by 20.7%, Top 10 by 19.4%

scores.rationale: A structured multi-pillar AI platform (SASVA, engineering/business hyperproductivity, data readiness) is monetizing into pricing and margin, but it is built atop third-party foundation stacks rather than proprietary deep technology.
scores.quote: our AI-led platform approach - engineering hyperproductivity, business hyperproductivity and enterprise data readiness.

scores.rationale: No evidence of any two-sided or self-reinforcing network in the four calls.

Reach is being deliberately widened via alliances, geo leadership hires and the Nagarro combination, but 27,500 people across 21 countries is not a distribution advantage rivals cannot match in this industry.
scores.quote: All of this is backed up by 27,500 of our team members across 21 countries.

scores.rationale: Large, rising growth capex — INR 6,355 cr Gopalpur greenfield, Dahej 17.5→22.5 MMTPA by March 2026, petchem in full swing and ~INR 5,000 cr FY26 capex funded by a INR 12,000 cr term-loan RFP — but incremental ROIC is unproven given Kochi still at only 27–29% utilization and no contracted volumes yet disclosed for the new 5 MMTPA.
scores.quote: Board of Directors has, in principle, approved an enhanced investment of INR 6,355 crores for setting up a 5 MMTPA land-based LNG terminal at Gopalpur Port

scores.rationale: No mention of advertising or promotional spend in any of the four calls.
No R&D discussion in any of the four calls.
No acquisitions discussed in the last-12-month calls; growth is entirely greenfield/brownfield.
Regular dividends (INR 7 interim, INR 3 final for FY26) but no buybacks and no articulated payout framework, with distribution now competing against a debt-funded capex cycle.
scores.quote: We have also declared Rs. 7 per share interim dividend, reflecting our commitment to shareholder returns.

scores.rationale: Structurally asset-heavy — multi-thousand-crore terminals, 8 storage tanks and INR 12,000 cr of debt-funded capex against ~INR 11,000 cr quarterly revenue at ~10% EBITDA margin — so the moat exists but asset-light it is not.
scores.quote: EBITDA is INR1,117...crores with a margin of around 10%

scores.rationale: Petronet is already the dominant Indian regas player with Dahej at 90–94% utilization and rivals unable to ramp, so share-gain runway is limited; management itself frames the new 5 MMTPA as riding incremental national imports rather than taking rival share.
scores.quote: rival terminals in the similar vicinity to Dahej are not able to ramp up volumes versus PLL Dahej

scores.rationale: Credible domestic expansion to the East Coast via the Gopalpur greenfield terminal, but execution is early-stage with environmental clearance still pending after the FSRU-to-land-based switch.
scores.quote: marking our first greenfield LNG project on India's East Coast, transitioning from the earlier 4 MMTPA FSRU-based plan

scores.rationale: Growth is purely a volume/utilization story at flat regas tariffs — new contracts are signed at identical pricing and FY26 PAT fell to INR 3,843 cr from INR 3,926 cr on lower volumes — with no pricing or mix uplift.
scores.quote: So the pricing is absolutely the same, what we charge under our other long-term agreement.

scores.rationale: Volumes are cycle-depressed (March 2026 Dahej utilization 53% on the Gulf crisis, spot spiking to $25) with an identifiable upturn from the 2027–28 global LNG supply wave and prices already easing to $15–17.
scores.quote: there is going to be a decent supply of LNG in times to come, specifically end of '27, early 2028, which means that the spot prices could reduce

scores.rationale: Indian gas demand is a secular grower with multiple Indian buyers tying up long-term volumes at Dahej, though the last-12-month record is uneven (9M FY26 volumes 682 TBTU vs 729 TBTU) and an analyst noted soft 5-year topline.
scores.quote: many Indian companies have gone out in the market and tied up volumes on long-term basis. Most of them have capacity at Dahej terminal

scores.rationale: Organic-only growth with no M&A and a stated refusal to take LNG trading risk onto the balance sheet, offset by a large debt-funded capex program (INR 12,000 cr loan RFP) and diversification into petrochemicals.
scores.quote: Puneet: And are you also trying to tie up the long-term volumes on your own balance sheet?... Vivek Mittal: That's not right now on the agenda.

scores.rationale: PSU-JV governance with heavy churn — five chairmen and four managing directors across FY21–FY25 — undermines independent long-term stewardship, and the calls are fronted by the CFO/GGMs rather than the MD.
scores.quote: Chairman: Arun Kumar Singh (FY2022–FY2023, exited); Chairman: Manoj Jain (FY2023, exited)

scores.rationale: Commentary is low-key, technocratic and numbers-first from finance and marketing executives with no celebrity CEO presence on any of the four calls.
scores.quote: Good morning. I am Saurav Mitra. Thank you for joining us for the earnings call for the quarter ended 31st December 2025.

scores.rationale: Internal promotion is visible in the call rosters (Chawla GGM→Executive Director, Mittal CGM→GGM within the year) but the top posts are government-appointed with high turnover and no talent programme is discussed.
scores.quote: MR. RAKESH CHAWLA – EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR, FINANCE AND ACCOUNTS

scores.rationale: Volunteered the ugly March utilization of 53% and disclosed exact UOP arrears and inventory gains when asked, though guidance is repeatedly withheld (Kochi utilization, Qatar downstream timelines).
scores.quote: the Dahej capacity utilization during March was around 53% and Kochi was slightly more than 20%

scores.rationale: The headline "highest ever quarterly PBT" of INR 1,795 cr coincided with a INR 630 cr UOP dues receipt and INR 95 cr inventory gain in a quarter when volumes actually fell to 219 TBTU, so results reflect asset position and one-offs more than operating skill.
scores.quote: the customers also made payment of outstanding Use of Pay dues amounting to INR 630 crore pertaining to calendar year 2022

scores.rationale: Dahej is the default terminal in customers' minds on the strength of unmatched storage and evacuation, not brand — a strong but not absolute position given Dabhol, Hazira and Mundra alternatives.
scores.quote: we have 8 tanks over there. And none of the terminals in India are having so much of storage capacity

scores.rationale: Effectively a regional West-Coast monopoly with switching costs embedded in long-term capacity contracts carrying use-or-pay penalties that customers are still settling years later.
scores.quote: PLL Dahej terminal enjoys some critical advantages in terms of evacuation... it already has evacuation capacity of 35 million metric tons

scores.rationale: Few terminals nationally, but the customers are the same large state entities that own Petronet (GAIL, IOCL, BPCL) and can shift cargoes to Dabhol or their own capacity, so end-customer negotiating power is real.
scores.quote: we understand that GAIL has been working their Dabhol unit in this monsoon

scores.rationale: Capital and evacuation requirements are high barriers and pricing remains rational (tariffs unchanged on new contracts), but Indian regas capacity is being added by rivals and PLL's own moat rests on being the lowest-cost operator rather than on absent entrants.
scores.quote: the pricing, we are one of the lowest cost operator and our charges are also one of the lowest in the industry

scores.rationale: Competing terminals in the same catchment are visibly failing to ramp utilization, leaving weak rivals from whom Dahej's new 5 MMTPA can draw volumes.
scores.quote: rival terminals in the similar vicinity to Dahej are not able to ramp up volumes versus PLL Dahej

scores.rationale: Far from under-the-radar — calls are hosted and attended by ICICI, IIFL, HSBC, Axis, Ambit, PhillipCapital and Ashika, and every capacity, tariff and project decision is publicly scrutinised.
scores.quote: MODERATOR: MR. BALAJI SUBRAMANIAN – IIFL CAPITAL SERVICES LIMITED

scores.rationale: No image or taste-based pricing power — this is a commodity tolling service at industry-low tariffs with ~10% EBITDA margin and demand swinging with spot LNG versus alternate fuels.
scores.quote: there was low demand from power sector and fertilizer sector compared to the Q1 of FY '25

scores.rationale: Customers buy reliability and flexibility — storage depth, guaranteed evacuation and uninterrupted operation through the Gulf crisis — with tariffs a secondary consideration.
scores.quote: the company has delivered a strong financial and operational performance during the current quarter, despite the challenging external environment arising from the ongoing crisis in the Gulf region

scores.rationale: The convenience proposition is explicit: evacuation headroom of 35 MMTPA against 22.5 MMTPA capacity plus eight tanks giving offtakers operational flexibility no Indian rival matches.
scores.quote: provides them with huge storage capacity... which gives flexibility to the offtakers in its operations

scores.rationale: Customer base is entirely corporate (GAIL, IOCL, BPCL, GSPC, Torrent, ONGC, MGL, Deepak Fertilisers) and is served correctly with low-cost TCO plus long-term capacity contracts that create lock-in.
scores.quote: Aim is also that we convert this into a long-term capacity agreement with ONGC.

scores.rationale: No technology differentiation or R&D intensity is discussed in any of the four calls.
No two-sided or self-reinforcing network dynamic is described; the business is bilateral tolling contracts.

Pipeline evacuation reach and storage at Dahej are the stated reason incremental volumes flow to PLL rather than nearby rivals, though the pipeline grid itself is owned by third parties and Kochi shows the moat fails without connectivity.
scores.quote: any terminal, simply having the regas capacity doesn't -- cannot function to its fullest capacity and efficiency

scores.rationale: As a lending NBFC the calls discuss loan-book deployment rather than capex, and no growth-versus-maintenance capex disclosure appears in any of the four calls.
No advertising or promotion spend is mentioned anywhere in the last-12-month calls.
No R&D spend or product-development programme is discussed in the recent calls.

The defining recent transaction is the government-announced PFC–REC merger — a transformational, complex, politically-driven restructuring of a subsidiary already 52.63% owned, the opposite of a small complementary bolt-on, with no OPM benefit yet demonstrable.
scores.quote: restructuring of PFC and REC . As you know that this was announced by Hon'ble Finance Minister in the Union Budget on 1st of February 2026

scores.rationale: A coherent, steadily rising dividend policy (FY25 ₹15.80 → FY26 ₹18.55 per share) paid quarterly through interims, though there are no buybacks and no valuation-linked distribution discipline.
scores.quote: total dividend for Financial Year '2 026 stands at INR 18.55 per share

scores.rationale: Structurally asset-heavy balance-sheet lender — an ~INR 11.64 lakh crore loan book earning a 3.55% NIM and 2.46% spread — the antithesis of asset-light high-turn economics, and the spread is compressing.
scores.quote: The spread at 2.46 % and NIM at 3.55%

scores.rationale: PFC is already the dominant player (largest NBFC loan book, largest renewable book), so runway to gain share is limited, and recent commentary shows it defending share against rising competition rather than capturing it.
scores.quote: due to lower interest rate cycle in India and increasing competition, we consciously priced our lending at competitive rates

scores.rationale: Business is entirely domestic and no geographic expansion plan is discussed; the JBIC facility is a funding source, not market entry.
Growth is explicitly volume-led at the expense of price — management deliberately cut lending rates, warned yields will fall further in FY27, and guided spreads down from 2.58% to 2.40–2.50%.
scores.quote: we consciously priced our lending at competitive rates to support business growth. As a result, the impact of this will be reflected in our yields numbers in Financial Year '2 027

scores.rationale: The credit cycle is clearly past its trough with 80% of the peak NPA book resolved and successive write-backs (KSK, Sinnar, TRN), though the interest-rate/spread cycle is now turning against PFC.
scores.quote: 80% of our NPA book has been resolved from its peak level

scores.rationale: The end market — Indian power capacity and the energy transition — is in durable secular expansion, evidenced by the INR 1.65 lakh crore renewable book and the national Viksit Bharat 2047 build-out.
scores.quote: As India moves towards the vision of "Viksit Bharat 2047 ", the power sector will be a key growth engine

scores.rationale: Prudent capitalisation (CRAR 23.44%, Tier-1 21.93%), 80% Stage-3 coverage and 100% provisioning on the Gensol default show conservatism, offset by a very large non-organic restructuring the board did not initiate.
scores.quote: CRAR is at 23.44% with Tier-1 capital at 21.93%. These levels give us a comfortable headroom for future growth

scores.rationale: As a government undertaking, the single most consequential strategic decision of the year was announced by the Finance Minister and requires cabinet and presidential approval, showing strategy is set outside the management team.
scores.quote: subject to regulatory approvals from MCA, RBI, SEBI, cabinet approval, presidential approval

scores.rationale: Communication is institutional and low-key — a PSU management team presenting numbers and process with no personality-driven promotion across all four calls.
scores.quote: At PFC, our investor communication is built on three T's : "Timeliness, Trust and Transparency"

scores.rationale: Senior succession is externally administered and gappy — the Director (Finance) is newly brought in and the Director (Commercial) seat sat unfilled after a 31 March 2026 retirement pending formal government appointment.
scores.quote: our Director (Commercial ) also retired on 31st of March 2026 and he has been shortlisted and we are awaiting the formal appointment

scores.rationale: Consistently candid across all four calls — pre-warned on forex hit to Q4 profit, disclosed the Gensol default with exact recoveries and 100% provisioning, and volunteered that FY26 rate-cutting will depress FY27 yields.
scores.quote: In Q4, we have m ade 100% provisioning on Gensol Engineering, an NPA with current outstanding of Rs. 263 crores

scores.rationale: Record headline profits flatter the underlying franchise — FY26's INR 20,051 crore included ~INR 1,800 crore of provision write-backs while NII growth halved from 24% to 13% and spreads compressed, so results overstate operating skill.
scores.quote: highest ever net profit of INR 20,051 crore with a 16% increase year -on-year basis. This was driven by a healthy net interest income growth of 13% along with provision reversals of around INR 1,800 crore

scores.rationale: PFC holds a quasi-institutional monopoly role in the sector's plumbing — nodal agency for RDSS and the annual Integrated Rating of DISCOMs — which no commercial lender replicates.
scores.quote: PFC has been serving as a nodal agency for this exercise for several years now

scores.rationale: Borrowers face low switching costs — banks are actively undercutting on rate and PFC had to reprice to retain business, indicating no captive or lock-in economics.
scores.quote: increasing competition, we consciously priced our lending at competitive rates

scores.rationale: The PFC–REC merger consolidates dedicated power-financing into effectively one state institution, but commercial banks compete freely for the same state utility and renewable borrowers, so end customers retain negotiating power.
scores.quote: The combined entity will be positioned as a single window financing partner for India's power sector

scores.rationale: Pricing rationality has visibly deteriorated in the last year, with management conceding it cut lending rates to defend growth and guiding spreads structurally lower.
scores.quote: we expect our spreads to be in the range of 2.4 0%to 2.5 0%

scores.rationale: No weak competitors are identified to take share from; the recent calls describe competitive pressure flowing toward PFC rather than away from rivals.
scores.quote: increasing competition

scores.rationale: PFC is India's largest NBFC by loan book and profit, covered by sell-side analysts and named in the Union Budget — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: our consolidated PAT is the highest among NBFCs at INR 33,625 crore

scores.rationale: There is no image- or taste-driven pricing power — PFC is a rate-taker that cut prices under competition, with spreads narrowing from 2.58% to a guided 2.40–2.50%.
scores.quote: we consciously priced our lending at competitive rates to support business growth

scores.rationale: State utilities and developers value PFC's sector expertise, appraisal discipline and reliability as a long-term counterparty, reinforced by its rating-agency and nodal role, though this trust does not yet translate into price insensitivity.
scores.quote: This project does not reflect upon PFC's apprais al methodology nor the risk mitigation strategies adopted by PFC

scores.rationale: PFC offers unmatched accessibility for power-sector borrowers — single-window financing across generation, transmission, distribution and renewables, plus direct institutional intimacy with every DISCOM.
scores.quote: positioned as a single window financing partner for India's power sector

scores.rationale: The customer base is entirely corporate/state-owned, correctly served with scale and reliability, but the calls show none of the switching-cost lock-in that corporate moats require — borrowers move on price.
scores.quote: increasing competition, we consciously priced our lending at competitive rates

scores.rationale: No technology capability, platform or R&D intensity is discussed in the recent calls.
No two-sided network dynamic is described anywhere in the last-12-month calls.

Reach into every state utility and government scheme — nodal-agency status, the DISCOM rating franchise and the country's largest renewable book — is a sector-financing distribution footprint competitors cannot easily replicate.
scores.quote: we continue to maintain the leadership position in the renewable energy financing with one of the largest renewable book of INR 1.65 lakh crore

scores.rationale: Large, clearly growth-oriented capex (₹700–750cr in FY26 across Greater Noida, Supa, Rajasthan, Sricity plus a ₹1,000cr Maharashtra MoU and a 1.2mn-unit refrigerator plant), but incremental returns are visibly diluting as ROCE fell 25.2%→20.8%→18.6% across the year and capex was itself cut from the ₹800–900cr originally planned.
scores.quote: We are continuing with our investment in Greater Noida, Supa, Rajasthan, and South India with FY26 CAPEX to be between Rs.700 crores to Rs.750 crores, down from Rs.800 crores to Rs.900 crores planned earlier.

scores.rationale: PGEL is a B2B ODM/contract manufacturer selling to brands; no advertising or promotion spend is discussed in any of the four calls.

New platforms and categories are being added (washing machine 'new platforms', POS devices, refrigerators), but these come via partner tie-ups and licensed platforms rather than disclosed in-house R&D spend or efficiency.
scores.quote: Washing machines grew by 36% with strong volume growth from new platforms.

scores.rationale: No acquisitions; growth-by-partnership instead — the Goodworth TV JV ramped to ₹670cr 9M revenue but at only ~2.5% EBITDA margin, and the compressor JV is stalled awaiting Chinese government clearance.
scores.quote: there is some delay in getting some clearance from the governments on this, especially from the China government on this project

scores.rationale: No buyback, dividend or distribution policy is mentioned anywhere in the last four calls.

Genuinely asset-light on fixed assets (net fixed asset turn held at 5–6x all year), but the 'protecting moat' half is absent — ROCE compressed from 25.2% to 18.6% and margins were squeezed at will by input costs and customers.
scores.quote: our net fixed asset turnover remains healthy over 6x

scores.rationale: Clear, repeated share capture: RAC grew 27% in 9M FY26 and +9% for the full year against an industry down ~15%, washing machines +52% FY26, with explicit wallet-share gains at anchor customers.
scores.quote: we have been able to grow our RAC business by 27% in 9 months of FY '26 despite the industry posting an almost 15% to 20% decline

scores.rationale: Expansion is domestic manufacturing-footprint only (Sricity, Supa, Maharashtra, Rajasthan) to serve existing Indian brand customers — no export markets and no premium brand that travels.
scores.quote: We have a plan. We have an intention to set up a refrigerator plant in the state of Andhra Pradesh.

scores.rationale: Growth is entirely volume/new-platform led and pricing power was explicitly negative — the company could not pass through 10–15% industry price hikes, forex or commodity inflation, losing ~250bps of gross margin.
scores.quote: This further reduced our pricing power and ability to pass through the increases in commodities and exchange rate impact.

scores.rationale: FY26 was a washout trough (industry −15%, channel choked, GST and BEE-rating disruptions) with an identifiable catalyst ahead in GST-driven penetration, though management itself is only 'cautiously optimistic' and the inventory overhang is not yet cleared.
scores.quote: We remain optimistic that the room AC business will see an increased, penetration-led growth with the recent rationalization of GST

scores.rationale: Two reinforcing secular drivers are cited and evidenced: low Indian consumer-durable penetration and the structural shift of brands toward outsourced manufacturing, which PGEL is capitalising on via wallet-share gains.
scores.quote: continue to benefit from the structural shift towards outsourcing in the Indian consumer global manufacturing

scores.rationale: Organic-only growth, still net cash (₹630cr at H1) and capex was voluntarily trimmed when demand turned, but working capital stress forced receivable discounting (~₹20cr extra finance cost) and elevated borrowing through the year.
scores.quote: To manage our cash flows, we had to get a lot of our receivables discounted, which led to an additional outflow of almost Rs.20 crores of financing costs.

scores.rationale: Management kept building through the downcycle — refrigerator plant, Sricity, ₹1,000cr Maharashtra land, POS entry — and repeatedly reaffirmed unchanged long-term priorities rather than retrenching.
scores.quote: our long-term investment, operational model and growth priorities remain unchanged

scores.rationale: Promoter-family management (Vishal/Vikas/Pramod Gupta, stable across FY21–FY26) presents in a plain operational register with no self-promotion, though the stock is well covered by Axis and JM Financial.
scores.quote: FY26 will now likely shape up to be a more measured year and that is fine.

scores.rationale: No discussion of talent development or leadership pipeline; the only workforce reference is reverse labour migration during the March LPG crisis.

Genuinely candid at the start of the year ('we got caught off guard', early guidance cut), but credibility eroded when they insisted on the guidance in February and then missed FY26 PAT badly (₹193.6cr vs ₹300–310cr guided), explained almost entirely by external shocks.
scores.quote: we are very sure of the numbers which we have guided you for

scores.rationale: Stripping the halo, FY25's strong results were substantially cycle-aided — one bad season collapsed EBITDA to ₹441.8cr from ₹519.2cr and PAT to ₹193.6cr from ₹290.9cr — though outgrowing a −15% industry is real, cycle-independent execution.
scores.quote: EBITDA stood at INR441.76 crores versus INR519.16 crores and profit after tax stood at INR193.61 crores versus INR290.92 crores last year.

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like hold on the customer's mind — brands cancelled 50–70% of planned orders across June–August at will and there is no aftermarket or service annuity.
scores.quote: they were cancelled to the tune of 50%-70% across most of the clients for the month of June, July and August

scores.rationale: Some stickiness exists via platform investment and anchor-customer wallet share, but switching costs are evidently weak given order cancellations and continuous OEM price renegotiation.
scores.quote: every OEM player are currently renegotiating their pricing

scores.rationale: The Indian RAC ODM space has several sizeable players and, decisively, the end customer (the brand) holds the negotiating power — PGEL absorbed inventory for clients and could not push through cost increases.
scores.quote: because of the kind of inventory what we have accumulated for our clients and those materials have not been taken by them

scores.rationale: Capacity is being added aggressively across the industry into a declining market, with margin-suppressing pricing behaviour across the whole value chain and admitted expectation of pricing pressure.
scores.quote: we believe that there might be some pressure on the pricing. That is why we have factored those things in our guidance.

scores.rationale: PGEL grew RAC 9% and washing machines 52% in a year the industry shrank ~15%, which necessarily means weaker competitors and in-house lines are donating volume to it.
scores.quote: For the full year, RAC revenue grew 9% year-on-year. The washing machine business grew phenomenally 52% on a full year basis.

scores.rationale: Far from under the radar — quarterly calls hosted by Axis Capital and JM Financial with buy-side participation, in a capital-magnet sector attracting large state-backed manufacturing incentives.
scores.quote: On behalf of JM Financial Institutional Securities, I welcome you all to the Q4 FY26 Earnings Call

scores.rationale: No image or taste premium whatsoever — this is contract manufacturing where gross margin fell ~250bps on input costs the company could not pass on, and demand proved highly unsteady.
scores.quote: Commodity inflation and currency depreciation resulted in estimated gross margin impact of approximately 250 basis points during the quarter, which we were not able to pass through.

scores.rationale: Management claims deepening trust with brand partners, but the assurance was materially breached in Q4 when LPG shortages and truck unavailability cost ~₹420cr of customer deliveries.
scores.quote: we lost production to the extent of approximately INR300 crores in -- due to the LPG crisis

scores.rationale: Multi-region plant footprint (Bhiwadi, Greater Noida, Supa, Rajasthan, Sricity) plus deep engagement across large and emerging brands gives genuine proximity and responsiveness to customers.
scores.quote: Client engagement across large and emerging brands remains strong.

scores.rationale: The customer base is correctly corporate (brands buying reliability and TCO) and PGEL is growing wallet share within anchor accounts, but the required lock-in is missing given mass order cancellation and annual price renegotiation.
scores.quote: We continue to gain wallet share within our anchor customers and deepen our trust with our brand partners

scores.rationale: Technology is largely sourced rather than owned — POS entry depends on a PAX Global agreement and the compressor venture is gated on Chinese government clearance; no R&D intensity or proprietary edge is claimed.
scores.quote: Regarding the POS machine, that agreement that we have entered into with the tax technologists and we are expecting to start some pilot production within the quarter 3 of FY '26

scores.rationale: Nothing in the four calls bears on two-sided or self-reinforcing network dynamics; the business model is bilateral contract manufacturing.
PGEL ships to brands rather than owning distribution, and its logistics were shown to be fragile when a truck shortage stranded ~₹120cr of finished goods at the plant.
scores.quote: The truck shortage, which resulted in an estimated sales loss of close to INR120 crores for the quarter as finished goods were stranded at our plant

scores.rationale: Real growth capex — INR110 cr Bangladesh expansion (INR66 cr committed) adding 6mn pieces, Bihar and Vietnam additions taking installed capacity to 101mn pieces, alongside 29% ROCE, though new units (Bihar, Guatemala) are still loss-making at ~INR13 cr a year.
scores.quote: Out of INR110 crores allocated, INR66 crores has already been committed

scores.rationale: As a B2B garment manufacturer, no advertising or promotion spend is discussed anywhere in the four calls.
No R&D spend, product-development pipeline or innovation metrics are mentioned in any of the four calls.
No acquisitions were announced or discussed in the last-12-month window; expansion was entirely greenfield capex.
No dividend, buyback or distribution policy is mentioned in the excerpts.
Asset-efficient with INR5,025 cr revenue on INR1,271 cr net worth, 33-day working capital and ROCE up 375bps to 29%, but the protecting moat in contract apparel manufacturing is thin.
scores.quote: Working capital days stood at 33 days... ROCE improved by 375 bps to 29%

scores.rationale: Clear share capture from a small base — Vietnam revenue +75% y/y while the country's garment exports de-grew, two major customers added in Dhaka, and brands consolidating volumes with PGIL as China sourcing migrates.
scores.quote: Vietnam as a country experienced a slight degrowth in its garment exports... Our operations have only become stronger

scores.rationale: Well-executed multi-country footprint (Vietnam, Indonesia, Bangladesh, Guatemala, Bihar) that demonstrably cushioned the India tariff shock, though Guatemala and Bihar are still loss-making and this is manufacturing-footprint rather than brand expansion.
scores.quote: Our strategy of geographical diversity has been working well for us

scores.rationale: Growth is explicitly attributed to higher realisation and value-added mix from Vietnam/Indonesia, but volume and utilisation gains (Vietnam 63%→80%+) also contribute and discounts were conceded to US clients during the tariff period.
scores.quote: driven by improved product mix and higher realization from our country of origin of Indonesia and Vietnam

scores.rationale: Positioned just past the trough of a tariff cycle — India duties fell from ~50% to 18% and then to a 10% Section 122 rate, with FTAs pending implementation and management guiding to renewed India growth from FY27.
scores.quote: we anticipate higher volumes, increased sourcing from India and renewed growth in our Indian operations from financial year '27 onwards

scores.rationale: The end market (apparel) is mature, but the China+1 sourcing migration and India's newly concluded FTAs with the US, EU, UK, Japan and Australia are a durable structural tailwind to PGIL's addressable pool.
scores.quote: We are seeing a lot of migration from China continue to happen both in Vietnam and Indonesia

scores.rationale: Entirely organic growth, no M&A, INR544 cr of cash and investments against a rising INR1,271 cr net worth, and capex continued through the tariff turmoil.
scores.quote: Cash and bank balance... INR416 crores with an additional INR128 crores investment in mutual fund and fixed deposit totaling to INR544 crores

scores.rationale: Early pre-emptive securing of Vietnam capacity paid off in a 75% growth quarter, and management reports being on track against a previously stated FY28 vision despite a year of tariff chaos.
scores.quote: we feel that we are solidly on track with our vision of FY '28 shared with all of you earlier

scores.rationale: Calls are run by the MD and CFO in a plain operational register — geography-by-geography updates, capacity and tariff mechanics, with no promotional or celebrity framing.
scores.quote: driven by our focused execution and the multi-location presence

scores.rationale: Only incidental references to ESOP expense and Bangladesh's 'experienced leadership' ecosystem; no evidence of a systematic internal talent pipeline either way.
scores.quote: skilled labor and a matured ecosystem of an experienced leadership

scores.rationale: Management quantifies its own problems — tariff cost of INR36 cr and INR13 cr of losses at Bihar and Guatemala are named explicitly, and India's tariff-period discounting is admitted — though the persistent 'adjusted EBITDA excluding' framing softens the reported number.
scores.quote: despite the discounts extended to the U.S. clients for the tariff... this particular move had a temporary impact on our margins

scores.rationale: Much of the FY26 outperformance traces to exogenous tariff arbitrage and China+1 relocation rather than demonstrable operating skill, so results should not be read as pure management quality; the offsetting evidence of skill is timely capacity pre-booking.
scores.quote: reflecting the success of the strategic decision and of us securing the capacities well in time

scores.rationale: Contract apparel manufacturing offers no monopoly-like position in the customer's mind and there is no aftermarket or services annuity — PGIL is one of many vendors on a brand's approved list.
scores.quote: we are broadening our client base even for India into the countries of Japan, Australia and the U.K.

scores.rationale: Switching costs are low — brands reallocate volumes across countries and vendors within a season, as PGIL itself does by pivoting US orders from India to Vietnam/Bangladesh/Guatemala.
scores.quote: Pearl Global plans to prioritize its other manufacturing hubs such as Vietnam, Bangladesh, Indonesia and Guatemala for fulfilling the U.S.A. orders

scores.rationale: Global garment manufacturing is highly fragmented while the customers are large US/EU retailers with strong negotiating power — demonstrated by PGIL absorbing tariff costs via discounts to keep relationships.
scores.quote: the discounts which we extended to U.S. clients during the tariff period to maintain the strong relationships

scores.rationale: Capital and skill barriers are modest across Bangladesh/Vietnam/Indonesia, and pricing is anything but rational — PGIL had to concede price to hold customers when tariffs rose.
scores.quote: Bangladesh continues to be a strong growth driver... competitive pricing

scores.rationale: China is a large, structurally retreating donor of share, and tariff-disadvantaged or duty-dependent rivals (Cambodia, single-country vendors) are visibly losing customers to diversified players.
scores.quote: customers have started visiting and are excited about this opportunity to diversify their sourcing into India more and from the overdependence on duty-free countries like Bangladesh and Cambodia

scores.rationale: The niche is unglamorous, but PGIL is a listed INR5,000 cr exporter running quarterly analyst calls in a sector under intense policy and capital attention — neither obscure nor spotlit.
scores.quote: India is currently at the center of geopolitical storm

scores.rationale: No image- or taste-driven pricing power at all — PGIL manufactures other companies' brands at ~9-10% EBITDA margins and had to discount when input costs (tariffs) rose.
scores.quote: Adjusted EBITDA margin stood at 9.3%

scores.rationale: Customers are buying reliability and de-risked, multi-country, compliant supply — top brands consolidated volumes with PGIL and it invests in sustainable/certified washing capacity.
scores.quote: Some of the most well-placed brands and the fastest-growing specialty brands of North America have consolidated their business with us

scores.rationale: Genuine convenience edge from nearshore Guatemala transit times and the ability to serve any market from a duty-advantaged origin, backed by long-standing direct customer relationships.
scores.quote: supported by the reduced transit time to the U.S.A. and only 10% reciprocal tariff

scores.rationale: Customers are corporate (global brands/retailers) and PGIL correctly sells reliability and landed cost rather than image, but the lock-in that should accompany a corporate relationship is weak given order shifting and tariff discounting.
scores.quote: deep customer relations and a solid order book

scores.rationale: No technology moat is evidenced — no R&D spend, proprietary process or product IP is discussed; the differentiators cited are location, tariff access and capacity.
scores.quote: sustainable laundry capacity expansion

scores.rationale: The business is a linear contract-manufacturing model with no two-sided network or self-reinforcing scale dynamic mentioned anywhere.
The five-country manufacturing and delivery footprint with duty-free access to every major market is a reach few peers can match and is the main reason customers concentrate volumes with PGIL.
scores.quote: India will have preferential access to all major global markets... Meanwhile, other manufacturing hubs of ours such as Bangladesh, Vietnam, Indonesia already benefit from this duty-free access

scores.rationale: Capex is overwhelmingly growth-oriented — ₹658cr in H1 FY26 on under-construction projects, office footprint expanded from ~2mn to ~4.8mn sq ft in two years, plus new malls at Kolkata and Surat pre-leasing well — with visible incremental returns (Mall of Asia rentals +33%).
scores.quote: Total capex (capital expenditure) for H1 FY26 was Rs. 658 crore, largely towards the construction of the various projects ongoing

scores.rationale: Marketing spend was cut 15% in Q3 FY26 yet footfalls, consumption and revenue-share income rose, showing high A&P efficiency via sponsored activations and hyper-local targeting, though spend is being optimised rather than built up.
scores.quote: the reduction of our retail marketing spend by 15% during Q3 FY26... we have proven that we can do more with less

scores.rationale: No R&D spend or programme is discussed anywhere in the four calls.

The ₹5,449cr ISMDPL buyout of CPP's 49% is large but simple and complementary — an asset platform the company itself seeded, already generating ₹617cr EBITDA, bought on a 36-month tranched structure that management says is accretive from year one; size and equity funding temper the score.
scores.quote: even if we choose to fund the entire first tranche through debt, the platform remains accretive to PML's earning

scores.rationale: The calls discuss capital deployment and funding (equity for the ISML buyout) but are silent on dividends, buybacks or any distribution policy.

This is a structurally asset-heavy business — ₹4,423cr FY26 revenue against a multi-million-sq-ft owned property base with ~₹1,300cr/yr of construction capex — so the moat is real but asset turn is inherently low.
scores.quote: we have now expanded to nearly 4.8 million sq. ft. today across four cities

scores.rationale: Consumption hit an all-time-high ₹16,587cr, up 21% with no new retail capacity added, and Phoenix is winning brand share as the preferred launch destination (South India's first Apple Store, largest Lego store, Onitsuka Tiger's first India concept store) — clear share capture with organised retail still a small slice of Indian retail.
scores.quote: Retail consumption reached an all-time high of Rs. 16,587 crore, growing 21% year-on-year... without adding any new retail capacity during the year

scores.rationale: Well-executed multi-city expansion across Mumbai, Pune, Bengaluru, Chennai, Indore, Ahmedabad, Lucknow and Bareilly, with new assets pre-leasing strongly in Kolkata (79%) and Surat (41%) before opening.
scores.quote: Phoenix Grand Victoria in Kolkata already at 79% leased and Phoenix Surat at 41% leased

scores.rationale: Growth is explicitly pricing- and mix-led — trading density up 23% at PMC Bangalore and 14% at PMC Pune on brand-mix premiumisation, 20%+ rental uplift on Palassio renewals, and 10-14% rental growth with zero area addition.
scores.quote: Phoenix Palassio entered its fifth year of operation, triggering a renewal cycle which enabled us to achieve over 20% rental growth across 120 renewal and new deals

scores.rationale: Mixed cyclical position — retail consumption is at an all-time high (late-cycle, not a trough) while offices are clearly coming off a cyclical bottom (occupancy 67%→83%) and hotels face a cautious macro backdrop.
scores.quote: our mature operational assets saw occupancy rise to 83%, up substantially from 67% at the start of the year

scores.rationale: End market is India's secular shift to organised, premium, experience-led retail — jewellery and electronics up over 30%, cinema 22%, with 36-50% of portfolio area repricing over 2-3 years and a pipeline visible to 2030.
scores.quote: jewellery and electronics grew by over 30%, reflecting both premiumization and healthy discretionary demand

scores.rationale: Net debt fell ₹500cr to ~₹2,200cr with net debt/EBITDA under 1x and cost of debt cut from 8.50% to 7.68%, and the large ISML buyout was funded primarily through equity and internal cash flows rather than levering up.
scores.quote: Net debt in fact declined by Rs. 500 crore in the H1 FY26... We have also reduced our average cost of debt from 8.50% to 7.68%

scores.rationale: Management pointed back to its 2020 QIP commitments and showed full delivery, and is now buying out its long-standing partner to control a 13-year, 1mn→13mn sq ft platform build-out to 2030 — long-horizon vision executed with tenacity.
scores.quote: a snippet of our 2020 QIP deck where we had promised three malls, two offices and one hotel... I am pleased to announce that we have delivered all of these assets in totality

scores.rationale: Calls are workmanlike and metric-driven with the MD routinely handing the substance to the CEO-Malls, CFO and Group President rather than centring himself, though the group is a widely-covered listed name with a marquee global partner.
scores.quote: I will now hand the call over to Ms. Rashmi Sen to take you through the performance of our retail portfolio in greater detail

scores.rationale: Evidence of internal promotion and pipeline-building — Rashmi Sen elevated after 15+ years in-house and explicitly mentoring successors, plus stated focus on leadership depth — tempered by notable churn in the MD/CFO ranks over the five-year history.
scores.quote: she continues to champion growth, operational excellence and strong brand partnerships while mentoring the next generation of retail leaders

scores.rationale: Management proactively explained the uncomfortable gap between 21% consumption growth and 10-14% rental growth with three specific structural reasons, and flagged closure-related drags and hotel softness rather than glossing over them.
scores.quote: The gap versus consumption growth reflects three factors: (i) Our MG plus revenue share lease structure... (ii) Newer assets... still in their ramp-up phase... (iii) Seasonal consumption growth in Q4 was driven by categories... that carry structurally lower revenue share ratios

scores.rationale: The results survive a halo check because they are traceable to specific operating actions rather than a rising tide — like-for-like growth with no area added, measurable trading-density uplift from churn, and disclosed drags — though rental conversion still lags and equity funding dilutes the headline accretion.
scores.quote: in the first nine months of FY26, we have already approached that level; despite no new mall additions and with large parts of flagship Phoenix Market City centers under repositioning

scores.rationale: Phoenix's flagship centres occupy a monopoly-like position in the retailer's mind as the default launch venue in their cities, evidenced by first-in-region flagships and 400 new store openings in one year.
scores.quote: Phoenix Mall of Asia, in particular has emerged as a preferred launch destination with notable openings including South India's first Apple Store

scores.rationale: Each asset is effectively a regional monopoly in its catchment with high tenant switching costs — retailers churning out lose the catchment, and Phoenix reprices at will (20%+ on renewal) with 36-50% of area resetting over 2-3 years.
scores.quote: With 36-50% of our portfolio area coming up for renewal over the next 2-3 years, the conversion of consumption growth into rental growth has a clear and near-term catalyst

scores.rationale: Premium mall ownership in India sits with a handful of players and tenants show little negotiating power — Phoenix raised rentals 10-14% and reset renewals 20%+ while adding no capacity — but the calls give no direct competitive-structure disclosure.
scores.quote: Retail rental income for the year grew to Rs. 2,157 crore, up 10% year-on-year, without any area addition in the portfolio during the year

scores.rationale: Entry requires scarce urban land and multi-thousand-crore multi-year capital, and pricing behaviour is rational — rentals and EBITDA held flat even as Q4 consumption moderated sequentially, with no sign of discounting to fill space.
scores.quote: Even as Q4 consumption moderated sequentially, retail rentals remained largely stable and retail EBITDA was essentially flat quarter-on-quarter

scores.rationale: Weaker retail formats are implicitly donating share as marquee global brands consolidate into Phoenix — 920 deals over 3.2mn sq ft and 400 store openings in a single year — but no competitor weakness is named directly.
scores.quote: During FY26, we completed approximately 920 deals covering 3.2 million sq. ft. We opened over 400 new stores across the portfolio

scores.rationale: The opposite of under-the-radar — a widely covered listed platform with a global pension partner, a ₹5,449cr headline transaction, CCI and shareholder approvals, and quarterly analyst calls.
scores.quote: The agreed consideration for the proposed transaction is Rs. 5,449 crores payable to CPP Investments over a 36-month period

scores.rationale: Luxury/premium positioning delivers real pricing power and very high margins — group EBITDA of ₹2,637cr on ₹4,423cr revenue (~60%) and hotel margins above 43% — with demand steady enough to grow 21% on an already high base.
scores.quote: consolidated revenue of Rs. 4,423 crore and EBITDA of Rs. 2,637 crore, up 16% and 22% respectively

scores.rationale: Retailers buy assured footfall and catchment certainty rather than cheap rent — the MG-plus-revenue-share structure sells downside protection to Phoenix and predictable traffic to tenants — and brands cite trust in the platform.
scores.quote: This broad-reach strength highlights resilient consumer demand and the trust that leading brands place in Phoenix as their preferred retail partner

scores.rationale: The integrated shop-work-live-unwind campus model plus a strong in-house leasing machine (920 deals, 2.2mn sq ft of office gross leasing in FY26) gives unmatched accessibility for consumers and direct intimacy with tenants.
scores.quote: At Phoenix, we are creating integrated destinations where people choose to shop, work, live and unwind

scores.rationale: The benefit match is well aligned to both customer types — experiential/intangible pull for retail consumers (Gourmet Village, Racquet Club) and long-lease switching-cost lock-in plus amenity-rich TCO for corporate occupiers.
scores.quote: Each office asset is integrated within our destination retail-led campuses, offering occupiers access to a differentiated, amenity-rich environment

scores.rationale: The calls contain no evidence of a technology advantage; sustainability and LEED certification are operating-cost measures, not a tech moat, and nothing is said either way about proprietary technology.

A genuine two-sided flywheel is visible — marquee brand additions pull footfall, which pulls further brands and drives dwell time and repeat visits — quantified by Mall of Asia's 112% consumption jump and the Gourmet Village halo on same-store sales.
scores.quote: increasing repeat visits, lengthening dwell times and boosting same-store sales growth across the center

scores.rationale: For premium brands, Phoenix effectively is the distribution network in India's top cities — a physical reach across eight-plus cities that rivals cannot replicate, which is why flagship launches route through it.
scores.quote: These launches have further strengthened the positioning of our malls as the preferred destination for leading global and domestic brands

scores.rationale: Large completed growth capex — Indri ENA/ethanol 78→220 KLPD, malt 12→30 KLPD and a 200 KLPD greenfield Chhattisgarh plant — already earning ~31.5% Alco-Bev EBITDA margins with only INR25-30 crores maintenance capex needed in FY27.
scores.quote: Our total distillery capacity now stands at a robust 450 KLPD, comprising of 30 KLPD of malt and 420 KLPD of ENA and ethanol

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotion spend, its quantum, or its return in the call.

No formal R&D line, but a demonstrated product-development engine — years of experimentation before Indri, then Camikara, Cashmir and revamped Whistler, with a further premium/luxury pipeline for FY27.
scores.quote: after years of experimentation, consumer feedback, and refinement, Piccadily Agro launched its own IMFL brand in 2022

scores.rationale: Only an open-ended exploration of brand-side acquisitions in India or abroad with no identified target and no completed deal to judge post-deal margins, though management says it will not buy for the sake of buying.
scores.quote: there is nothing in particular we have it in mind, but anything which could add strategic depth to our portfolio either in India or international will fit into our scheme of things

scores.rationale: No mention of dividends, buybacks or any distribution policy in the call.

The model is structurally asset- and working-capital-heavy — 450 KLPD of distillery assets, 85,000 maturing barrels going to 1 lakh, INR100 crores added malt inventory and ~80-90 day DSO funding a 132% jump in short-term borrowings.
scores.quote: we have increased our malt also, malt inventory also about INR100 crores. So that's also added to the working capital

scores.rationale: Small base with long runway (top-15 global single malt aspiring to top-5) and share gains in a premium segment growing 14-15%, but FY26 Indri growth of only ~16% on supply constraints shows capture was capped.
scores.quote: currently with Indri we are a top 15 brand in the world in single malts. In a year or two, we'll be in top 10

scores.rationale: Executed expansion to 29 states/UTs, CSD, 29 international markets and 30 duty-free outlets with exports already ~25% of IMFL and land plus licences secured for a Scotland distillery.
scores.quote: We are now present across 29 states and union territories in India, the CSD network, and 29 international markets in 30 duty free outlets

scores.rationale: The portfolio is premium/luxury with 45-50% IMFL EBITDA margins, but management explicitly guided that value and volume growth will be broadly the same, so growth is not pricing- or mix-led.
scores.quote: our value growth and volume growth more or less would be similar because we don't do any mass products

scores.rationale: The only cyclical exposure — sugar, whose EBITDA margin fell from 11% to 2% — is being demerged rather than played as a cycle-bottom bet, and the Alco-Bev business is not cyclical.
scores.quote: sugar margins drop, which was 11% EBITDA margin last year and last year same quarter and 2% this year quarter

scores.rationale: Premium Indian spirits is in secular expansion, with the premium segment growing 14-15% on demographic and income tailwinds that management identified over a decade ago and has been proven right on.
scores.quote: broadly speaking about the growth in premium segment is about 14% to 15%

scores.rationale: Organic focus with a simplifying demerger of sugar and only INR25-30 crores FY27 capex, tempered by a 132% jump in short-term borrowings and open-ended acquisition exploration.
scores.quote: intent is very clear that we want to be a global Alco-Bev company. We want to pool our human and capital resources just for the Alco-Bev business

scores.rationale: A multi-decade, patiently executed arc — malt plant and barrel procurement from 2010, own brand only in 2022, and a stated 3-5 year ambition to be a top-5 global single malt.
scores.quote: In 2010, it further expanded by installing a 12 KLPD malt plant at the same location and began procuring barrels for maturation

scores.rationale: Operationally low-key and refusing brand-level disclosure, but the commentary leans on superlatives and global-ranking aspirations rather than substance-only framing.
scores.quote: which is the fastest growth by any listed Alco-Bev company

scores.rationale: A professional leadership bench is in place (CFO, President Operations, CEO IMFL, President Sales) and the HORECA team was recalibrated, but no evidence of systematic talent development or an internal pipeline.
scores.quote: we have recalibrated a team on HORECA, so there will be a bigger focus on HORECA too

scores.rationale: Candid on sugar drag, supply constraints and the auditor change, but repeatedly refused brand-level volumes, deflected the direct question on Indri's 16% growth, and redirected margin questions from percentage to absolute value.
scores.quote: these kind of a breakup we don't come up in the forums. That's a matter of internal dimension

scores.rationale: Strong FY26 numbers rest heavily on newly commissioned capacity and a booming category rather than demonstrated skill, and the 60-70% FY27 guidance is unproven against a flagship that grew only ~16% last year.
scores.quote: we expect coming financial year FY '27 as an exceptional year for us. It's going to be exceptional year where the company is looking to grow at 60% to 70%

scores.rationale: Indri owns a distinctive terroir-based identity in the consumer's mind as India's flagship single malt, though rivals are now entering the same INR4,000-5,000 price point.
scores.quote: shaped in part by Indri’s unique climate with temperatures ranging from zero degrees to fifty degrees Celsius, which imparts distinct flavors

scores.rationale: State excise licensing and CSD/paramilitary listings (30% of IMFL) give some regional protection, but consumer spirits carry essentially no switching costs and no captive aftermarket.
scores.quote: our CSD and paramilitary is about 30% of our portfolio

scores.rationale: The Indian single malt space is opening up rather than consolidating, with new players entering the company's exact price band.
scores.quote: some of the other players have also entered in our price point of INR4,000 to INR5,000 range from a single malt perspective

scores.rationale: Real barriers exist — licences, maturation time and an 85,000-barrel aged inventory — and pricing is rational with no discount war, but new entrants are arriving at the same price point.
scores.quote: Currently we are holding about 85,000 barrel filled

scores.rationale: No discussion of weak competitors losing share; competition is described only as new and category-expanding.
Far from under the radar — institutional coverage from Alchemy, Kotak, Dolat and others on the call, with explicit global-brand ambitions.
scores.quote: we also aspire to be a global brand, just not a domestic brand

scores.rationale: Brand and provenance-driven pricing power shows up directly in margins — ~45-50% IMFL EBITDA and 31.5% Alco-Bev EBITDA against robust demand.
scores.quote: our IMFL EBITDA margins are quite high as we deal into premium products. So our EBITDA margins are much higher than the industry, so around 45% to 50%

scores.rationale: No discussion of customers buying reliability or certainty; the proposition described is taste, image and premium positioning.
Broad and deepening reach — presence in most A-category outlets across operating states plus a rebuilt HORECA push and width-and-depth distribution strategy.
scores.quote: most of the A-category outlets in the states we are operating we are available

scores.rationale: Correct match of benefit to customer — image/taste intangibles sold to retail consumers, complemented by institutional CSD/paramilitary (30%) and export channels.
scores.quote: About 25% or so is export

scores.rationale: The advantage is climate, maturation time and blending craft, not technology; there is no R&D intensity or multi-product technical edge described.
scores.quote: This region's raw and climate conditions became a key advantage

scores.rationale: A branded spirits business with no two-sided network described or plausibly present; scale brings capacity, not self-reinforcing user value.
A genuinely wide multi-channel footprint (29 states, CSD, 29 export markets, duty free) that is a real asset, though not yet a reach global majors cannot match.
scores.quote: Both in terms of WOD, Width Of Distribution, and in terms of depth

scores.rationale: Capex rose year-on-year and is explicitly directed at capacity plus new GTM initiatives while EBITDA grew 31% in Q4 and consolidated margins expanded 120bps for FY26, implying healthy incremental returns, though no project-level ROIC disclosure.
scores.quote: we continue to invest behind capacity as well as other initiatives. So our capex in the year also was higher than what we had spent in the previous year

scores.rationale: A&SP was stepped up hard (up ~80% YoY in Q2, +150-160bps of sales, held to a disciplined 3-5% corridor) using gross-margin tailwinds, and coincided with Consumer & Bazaar UVG accelerating from 9.3% to 15.4%.
scores.quote: advertising and sales promotion, which in absolute terms was nearly 80% higher than second quarter last year

scores.rationale: The calls never quantify R&D spend or output; when asked about investment behind new product launches management answered in terms of A&SP and go-to-market, leaving R&D efficiency genuinely unevidenced.

No acquisitions in the window; instead a disciplined exit — BuildNext was swapped into JSW One for an admittedly insignificant stake, showing willingness to hand a sub-scale venture to a better owner rather than empire-build.
scores.quote: Our shareholding in JSW will be quite insignificant... we felt that the business is best served with an owner like JSW

scores.rationale: A coherent, generous policy — special interim dividend of INR10, a 1:1 bonus after 15 years, final dividend of INR11.5 taking payout to ~70% — but distribution is entirely dividends, with no valuation-disciplined buyback to judge.
scores.quote: including the special dividend, the payout ratio will be around 70%

scores.rationale: Asset turnover is never discussed; only qualitative comments on cash and working capital appear, which is insufficient to judge asset-light economics from these excerpts.

Management claims growth well ahead of category in tile adhesives with leadership already in retail and closing on overall leadership, plus a full portfolio build and a low-penetration category leaving long runway.
scores.quote: We are already leaders in tile adhesive when it comes to retail business... our endeavour is to be actually growing much, much faster than the market

scores.rationale: International subsidiaries grew only 4.5-8% and exports fell 13.5% in Q3 on tariffs and Gulf supply-chain disruption; EU market development is credible but explicitly a next-fiscal story, so expansion is neither well-executed nor failing.
scores.quote: our exports in totality declined by 13.5%

scores.rationale: Growth is almost purely volume-led — Q4 value growth of 15.3% against UVG of 15.3% and Q2 value 10.4% vs UVG 10.3% — so pricing/mix contributed essentially nothing despite premiumization talk.
scores.quote: revenue at INR 3,272 crores grew by 15.3% in value terms and was underpinned by underlying volume growth of 15.3%

scores.rationale: Management sees an urban demand upturn beginning (after ~16-20 quarters of rural outperformance) aided by GST 2.0 and tax cuts, with benign VAM at $830 vs $980 — consistent with being early in a recovery rather than late.
scores.quote: I definitely believe that in the quarter that is gone by... there has been a buoyancy in urban demand

scores.rationale: End markets are structurally under-penetrated — only one in four Indians use tiles, tiles are moving to more sophisticated formats needing adhesives, and construction plus rural penetration is a multi-year runway.
scores.quote: one in four people only use tiles... the objective... is to grow the category and to grow it exponentially

scores.rationale: Wholly organic growth, no large M&A, non-core BuildNext divested, treasury surplus rather than leverage, and gross-margin windfalls deliberately reinvested into A&SP and GTM instead of being banked.
scores.quote: would we be deploying the expansion, if at all, in gross margin for investments? The answer is yes

scores.rationale: Evidence of long-horizon category-building — a full pyramid portfolio in tile adhesives, a new architect/interior-designer GTM, Pidilite Professional Solutions — and a publicly held 20-24% EBITDA corridor rather than chasing short-term margin.
scores.quote: We stay committed to our corridor of 20% to 24%

scores.rationale: Communication is professional and substance-heavy, but this is a widely-covered large cap whose MD does same-day media rounds, so it is neither celebrity-driven nor genuinely under the radar.
scores.quote: I said this in the morning in media interactions also

scores.rationale: Internal progression exists (Kavinder Singh moving JMD to MD/Chairman), but the five-year history shows repeated churn at MD, Chairman and CFO level, and the calls offer no evidence of a systematic talent-development engine.

Consistently specific and self-disclosing — quantifying the INR47cr wage-code one-off, the 13.5% export decline, Nina waterproofing down 16%, weakness in Kerala, and a competitor's stronghold in Hyderabad — rather than burying negatives.
scores.quote: a onetime charge of INR47 crores in stand-alone... Nina waterproofing business would have declined by 16%

scores.rationale: Results survive a skeptical read because management itself separates tailwinds from execution — VAM fell from $980 to $830 and they disclose exactly how much margin was spent back — though the strong Q4 leans on a benign input cycle and easy urban base.
scores.quote: VAM consumption in the quarter was at about $830 as compared to $884 in the same period last year

scores.rationale: Brand-level ownership of the customer's mind is evident (Roff leadership in retail tile adhesive, mass-media Roff tile cleaner, category defined by the company), but the calls show real competition rather than a true monopoly position.
scores.quote: now we are inching towards leadership overall in the country

scores.rationale: The category shows entrenched regional strongholds where incumbency has held for two decades — management's own framing of Hyderabad as their competitor's 'gadh' cuts both ways and implies durable local lock-in elsewhere for Pidilite.
scores.quote: Hyderabad tends to be the bastion or the 'gadh' of our competitor who started the business there

scores.rationale: Structure is not a stable oligopoly — legacy paint majors have entered tile adhesives and competitive intensity is called out in Gujarat, Hyderabad and Kerala — though Pidilite still retains a price premium.
scores.quote: Competitive intensity in some parts of these states does remain

scores.rationale: New entrants have arrived (paint players entering tile adhesive) which argues against high barriers, but pricing remains rational with Pidilite holding a premium even at the base of the pyramid rather than discounting to defend.
scores.quote: at the very bottom, we continue to enjoy a marginal premium over our competitors

scores.rationale: Share is being taken from cement-based/unorganised alternatives and from a competitor on its home turf, giving identifiable donators, though the newer entrants are strong paint majors rather than weak players.
scores.quote: if you were to ask the other side, you will perhaps see that there is a lot of heat on from our side there

scores.rationale: This is a heavily-covered large cap — calls hosted by Kotak, Equirus and ICICI with sell-side regulars — the opposite of a niche capital and competitors ignore.

Brand strength supports a premium and steady demand with gross margins improving 100-200bps and a 20-24% EBITDA corridor, but realised pricing was near zero this year, so pricing power was not actually exercised.
scores.quote: Our gross margins at a stand-alone level improved by about 200 basis points

scores.rationale: Demand is driven by reliability of bonded outcomes — thinner, vitrified and vertical/exterior tiles requiring 'more sophisticated solutions' — where failure cost dwarfs product price, letting Roff sell at ~2x cement cost.
scores.quote: Tiles are getting thinner, vitreous, also on vertical surfaces... So, you need more sophisticated solutions

scores.rationale: Deep customer intimacy is evident in district-, town- and dealer-level management plus new influencer-facing GTM for architects and interior designers and expanding e-commerce/quick-commerce presence.
scores.quote: we keep looking granularly at state by state sometimes, many times at districts and even town level and find solutions right up to that and sometimes even at dealer level

scores.rationale: The benefit type is well matched by segment — brand and mass media for retail Consumer & Bazaar (UVG 15.4%) versus specification-led Pidilite Professional Solutions and project sales for B2B (UVG 14.8%) — though B2B exposure to exports proved fragile.
scores.quote: Consumer and Bazaar was 15.4% and B2B was 14.8%

scores.rationale: There is a broad formulation portfolio spanning the full price pyramid into sophisticated adhesives, but the calls give no R&D intensity figures or evidence of a defensible multi-product technology lead.
scores.quote: We have almost a complete portfolio right up to the top

scores.rationale: No two-sided network is described; the only marketplace discussion concerns third-party platforms like JSW One and Birla Pivot, not a Pidilite network.

Reach is the standout asset — rural outgrowing urban for 16-20 consecutive quarters on penetration, dealer-level granularity, and new channels layered on (architect/ID programme, projects, quick commerce) — a footprint entrants cannot replicate quickly.
scores.quote: rural still continues to do better than urban. So this has been a trend now over 5 years, if I'm not mistaken, maybe 16 to 20 quarters

scores.rationale: Committed Rs. 700–800 crore of investment for the year directed at new growth platforms (pharma CRDMO assets, biologicals research centre, electronic chemicals), but incremental returns are unproven with revenue down 12% and the money going into loss-making/sub-scale verticals.
scores.quote: based on our growth expectations, we shall continue to invest about Rs. 700 crore to Rs. 800 crore during the year

scores.rationale: Brand-building spend shows up mainly as domestic new-brand launches and a direct-to-farmer engagement platform rather than disclosed A&P outlay, so the effect on brand equity is suggestive but unquantified.
scores.quote: We have launched our direct to farmer mobile app, 'PI Mitra Kisan', a one-stop farmer engagement solution offering crop advisory, product guidance and loyalty benefits

scores.rationale: R&D is visibly converting into commercial output — 5 new molecules commercialised in FY26 with new products now 18% of AgChem exports, 4 domestic launches, 20+ pipeline products, and India's first in-house NCE filed for registration.
scores.quote: New products now contributing 18% of AgChem Exports highlights our focused derisking strategy and innovation led approach

scores.rationale: The Plant Health Care deal is a small, complementary bolt-on that gave the biologicals platform global access and peptide/Harpin technology, but it remains investment-stage with no evidence yet of post-deal margin accretion.
scores.quote: Our acquisition of a differentiated technology platforms has given us global market access and advanced R&D capabilities

scores.rationale: The calls discuss the Rs. 34 bn net cash only as a source of strategic investment capacity; no buyback, dividend policy or distribution philosophy is mentioned.
scores.quote: cash balance of INR 34,265 million enabling the company to pursue future strategic investments

scores.rationale: This is an asset-heavy multi-site manufacturer adding capacity into a revenue decline, with trade working capital stuck at 139 days of sales — the opposite of an asset-light high-turn profile.
scores.quote: We have sustained our Trade working capital in terms of days of sales at 139 days despite of volatile market scenario

scores.rationale: No evidence of share capture in the window — exports fell on volume in line with the industry and domestic declined on lower demand in PI's key crops — though the 18% new-product contribution and new client additions suggest positional gains within CSM.
scores.quote: Decline in AgChem Exports is primarily driven by lower volumes reflecting the broader global industry contraction

scores.rationale: Deliberate multi-geography build-out with BD teams in the US and Europe, an India–Italy pharma operating model, and biologicals registrations/market development across US, Brazil, Mexico and Europe — credible but still spending ahead of revenue.
scores.quote: We continue to allocate capital towards product innovation, market development and strategic partnerships in the region, including the U.S., Brazil and Europe, Mexico and India

scores.rationale: Mix is doing real work — gross margin expanded to 58–59% on favourable product mix — but pricing is outright negative across both export generics and domestic, so growth is not pricing-led.
scores.quote: product pricing continues to remain soft, particularly for the generic category

scores.rationale: Management places the industry in the late phase of a multi-year downcycle with channel inventories normalising and delivered the guided Q4 sequential uptick, but the recovery date has slipped repeatedly across the four calls and the Middle East conflict added fresh disruption.
scores.quote: we believe the sector is transitioning out of downcycle

scores.rationale: Underlying drivers (food demand, shrinking arable land, resistance management, climate-driven biologicals demand, CRDMO outsourcing) are secular, but the core crop-protection market itself has been contracting for over two years.
scores.quote: the demand for biologicals for integrated crop health management is growing faster because of the challenges posed by climate change

scores.rationale: Debt-free with Rs. 34 bn net cash, one small bolt-on rather than big M&A, and continued counter-cyclical investment in R&D and capacity right through the downcycle while holding 25% EBITDA margin.
scores.quote: Our strong Debt free balance sheet supported with net cash of Rs 34 Bn provides resilience and flexibility for strategic investments

scores.rationale: A decade-long in-house discovery programme has produced India's first NCE now nearing market, and biologicals has been pursued for two decades — long-horizon bets sustained through a brutal cycle.
scores.quote: Our first NCE, Pioxaniliprole, discovered in India is now coming soon to the markets demonstrating our ability to invent at a global scale

scores.rationale: Calls are led by operating detail with vertical CEOs rather than personality, though there is some self-promotional framing around ESG rankings and the 'next orbit' narrative.
scores.quote: PI has improved its S&P Global Corporate Sustainability ranking at 98% percentile

scores.rationale: A deep bench of named vertical CEOs exists and the JMD's exit was handled with an internal continuity plan, but the leadership appears largely externally recruited and the 5-year history shows repeated MD/CFO turnover.
scores.quote: He has stepped down from his executive responsibilities, including IR, to focus on his health, while continuing to be associated with PI as a Non-Executive Director

scores.rationale: Management pre-flagged the H2-weighted plan and named specific negatives — regulatory disruption in biologicals, crop damage, PI-specific crop exposure — but softened repeated recovery-timeline misses rather than owning them squarely.
scores.quote: lower crop acreages impacting key crops for PI

scores.rationale: Judged on skill rather than headline results: revenue fell yet the committed 25% EBITDA margin and guided Q4 sequential growth were both delivered, which is process discipline visible independent of a bad cycle.
scores.quote: at EBITDA level, we delivered what we committed at the start of the year a resilient margin of 25% for full year

scores.rationale: In CSM, PI is typically the exclusive contracted manufacturer of an innovator's patented molecule, a monopoly-like position per molecule, though it is contract-dependent rather than owned.
scores.quote: global companies continue to elevate their strategic partnerships across the value chain in the pursuit of cost optimization

scores.rationale: Switching costs are real — process technology, plant qualification and registrations lock innovators in — but customer delivery schedules dictated PI's volumes all year, showing the lock-in does not confer volume control.
scores.quote: Agchem exports moderated in line with the overall demand softening, inventory levels of many key products and resulting customer supply schedules

scores.rationale: Chinese overcapacity has fragmented supply and caused value erosion, while the end customers are a handful of global innovators with strong negotiating power over volumes and price.
scores.quote: sharp price deflation from Chinese overcapacity

scores.rationale: Pricing in the industry is plainly irrational with excess Chinese capacity driving value erosion in generics; PI's own barrier rests on patented-molecule contracts, not on industry-wide entry barriers.
scores.quote: This demand softness has been coupled with excess capacity in China, causing value erosion, particularly in the generic products

scores.rationale: The China Plus One shift by global innovators creates identifiable weak/disfavoured competitors from whom PI can take contracted volumes, and domestic regulatory transitions have disrupted smaller biologicals players.
scores.quote: a secular trend on global innovators pushing the China Plus One strategy

scores.rationale: PI is a large, well-covered listed company actively courting visibility through global ESG rankings and its NCE narrative — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: we are pleased to inform that PI has featured in the S&P Global Sustainability yearbook

scores.rationale: Gross margin near 58–59% is high, but it comes from mix and operational efficiency rather than image-driven pricing power, and realisations were falling all year.
scores.quote: our gross margin expanded to 59% during the quarter, supported by a favorable product mix

scores.rationale: CSM customers explicitly buy trust, IP security and execution reliability, and management frames the winning proposition in exactly those terms rather than price.
scores.quote: Innovators and integrated R&D-led manufacturers with proven trust, scale and execution will be the long-term winners

scores.rationale: Domestic side is investing in reach and direct grower intimacy through a technology-augmented distribution model and a direct-to-farmer app, though no evidence it is superior to Indian peers' feet-on-street networks.
scores.quote: We are investing in technology-based augmentation in our distribution business in order to drive customer centricity and efficiency

scores.rationale: The benefit match is sensible on both sides — reliability and switching-cost lock-in for corporate innovator customers in CSM/CRDMO, and brand plus advisory engagement for retail farmers domestically.
scores.quote: deepening relationship with the biotech and the big pharma innovators

scores.rationale: Multi-platform technical depth is evidenced by flow chemistry and biotech process capability, a proprietary peptide/Harpin biologicals platform, an integrated single-site research centre at Udaipur, and the first NCE discovered in India.
scores.quote: The teams are developing technology platforms that are giving opportunities across new vertical such as, biologicals, specialty chemicals and electronic chemicals

scores.rationale: Nothing in the four calls describes a two-sided or self-reinforcing network; the business model is bilateral contract manufacturing and product sales.

Distribution reach is being genuinely extended — Indian retail network plus global biologicals market access acquired through Plant Health Care and BD presence in US/Europe — but it is not shown to be unmatchable by rivals.
scores.quote: In India, we are well on our way to becoming one of the largest biological products companies, both in terms of product portfolio and revenue

scores.rationale: Management repeatedly cites heavy growth investment — scaling to ~2 million touch points, funding international entry, and building new platforms — alongside a 500bps adjusted-EBITDA margin improvement and positive FY26 operating cash flow, suggesting the spend is growth-oriented rather than maintenance, though incremental ROIC is not disclosed.
scores.quote: We continue to invest heavily to take our products into global markets
