scores.rationale: Clear growth (not maintenance) capex — ~70 new centres a year with an INR200 crore outlay plus INR400 crore into the K-12 school company — and centre-level economics reaching 13-15% EBITDA by year three, though returns take three years and new verticals are still pre-profit.
scores.quote: We are looking at 70 centers next year with an outlay of INR200 crores... In the third year of operations, anywhere between ~13%-15% EBITDA margin

scores.rationale: The free-YouTube 'zero CAC' funnel builds brand equity and fills the paid funnel while marketing spend actually fell INR20 crores in the quarter with further leverage expected.
scores.quote: we call it as a zero CAC model... Our marketing spends dropped by almost like INR20 crores in this quarter

scores.rationale: Sustained AI/tech investment (Aryabhata, Ask AI, PW Talks) with tech-and-product pod costs up 40% yet total tech spend leveraging on scale, but the product payoff is asserted rather than yet quantified.
scores.quote: our AI pod cost of the tech and product team going up by 40% from last year

scores.rationale: Bolt-ons are small, category- or geography-complementary and post-deal economics improved materially — Sarrthi doubled revenue at 68% EBITDA margin, Utkarsh swung from negative to 6% pre-Ind AS EBITDA, Xylem went from INR90 crore to INR330-340 crore.
scores.quote: Utkarsh Classes... reported 6% pre-Ind AS EBITDA against a negative for last year... in Xylem... When we bought the acquisition, I think they were INR90 crores in top line

scores.rationale: No buyback, dividend or distribution policy is mentioned in either call; the INR5,000 crore treasury is discussed only in terms of reinvestment.
The majority-and-rising online business (51% of revenue, growing 38%) is asset-light with a community moat, but ~46% of revenue sits in offline centres requiring ~INR2.5 crore of capex each.
scores.quote: our online segment grew at, now contributes almost like 51% and grew at 38% year-over-year... A center starts with an investment of ~INR2.5 crores

scores.rationale: Explicit long runway with under 2% share of the addressable student base, alongside demonstrated capture — Hindi-heartland share gains and UPSC market leadership after Sarrthi.
scores.quote: of those ~25 crores kids, we are having less than ~2% market share... we have taken a good market share in Hindi heartland

scores.rationale: Well-executed domestic expansion into the South via Xylem (13 new centres) and five regional languages with 94,000 paid vernacular students, but this is intra-India replication, not a premium brand travelling across borders.
scores.quote: We've started batches in five regional languages and enrolled 94,000 paid students in the first nine months

scores.rationale: Growth is overwhelmingly volume/enrolment-led by design — online ACPU rose only ~8% against 30%+ revenue growth, and management explicitly refuses to price up to protect the affordability mission.
scores.quote: We have increased our online ACPUs by just ~8%. Still, we have delivered a growth of more than ~30%

scores.rationale: Management discusses only intra-year seasonality of quarters, not any macro cycle position, so there is no evidence of being near a cyclical bottom.
End markets are in secular expansion — a 6 crore-student test-prep TAM compounding at 13-15%, a K-12 market four times larger, and rising smartphone/internet penetration opening new student cohorts.
scores.quote: the TAM is of 6 crores children at this point of time which is growing at a 13%-15% CAGR. But this K-12 market is like four times bigger

scores.rationale: Net-cash balance sheet with INR5,000 crore treasury and INR600 crore operating cash flow, disciplined centre-level rental/utilisation thresholds and stated caution on cultural fit in M&A — tempered by simultaneous entry into K-12 schools, state boards, vernacular and AI at once.
scores.quote: For any new center signing, the rental should be below a critical threshold... it is very important that there is cultural alignment, strategic alignment

scores.rationale: Management frames decisions on a five-to-ten-year horizon — fixing schooling 'at the root', K-12 EBITDA only by FY29-30, centre openings compounding for a decade — and has stuck to the free-content model since 2016 despite listing pressure.
scores.quote: the entire coaching is an outcome of bad schooling in the country, we want to fix it at the root... this will become a significant EBITDA... by FY '29-'30

scores.rationale: The business is deliberately built around a celebrity founder-teacher's personal following across 250 YouTube channels, and the calls carry promotional flourishes ('stellar listing', 'we find ourselves significantly ahead') rather than low-profile understatement.
scores.quote: Physicswallah started as a YouTube channel back in 2016 by Alakh Sir. And until 2020 it became India's largest YouTube channel

scores.rationale: Wide ESOP issuance (INR125 crore charge for nine months vs INR73 crore), deliberate AI-talent hiring and an entrepreneurial internal culture are cited, but no explicit succession or leadership-pipeline system is described.
scores.quote: our ESOP expenses now are at INR125 crores for nine months against the 73 for last year

scores.rationale: Disclosure is granular and unflattering where needed — centre-level year-one -6% EBITDA, peak offline losses from the 170-centre build, and a called-out INR23 crore one-time hit — though as a newly listed firm there is no record yet of owning a real mistake.
scores.quote: minus ~6% EBITDA is contributed by a typical offline learning VidyaPeeth NEET JEE center... because of offline, the contribution of losses has gone to the peak

scores.rationale: The assessment is vulnerable to halo — a charismatic founder, a maiden post-IPO call opening with congratulations, and self-declared leadership in AI and UPSC, with only two quarters of listed delivery against promises to verify skill versus momentum.
scores.quote: We find ourselves significantly ahead of the AI initiatives at PW

scores.rationale: Strong mind-share position — India's largest education YouTube presence, 3.4 million daily active users engaging 106 minutes a day, and claimed UPSC category leadership — but this is brand affinity in a contested category rather than a true aftermarket lock.
scores.quote: Currently having 3.4 million daily active users on our mobile app and getting engaged for 106 minutes on a daily average basis

scores.rationale: There is local leadership logic (centres opened only where PW is already number one online) but coaching students face negligible switching costs and no captive aftermarket is described.
scores.quote: wherever we became number one in terms of number of students, we start our offline learning centers as well

scores.rationale: The market is fragmented rather than a stable oligopoly — 40+ exam categories with regional players PW is buying up (Xylem, Utkarsh, Sarrthi) and an 'unorganized' K-12 opportunity, while price-sensitive retail customers can walk away freely.
scores.quote: Until now, this opportunity has not been very organized; it's a very large market opportunity

scores.rationale: PW itself competes by collapsing price ('disrupted the prices a lot', a year of IIT/NEET prep for ~INR4,000) and big-tech entry is now visible in the category, indicating low entry barriers and non-rational pricing.
scores.quote: we have already disrupted the prices a lot... the entire preparation of IIT and NEET, which is a year-long live learning, is still happening for ~INR4,000

scores.rationale: Legacy coaching chains are visibly slow and weak — PW built in 3.5 years what incumbents took 40 years to build — and acquired laggards (Utkarsh loss-making, Xylem sub-scale) turned around quickly under PW, confirming donatable share.
scores.quote: What we did offline in 3.5 years, our competition took 40 years to achieve. Because they are traditional companies

scores.rationale: The opposite of obscure — India's largest listed education company post a high-profile IPO, covered by Jefferies, Goldman Sachs, Kotak and Axis on its maiden call, with capital flooding into the sector.
scores.quote: we are India's biggest education company which is listed... access to the capital becomes easier once you are listed

scores.rationale: Latent pricing power exists (management says there is 'a lot of scope for ARPU improvement') but it is deliberately not exercised, and the proposition sold to customers is cheapness rather than image or taste.
scores.quote: the whole day's study is ~INR10 per day, which means we are getting it done in less money than a tea

scores.rationale: Customers do buy outcome certainty — selection guarantee, teacher ratings, learning outcomes and city-level result share are the tracked metrics — but affordability, not trust-over-price, remains the headline pitch.
scores.quote: How are the student-teacher ratios and learning outcomes? How are we producing results in that city?

scores.rationale: Access is the core benefit: the app reaches the remotest villages, 3.4 million DAU with 106 minutes of daily engagement, 300+ tech-enabled centres, and ~80% of offline admissions sourced from the online funnel.
scores.quote: ~80% of our offline admissions happen through online. So, all these processes make us a very unique offline company

scores.rationale: The customer is retail (students and parents) and the offer is matched to it — community-driven brand affinity, free content and low price points — with parents actively seeking the national test-prep brand for schools too.
scores.quote: From a parent side, there is a great affinity because they want to get enrolled in a test prep national brand-centric school

scores.rationale: Genuine in-house AI work (Aryabhata model, Ask AI, PW Talks) and tech-enabled centre operations, but management's own example of Gemini entering mock testing shows the tech edge is contestable by far larger players.
scores.quote: the recent announcement about Gemini entering into mock testing and that actually validates our investments that we did in Aryabhata

scores.rationale: A self-reinforcing community flywheel — free content builds audience, audience converts to paid app users whose results feed the next cohort, now replicated across 250 channels and 2.2 million regional subscribers — though it is one-sided rather than a true two-sided network.
scores.quote: create communities on JEE and NEET, make it free on YouTube, your child will download your app, take your paid courses, keep your marketing expense low

scores.rationale: Distribution reach is the hardest asset to replicate: 250 YouTube channels feeding a zero-CAC funnel into an app with 3.4 million DAU, 300+ centres sited off that online demand, and 30 regional channels extending vernacular reach.
scores.quote: teaching everything for free on internet across now 250 YouTube channels. So that gives us a very strong social media presence and this gives us a very strong top of the funnel

scores.rationale: Multiple simultaneous growth (not maintenance) projects — Sangli Global coil factory pulled forward to June 2026, a new Global Engineering & Technology Centre, phased Mehru line commissioning, completed Cochin expansion, a dedicated PCS/BESS factory and an evaluated Turkey instrument-transformer plant — funded off a net-cash balance sheet while standalone EBITDA margins ran at 34%.
scores.quote: The Sangli Global coil factory construction timeline has been advanced... targeting completion by June 2026 ahead of our earlier schedule... the board also has approved an additional investment for setting up a Global Engineering and Technology center at Sangli

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend in any of the four calls — it is a B2B qualification-driven business.

R&D is visibly converting into new product categories and customer qualifications: the PCS for grid-scale storage was developed in-house, GIS trial product targeted for mid-2026, 765 kV development at Mehru, and HVDC/STATCOM approvals with all leading global OEMs.
scores.quote: It has been developed in-house by our own R&D and engineering team, the result of investments over several years in power electronics design, testing capability and engineering depth.

scores.rationale: Deals are small, complementary bolt-ons with clear post-deal margin improvement (Mehru 9.5% → 12% → 16.4% → ~20% EBITDA; Sukrut operationally positive in its first month), but the acquirees were weak rather than already strong and the deal cadence is high for a newly listed company.
scores.quote: the company turned operationally positive in its very first month under the new management, something that has not been achieved over the past 5 years

scores.rationale: There is a coherent, explained policy — promoters forgoing salary and their dividend share to preserve cash — but the direction of travel is capital raising and dilution, not buybacks or returns.
scores.quote: the promoters in the management have collectively decided to forgo any incremental salary for the second consecutive year and to forgo our share of dividend again this year

scores.rationale: The moat is real but the model is capital-intensive and getting more so — factories, ovens, engineering centre and a new PCS plant — with Mehru's entire facility capped at roughly INR 450-500 crores of revenue, so asset-light is not the description.
scores.quote: The maximum capacity that the current factory can deliver is about INR450 crores to INR500 crores

scores.rationale: A small player explicitly competing against far larger global names, winning first-time landmark HVDC/FACTS orders and newly approved with all leading global OEMs — substantial runway plus demonstrated capture.
scores.quote: we achieved historic order wins in the HVDC segment, including high-voltage smoothing reactors from Rihand-Dadri LCC HVDC project... and converter reactors for a VSC HVDC project in a G20 nation

scores.rationale: Execution is broad and real — large FACTS orders in Sweden, US traction despite tariffs, demand from Middle East/Europe/Australia, Turkish operations executing large orders, plus an evaluated Turkey plant for European proximity and stated North America ambitions.
scores.quote: Internationally, we secured large FACTS orders in Sweden for a steel facilities grid stabilization project... Demand has been particularly robust from the Middle East, Europe, United States and Australia

scores.rationale: Growth is overwhelmingly capacity/volume and acquisition-led (revenue +112-126% on near-full utilisation), with pricing used defensively to pass through aluminium costs and margin deliberately sacrificed in power electronics to buy scale.
scores.quote: we chose to chase growth in our power electronics business, accepting some margin sacrifice to do so

scores.rationale: Positioned early in a multi-year grid-capex upcycle that is currently supply-constrained rather than demand-constrained, which favours the incumbent qualified supplier.
scores.quote: this demand is now constrained by supply, especially for technical advanced products like ours. This is creating a shift towards a supply-driven environment

scores.rationale: The end market — HVDC, FACTS, renewable integration, grid modernisation and data-centre power quality — is in explicit multi-year secular expansion, repeated consistently across all four calls.
scores.quote: These structural tailwinds are creating a multi-year opportunity cycle, and Quality Power is well-positioned at the core of the transformation.

scores.rationale: Prudent leverage and stated valuation discipline (group debt INR 13 crores against INR 250 crores cash; promoter interest-free loan; forgone pay and dividend), tempered by an active acquisition programme and an enabling fundraise resolution rather than a purely organic posture.
scores.quote: Group debt stands at INR13 crores against cash and cash equivalents of INR250 crores... We are extremely disciplined on valuation and return of capital

scores.rationale: Consistent evidence of patient, self-directed capability building — years of investment in approvals and technology now converting into HVDC qualification, and an explicit philosophy of investing ahead of demand.
scores.quote: investing in capability ahead of demand, trusting our own R&D, and moving the technology bar one step at a time

scores.rationale: Substance dominates the operating content, but the calls carry a promotional flavour — hosted throughout by the IPO's merchant-banker group, with the JMD narrating his own executive-education programme and Arthashastra/Sun Tzu framing.
scores.quote: Earlier last month I spent time at the FLAME University as a part of the Next Orbit program.

scores.rationale: Visible internal pipeline — the Chief Business Officer was elevated to CEO within the year — alongside deliberate manpower build-out and a new leadership team installed at Sukrut, though no formal development system is described.
scores.quote: Mr. Sanjog Matre, Chief Business Officer who is now been elevated to Chief Executive Officer

scores.rationale: Proactively corrected a misstated prior-year profit figure, flagged the PAT distortion from a prior forex gain, explained the INR 25.7 crore IndAS 29 hyperinflation hit, disclosed supply-chain and labour-code impacts, and explicitly framed candour about risk as an obligation.
scores.quote: Our responsibility is not only to talk about the achievements, but equally to be open about risks, execution challenges and areas of caution

scores.rationale: The headline results are hard to separate from an industry-wide supply-constrained boom, consolidation of newly acquired entities and a one-time Turkish year-end revenue uplift, and the calls are hosted by the IPO banker's own research arm — so recent numbers overstate demonstrated standalone skill.
scores.quote: we successfully executed multiple large value orders through our Turkish operation. As this also coincided with their financial year end the timing led to a noticeable uplift in quarterly revenues

scores.rationale: Not monopolistic, but it holds a scarce qualified-vendor position in the customer's mind for the most technically demanding products, having been approved by essentially every major global OEM including Chinese ones.
scores.quote: We are now approved suppliers of HVDC and STATCOM products with all the leading global companies, including the Chinese OEMs.

scores.rationale: Switching costs come from long qualification cycles and continuous customer audits on HVDC/STATCOM lines, which lock in an approved supplier once designed in, though no captive aftermarket is described.
scores.quote: the increase in customer audits at our facilities particularly for HVDC and STATCOM projects. The growing frequency of these audits reflects increasing confidence from global customers

scores.rationale: Few qualified suppliers globally in a supply-constrained market shifts negotiating power towards the vendor, evidenced by an order book taken selectively to protect margin rather than to fill capacity.
scores.quote: Our order book stands at around INR 830 crores, maintained with discipline to protect margins and execution quality.

scores.rationale: Entry barriers are severe — global OEM approvals, extreme technical complexity and scarce inputs — and pricing behaviour is rational, with capacity rationed to margin rather than discounted and cost inflation passed through.
scores.quote: These projects are at the highest end of technical complexity and signify a growing confidence in our capabilities.

scores.rationale: Weak players exist and are being absorbed rather than merely out-competed — Sukrut had not been operationally positive in five years — and Mehru is targeted to become the lowest-cost producer in its category, implying weaker rivals to take share from.
scores.quote: Mehru continues its strong growth momentum, and with the new lines being commissioned, is on track to become both the largest and most cost-competitive producer in its category.

scores.rationale: A Sangli-based niche maker of specialised high-voltage coils and reactors, self-described as a small technology company against far larger global names — an unglamorous segment, though the recent large IPO reduces the obscurity.
scores.quote: how we have built Quality Power as a small technology company competing against far larger global names

scores.rationale: Gross margin of 40% and record 34% standalone EBITDA indicate genuine pricing power, but it derives from engineering scarcity and qualification rather than brand image or taste.
scores.quote: EBITDA at INR 97.7 crores, a 67% rise and gross margin maintained at 40%

scores.rationale: Customers are buying certainty on critical grid infrastructure — the qualification, repeated audits and delivery reliability are the purchase criteria, with price clearly secondary to trust.
scores.quote: our teams have delivered with remarkable precision and consistency... ensuring customer deliveries and project continuity

scores.rationale: Deliberate proximity-based service build-out — Cochin expansion for domestic coil products and an evaluated Turkish instrument-transformer plant to serve Europe closer — though no distinctive sales-force intimacy is evidenced.
scores.quote: evaluating the establishment of a instrument transformer manufacturing facility in Turkey through our group entities aimed at serving the European markets with greater proximity and responsiveness

scores.rationale: The customer base is entirely corporate/utility (utilities, renewable developers, data centres, industrial users, OEMs) and the benefit offered is correctly matched — reliability and technical qualification with approval-based lock-in, not consumer intangibles.
scores.quote: We are seeing a very strong quotation pipeline across utilities, renewable developers, data centers, and industrial users

scores.rationale: A deep and widening multi-product technology edge — HVDC smoothing and converter reactors, FACTS/STATCOM, an in-house PCS inverter for BESS, GIS via the Hyosung partnership and 765 kV at Mehru — backed by a dedicated engineering centre.
scores.quote: They are one effort, building a technology moat and a scale moat together.

scores.rationale: Nothing in the calls describes a two-sided or self-reinforcing network; the business is project-based industrial equipment supply.

Reach is being widened deliberately — Sukrut opens access to the transformer manufacturer channel across geographies and the group now serves Europe, US, Middle East and Australia — but it is not yet a reach rivals cannot match.
scores.quote: allows us access to hundreds of transformer manufacturers in India and abroad for our instrument transformer and composite product lines

scores.rationale: Investment talk is present but generic and margin-dilutive rather than a quantified, high-ROIC growth capex programme; no capex or incremental-return disclosure in any of the four calls.
scores.quote: EBITDA remained stable at INR 189 crores with significant investments made in verticalization, technology investments and hiring of recruiters

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotion spend in any of the four calls.
No R&D line or efficiency metric; only a directional AI/product investment plan whose returns are not yet demonstrated.
scores.quote: Our digital platforms continue to remain investment-focused with a layer of AI. We have sharpened our focus towards AI-led solutions with a plan for the coming three years.

scores.rationale: Only a passing reference to M&A-led headcount and demerger costs — no acquisition economics, size or post-deal margin evidence to judge.
scores.quote: partially offset by growth in M&A-led headcount additions

scores.rationale: A clear, stated dividend commitment with a special plus final dividend backed by 80% EBITDA-to-OCF conversion, though no buyback discipline is evidenced.
scores.quote: The Board has thus approved a special dividend of INR 3 per share... and a final dividend of INR 3 per share, staying true to our commitments to reward our shareholders.

scores.rationale: Genuinely asset-light with very high turnover (INR15,305 crores revenue, 20% ROE, 24-day DSO), but the 2.2% EBITDA margin shows no protecting moat behind that turnover.
scores.quote: revenues stand at INR 15,305 crores... This marks a healthy ROE of 20%

scores.rationale: Consistent contract wins (281 in General Staffing, 61 professional logos, 125 overseas) and formalization-driven consolidation support share capture, though it is already India's largest player and headcount was flat.
scores.quote: we added 281 new contracts in General Staffing, continued scaling high margin Professional Staffing with strong GCC traction, adding 61 new logos

scores.rationale: Overseas expansion is executing well with Middle East, Malaysia and Philippines all growing strongly and margins crossing 6-7%, offsetting Singapore weakness — but off a small base and not on brand premium.
scores.quote: Malaysia has delivered strong revenue growth of 83% year-on-year... Philippines posted 49% revenue growth at a 10% EBITDA margin

scores.rationale: Profit growth is clearly mix-led — shifting to GCC/professional staffing and rationalizing low-yield contracts — while headcount volume was broadly flat, though absolute pricing power remains thin.
scores.quote: high margin businesses now contribute 50% of the total profitability, a structural shift that is beginning to reflect in our margin trajectory

scores.rationale: General staffing appears to be off its trough — a first uptick in June 2025 after a six-month decline, and healthy open mandates pointing to a Q4 pickup — but Labour Code disruption keeps the upturn tentative.
scores.quote: The open mandate remained healthy at over 37,000 as we began the fourth quarter, giving us confidence of a pickup in demand

scores.rationale: Two credible secular tailwinds — labour formalization under the new Labour Code and India's GCC build-out (71-73% of professional staffing) — though headline revenue growth of only 3-6% tempers the claim.
scores.quote: we believe the Labour Code will drive greater formalization, consolidation and stronger governance, creating structural tailwinds for Quess given our scale and compliance capabilities

scores.rationale: Organic focus with tight working capital (DSO 24 days, 80-109% OCF conversion) and explicit capital-allocation discipline, with no large acquisitions in the window.
scores.quote: our EBITDA-to-operating cash flow conversion remains strong at 80%, highlighting the disciplined working capital management

scores.rationale: A multi-year deployment-mix strategy has been pursued consistently — professional staffing EBITDA doubled over two years on flat headcount, and Singapore was deliberately rebuilt around general staffing.
scores.quote: over the past 2 years, we -- even with the headcount remaining stable at around 6,000, segment EBITDA has doubled, highlighting the success of our deployment mix optimization strategy

scores.rationale: Calls are operational and metric-driven with no personality cult, but management repeatedly foregrounds awards and rankings in prepared remarks.
scores.quote: Quess has been ranked 36th among India's Best Employer 2025 by TIME and Statista ranking

scores.rationale: Negatives are disclosed specifically and in advance — the NBFC ramp-down flagged a quarter earlier, discontinued projects, Labour Code exceptional item and Singapore softness — rather than buried.
scores.quote: Due to a ramp down by an NBFC that we had called out in Q4 FY25, of around 38,000 associates in Q4, the headcount growth still shows a marginal decline of 5%

scores.rationale: Stripping away the award citations and 'record quarter' framing, underlying results are modest — ~3-6% revenue growth at 2.2% EBITDA margin — so skill cannot be cleanly separated from cyclical recovery and mix arithmetic on a small profit base.
scores.quote: While revenue growth remained moderate, the quality of growth has significantly improved

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like position in the customer's mind; the 2% EBITDA margin and need to rationalize low-yield contracts indicate a commoditized service with no aftermarket annuity.
scores.quote: rationalization of low-yield engagements

scores.rationale: Switching costs are low in staffing — a single NBFC client exit removed 38,000 associates — with only modest stickiness from Collect & Pay and compliance handling.
scores.quote: a ramp down by an NBFC... of around 38,000 associates

scores.rationale: The Indian staffing market is fragmented with substantial customer negotiating power, evidenced by EBITDA margins of only ~2% despite being the largest player.
scores.quote: EBITDA margins increased by 7 basis points quarter-on-quarter to 1.9%

scores.rationale: Barriers are inherently low but rising modestly with Labour Code compliance requirements, and management shows some pricing discipline by walking away from low-margin work.
scores.quote: supported by strong client demand, pricing discipline and deeper wallet share with existing customers

scores.rationale: Labour Code compliance burdens should push work from smaller/unorganized operators toward scaled, compliant players like Quess.
scores.quote: the Labour Code will drive greater formalization, consolidation and stronger governance, creating structural tailwinds for Quess given our scale and compliance capabilities

scores.rationale: Quess is a listed, broker-hosted, award-publicizing market leader — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: we have been recognized as India's number 1 staffing company for 2025 by Staffing Industry Analysts

scores.rationale: No image- or taste-driven pricing power; margins are structurally thin at ~2% EBITDA and growth depends on winning contracts rather than commanding price.
scores.quote: Operating margins improved to 1.9% with a sequential expansion of 7 basis points

scores.rationale: Clients demonstrably buy compliance certainty — over 830 Labour Code advisory consultations in one quarter — positioning Quess as a risk-transfer partner rather than purely a price vendor.
scores.quote: we conducted over 830 client consultations on the impact of Labour Code changes

scores.rationale: The sourcing and fulfilment engine is a genuine accessibility advantage at scale, with 115,000 gross additions in a quarter and a 12.6 million candidate database.
scores.quote: we have done gross additions of 115,000 versus 79,000 gross additions in previous quarter, reflecting the strength of our robust hiring systems

scores.rationale: Customers are corporate and Quess offers the right benefit (reliability and compliance), but without the switching-cost lock-in the framework requires, as shown by abrupt client ramp-downs.
scores.quote: reinforcing our leadership position across BFSI, manufacturing, retail and infrastructure

scores.rationale: AI is being layered onto sourcing and platforms with external recognition, but there is no evidence of a deep, multi-product technology edge or meaningful R&D intensity.
scores.quote: recognized with "LinkedIn Talent Award 2025" for "AI Pioneer"

scores.rationale: Hamara Jobs and the ONDC tie-up have the shape of a two-sided network with 12.6 million profiles, but the platform remains pre-monetization and in investment phase, so no self-reinforcing effect is yet demonstrated.
scores.quote: Hamara Jobs platform now boasts over 12.6 million registered candidate profile

scores.rationale: Scale of reach is the clearest durable advantage — India's largest staffing platform with ~478,000 associates and pan-India Tier 2/3 sourcing that smaller rivals cannot replicate.
scores.quote: We ended the year with a headcount of approximately 4,78,594 associates, reinforcing our position as India's largest staffing platform

scores.rationale: Management explicitly states capex is now mainly maintenance/efficiency rather than growth, with the growth story funded by existing capacity and deleveraging instead of fresh expansion spend.
scores.quote: ongoing Capex largely directed toward maintenance, efficiency improvement and essential capacity optimization

scores.rationale: A&SP rose from ~5.5% to 6.9% of IMFL revenue with a guided 6-8% band, and the spend visibly converted into brand equity and volume (After Dark +60% to 3.1m cases, Magic Moments +21% to 8.6m cases) while EBITDA margin still expanded 565bps in Q4.
scores.quote: Our A&SP investment were at 6.9% of IMFL revenues, compared to 5.5% in Q3 FY25... we continue to guide for A&SP spending in the range of 6-8%

scores.rationale: No formal R&D line, but a consistent innovation pipeline (Morpheus Super Premium, Spirit of Kashmyr, Rampur 1943 Virasat, Flavours of India variants) is repeatedly translating into new revenue streams within a year of launch.
scores.quote: New flavour innovations including Flavours of India category are contributing to this robust momentum

scores.rationale: Only small, complementary moves — a stake increase in D'YAVOL Spirits and a wholly-owned Scotland subsidiary to secure matured malt supply — with no large or diversifying acquisition, and margins improved through the period.
scores.quote: The Board of Directors has approved setting up a 100% wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company in Scotland... towards securing access to the matured malt supply chain

scores.rationale: A formal minimum 20%-of-PAT dividend policy was articulated in Q4 FY26 alongside deleveraging, which is coherent and disciplined, though there is no buyback programme or valuation-linked repurchase discipline.
scores.quote: the Board has articulated a strong dividend policy with a minimum payout of 20% of profit after tax

scores.rationale: Revenue crossed Rs 6,000 crores and EBITDA Rs 1,000 crores off an asset base needing only maintenance capex, with management citing better asset utilisation lifting ROE/ROCE, protected by brand and licensing barriers.
scores.quote: Higher operating profit and better asset utilization have contributed to improved ROE and ROCE

scores.rationale: Demonstrated share capture with Andhra Pradesh share rising from ~10% to ~30% to become the leading player, plus a small base in the 75-million-case whisky segment After Dark is attacking, so runway remains large.
scores.quote: market share increasing from around 10% in first half of last year to over 30% in quarter 2 of FY26, making us the leading player in the state

scores.rationale: Well-executed state-by-state rollout (After Dark to 18 states, Morpheus to 10, Kashmyr to 7) and early international validation via Rampur on Air India, but exports faced trade headwinds so international expansion is unproven.
scores.quote: The brand has expanded its footprint to 18 states, reinforcing its national presence

scores.rationale: Mix is a genuine driver — P&A volume +28% in Q4 and gross margin up 450bps on premiumisation — but headline growth was largely volume-led with P&A realisation improving only ~2.1-2.8%, so pricing power in the numbers is modest.
scores.quote: recording 26% volume growth and 29% value growth, with realizations improving by 2.8% on year-on-year basis

scores.rationale: The company is benefiting from an already-favourable input cost cycle (benign ENA/grain prices contributed 225bps of gross margin expansion) rather than sitting near a cyclical bottom, with West Asia flagged as a possible reversal risk.
scores.quote: Raw material accounted for 225 bps of gross margin expansion during the quarter as compared to last year Q3

scores.rationale: Management consistently frames demand as a permanent premiumisation shift driven by rising affluence and lifestyle consumption, and the P&A/luxury mix data across all four calls corroborates it.
scores.quote: The Indian AlcoBev industry is undergoing a structural shift from traditional consumption patterns to a more lifestyle-driven category

scores.rationale: Organic, brand-led growth with net debt down Rs 329 crores in FY26 and a stated path to debt-free by H1 FY27, selective capex and only a tiny bolt-on stake purchase — no large M&A or leverage build.
scores.quote: net debt reduced by INR 329 crores during the year... we are on track to become debt-free in H1 FY27

scores.rationale: Promoter-led team is executing a multi-year premiumisation plan — Rampur single malt heritage, After Dark rebuilt from 2022 to 3.1m cases, luxury portfolio hitting the guided ~Rs 500 crore mark — with a stated 3-year vision for Magic Moments.
scores.quote: our vision is over the next 3 years to see Magic [Moments] come up to 10 million cases

scores.rationale: Communication is competent but distinctly promotional in tone ('defining phase of acceleration', repeated 'highest-ever' framing) and leans on celebrity validation events, though no personal cult of the promoters is evident.
scores.quote: The third quarter represents a defining phase of acceleration for Radico Khaitan

scores.rationale: The calls contain no discussion of talent development, succession or internal leadership pipeline; a Chief Sales Officer simply appears on the Q4 call without context.

Management gives specific quantified guidance and explains shortfalls and adverse drivers openly (regular-volume degrowth attributed to base effect and Maharashtra/Karnataka policy, West Asia risk flagged), though the Rs 475 crore luxury outcome versus Rs 500 crore guidance was described as 'in line'.
scores.quote: Regular volume degrowth was due to a higher base in Q4 FY25 after the change in the route to the market in the state of Andhra Pradesh and the impact of policy changes in Maharashtra and Karnataka

scores.rationale: Stripping out luck, a large slice of the record year came from exogenous factors — the Andhra route-to-market change and 225bps of raw-material-driven margin — so execution skill is real but materially flattered by tailwinds.
scores.quote: The change in route to market in Andhra Pradesh was a key driver of this rebound

scores.rationale: Magic Moments occupies a near-category-defining position in Indian vodka at 8.6m cases and Rampur owns the Indian single malt prestige niche, giving mind-space monopolies in narrow categories.
scores.quote: Magic Moments Vodka continued its strong trajectory with 21% volume growth during the year to reach 8.6 million cases... further strengthening its leadership in the vodka category

scores.rationale: There are no customer switching costs and the state governments — not the company — control route to market and pricing, as shown by policy changes in Andhra, Maharashtra and Karnataka swinging volumes materially.
scores.quote: the impact of policy changes in Maharashtra and Karnataka

scores.rationale: Indian IMFL is a consolidated few-player market where Radico can price a new brand above peers and the retail end-consumer has no negotiating power, though state excise authorities are a powerful counterparty.
scores.quote: initial response to the brand has been very encouraging, though we have priced at higher than peer's brands in the same segment

scores.rationale: No image- or taste-based pricing power is evident: realisations fell for most of the year, demand for high-value products dropped with crop prices, and Q4 EBITDA was around zero.

scores.rationale: There is a genuine trust/compliance angle — in-house bio-stimulant production for state compliance and regulatory tightening that favours quality-assured organized supply — but customers still switch on price.
scores.quote: We progressed in compliance in majority of the states post successful migration of bio -stimulant production inhouse.

scores.rationale: Rallis is investing hard in reach and farmer intimacy — Sampark Plus for field demand capture, Saksham GIS village targeting, retailer enrolment on Anubandh Edge and product demonstrations.
scores.quote: We also launched Saksham (GIS platform) which enables scientific identification of high -potential villages for targeted market expansion.

scores.rationale: The mix is split between retail farmers (B2C formulations, seeds) served via reach and promotion and corporate buyers (B2B technicals, CSM) won on registrations and cost, but neither side shows the matching intangible or lock-in advantage — CSM revenue even moved on customer dispatch phasing.
scores.quote: CSM quarter 2 revenues impacted due to customer phasing -off of dispatch plan for key products.

scores.rationale: There is real but narrow technical depth — a granted Indian patent for a three-way wheat herbicide, a US process patent for Mesotrione, a patented paddy herbicide registration and efficient-technology capacity — set against a mostly generic portfolio.
scores.quote: We have been granted Indian patent for Metsulfuron Methyl+ Clodinafop -Propargyl +Metribuzin

scores.rationale: The business is transactional product sales; the only platform-like initiative, the Idea2Impact open-innovation ecosystem, is a sourcing channel with no self-reinforcing two-sided dynamic.
scores.quote: Idea2impact which is an open -innovation platform to co -create, validate, and scale farmer -centric solutions

scores.rationale: Farmer and retailer reach, digitally enabled field operations and demonstration-led demand creation are the clearest defensible asset described, and management credits volume growth to exactly this.
scores.quote: 13% growth in Q3FY26 ... driven by volume growth of 25% ... new product promotion, & increased digital engagement

scores.rationale: Growth capex is large and rising (Kolimigundla, RR Nagar Line-3, Odisha grinding, WHRS, plus a Rs.1,250 Cr Kurnool doubling) but guidance was revised twice in one year and Rs.9,800 Cr of spend has produced only ~Rs.1,400 Cr average EBITDA with net debt/EBITDA at 3.22x, so incremental returns are unproven.
scores.quote: earlier we had guided Rs.900 Crores for FY2024 which was subsequently revised to Rs.1,600 Crores... Now, the guidance is further revised to Rs.2,000 Crores

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend in any of the four calls.
No formal R&D line, but in-house engineering delivered debottlenecking (design, engineering and execution) and a 12-variant product range that is converting into repeat orders.
scores.quote: Our in-house team had carried out the de-bottlenecking activities that included design, engineering and execution.

scores.rationale: Only inorganic activity is small complementary asset purchases — limestone-bearing land adjacent to existing plants and mining lands bought from Prism Cement — rather than corporate acquisitions.
scores.quote: These mines are very near to our factory and adjacent to our compound wall... it will augment our limestone reserves by another 140 million tons

scores.rationale: Dividends, buybacks or any distribution policy are never mentioned across the four calls.

Business is capital-heavy and getting heavier — roughly Rs.1,700 Cr of capex per million ton of capacity, cement utilisation only 74-82%, and net debt near Rs.5,000 Cr against Rs.1,400 Cr average EBITDA.
scores.quote: in last seven years from FY19 to FY25... we spend 12,173 odd Crores and the capacity that we will be adding by FY2025 would be 7.2 million ton

scores.rationale: Volume growth of 46% and 38% year-on-year, far ahead of the industry, with utilisation lifting from 66% to 82%, showing clear share capture from a non-dominant base.
scores.quote: sale of cement has improved to 4.61 million tons, compared to 3.35 million tons in the corresponding period, with a growth of 38%

scores.rationale: Expansion into the East (Odisha grinding doubled to 1.8 MTPA) and land acquisition for Karnataka/Bommanahalli to reach western markets is proceeding, though it is regional adjacency and north/west mining bids have failed so far.
scores.quote: we got one mining asset in Karnataka. We are in the process of buying land there also... then we can enter into western markets also

scores.rationale: Growth is overwhelmingly volume-led with prices repeatedly under pressure — Q3FY24 volume rose 10% but revenue only 5%, implying falling realisations, with premium mix improving only marginally from 26% to 27%.
scores.quote: The cement prices have been under pressure during this quarter... sale of cement has improved by 10%... Net revenue for the current quarter has grown by 5%

scores.rationale: Fuel costs have rolled off their peak (pet coke $178 to ~$120) and blended EBITDA/ton has recovered from Rs.823 to Rs.1,007, indicating the company is coming off a cyclical trough in margins.
scores.quote: Blended EBITDA per ton for the current quarter is Rs.1007 as against Rs.808 in the corresponding period with a growth of 25%

scores.rationale: Management points to a large, durable infrastructure and housing spending cycle (PMAY, railways, ports, ~INR 14 lakh crore outlay) supporting Indian cement demand.
scores.quote: increased allocation is made towards the PMAY scheme, capital outlay for railways, urban infrastructure development... around INR 14 lakh crores. This is a big positive for the cement industry

scores.rationale: Growth is entirely organic and counter-cyclical with no large M&A, but leverage is not prudent — net debt near Rs.5,000 Cr at 3.22x EBITDA held for years and repeated upward capex revisions.
scores.quote: The net debt is as on December 31, 2023, is Rs.4,993 Crores... and the net debt to EBITDA is at 3.22 times

scores.rationale: A multi-year self-funded capacity build from 12 to 22 MTPA plus a green-power programme taking renewable share from 22% to a targeted 45% shows long-horizon execution independent of the cycle.
scores.quote: out of which Rs.7,800 Crores were from free cash flow from operations for the said period

scores.rationale: Calls are plain, operational and unpromotional, run by the CEO/CFO with factual capacity and cost updates rather than any celebrity positioning.
scores.quote: This ends my short introduction to the call. Now we are open to questions.

scores.rationale: Capacity was added through internally executed debottlenecking rather than outside contractors, evidencing genuine internal engineering depth, though no formal talent programme is described.
scores.quote: Our in-house team had carried out the de-bottlenecking activities

scores.rationale: Management refused to break down a capex overshoot analysts explicitly questioned and had dropped project-wise capex disclosure from the presentation, deflecting rather than owning the guidance misses.
scores.quote: Sorry, I don't want to elaborate. Okay, maybe whenever other companies elaborate the details, we will give you the details.

scores.rationale: Headline volume and EBITDA growth mainly reflect newly commissioned capacity meeting a strong demand cycle and falling pet coke, while PBT fell year-on-year in Q3FY23 and leverage rose — results outrun demonstrated capital-allocation skill.
scores.quote: Profit before tax stood at INR 97 crores during the quarter as against INR 113 crores during the corresponding period

scores.rationale: Application-specific product range and a 27-28% premium share suggest some brand preference, but nothing approaching a monopoly position in the customer's mind.
scores.quote: the share of premium products have improved to 27% from 26%

scores.rationale: Its core South Indian market shows no captive pricing power — prices slipped even during strong demand — and cement carries no switching costs.
scores.quote: The cement demand has been strong, but the prices have been under constant pressure during this quarter.

scores.rationale: Pricing behaviour described across all four calls is volatile and buyer-favourable, indicating a fragmented, competitive South Indian market rather than a stable oligopoly.
scores.quote: The prices are very volatile. We cannot assume the prices

scores.rationale: Mining leases are a genuine entry barrier that even Ramco cannot overcome in new regions, but industry pricing is plainly irrational, with prices falling into strong demand.
scores.quote: As of now, we do not have any mining leases in those areas, so it is not possible. So we also participated in many bids. But we were not successful.

scores.rationale: Ramco is growing volumes multiples of industry rates and buying mining land from a weakened peer, indicating share is available from struggling competitors.
scores.quote: consequent to the acquisition of mining lands from Prism Cement

scores.rationale: The company is a well-covered listed mid-cap with calls hosted by Antique, B&K and ICICI and questions from Jefferies, Ambit, Axis and Investec — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: We have our first question from the line of Parth Bhavsar from Investec.

scores.rationale: Rising premium-product share hints at brand pull, but there is no evident pricing power — realisations fell and EBITDA margin is only 18-19%.
scores.quote: The share of premium products has improved to 28% in the current quarter from 25%

scores.rationale: Management attributes growth to matching product to application and earning repeat orders, indicating customers buy reliability/fit rather than lowest price.
scores.quote: we are able to tailor-made and we meet the requirements of different customers, we are able to get repeat orders

scores.rationale: Deliberate investment in servicing infrastructure — split grinding units, railway sidings, logistics — was cited as a direct cause of outsized volume capture.
scores.quote: we created necessary infrastructure to service this... we invested so much money to create the infrastructure to service this kind of spurt in demand

scores.rationale: Serves both retail IHB and infra/corporate demand, with a 12-variety application-matched range and a premium tier aimed at the retail builder.
scores.quote: we are also promoting what is called the right cement for the right application. Nearly 12 types of cement we are manufacturing.

scores.rationale: Technical capability is real but process-level — in-house debottlenecking and WHRS/green power to 38% — not a differentiated multi-product technology edge with high R&D intensity.
scores.quote: The overall green power usage has significantly improved to 38% during the quarter from 22%

scores.rationale: No network-effect dynamics are discussed or applicable in anything the calls cover.
A spread of grinding units across Tamil Nadu, Andhra, Karnataka and Odisha with railway sidings gives regional reach that management credits for servicing demand spikes.
scores.quote: railway siding will be commissioned in June 2024... Expansion of grinding plant from 0.9 MTPA to 1.8 MTPA in Odisha

scores.rationale: Asset-light SaaS where growth investment flows into GTM expansion and platform build rather than capex, with visible returns (APAC/Middle East best-ever sales quarter, LATAM +52%), though incremental ROIC on growth spend is not quantified.
scores.quote: The GTM expansion investments made earlier this year are now delivering visible results across regions

scores.rationale: No disclosure of the company's own A&P spend or brand-building budget; the marketing discussed is the product it sells to customers, not its own promotion.

R&D consistently converts into shipped, monetized products across all four calls — Rev AI, Demand AI, Content AI from RG Labs, then MCP booking integration, UNO VIVA voice AI, RateIQ, Agentic ARI and AI Concierge with measurable customer ROI.
scores.quote: AI Concierge... Hotels use AI Concierge are seeing up to 300% increase in ancillary revenue, 75% improvement in NPS, automation of up to 80% of guests queries.

scores.rationale: Bolt-on track record is decent (my hotel shop completed MarTech; BCV/SoHo turned profitable after years of losses), but Sojern is a large debt-funded transformational deal that inflated amortization and finance costs and pushed reported PAT down — synergies are ahead of plan but the deal is neither small nor simple.
scores.quote: SoHo, the erstwhile BCV business, this was the only acquisition in our portfolio that was not profitable since the acquisition. This quarter, SoHo achieved profitability.

scores.rationale: No dividend, buyback or distribution policy is discussed in any of the excerpts; free cash flow is being directed to acquisition debt repayment instead.
Asset-light SaaS/data model with negligible physical capital and a claimed data-scale moat, though the Sojern goodwill/intangibles now weigh on the asset base.
scores.quote: RateGain today operates the world's largest single source of travel intent data at a scale no other provider in our market can match.

scores.rationale: Clear runway and evidence of share capture in MarTech/DMO and new logo wins across airlines, but organic growth slowed to 4-5% in Q3 and a large customer had earlier been lost, so share gain is uneven.
scores.quote: The organic year -on-year growth for this quarter was in 4% to 5% range

scores.rationale: Well-executed multi-region expansion: five new markets added, best-ever sales quarter in APAC/Middle East, LATAM growing 52%, and APMEA named the priority growth engine for FY27.
scores.quote: we also expanded into five new markets, the Maldives, Sri Lanka, Phuket and select destinations in the Middle East and Africa

scores.rationale: Headline growth is dominated by acquisition scale and customer/volume additions rather than price; the move to performance-linked pricing ties revenue to customer outcomes and management asserts pricing power, but no realized price/mix uplift is quantified.
scores.quote: we are increasingly moving towards performance -linked pricing, where customers pay based on outcomes delivered

scores.rationale: Travel demand is described as resilient and mid-cycle rather than near a cyclical bottom, with regional divergence and a North America dip — no identifiable upturn from a trough.
scores.quote: Global Health Index stood at 101, reflecting the sector's ability to sustain momentum despite ongoing geopolitical challenges.

scores.rationale: End market is in secular expansion — digital adoption in travel accelerating, online bookings expanding globally, and a structural shift to AI-led discovery that the company is positioned to serve.
scores.quote: Travel continues to be resilient. Digital adoption is accelerating. Online bookings are expanding globally

scores.rationale: Despite repeated 'discipline in organic growth focus' language, management took on large acquisition debt for Sojern while organic growth decelerated to 4-6%, making leverage and inorganic dependence the dominant story this year.
scores.quote: we've already repaid approximately $25 million of acquisition -related debt, representing 20% of gross loan amount within the first 90 days of deal closure. We aim to be net debt positive within 30 months.

scores.rationale: Founder-led with a multi-year target set at the start of FY24 and delivered a full year early, plus sustained tenacity in product innovation and a customer win-back after 18 months.
scores.quote: at the beginning of FY24, I had laid out our medium -term vision of doubling revenue... to INR 2,000 crores by FY27... we are well ahead of that goal... achieving this milestone a year ahead of schedule.

scores.rationale: Commentary leans heavily on media coverage, awards counts and superlative self-description, which is the opposite of low-profile substance-over-celebrity.
scores.quote: our data has driven record -breaking coverage across the world's most influential business publication including the New York Times, Reuters, the Financial Times... 78 dedicated articles since March alone.

scores.rationale: Repeated Great Place to Work certifications across India, Spain and the US and policy harmonization post-acquisition show people investment, but senior hires are external (Chief Customer Officer from Cvent/WNS) and CFO turnover is visible, with no described internal pipeline.
scores.quote: We were recognized as a great place to work in India for the seventh consecutive year.

scores.rationale: Management addressed the PAT decline head-on with itemized reasons and disclosed weak organic growth, a lost customer and the loss-making BCV asset — though the framing is consistently promotional and the deferral explanation is convenient.
scores.quote: The reported PAT declined year -on-year and the reasons are transparent. There was an increased amortization from acquisition accounting.

scores.rationale: Headline results (revenue +175%, +94%) are almost entirely acquisition-driven while the underlying organic engine grew 4-6% and reported PAT fell, so the impressive optics substantially overstate demonstrated operating skill.
scores.quote: we reported the highest ever quarterly revenue of INR716 crores, up 175% year -on-year. Within this, the RateGain organic revenue stood at INR311 crores, up 19.3%

scores.rationale: Claims a near-monopoly position specifically in destination management organizations and the largest single source of travel intent data, though this is self-asserted and confined to one ~$90m niche.
scores.quote: we're now the most dominant provider in the space of destination management organization. No other provider even comes close. It's about a $90 million business for us

scores.rationale: Deep workflow embedding and long-term renewals suggest real switching costs, evidenced by a four-year Singapore Airlines extension and a churned customer returning after finding no adequate substitute.
scores.quote: Singapore Airlines extended its partnership with RateGain for an additional 4 years

scores.rationale: The combined Sojern/Adara entity implies consolidation in travel intent data, but the excerpts describe no stable competitive structure and enterprise OTA/hotel-chain customers are large and powerful buyers.
scores.quote: No other player in our market combines travel intent data at this scale, distribution infrastructure of this depth and the AI -powered commercial intelligence under one roof.

scores.rationale: Data scale and integrations create some barrier, but the company itself notes broad AI market noise and the loss of a customer to industry consolidation, and no evidence is given on pricing rationality or absence of new entrants.
scores.quote: There is broad market noise around AI.

scores.rationale: Weak competitors exist to take share from — a departed customer returned after a rival failed to deliver comparable lift, and Sojern's acquired assets were themselves underperforming until restructured.
scores.quote: a large customer that had exited approximately 18 months ago has returned via pilot on Demand Booster... After demonstrating the revenue lift, they were missing by moving away, they have reengaged.

scores.rationale: The company actively courts visibility through global media coverage, award announcements and industry-conversation positioning, the opposite of an under-the-radar niche.
scores.quote: positioning us at the center of industry conversation regarding destination intelligence

scores.rationale: Pricing power is asserted via the data moat, but demand is B2B ROI-driven with a shift to outcome-based pricing rather than image-led, and no gross margin or realized price evidence is given.
scores.quote: Both translate directly into pricing power and commercial momentum as we move through FY27.

scores.rationale: Customers buy reliability and measurable certainty — closed-loop attribution, parity intelligence and long-standing enterprise partnerships renewed on trust rather than price.
scores.quote: Singapore Airlines extended its long -standing partnership, reinforcing trust in our pricing intelligence stack.

scores.rationale: Integrated single-stack proposition plus on-the-ground local sales teams and a new Chief Customer Officer improve accessibility and customer intimacy.
scores.quote: Our expanded GTM teams in APAC and Middle East delivered their best quarter in terms of new sales, validating our decision to strengthen local presence in these regions.

scores.rationale: Corporate customer base is correctly served with ROI/TCO proof and workflow lock-in, which is the right benefit match for enterprise buyers.
scores.quote: Across DaaS, we are embedding intelligence into workflows not adding just surface -based analytics that creates durability.

scores.rationale: Multi-product AI stack spanning marketing, pricing, distribution and guest engagement with industry-first launches (MCP booking integration, Agentic ARI, voice AI) and demonstrable customer benefit.
scores.quote: we now offer Demand AI for smarter audience targeting, Rev AI for pricing intelligence, smart ARI... Navigator AI... AI Concierge... and VIVA voice AI

scores.rationale: Consolidated data partnerships and the largest travel intent dataset create a scale-based data advantage that improves with more customers, though no explicit two-sided self-reinforcing loop is demonstrated.
scores.quote: we have also consolidated the data partnership that Adara and Sojern each brought into the combined entity

scores.rationale: Deep connectivity infrastructure across 13,000+ customers, top hotel chains, OTAs and airlines plus embedded payments gives reach rivals would struggle to replicate.
scores.quote: With 13,000 -plus customers across the combined business, the cross -sell opportunity ahead of us is significant

scores.rationale: Multiple genuinely growth-oriented projects funded from internal accruals — Odisha spiral plant Phase-I/II, ~$40mn overseas cold-finishing, Finow capacity tripling (~Rs 250cr), RTL automation line, Saudi SS plant — but incremental ROIC is unproven with plants at 50-60% utilization and FY26 standalone sales down sharply.
scores.quote: we had two projects which were ongoing. One was a spiral welded plant in Odisha... And then we had the stainless-steel cold finishing capacities

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend in any of the four calls.

No R&D line is disclosed, but product/process development consistently yields new qualified products — hydrogen-compliant welded pipes to Europe, API monogram and API 5LC/5CT range, 18-metre spiral pipes, heavy-thickness pipes, instrumentation tubes in coil form.
scores.quote: We successfully pioneered supply of hydrogen-compli ant carbon steel welded pipes to Europe.

scores.rationale: Deals are small, complementary bolt-ons (buying out minorities in Ravi Technoforge and Ratnamani Trade EU, the Finow spooling JV, the 75-25 SESCO JV) and post-deal operating margins improved at both subsidiaries.
scores.quote: EBITDA margins improved from 10% to 12% due to operational efficiencies

scores.rationale: Dividend policy is explained with a clear rationale but was cut from Rs 14 to Rs 10 to conserve resources, and there is no buyback programme at all.
scores.quote: conservation of resources till things settle down, the Board has decided to recommend a lower dividend of INR10 per share

scores.rationale: The business is heavy and capital-intensive with plants running at 50-60% utilization and falling volumes, so asset turn is structurally low and currently deteriorating.
scores.quote: Presently, all our plants are operating at 50% to 60% utilization

scores.rationale: Stainless-steel volumes rose and the extruded niche faces only one prospective entrant, but carbon-steel volumes fell and competitive intensity is rising, so there is no clear evidence of share capture.
scores.quote: The stainless-steel volume in the last fiscal year actually went up, not down, but the prices were down.

scores.rationale: Credible, funded international build-out — Saudi JV with SESCO now holding Commercial Registration, GCC and Europe demand, Switzerland entity taken to 100%, exports ~Rs 700cr of the Rs 2,160cr order book — though the Saudi plant is only starting construction.
scores.quote: In Saudi Arabia, our subsidiary has now received the CR, which is Commercial Registration.

scores.rationale: Growth is mix-led rather than price-led: higher value-added products protected margins in both FY25 Q4 and FY26 even as realizations fell, but soft metal prices are a persistent drag on pricing.
scores.quote: our continued focus on operational efficiency, cost optimization and improved product mix with higher value-added products ensured that there was no negative impact on the EBITDA margins

scores.rationale: The company appears to be near a cyclical trough — muted domestic demand and delayed project cycles for two years — with an identifiable upturn signalled by improving enquiries and expected tenders.
scores.quote: inquiry levels have started showing signs of improvement across key markets

scores.rationale: Part of the portfolio sits in secular end-markets (nuclear spooling order book, hydrogen-compliant pipes, water infrastructure, bearing rings), but the core carbon-steel oil & gas business remains cyclical and currently subdued.
scores.quote: all the orders that we have at RFSS is for the nuclear power industry

scores.rationale: Standalone debt-free through the whole window with Rs 521cr operating cash generation, capex funded internally and continued counter-cyclically into a downturn, and no large or transformational M&A.
scores.quote: I'm also happy to share that company continues to remain debt-free on a stand-alone basis.

scores.rationale: Projects flagged in Nov 2024 were delivered on the stated schedule across the window — Odisha Phase-I commissioned, cold finishing started, Finow expansion progressing — showing consistent follow-through despite a weak demand cycle.
scores.quote: we commissioned the Phase-I of Orissa plant and the Phase-II is expected to be commissioned in the next quarter

scores.rationale: Calls are attended only by the CEO and CFO, delivered in plain operational detail with no promotional framing or celebrity positioning.
scores.quote: The company has referred to publicly available documents / information for discussions

scores.rationale: No discussion of talent development, succession or leadership pipeline in any of the four calls.

Management states weakness plainly rather than spinning it — flagging muted demand, guiding to flat-to-lower revenue, explaining the dividend cut, and correcting a questioner with specifics rather than deflecting.
scores.quote: While revenue may stay flattish or show a slight dip, we expect that a strong focus on operational efficiency and cost control should help maintaining EBITDA

scores.rationale: The assessment survives separating results from skill: reported results actually deteriorated (Q4 standalone sales fell from Rs 1,575cr to Rs 893cr) yet margins and debt-free status were held, so the positive read rests on demonstrated cost/mix execution rather than on a flattering headline.
scores.quote: Despite lower revenues, the group-maintained profitability margin and absolute EBITDA and net profit broadly in line with the previous year.

scores.rationale: Nuclear pipe spooling is a near-uncontested position — management says there is essentially no competition for nuclear projects and capacity is fully booked for them.
scores.quote: not much competition at the moment for the nuclear project

scores.rationale: Customer approvals and third-party certifications (API monogram, API 5LC/5CT, nuclear qualification) act as switching costs that gate who can bid, though these are obtainable by determined rivals.
scores.quote: Our Kutch plant received the API monogram certification from American Petroleum Institute, enabling new business opportunities

scores.rationale: Industry structure is deteriorating rather than oligopolistic — excess domestic stainless-steel capacity, new entrants from carbon steel, and project customers bidding out tenders hold the negotiating power.
scores.quote: there is excess capacity available in domestic stainless-steel pipe industry, while demand also remains weak

scores.rationale: Entry barriers are visibly eroding with almost every carbon-steel player moving into stainless steel amid weak demand; the only defence cited is the narrower extruded segment where one new player is still expected.
scores.quote: a lot of carbon steel players plus other players, the competition intensity in stainless steel or carbon steel is increasing

scores.rationale: No discussion of weak or exiting competitors from whom share could be taken; the competitive commentary describes entrants, not donators.
The nuclear spooling and bearing-ring businesses are small, unglamorous niches that attract little competitive or capital attention, though the parent pipe business is well covered by the street.
scores.quote: There are a lot of pipes, spooling fabricators in India. However they are mostly into oil and gas segment.

scores.rationale: Gross margin is respectable at 34% but demand is project-tendered and realizations track metal prices, with no evidence of image- or taste-driven pricing power.
scores.quote: we maintained a healthy gross profit margin of 34%

scores.rationale: Customers in nuclear, hydrogen and oil & gas applications are buying certified reliability, which is why approvals and monograms rather than price open the business.
scores.quote: Customer approval is in place. Executions will start.

scores.rationale: The Saudi JV is explicitly a proximity-and-service play to sit closer to GCC customers, indicating deliberate investment in accessibility, though no broad distribution intimacy is evidenced.
scores.quote: This strategic move will strengthen our local presence, enhance our brand visibility and allow us to better serve customers across Saudi Arabia and GCC region.

scores.rationale: The customer base is entirely corporate/EPC and the benefit offered matches it — certification-based reliability and approval-driven lock-in rather than retail-style intangibles.
scores.quote: our still our focus remains on high value-added extruded products

scores.rationale: A real but narrow process/metallurgy edge in high value-added extruded and specialized pipes (hydrogen-compliant, heavy-thickness, 18-metre spiral, API 5CT), rather than a deep multi-product technology moat with high R&D intensity.
scores.quote: our still our focus remains on high value-added extruded products, where only one new player is supposed to come

scores.rationale: No evidence of any network-effect dynamic in a project-order pipe business.
Sales are direct, tender- and project-based rather than distribution-led, and the only reach initiative mentioned is the still-unbuilt Saudi facility.
scores.quote: We are in the process of establishing a stainless-steel manufacturing facility in the region.

scores.rationale: Capex is described as calibrated and modest — debottlenecking/automation plus asset-light franchise stores — with no evidence of high, rising growth capex or measured incremental ROIC.
scores.quote: Capital allocation remains focused on debottlenecking, automation and selective expansion

scores.rationale: A&P was deliberately stepped up but visibly compressed apparel EBITDA margin (13% to 5.2%) without a matching sales lift, and the new CEO concedes marketing has been fragmented rather than brand-building.
scores.quote: EBITDA margin of 5.2% ... on account of increased marketing spend and input costs and lower sales

scores.rationale: No formal R&D line, but continuous fabric innovation (techno-series, bio-polished merino, Super Luxe) is translating into realised price — ASP up ~INR26/meter.
scores.quote: Average selling price increases by about INR 26 per meter, reflecting the growing contribution of premium and technical fabrics

scores.rationale: No acquisitions were discussed in any of the four calls.
No buyback, dividend or distribution policy was mentioned in the excerpts.
Working capital improved from 87 to 77 days and store growth is franchise/asset-light, but the business still carries owned textile and garmenting plants, so asset-lightness is only partial.
scores.quote: Shorter format stores, an asset-light franchise-led model, and capital partnering enable us to grow efficiently while protecting returns

scores.rationale: The trade channel is compounding at double digits against mid-single-digit industry growth, evidencing share capture, though Raymond is already the dominant branded suiting player which caps the runway.
scores.quote: Industry growth remains amid single digits, while the ... Raymond Lifestyle trade channel is growing in double digits

scores.rationale: Deliberate, executed diversification of exports away from the US plus Tier-2/3 domestic formats, with Q4 garmenting up 38% and highest-ever March revenue.
scores.quote: we have reduced our dependency on the US market from about 50% to 35%. We are increasingly focusing on UK, Europe and Asia-Pacific

scores.rationale: Management repeatedly attributes growth to volume (wedding dates, festive, GST-driven volume) with mix/ASP contributing mainly to margin, so growth is not primarily price/mix-led.
scores.quote: accelerate volume-led growth across both urban and Tier-2 or Tier-3 markets

scores.rationale: FY26 is explicitly framed as a recovery year off a weak base, with garmenting swinging from losses to profit post the US-India trade deal and FTAs still to be implemented.
scores.quote: FY26 has been a year of recovery for Raymond Lifestyle

scores.rationale: Management identifies durable structural drivers — premiumisation, post-GST formalisation and price-inelastic wedding consumption — supported by Tier-2/3 penetration.
scores.quote: premiumization of the demand, continued formalization post-GST and strong price inelastic consumption around weddings and occasions

scores.rationale: Balance sheet is net cash with improving working capital, growth is organic (stores, product) with no large M&A and active pruning of weak stores.
scores.quote: We remain debt-free with a net cash surplus of INR179 crores

scores.rationale: Extreme leadership churn across the four calls — group CFO, interim CFO, new CFO, new CEO and new CMO all within twelve months — undercuts evidence of a tenacious, continuously executed long-term plan.
scores.quote: It is my privilege to address you for the first time

scores.rationale: The organisation is visibly promoter/chairman-centric and publicity-forward, with a dedicated "Chairman's Office" role, a "Chairman's Collection" launch and high-profile cricket/cinema campaigns.
scores.quote: MR. AMIT AGARWAL – PRESIDENT OF CHAIRMAN'S OFFICE

scores.rationale: Every senior seat filled in the window came from outside (CEO, CFO from Bajaj Electricals, CMO from HUL), indicating no internal leadership pipeline.
scores.quote: Our new CMO, Kalpana Singh, has just joined in March from HUL

scores.rationale: The new CEO voluntarily unbundles loss-making emerging businesses from the core four brands, flags the prior-year one-time subsidy inflating the base, and admits marketing has been fragmented.
scores.quote: last year Q4 EBITDA of INR61 crores had a INR53 crores one-time subsidy from the government

scores.rationale: Much of the reported improvement traces to exogenous tailwinds — favourable wedding dates, GST/income-tax cuts, the US-India trade deal and FTAs — rather than demonstrated managerial skill, so the record does not separate cleanly from luck.
scores.quote: higher wedding dates leading to robust volume growth

scores.rationale: Raymond holds a mind-monopoly position in Indian premium suiting fabric, sustaining ~20% segment EBITDA margins and describing itself as the leader in luxury fabrics.
scores.quote: These offerings reinforce our leadership in luxury fabrics

scores.rationale: No evidence of switching costs or captive aftermarket; the dealer/trade network gives reach but B2B shirting and garmenting customers are freely substitutable.
scores.quote: strong demand from our B2B customers for our cotton and linen fabric shirting offerings

scores.rationale: The end market is fragmented and still largely unorganised, and in garmenting the customer clearly holds power — tariffs had to be absorbed via duty-paid terms and margins.
scores.quote: We also implemented duty-paid terms for US clients, which helped us keep the clients with us

scores.rationale: Pricing discipline held through a ~25% wool cost spike with no mention of discount wars, but apparel/garmenting entry barriers are inherently low.
scores.quote: Despite input cost volatility, including a nearly 25% increase in wool prices, our margins have remained resilient, driven by product mix, pricing discipline

scores.rationale: Weak unorganised players and small exporters unable to realign supply chains are ceding share to organised branded players, which Raymond is capturing.
scores.quote: reinforcing the shift towards organized, branded players

scores.rationale: The opposite of obscure — a centenary-celebrating iconic listed brand advertising through cricket and cinema and covered by multiple brokerages.
scores.quote: We have increased our presence in high-impact media like cricket and cinema

scores.rationale: Brand image supports premium pricing and inelastic occasion demand, delivering 20% branded-textile EBITDA margins and rising ASPs.
scores.quote: EBITDA margin reaching up to 20% in the second quarter of fiscal '26

scores.rationale: Quality/craftsmanship claims are made but there is no evidence customers buy Raymond primarily for certainty or that price is secondary to trust.
scores.quote: championing India's heritage of craftsmanship while redefining luxury

scores.rationale: Wide multi-format reach (1,675 stores plus EBO/MBO/online and a dealer trade channel) backed by auto-replenishment gives genuine accessibility.
scores.quote: our store count stood at 1,675 stores vis-a-vis 1,540 stores on 30th June 2024

scores.rationale: The retail side is correctly served with brand intangibles, but the corporate/B2B side (garmenting, shirting) shows no switching-cost lock-in and had to concede duty-paid terms to retain clients.
scores.quote: our new ventures are currently in strategic investment phase

scores.rationale: Functional fabric innovation exists (techno-series, stretch/stain-resistant, bio-polished merino) but it is incremental product development, not a deep multi-product tech edge with high R&D intensity.
scores.quote: we expanded our techno-series in fabrics ... stretch, wrinkle-resistant and stain-resistant

scores.rationale: Nothing in the calls speaks to a two-sided or self-reinforcing network.

A nationwide multi-format retail plus dealer network that rivals struggle to match is the clearest structural advantage, with the trade channel outgrowing the industry, though store rationalisation shows the footprint is not uniformly productive.
scores.quote: we exited 35 underperforming stores during this quarter

scores.rationale: Capex is clearly growth-led — 67 net new restaurants year-over-year to 577 (targeting ~600 by March 2026) and an almost-doubled India store count in three years, with restaurant EBITDA up 25.7% — though incremental returns are still modest at the company level.
scores.quote: we ended December 31 with 577 restaurants... That's an increase of, as of December, 67 year-over-year

scores.rationale: A&P is real and traffic-productive (Korean Kimchi digital campaign lifting APC, Rs.99 cafe campaign) but the mainstay is a long-running discount value platform on a franchised brand whose equity accrues largely to the franchisor.
scores.quote: You might have seen our ad on the Korean Kimchi that was aired digitally. And that has driven significant volumes at a very higher APC

scores.rationale: No formal R&D line, but there is credible in-house product/equipment development — a broiler designed in-house with a US vendor partner now in 250+ restaurants, and menu reformulation from customer research.
