scores.quote: this was designed in-house along with our vendor partner in the U.S. by Nitin and his team

scores.rationale: No acquisitions of any kind are discussed in the last-12-month calls; the only portfolio activity is a prospective exit of Popeyes, not a bolt-on.
No dividend, buyback, or capital-return policy is mentioned anywhere in the four calls.

Company-owned QSR restaurants are structurally asset-heavy (fit-outs, kiosks, broilers, leases) and the moat is a licensed franchise rather than an owned one, so high turnover with protection is absent.
scores.quote: 93% of our restaurants have self-ordering kiosks... We have just installed the new broiler in over 250 restaurants

scores.rationale: With only ~580 outlets versus far larger QSR rivals there is ample runway, and 11-12 consecutive quarters of positive SSSG culminating in 6.3% in a weak market indicates actual share capture.
scores.quote: we ended the fourth quarter with a 6.3% SSSG growth, which is the highest that we have achieved in the last 12 quarters

scores.rationale: India footprint expansion into new cities is executing well, but the overseas leg (Indonesia) has been a multi-year drag with Popeyes explicitly failing and slated to leave the portfolio.
scores.quote: That business is struggling... it has to be part of someone else's portfolio, not ours

scores.rationale: Growth is explicitly traffic/volume-led off a value price ladder (2for79/2for99), with premium mix only recently added as a second layer.
scores.quote: we continue to build volumes which is what I've been talking to you about for many quarters now... in the last 3 years, we have grown traffic in our dine-in business by 18%

scores.rationale: Management repeatedly flags a depressed discretionary eating-out cycle while the company's own SSSG accelerated to a 12-quarter high, consistent with sitting near a cyclical trough with an upturn ahead.
scores.quote: very excited to share with you the Q3 results in this very, very difficult and tough sales environment

scores.rationale: Indian organised QSR is a secularly under-penetrated end market, evidenced by the company adding 60+ net stores a year into new cities while still growing same-store traffic.
scores.quote: expanding the offerings to more and more consumers, as we also expand our portfolio, our footprint in different cities and different markets

scores.rationale: Organic-only growth, sustained cost discipline (~Rs.20 crore of Indonesia G&A taken out, utility and rent reduction programmes), store rationalisation and a willingness to exit a loss-making brand rather than double down.
scores.quote: We have saved almost Rs. 15 crores, and then subsequently Rs. 4.5 crores on top of that, so approximately Rs. 20 crores in saving on G&A

scores.rationale: The same barbell/digital/profitability strategy has been restated and compounded unchanged across all four calls, delivering 11-12 straight quarters of positive SSSG and a claimed 3-year doubling of stores.
scores.quote: priorities for India haven't changed. We are set on our goal, just, which we shared with you at least two years ago

scores.rationale: Commentary is operationally grounded and credits named functional leaders rather than the CEO, but the tone is markedly promotional and self-congratulatory, so it is neither celebrity-driven nor genuinely low-key.
scores.quote: congratulate them as well, as they build the digital

scores.rationale: A Great Place to Work certification plus repeated naming of an internal bench across supply chain, operations, marketing and CRM points to systematic talent building.
scores.quote: We were certified as a great place to work, which is a prestigious global credit that we received

scores.rationale: Management openly names its failures — Popeyes struggling, Indonesia sales hit by disruption, and it voluntarily discounts its own good metric as a small-base effect.
scores.quote: 51% growth in monthly active users over the previous year... 51% might be on a very small base

scores.rationale: The improvements look attributable to identifiable operating levers (supply chain proximity lifting gross margin 2.1%, lower delivery discounts, utility savings) rather than luck, but the base is low and absolute company EBITDA of ~Rs.40 crore on Rs.577 crore revenue keeps the skill claim unproven.
scores.quote: Gross margin, we delivered 69.9%... driven predominantly by the work we are doing on supply chain, getting the products closer to the restaurant

scores.rationale: Burger King India holds no monopoly-like position in the consumer's mind — it competes head-on in burgers and is now also pushing into cafe/coffee where incumbents are entrenched.
scores.quote: we have now covered the entire landscape here in India with cafes... we then went out to start talking about the coffee

scores.rationale: QSR customers face zero switching costs and there is no captive aftermarket; retention has to be manufactured through a CRM programme still in its acquisition phase.
scores.quote: we have started this journey, and we will continue to stay stable with this journey

scores.rationale: The Indian QSR market is fragmented and price-competitive with the customer holding all the negotiating power, forcing a permanent entry-price value ladder to keep traffic.
scores.quote: Value consistently, for the last 12 years, we've been driving value. The leadership in this industry in value, we maintain that

scores.rationale: Barriers are low and pricing is far from rational — a Rs.79/Rs.99 two-item entry price has run continuously for years, and delivery required deliberate discount withdrawal to restore margin.
scores.quote: on delivery, we have reduced discounts significantly

scores.rationale: Delivering 11-12 consecutive positive-SSSG quarters while describing the overall environment as very tough implies weaker peers are ceding traffic.
scores.quote: This is the 11th consecutive quarter that we are reporting positive sales

scores.rationale: This is a listed global-brand franchisee covered by mainstream brokerages with quarterly hosted calls — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: Restaurant Brands Asia Q3 FY '26 Earnings Conference Call hosted by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Limited

scores.rationale: Gross margin near 70% and a premium tier commanding higher APC show some image-based pull, but demand is still bought with a standing value promotion rather than pricing power.
scores.quote: Gross margin, we delivered 69.9%, well on our way to cross the 70% mark

scores.rationale: There is investment in consistency and product quality (customer research behind Kings Collection 2.0, fresher supply chain) but price, not trust, is clearly the primary purchase driver.
scores.quote: we have done extreme customer surveys and research, and we have enhanced the quality of those burgers

scores.rationale: Accessibility and direct customer intimacy are genuine strengths — ~580 outlets, kiosks in 93% of stores, 91-92% digital orders and an owned app running 80-100 transactions per restaurant per day.
scores.quote: we are doing upwards of between 80 to 100 transactions on our app on a daily basis per restaurant

scores.rationale: The customer base is purely retail and management is correctly building intangible/brand layers on top of value, but the intangible layer is early and the mix is still dominated by price-led entry offers.
scores.quote: now to add a layer of premium. So that -- this strategy of doing this together is where we ended up with a 6.3% SSSG growth

scores.rationale: Digital ordering, CRM and planned AI deployment are well executed operationally but are industry-standard QSR tooling bought from vendors, not a proprietary multi-product technology edge.
scores.quote: the next generation out of this digital platform is to integrate this into the AI

scores.rationale: No two-sided network exists; the app is a one-way loyalty and ordering channel whose value does not rise with the number of other users.
scores.quote: what CRM really does is build frequency of existing base of customers

scores.rationale: Supply chain is being genuinely improved by moving product closer to restaurants and adding suppliers, but a ~580-store footprint is well short of a reach rivals cannot match.
scores.quote: we are moving the food closer to the restaurant... less transportation time, less transportation costs

scores.rationale: Genuine growth investment in distribution and tech — 18 branches added in Q3 FY26 with more planned, in-housing of collections, core tech refresh — but incremental returns are still thin (PAT only INR214 crores in Q3).
scores.quote: we accelerated branch expansion by adding 18 branches and we will sustain this momentum to strengthen our physical footprint

scores.rationale: Brand spend is named only as a future use of the Emirates NBD capital, with no evidence of A&P building durable brand equity today.
scores.quote: invest meaningfully in technology, brand and distribution

scores.rationale: Digital product work (unified mobile app, Suvidha app for JLG, GIFT City products) is ongoing but is standard catch-up build, not R&D yielding differentiated products.
scores.quote: recent digital initiatives including the launch of our unified mobile app for all the customers and Suvidha app for our JLG customers

scores.rationale: The Emirates NBD transaction is a control sale rather than a bolt-on, though the merging piece (ENBD's India corporate branches) is small, complementary and on a similar tech platform per management.
scores.quote: Post completion, the Indian business of Emirates NBD will merge with RBL Bank

scores.rationale: No buybacks or dividend policy discussed; instead a ~US$3 billion preferential issue that massively dilutes existing holders and pushes ROE down for years.
scores.quote: Emirates NBD... will invest approximately US$3 billion through a preferential issue... to acquire a 60% stake

scores.rationale: Balance-sheet-heavy bank with weak asset productivity — cost-to-income 66.3%, PAT of only INR214 crores on INR1.03 lakh crores of advances, and no moat protecting returns.
scores.quote: Our cost-to-income ratio as a consequence is 66.3% versus 70.7% last quarter

scores.rationale: A small bank with clear runway, showing share capture in chosen niches — commercial banking +30% Y-o-Y and secured retail +25% Y-o-Y in Q3 FY26, well ahead of system credit growth.
scores.quote: secured retail assets grew 25% Y-o-Y... commercial banking business grew 30% Y-o-Y

scores.rationale: Credible, calibrated footprint expansion — new branches, selective entry into new geographies for commercial banking, GIFT City, plus an India–Middle East corridor opening via Emirates NBD.
scores.quote: selective expansion into the new geographies... access to the vibrant trade corridor between India and Middle East

scores.rationale: Growth is volume- and mix-shift-led with negative pricing: yields fell ~50 bps sequentially, NIM dropped from 4.89% to 4.5%, and the bank still pays roughly 1% more for deposits than large private peers.
scores.quote: our yield on advances was lower by 50 basis points sequentially

scores.rationale: Clear evidence of positioning at a cyclical trough with an identifiable upturn — margins bottomed in Q1 FY26 and rose to 4.63% by Q3, MFI collection efficiency at 99.5%, and unsecured advances stopped degrowing.
scores.quote: Q1 marked the low point for margins... the early bucket collection efficiency is 99.5%

scores.rationale: Indian retail credit and deposits are in secular expansion, and the bank's chosen segments (secured business loans, housing, gold, commercial SME) are structurally growing end markets.
scores.quote: secured business loans now above INR10,000 crores, and secured working capital and tractor finance portfolio crossing INR2,000 crores and INR3,000 crores

scores.rationale: Demonstrated risk discipline — shrank the JLG book 23%, adopted MFIN guardrails ahead of the industry, took 100% NPA provisioning on JLG and 75% on SMA buckets, and bought CGFMU cover on 90% of disbursals.
scores.quote: we proactively implemented enhanced credit guardrails, including MFIN Guardrails 2 as early as November that is well ahead of most of the players in the industry

scores.rationale: Management executed a consistent two-year granularization plan with tenacity, but independence is materially ceded by selling 60% control to Emirates NBD.
scores.quote: from being a midsized Indian bank to be a future-ready institution backed by one of the most respected financial groups in the region

scores.rationale: Calls are largely operational and data-dense, but the Q2 FY26 framing of the transaction leaned on promotional language rather than pure substance.
scores.quote: Yesterday was a landmark day for RBL Bank. We announced a historic strategic transaction

scores.rationale: A broad functional bench appears on calls (credit cards, treasury, branch banking, collections heads) and collections were brought in-house, but no systematic talent-development or succession programme is described.
scores.quote: we fast-tracked the in-house migration of collection services

scores.rationale: Management discloses bad news specifically and early — naming card stress, quantifying slippages, flagging two more weak quarters ahead, and explaining the NIM decline line by line.
scores.quote: The credit card slippages continue to be slightly elevated, and we expect this trend to continue for 2 quarters -- 2 more quarters

scores.rationale: The improving narrative rests heavily on a cyclical MFI recovery and an external capital windfall rather than demonstrated earning power — profitability remains weak with PAT of INR214 crores and margins only just recovering.
scores.quote: our net profit for the quarter was INR214 crores

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like position in any product — the bank is a small player in credit cards, MFI and SME lending, and even lost its Bajaj co-brand sourcing engine.
scores.quote: post cessation of our new sourcing through our Bajaj partnership

scores.rationale: No regional monopoly or captive aftermarket; 562 branches spread thinly and deposits must be won on price against larger banks.
scores.quote: despite headwinds of higher competitive intensity and tighter liquidity conditions for most of the year

scores.rationale: Indian banking is fragmented and RBL is a price-taker, paying roughly 100 bps more for deposits than large private banks, meaning customers hold the negotiating power.
scores.quote: if you look at our cost of deposits, I would say, give or take, we are maybe 1% or so higher than, let's say, the large private sector banks

scores.rationale: Bank licensing is a genuine regulatory barrier, but deposit pricing is competitive rather than rational and ownership has just changed hands entirely.
scores.quote: headwinds of higher competitive intensity

scores.rationale: The calls do not identify weaker competitors ceding share; the industry stress described hit RBL alongside peers rather than creating share donators.
The opposite of under-the-radar — a listed, heavily covered bank that has just attracted a US$3 billion strategic bid drawing broad analyst and capital attention.
scores.quote: Congratulations team for the landmark deal, really fantastic

scores.rationale: No image-driven pricing power — the bank must pay above-market deposit rates and is deliberately narrowing that gap rather than commanding a premium.
scores.quote: building granular liabilities with a narrower cost of deposit gap versus larger peers

scores.rationale: Trust is currently a weakness priced into a higher cost of funds and AA- rating, though the Emirates NBD backing is expected to improve perceived safety and rating.
scores.quote: we would definitely expect the rating upgrades to happen

scores.rationale: Genuine access advantage in its niches through branches plus the wholly owned RFL business-correspondent network, with over 60% of retail asset leads now branch-sourced and all gold loans originated in-branch.
scores.quote: With over 60% of the leads now sourced from the branches. In fact, our entire organic gold business originates through branches

scores.rationale: The retail/wholesale mix at 59:41 with a cross-sell-led strategy is coherent, but there is no evidence of intangible pull with retail or switching-cost lock-in with corporates.
scores.quote: deepening customer relationship through higher product penetration across our large existing customer base

scores.rationale: Technology is a catch-up item, not an edge — the core is being refreshed for stability and the acquirer's platform is described as merely similar.
scores.quote: as we embark on a tech refresh to strengthen our core and simplify the front-end experience

scores.rationale: No two-sided network dynamic is evident; growth comes from branch and BC sourcing, and the loss of the Bajaj co-brand showed the franchise did not compound on its own.
scores.quote: The cards in force grew sequentially after 6 to 7 quarters of reduction

scores.rationale: The 562-branch plus RFL BC network is a real and improving sourcing channel, but at INR400 crores monthly branch disbursal it is subscale versus larger banks and not a reach rivals cannot match.
scores.quote: The disbursal from branches is at a monthly run rate of INR400 crores

scores.rationale: The NBFC analogue of growth capex — balance-sheet deployment — is high and rising, with record H1 FY26 disbursements up 27% YoY earning a 22% return on net worth, though loan-book growth of only 7% shows the incremental deployment is partly offset by runoff.
scores.quote: highest ever half-yearly disbursements of Rs. 1,15,470 crores in this half year, which is a growth of 27%

scores.rationale: No advertising or promotion spend is discussed in any of the four calls.
No R&D spend or programme is disclosed; the only technology reference is an award for generative AI implementation, which is not R&D evidence.
scores.quote: technology awards for generative AI implementation

scores.rationale: Management notes Maharatna status permits JVs, subsidiaries and M&A, but no acquisition was executed or discussed in the last twelve months.
scores.quote: It also allows us strategic investments by incorporating JV, subsidiaries and M&A activities in India and abroad.

scores.rationale: A coherent, rising quarterly-interim dividend policy — INR18/share in FY25 (+13% YoY, INR4,740 crores) and INR9.20 already in H1 FY26 — but distribution is dividend-only with no buyback and no valuation-linked discipline.
scores.quote: total dividend of almost INR18 per share for the financial year '24-'25, which is a growth of almost 13%

scores.rationale: REC is structurally asset-heavy — a INR5.82 lakh crore balance sheet levered 6.07x earning a 2.89% spread — the opposite of asset-light, even though the AAA/sovereign-parity rating provides a funding moat.
scores.quote: The debt-equity ratio or the gearing ratio of the company has improved to 6.07x.

scores.rationale: Renewables and infrastructure lending are growing fast (RE book +49% YoY), but the overall loan book grew only 7% as banks refinanced away large exposures, so there is no net share capture in the last year.
scores.quote: The loan book has reached Rs. 5.82 lakh crores, a growth of 7% YoY.

scores.rationale: Expansion is entirely domestic; the only overseas activity is funding diversification through yen and USD green bonds, not entry into new lending geographies.
scores.quote: maiden yen bond issuance of JPY61 billion and the USD Green bond issuance of $500 million

scores.rationale: Growth is volume-led — yields are flat at ~10.06% and spread slipped to 2.89% in Q2 FY26 from 2.96% in Q1 — with earnings driven by disbursement volume and NPA reversals rather than pricing or mix.
scores.quote: The yield on loan assets for the half year was 10.06%. The cost of funds at 7.17%. The consequent interest spread was 2.89%

scores.rationale: The power-financing cycle is clearly in an upswing with DISCOM legacy dues collapsing from INR1.35 lakh crores to ~INR25,000 crores and the ACS-ARR gap narrowing, though REC is already well into the upturn rather than at the bottom.
scores.quote: The legacy dues of the generation and transmission companies, which stood at INR1.35 lakh crores roughly 3 years back, has reduced to nearly INR25,000 crores.

scores.rationale: The end market is in secular expansion — India's energy transition, RDSS distribution reform and the 1-crore-home rooftop solar programme — with REC targeting a INR10 lakh crore book and INR3 lakh crores of RE disbursement by 2030.
scores.quote: We have targeted a INR10 lakh crore loan book by the year 2030.

scores.rationale: Growth is fully organic with no M&A, capital adequacy at 23.74% against a 15% requirement and gearing improving to 6.07x, indicating prudent leverage — though as a PSU much of the lending is policy-directed rather than independently chosen.
scores.quote: The capital adequacy ratio is sitting comfortably at 23.74%, as against the RBI requirement of 15%.

scores.rationale: Long-dated 2030 targets are articulated, but the chairmanship turned over again within the window to a deputed IAS officer with no prior REC tenure, so continuity and independence of the leadership are structurally weak.
scores.quote: Shri Jitendra Srivastava has assumed charge of CMD REC on 22nd April 2025. He is an IAS officer of year 2000 batch from Bihar Cadre.

scores.rationale: Management is bureaucratic and non-celebrity in style, but the calls devote substantial airtime to award-collecting self-promotion rather than substance.
scores.quote: So you name it, we have it.

scores.rationale: REC runs its own training institute, but the top job is filled by government deputation from outside the organisation rather than an internal pipeline, and no talent-development programme is discussed on the calls.
scores.quote: He has held other several key administrative and leadership roles across the Government of India and the Government of Bihar.

scores.rationale: Management volunteers unflattering detail — quantifying how prepayments suppressed loan growth, naming each stressed asset with expected recovery percentages, and admitting NCLT resolution timing may slip beyond the quarter.
scores.quote: Had the prepayment not been received, the growth in our loan book would have been close to 18% on a year-on-year basis.

scores.rationale: Strong headline results rest largely on structural PSU privileges — sovereign-parity ratings, nodal-agency mandates and 86% state-sector lending that carries no NPAs — rather than demonstrable management skill, so the record does not survive a halo-adjusted reading.
scores.quote: there are no NPAs in the state sector

scores.rationale: REC holds a quasi-monopoly administrative position as Government of India's nodal implementing agency for the flagship power schemes, a role no private lender can occupy.
scores.quote: We are the nodal agencies for various Government of India flagship schemes such as RDSS, Saubhagya, Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana, Rooftop solar.

scores.rationale: Switching costs are demonstrably low — roughly INR35,000 crores of prepayments in FY25 plus an INR11,400 crore Kaleshwaram prepayment in Q2 FY26 show borrowers refinance away freely when banks price cheaper.
scores.quote: we have recovered a prepayment of Rs. 11,400 crores from Kaleshwaram Irrigation Project

scores.rationale: REC operates in a narrow field of power-sector lenders alongside parent PFC and IREDA, but state borrowers retain real negotiating power and use it, as the repeated prepayment-driven refinancing shows.
scores.quote: This year, we have received prepayments of almost INR15,000 crores in quarter 4 of '24-'25

scores.rationale: High barriers exist via AAA ratings and Maharatna/nodal status, and spread discipline is maintained within a guided 2.75%-3% band, but commercial banks compete aggressively enough on rate to pull assets off the book.
scores.quote: we will maintain the spread in the range of 2.75% to 3% and the NIM in the range of 3.5% to 3.75%

scores.rationale: No weak competitors are identified to take share from; the flow in the last year runs the other way, with better-priced bank funding taking assets away from REC.
scores.quote: because of some prepayment, the loan book has grown by only 14%

scores.rationale: REC is a Maharatna PSU with quarterly broker-hosted calls, heavy FII ownership at ~18-21% and a roster of public awards — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: The FPI and FII continue to hold more than 20% in REC since IPO in 2008

scores.rationale: The product is undifferentiated credit with no image-driven pricing power; the ~2.9% spread is set by funding cost arbitrage, and borrowers switch on price.
scores.quote: The yields on our assets has improved to 10.05%. The cost of our funds stand at around 7.11%, and our resultant spread is at 2.94%.

scores.rationale: State utilities come to REC for the certainty of long-tenor, scheme-linked power-sector funding backed by five decades of sector expertise, not for the cheapest rate — evidenced by 86-87% of the book being state sector.
scores.quote: the state sector constitutes 86% of the portfolio and the private sector 14%

scores.rationale: REC maintains 20 regional offices, state offices and a dedicated training centre giving it direct, on-the-ground intimacy with DISCOMs across the country.
scores.quote: Regional Offices: Bengaluru, Bhopal, Bhubaneswar, Chennai, Dehradun, Guwahati, Hyderabad, Jaipur, Jammu, Kolkata

scores.rationale: The customer base is correctly corporate/institutional and served on reliability and long-tenor certainty, but the lock-in half of the equation is missing given repeated large prepayments.
scores.quote: we provide both capex and non-capex loans to state electricity boards, state power utilities, power departments

scores.rationale: There is no product-technology edge — only process certifications and an internal generative-AI award, neither of which delivers a differentiated customer benefit.
scores.quote: REC became the first Indian public sector NBFC to get ISO 31000:2018 certificate

scores.rationale: The lending model is bilateral and shows no self-reinforcing two-sided dynamic; scale brings funding cost benefits, not network effects, and nothing in the calls suggests otherwise.

REC's nationwide office network plus its administrative reach as nodal agency monitoring 19 states and 32 DISCOMs gives it an origination and servicing footprint in power lending that private rivals cannot replicate.
scores.quote: we have been assigned 19 states and union territories covering 32 DISCOMs for overseeing and monitoring the implementation of the RDSS scheme

scores.rationale: Investment is platform/capability-led rather than heavy fixed capex (CloudQuarks 2.0, AI lab, presales teams) and is being funded while returns stay high, with ROCE at 22% in FY26.
scores.quote: ROCE was at 22% despite the investments we are making in the growth areas

scores.rationale: No A&P spend, brand-building budget or marketing efficiency is discussed in any of the four calls beyond attending trade events like GITEX.
No formal R&D line, but repeated capability spend is converting into shipped products — CloudQuarks 2.0, an AI capability centre in Chennai and an AI Exchange marketplace with 200+ agents.
scores.quote: We have launched an AI Exchange, which is like a marketplace with over 200 AI agents

scores.rationale: The only M&A evidence in the window is unwinding a prior acquisition — Arena losses every quarter, divestment of Paynet and the Vodafone contract, and a trade-name impairment hitting group PAT by INR75.2 crores.
scores.quote: an impairment loss has been recognized and disclosed as an exceptional item... impact on the group PAT after minority interest is INR75.2 crores

scores.rationale: Dividends, buybacks or any distribution policy are not mentioned in the excerpts.

Extremely asset-light and capital-efficient — INR119,347 crores of revenue on working capital of 28-30 days with 22% ROCE — but the moat protecting it is distribution scale, not a pricing moat (PAT margin only ~1.3%).
scores.quote: lowering our working capital days to 30 days. ROCE was at 22%

scores.rationale: Evidence of active share capture — ranked #1 IT distributor in India three years running with the gap to #2 widening, upcountry business up 45%, and SSG growing 31-48% — though its core position is already leading, limiting runway there.
scores.quote: this is the third consecutive year in a row, and we are also happy to share that the lead has increased between number 1 and number 2

scores.rationale: Broad-based multi-geography growth (India 25-50%, UAE 19-23%, GCCL 22-29%, Africa 8-14%) with new SSG-led entries into ASEAN, CIS and South Africa, offset by the Turkey (Arena) misstep.
scores.quote: our geographical expansions in the recent period are all focused on SSG, be it ASEAN countries, be it CIS countries, even South Africa

scores.rationale: Growth is volume- and deal-driven with no own pricing power (PC uplift came from vendor component-shortage price increases, mobility is explicitly volume-led), though mix is genuinely improving as higher-margin SSG rose from 15% to 17-18% of top line.
scores.quote: While this segment remains volume driven, it continues to play a critical role for Redington in driving scale

scores.rationale: The PC end-market appears early in an upcycle — refresh cycle signs in Q2 turned into 21% then 28% ESG growth with AI-PC penetration in India commercial rising from 28% to 41%.
scores.quote: We see signs of the PC refresh cycle. And we also see increased AI PC penetration

scores.rationale: Core growth engine sits in secular end-markets — cloud, cybersecurity, software and data centres — with SSG compounding at 29-40% and industry distribution mix shifting structurally from hardware to software.
scores.quote: globally for all distribution, hardware has actually declined... Software has grown 20% plus, and software has become 31% of all tech distribution globally

scores.rationale: Organic-only growth in the window, active pruning of weak assets (Paynet, Lira/Vodafone contract), tight working capital at 28-30 days and opex growing slower than revenue every quarter.
scores.quote: FY26 has been a year of strong growth, transformation and disciplined execution... maintained capital discipline

scores.rationale: A multi-year SSG build has been executed to plan — 2x revenue over three years, vertical reorganised globally, with a stated ambition to double again — and they have stuck with the Arena turnaround through repeated painful quarters.
scores.quote: for the last 3 years, we have grown 2x in this 3-year period. Our expectation... in the next 3 years, we should be more than doubling our revenue

scores.rationale: Communication is operationally detailed and largely substance-driven, but the calls lean noticeably on award citations and superlatives ('best quarter so far') in every opening statement.
scores.quote: we are also proud to share the news that VAR India for FY '25 has awarded Redington as number 1 IT distributor in India

scores.rationale: Systematic capability building via Redington Academy certifications, technical presales/solutioning teams and AI learning centres, plus a visibly deep bench of named business leaders presented at the June investor event.
scores.quote: investing in the Redington Academy to create more certified professionals within the company and, of course, within our channel partners

scores.rationale: Consistently owns bad news in detail — Arena losses quantified every quarter, the trade-name impairment, the TSG 7% decline explained by deal timing, war-related opex — and the CFO publicly corrected IR's SSG growth figure to strip out a currency benefit.
scores.quote: Just now Palak said 37%. I just want to correct that 37% is basis Indian rupee reporting... which has an advantage because of the depreciation

scores.rationale: Strong headline results are partly exogenous — component-shortage price increases, a PC refresh cycle and large lumpy deals (INR1,100 crores in TSG) — while PAT margin stayed flat near 1.3%, so the record numbers should not be read as proof of durable skill.
scores.quote: PC demand was strong, partially driven by the component shortage, as I mentioned before, and anticipated larger price increases

scores.rationale: Holds a leading, trusted position in distributors' and brands' minds but nothing monopoly-like — no aftermarket or captive service annuity of its own beyond a sub-1% professional services book.
scores.quote: A defining feature of Redington's market perception is trust

scores.rationale: Hardware distribution is explicitly transactional with no switching costs, though SSG introduces genuine stickiness with 74% of its revenue recurring.
scores.quote: unlike in the hardware business where the relationship is more transactional... That's not the case in the case of SSG. Here, it is more an annuity business

scores.rationale: The structure is a concentrated distributor field where Redington leads, but the ~1.3% PAT margin shows both vendors and channel partners retain heavy negotiating power.
scores.quote: PAT percentage was at 1.41% for the group

scores.rationale: Scale, credit and logistics create real barriers — the lead over #2 is widening and branded players are taking share from unorganised white label — with no evidence of discount wars in the calls.
scores.quote: desktop PCs saw a surge as brands gained share from the white label due to the component shortage

scores.rationale: Identifiable weak donors exist — the widening gap to the #2 distributor and white-label assemblers ceding share to branded PCs that Redington distributes.
scores.quote: the lead has increased between number 1 and number 2

scores.rationale: This is a highly visible $13.5 billion listed leader running dedicated investor days and publicising industry awards — the opposite of an ignored niche.
scores.quote: We closed the year at INR 119,347 crores, nearly $13.5 billion

scores.rationale: No image- or taste-driven pricing power; margins are wafer-thin at ~1.3% PAT and growth depends on vendor brands' pull rather than Redington's own.
scores.quote: Overall, PAT percentage was at 1.41% for the group

scores.rationale: Trust and reliability are the explicit value proposition, validated by the 'most trusted distributor' award and by maintaining business continuity for partners through the West Asia conflict.
scores.quote: our teams on the ground demonstrated strong resilience, ensuring business continuity after multiple data center attacks

scores.rationale: Access and intimacy are the core strength — direct-to-retail execution, 45% upcountry growth, and over a third of India business now transacting through its own digital platform.
scores.quote: More than a third of our business in India this quarter went through the digital platform

scores.rationale: The benefit type is well matched to a mostly corporate/channel customer base — recurring annuity contracts and lifecycle management for enterprise cloud/software, scale-and-reach for consumer mobility.
scores.quote: About 74 percentage of our last year revenue is recurring

scores.rationale: It resells others' technology (Microsoft, AWS, Autodesk, Red Hat, Fortinet, Palo Alto); its own tech is a distribution platform and AI go-to-market layer, useful but not a deep proprietary edge.
scores.quote: The top six vendors are Microsoft, AWS, Autodesk, Red Hat, Fortinet, Palo Alto

scores.rationale: Early but real two-sided ecosystem forming — the AI Exchange and marketplaces deliberately bring ISVs, AI innovators and customers together through the partner network, though it is only quarters old.
scores.quote: creating ecosystems in just marketplaces where we can bring managed print service providers and ISVs together

scores.rationale: Reach is the durable advantage — #1 in India with a widening lead, across India/UAE/KSA/GCCL/Africa, extended by upcountry expansion and platform-led distribution that rivals have not matched.
scores.quote: There was continued traction in upcountry expansion initiatives. We grew 45% in the up-country part of the business

scores.rationale: Growth spend is real but deliberately asset-light — new stores held to return thresholds, marketplace warehouses scaled from two to seven, plus SAP — with FY26 PAT up 32.4% suggesting decent incremental returns, though no capex figures are disclosed.
scores.quote: from a two warehouse to a seven warehouse... It is not the store count that we are chasing. Every location we open has to clear our return thresholds from day one.

scores.rationale: Management claims measurable A&P payback via brand-led activations, but gives no spend numbers and the always-on 70%-off construct means promotion is discount-driven as much as equity-building.
scores.quote: Our marketing investments in the brand have driven measurable improvement in both new customer acquisition and repeat purchase rates... RedTape 10K Run in Delhi and Chandigarh

scores.rationale: No R&D function or spend is disclosed; what exists is product/material development (EVA to ETPU, premium leather, new brand launches) that is lifting ASPs but is design work, not durable technical R&D.
scores.quote: We are in fact going away from basic EVA shoes to ETPU shoes. We have also launched a premium leather collection

scores.rationale: No acquisitions were discussed in any of the three calls — all four brands (RedTape, Ozark, Bond Street, Mode) are stated to be homegrown — so there is no M&A record to judge.
scores.quote: We have built a new brand name Ozark

scores.rationale: A final dividend of INR2 per INR2 face-value share was declared against FY26 PAT of INR244 crores, but no distribution policy, payout target, or buyback was articulated.
scores.quote: the Board has recommended a final INR2 per equity share on the face value of INR2

scores.rationale: The stated capital-light manufacturing model is undermined by very heavy working capital — 175 days of inventory on sales (over 300 on COGS), worse than Bata/Metro, with no aging provisioning — and rising working-capital days flagged in Q2.
scores.quote: we have 175 days of inventory on sales. And on COGS... this number is higher than 300... significantly higher when I look at your peers such as Metro or Bata

scores.rationale: Revenue grew 19.6% with 17.8% Q4 SSSG off a small base in a deeply underpenetrated branded market, indicating genuine share capture with ample runway, though no market-share data is given.
scores.quote: Our SSSG, which is the same-store sales growth was 17.8% in Q4... revenue came at INR2,415 crores, a growth of 19.6% over FY25

scores.rationale: Expansion is domestic-only but well spread — 223 exclusive showrooms across 161 cities and omnichannel reach in ~300 cities focused on Tier 2/3 — with no evidence of the brand travelling internationally.
scores.quote: an omnichannel presence across 300 cities... The Tier 2 and Tier 3 opportunities are far from played out

scores.rationale: Mix and ASP are improving (8-10% footwear ASP uptick, premium leather and Ozark at INR2,100-2,500), but FY26's acceleration was explicitly volume-led by the GST cut and the brand never sells at MRP, capping true pricing power.
scores.quote: The GST reduction on footwear below INR2,500 was a meaningful volume catalyst for us... we are a brand, which offers discounts all year long. We don't sell anything on MRP

scores.rationale: The business appears to be coming off a cyclical trough — a soft H1 with GST-transition hesitation and prior-year BIS/Bangladesh supply disruption — into an accelerating discretionary upcycle.
scores.quote: the first half had its moments of softness, the second half and particularly Q3, carrying into Q4, showed us clearly that the underlying demand... is very much intact

scores.rationale: The end market is in clear secular expansion — unorganized-to-organized migration in branded footwear and lifestyle apparel, low penetration, and rising per-capita discretionary spend in Tier 2/3.
scores.quote: the structural shift from unorganized to organized retail in both footwear and apparel continues to work in our favour... deeply underpenetrated relative to its eventual potential

scores.rationale: Growth is entirely organic with no M&A, non-performing stores are closed, new stores must clear return hurdles and margins expanded from 17.5% to 19%, but the 250-day inventory build was undisciplined capital allocation.
scores.quote: we do have opened some stores, but we have also closed some non-performing stores... we had reached a high of 250 days plus also

scores.rationale: Management points to a deliberately built multi-brand architecture with distinct occasion positioning that is only now paying off, alongside 30 years of brand equity — evidence of a long-held plan being executed.
scores.quote: the multi-brand architecture we have built over the years is genuinely starting to work for us, and it's starting to work the way we intended

scores.rationale: Calls are run by the Whole-Time Director and CFO rather than promoter-celebrities, but the CFO's opening is promotional in tone and there is no strong evidence either way.
scores.quote: what this company has is a set of most powerful brands that this country has seen

scores.rationale: People are named as an investment priority but with no detail on development systems or succession, and the CFO seat changed hands (Abhinav Jain to Vivek Agnihotri) with two MDs/Chairman exiting since FY23.
scores.quote: we have been investing behind three brands; brand, people and technology

scores.rationale: Disclosure quality is weak — the Q2 opening garbled its own revenue history (INR218 crores for 2025), store counts are inconsistent across calls (623/513 vs 223), the lease-liability and dead-stock questions went unanswered, and no inventory provisioning is done at all.
scores.quote: We do not measure as such. There is no method to measure as such... We don't do as such any provisioning

scores.rationale: The headline FY26 numbers flatter the operator — a large part of the volume came from an exogenous GST cut and an easy base after prior-year BIS/Bangladesh stockouts, so results should not be read as proof of skill.
scores.quote: The GST reduction on footwear below INR2,500 was a meaningful volume catalyst for us, specifically because nearly all of our products sit in that bracket

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like position exists — it is one of many brands in casual footwear and apparel, and even its own newer brands are described as fighting in a crowded segment with no aftermarket or services annuity.
scores.quote: Both brands continue to hold their ground during the year in what is a very competitive segment

scores.rationale: Discretionary fashion retail carries no switching costs — the customer can buy any brand on the same Myntra or Flipkart page — and management admits it cannot even measure repeat versus new customers.
scores.quote: It is primarily through the Flipkart's and Myntra's of the world

scores.rationale: The industry is fragmented rather than an oligopoly, with a large unorganized segment plus multiple listed peers (Bata, Metro and others) and consumers holding full choice.
scores.quote: significantly higher when I look at your peers such as Metro or Bata

scores.rationale: Barriers are low — the company itself launched three new brands in a single year — and pricing is structurally irrational, with a permanent 70%-off construct on an inflated MRP rather than disciplined price realisation.
scores.quote: The strategy is such that the MRP is jacked up and the 70% off is a constant factor for our customer

scores.rationale: A large unorganized footwear and apparel base in Tier 2/3 towns is the explicit donator pool the company is taking share from, though organized peers are also chasing the same shift.
scores.quote: The Indian consumer, especially in Tier 2 and Tier 3 towns where the majority of our stores sit, is making a clear and steady shift towards organized branded product

scores.rationale: This is not an ignored niche — a ~INR2,400 crore consumer brand with calls hosted by Nuvama and EY and questions from IIFL Capital sits squarely in the attention of institutional capital.
scores.quote: First question is from the line of Sameer Gupta from IIFL Capital

scores.rationale: Gross margin of 43.4% and 30 years of brand equity indicate some image-based pull and ASPs are rising, but a brand that never sells at MRP and discounts all year is renting demand rather than commanding it.
scores.quote: gross margin is 43.4%... we are a brand, which offers discounts all year long

scores.rationale: There is brand trust that lets the flagship carry consumers into adjacent categories, but the purchase is fashion-discretionary where price is clearly not secondary, given the permanent discount architecture.
scores.quote: The consumer who already trusts RedTape for footwear does not need a lot of convincing to pick up a bag or a pair of sunglasses at the same store

scores.rationale: Accessibility is a genuine strength — 623 retail touchpoints, 70:30 offline:online split run on a self-operated marketplace model, and warehouses deliberately pushed closer to consumers for quick commerce.
scores.quote: we have opened some new online warehouses in Ludhiana, Hyderabad, Howrah... because in this world of quick commerce and everything, you have to be closer to the customers

scores.rationale: The customer base is purely retail and the benefits offered are correctly matched — brand image, store experience and omnichannel convenience — with sales booked B2C rather than wholesaled to intermediaries.
scores.quote: whatever sales you see in our online portals is actually B2C

scores.rationale: No technology edge is claimed beyond an ERP rollout and material upgrades; SAP is table-stakes infrastructure, not a differentiator, and R&D intensity is not disclosed.
scores.quote: Since the introduction of SAP, we have seen improvements in the overall reporting systems

scores.rationale: The business model is single-sided brand retail with no self-reinforcing network; scale benefits described are purely vendor-negotiation and operating leverage.
scores.quote: we have more negotiation power because our volumes have grown up very highly

scores.rationale: Distribution reach is broad and multi-format — 623 retail touchpoints across offline EBOs, factory shops, SIS and seven owned marketplace warehouses spanning 300 cities — but it is matchable by larger incumbents rather than unassailable.
scores.quote: 303 online stores in 171 cities, 186 offline stores, exclusive showrooms in 134 cities, 6 factory shops in three cities, 9 shop-in-shop outlet in eight cities, and SIS model of 119 stores in 58 cities

scores.rationale: Real growth capex is visible — Silvassa wind facility, EV fleet additions and capitalisation lifting depreciation — but incremental returns are unproven (mobility at -50% margin, wind revenue only starting in Q4).
scores.quote: Depreciation increase is aligned with the capacity expansion and asset capitalization, positioning us for higher throughput in the coming quarters.

scores.rationale: No A&P spend is discussed in any of the four calls; only a fleet re-branding from Refex eVeelz to Refex Mobility is mentioned.
scores.quote: We have transitioned our green mobility fleet branding from Refex eVeelz to Refex Mobility

scores.rationale: Internal technology build-out in wind produced a differentiated 5.3 MW LIDAR-equipped platform with ALMM approval and Rs.1,860 crores of cumulative orders, though no R&D spend or long-run efficiency data is given.
scores.quote: the business also achieved an important milestone with the receipt of ALMM approval for our wind turbine platform

scores.rationale: No acquisitions in the window — corporate activity is internal restructuring (merger of RGML into RIL then demerger of mobility) and a new wholly-owned subsidiary, so there is no bolt-on record to judge.
scores.quote: first the merger of RGML into RIL, followed by a de-merger of Mobility Undertaking from RIL into a separate listed entity

scores.rationale: A modest Rs.0.50 dividend was reinstated after being skipped the prior year for reinvestment, with no buybacks and no stated distribution framework.
scores.quote: the Board has declared a dividend of INR0.50 per share... barring last year when we prioritized reinvestment into growth initiatives

scores.rationale: Ash and coal handling turns capital reasonably as a service contract business, but mobility is asset-heavy with EMIs running before utilisation and the group is now adding a capital-intensive turbine plant, with no protective moat cited.
scores.quote: Green Mobility requires a lot of time for stabilization and deployment of vehicle from the time we own the vehicle, while our EMIs get calculated from the day we acquire

scores.rationale: Order book in ash and coal grew to roughly Rs.1,200–1,500 crores with repeated new contract wins, and wind won marquee first customers, indicating a small player capturing share rather than a saturated incumbent.
scores.quote: There is already an open order of close to about Rs.1500 Crores for the ash and coal handling business

scores.rationale: Expansion is domestic site-by-site with a claimed nationwide presence and a new Silvassa facility; no international or premium-brand travel is evidenced.
scores.quote: With our execution capabilities, operational expertise and nationwide presence

scores.rationale: Top-line moves are explicitly volume/monsoon driven, though Q4 margin expansion to 20.1% came from business mix rather than price, and wind is priced to be competitive rather than premium.
scores.quote: This improvement was driven primarily by higher ash and coal volumes handled during the quarter.

scores.rationale: The core business is emerging from a monsoon-depressed first half into sequential recovery, and wind is entering the start of an execution upcycle with policy support.
scores.quote: Q3 FY2026 marked a very strong sequential recovery for Refex... as site accessibility and ground condition normalized

scores.rationale: Both main end markets are described as in secular expansion — regulator-driven ash utilisation compliance and rising domestic wind capacity addition targets, with an added EV policy push.
scores.quote: While we see there's a lot of pressure from the government and various authorities on the environment compliances, we see this division growing exponentially.

scores.rationale: They pruned non-core verticals (power trading wound down, refrigerant gas in liquidation, mobility demerged) and claim no fundraising need, but simultaneously entered capital-intensive turbine manufacturing, drawing direct investor criticism of capital allocation.
scores.quote: It seems to be there is a miscalculation in your capital allocation, sir.

scores.rationale: Management defended a contrarian long-horizon bet on a 5.3 MW turbine against pointed analyst skepticism with specific logistics, hub-height and generation arguments, and followed through to first deliveries.
scores.quote: So I think these technologies are definitely proven around the world and the orders we have got are from the likes of Jindal Steel, Torrent and KP Green

scores.rationale: Calls are plain and analyst-light with no promotional celebrity posture, but the December income tax search and disputed press coverage put management in the news during the window.
scores.quote: we had an income tax search on 9th of December in our office premises and my house and the senior executive

scores.rationale: Headcount was raised 70% for project readiness and a CEO was hired for mobility, but the key appointment was external and no internal development pipeline is described.
scores.quote: we have appointed Mr. Anirudh Arun as our CEO for the Green Mobility vertical

scores.rationale: They disclosed loss-making segment margins unprompted, admitted mobility is a drag, addressed the tax search directly and named the businesses being exited, though weak quarters lean heavily on the monsoon explanation.
scores.quote: Green Mobility has been minus 50%. Power trading also has been negative.

scores.rationale: Headline Q4 optics (EBITDA margin 20.1% vs 10.4%, PAT +67%) sit against full-year standalone revenue falling to Rs.2,039 crores from Rs.2,259 crores, so results owe much to portfolio pruning and mix rather than demonstrated operating skill.
scores.quote: While the revenue were lower year-on-year basis, the moderation was largely attributed to the plant transitions and restructuring

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like standing is evidenced; ash handling is a contracted service to power plants at 7–10% margins and wind is a late challenger to established manufacturers.
scores.quote: That is already it has been given it is anywhere in the range from 7% to 10%.

scores.rationale: There is some embedded-site stickiness in ash handling contracts, but nothing in the calls demonstrates captive aftermarket economics or hard switching costs.
scores.quote: Our contracts remain intact. Customer relationships are strong

scores.rationale: Customers are large power utilities and IPPs awarding tendered contracts, and the wind segment is contested by established players, leaving negotiating power with the buyer.
scores.quote: we see different listed company... how are we competing with them since these are established players in the market

scores.rationale: Low single-digit-to-low-teens margins and the company's own recent entry into wind manufacturing point to modest entry barriers, with pricing set competitively rather than rationally protected.
scores.quote: We are competitive in the market. We already got two orders that shows that our price is competitive

scores.rationale: Incumbent turbine makers still selling 3.3–4.2 MW machines are positioned as the source of share for the larger 5.3 MW platform, which management claims yields 3–3.5% more generation.
scores.quote: this will definitely give you more than 3% to 3.5% of additional generation

scores.rationale: Ash and coal handling is an unglamorous compliance-driven logistics niche with little competitive or capital attention, and calls are attended largely by individual investors and small offices.
scores.quote: Demand for integrated ash logistics, material handling and environment compliance solutions is steadily increasing.

scores.rationale: Gross margins are structurally thin (COGS 79–81%, ash handling margin ~11.8%, refrigerant gas 0.9%) with no image- or taste-driven pricing power.
scores.quote: While cost of goods sold increased from 79% to 81%, this was largely due to a change in margin mix

scores.rationale: Customers buy compliance certainty and uninterrupted plant operation, which management cites as service stickiness, and wind buyers conducted detailed diligence before ordering.
scores.quote: Our long-term fundamentals remain robust, which are high service stickiness

scores.rationale: On-site nationwide execution teams and direct enterprise engagement give close customer proximity in both ash handling and mobility.
scores.quote: teams on the ground engaging closely with the corporate clients to chart a ready to deploy fleet expansion

scores.rationale: The customer base is entirely corporate — thermal power plants, IPPs like Jindal Steel and Torrent, and enterprise fleet clients — and the offer is framed on reliability and compliance rather than consumer intangibles, matching benefit to customer type.
scores.quote: teams actively engaging enterprise clients and working towards calibrated fleet expansion with a clear focus on utilization and unit economics

scores.rationale: A differentiated 5.3 MW LIDAR turbine with ALMM approval plus technology-led ash utilisation suggests a real but young and single-product technical edge, not yet validated by returns.
scores.quote: all our machines contain LIDAR, which actually detects the direction of the wind... which is the first time in the country

scores.rationale: The businesses are contract services and equipment manufacturing with no two-sided or self-reinforcing network described anywhere in the calls.
Nationwide multi-site ash handling execution and secured heavy-logistics capability for large turbines constitute reach that is hard to replicate quickly, though not shown to be unmatched.
scores.quote: We have spoken to all the large logistics companies in the country... All these logistics companies have confirmed that they can transport and move these equipments

scores.rationale: Capex is small and shrinking relative to revenue (INR 62 crores net of subsidy on INR 2,790 crores FY25 sales) and management explicitly says no capacity addition is needed, indicating maintenance-level rather than growth spend.
scores.quote: The company has incurred a capex of INR 62 crores net of capital subsidy... regarding capacity enhancement, we already have a good capacity. So it's not there right now... Not required.

scores.rationale: A&P was cut pro-cyclically during the demand downturn to protect margins (3% of revenue in FY25, guided ~4% in FY26), which is margin management rather than durable brand-equity building.
scores.quote: Other expenses, yes, definitely, there is a reduction in advertisement as compared to last year

scores.rationale: No R&D spend, pipeline or product-development discussion appears in any of the four calls.
No acquisitions, bolt-ons or inorganic activity are mentioned anywhere in the last-12-months calls.
Dividends, buybacks or any distribution policy are not discussed in the excerpts; only net-debt-free status and a INR 357 crore treasury are noted.

Asset turn is deteriorating — revenue fell from INR 2,790 crores (FY25) to INR 2,702 crores (FY26) on an asset base management itself describes as having spare capacity, and higher depreciation was flagged as hurting profitability.
scores.quote: Higher depreciation in the quarter has impacted the profitability of the company.

scores.rationale: The company lost share to proliferating unorganized players through FY25 and chose not to cut prices, but GST 2.0 and distributor additions (550 to 630) restored 8% growth in Q4 FY26, so share capture is only just beginning.
scores.quote: there is a mushrooming of local players, the unorganized players... Temporarily, we can say, yes. But in long term, I think we will be able to gain back the market share.

scores.rationale: No international or new-geography expansion is discussed; commentary is limited to domestic regional demand differences (East weakest).

Growth is volume/recovery-led with price increases being pure cost pass-through (15-18% taken purely to offset 15-20% input and labour inflation) and mix stuck at 80:20 open-to-closed footwear for years.
scores.quote: The revenue growth was driven by a strong volume growth... roughly around 15% to 18% is the increase... So your margin is protected in a way? Yes, that is the intent

scores.rationale: The company appears to be exiting a multi-quarter demand trough (Q1 FY26 -12%, Q2 -8%, Q4 +8%) with an identifiable catalyst in the GST cut from 12% to 5%.
scores.quote: in the first quarter, we were minus 12%. Second quarter, we are minus 8%... Next year is definitely going to be a much better growth.

scores.rationale: The GST 2.0 shift structurally tilts the mass footwear market toward organized players, a durable formalization tailwind, though the underlying end market itself is mature and mass-demand remains muted.
scores.quote: The rollout of GST 2.0, which reduced tax rate on footwear priced below INR2,500 to 5% has strengthened our competitiveness versus the unorganized sector

scores.rationale: Management remained net debt free with positive operating cash flow, made no acquisitions, tightened distributor credit, and invested in distribution transformation through a downturn at the cost of near-term sales.
scores.quote: Our company continues to be net debt free and due to working capital efficiency, reported investments of INR 357 crores

scores.rationale: They pushed a painful DMS/secondary-sales distribution overhaul against active distributor resistance and refused to dilute prices despite share loss, accepting short-term pain for a structural change.
scores.quote: We are facing resistance but we'll overcome... It has been a wholesale-driven company, but now it has to be a distribution-led company.

scores.rationale: Calls are sober, metric-focused and often opened by the CFO or Company Secretary, with no promotional or celebrity-style positioning across all four calls.
scores.quote: myself, Ankit Jain, Company Secretary and Compliance Officer of the company

scores.rationale: Senior finance leadership churned twice inside twelve months (Sushil Batra to Prince Jain as CFO by Nov 2025, then Prince Jain absent by Jun 2026) and top roles remain concentrated in the Dua family via a new Co-CEO structure.
scores.quote: MR. GAURAV KUMAAR DUA CO-CEO AND WHOLE TIME DIRECTOR / MR. RITESH DUA CO-CEO

scores.rationale: Management gives specific negative numbers, admits temporary share loss, distributor resistance and unrefundable inverted-duty exposure rather than deflecting.
scores.quote: we are facing good resistance from a lot of distributors because they don't want to become really fully transparent

scores.rationale: There is little halo risk to correct for since results have been weak (three years of flat-to-declining revenue) and the recent PAT improvement is transparently attributed to cost control and treasury income rather than franchise strength.
scores.quote: PAT margins improved by 34 basis points year-on-year to 5.8%, reflecting disciplined cost control

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like hold on the customer is evident — consumers down-traded to cheaper local products and management admitted direct pressure to cut prices.
scores.quote: So there was a pressure on us to reduce the prices which we have not.

scores.rationale: Mass-market footwear carries no switching costs or captive aftermarket, and the calls show buyers moving freely to unorganized alternatives on price.
scores.quote: consumers down-trading to lower price on organized competition

scores.rationale: The industry is highly fragmented with continual new unorganized entrants and price-sensitive end consumers, the opposite of a stable oligopoly.
scores.quote: there is a mushrooming of local players, the unorganized players, new and new unorganized players have also come into the play

scores.rationale: Barriers are demonstrably low — new local entrants proliferated during the downturn and created industry-wide price pressure that Relaxo had to actively resist.
scores.quote: because of multiple factors, they were able to enter

scores.rationale: A large weak unorganized segment exists from which Relaxo can take share, and the GST 2.0 rate cut has materially improved its relative competitiveness against them.
scores.quote: branded and layers, we became more competitive in the market so that the taxes came down. So, it helped the organized players.

scores.rationale: Relaxo is a widely covered listed name hosted by multiple institutional brokers with numerous analysts on every call, and its categories attract constant new entrants.
scores.quote: hosted by IIFL Capital Services Limited

scores.rationale: Brands like Sparx retain some pull and the company held prices rather than discounting, but there is no evident pricing power beyond cost pass-through and consumers down-traded away during weakness.
scores.quote: Sparx, I think we are able to maintain the momentum in Sparx compared to the other open footwear

scores.rationale: Positioning rests on affordability plus quality rather than certainty for which price is secondary, and the Hawai/mass segment proved highly price-elastic.
scores.quote: supported by our portfolio of affordable and high-quality products

scores.rationale: Reach is a genuine strength — roughly 70,000 retailers, distributors expanded from 550 to 630, plus retail, e-commerce, LFR channels and a dealer app — though the network is mid-restructuring.
scores.quote: if you see 2 years back, we were at 55,000. Now we are at 70,000 retailers

scores.rationale: The customer is retail/mass consumer where intangibles should dominate, yet the benefit actually delivered is price-value, evidenced by down-trading to unorganized substitutes.
scores.quote: rural segment & middle income segment there has been, what we experienced, pressure on demand

scores.rationale: No technology or R&D edge surfaces in any call; differentiation efforts are licensing-led (Disney/Marvel) and the portfolio remains 80% open footwear competing with local makers.
scores.quote: We just started with Disney and Marvel and, the figure is quite low.

scores.rationale: Customers are government and institutional bodies and RITES matches them with reliability, price-variation-protected contracts and single-window delivery, though competitive tendering means little switching-cost lock-in.

scores.rationale: No technology platform, proprietary capability or R&D intensity is discussed in the four calls.

scores.rationale: No mention of advertising or promotional spend in any of the four calls.

scores.rationale: Several end markets show secular rather than merely cyclical expansion — Indian Railways bogie/wheel localisation, supply-chain diversification into India, and the EU FTA opening European forged/cast sourcing.

scores.rationale: Leverage-funded expansion plus multiple JVs/amalgamations and ambitions into aerospace, titanium and semiconductors sit against a stated intent to deleverage and promoter cash infusion — expansionist rather than conservative, but not reckless.

scores.rationale: A multi-year deliberate push into railways and passenger vehicles, pursued through a weak export cycle, is now visibly converting into approvals, bulk dispatches and an 80,000-wheel contract.

scores.rationale: The forged wheel JV and approved railway bogie-frame assembly place it among a very small approved supplier set to Indian Railways, with contracted offtake through FY28.

scores.rationale: No two-sided network dynamic is present or discussed in a component-manufacturing business.

scores.rationale: No discussion of advertising or promotional spend in any of the four calls.

scores.rationale: Organic-first posture with a deliberate exit from unprofitable volume, one small internally-funded bolt-on, profitability since inception and >100% cash conversion.
