scores.rationale: Cluster density plus the exclusive Jewar airport tie-up creates a quasi-regional lock in specific catchments, but patient switching costs in hospitals are inherently low.
scores.quote: we have accelerated our medical value travel initiatives... exclusive hospital partner for the now-operational Noida International Airport at Jewar

scores.rationale: NCR hospital care is a crowded, fragmented market with large national chains and a payer base (CGHS, TPAs) that sets tariffs, so pricing power sits partly with the customer rather than the provider.
scores.quote: the long-awaited central government health scheme (CGHS) rate revision after more than a decade, effective October 13, 2025

scores.rationale: Capital intensity and clinician scarcity are real barriers and pricing is administered rather than discount-driven, yet Yatharth's own rapid greenfield and acquisition entries show the market remains open to new capacity.
scores.quote: we have seeded our next high potential cluster in the Gurugram market through the acquisition of an ultra-modern under-construction super-speciality hospital

scores.rationale: Sub-scale standalone hospitals are visible donors — one was bought outright in Agra, and legacy capacity in Faridabad ceded preference to Yatharth within three months.
scores.quote: Faridabad Sector-20 has already reached a monthly revenue run rate of INR7 crores to INR8 crores within just 3 months of launch

scores.rationale: The company is anything but under the radar — calls hosted in succession by PhillipCapital, Elara, Nuvama and Antique, with management actively promoting its growth story.
scores.quote: hosted by Antique Stock Broking Limited

scores.rationale: Reputation for complex quaternary care supports rising realisation and a healthy margin structure, though the brand is young relative to established NCR names.
scores.quote: Our Noida Extension hospital achieved its highest-ever ARPOB of approx. INR44,000, up 16% year-over-year, supported by approximately 70% contribution from super-specialty services

scores.rationale: The pitch is explicitly reliability and outcomes in high-stakes care — complex tumour, stroke and neurosurgical cases — where trust, not price, drives selection.
scores.quote: These cases highlight our clinical capabilities, advanced infrastructure and growing reputation as a leading quaternary care provider in the region

scores.rationale: Deliberate proximity strategy — dense NCR clusters, an Agra feeder hub on the Yamuna Expressway corridor, and an airport examination room — improves accessibility for target catchments.
scores.quote: With strong connectivity to our Noida and Faridabad facilities, we expect the Agra hospital to evolve into a key feeder hub for oncology

scores.rationale: The payer mix is being deliberately steered toward retail cash and private-insurance patients at new units while retaining institutional government business at repriced rates.
scores.quote: Both these hospitals derived 100% of their revenues from cash and TPA, that is private insurances, reflecting our focus towards payer mix from day 1

scores.rationale: Technology is adopted early but purchased off the shelf — robots, navigation systems, Rapid AI — giving local first-mover advantage rather than proprietary, defensible technology.
scores.quote: We also adopted Rapid AI, an advanced AI-enabled neuroimaging technology for fast and accurate stroke detection

scores.rationale: Only a mild internal referral network exists between feeder and quaternary units; there is no self-reinforcing two-sided network described.
scores.quote: we expect the Agra hospital to evolve into a key feeder hub for oncology and other high-value specialities

scores.rationale: A hub-and-spoke NCR-Agra network plus overseas representative offices in Baghdad, Tashkent and Africa builds referral reach that single-site rivals cannot match, though national chains can.
scores.quote: we established Yatharth representative offices in Baghdad and Tashkent in partnership with Chinor Medical Centre and expanding into Cameroon

scores.rationale: Growth spend is real but modest — an 80-branch annual build-out delivered (76 in 9M) plus stated investment in people/product/process/technology, with evidence of returns via branch-sourced disbursements rising from 37% to 52%.
scores.quote: expanded our branch network to 1,328 branches by adding 33 new branches in Quarter 3, and overall, 76 branches in the 9 months of current financial year against a full year target of 80

scores.rationale: Only a passing mention of award-winning NRI campaigns with no spend, brand-equity or sales-linkage disclosure.
scores.quote: Our NRI homecoming campaigns earned several awards for being most disruptive in the use of AI

scores.rationale: No R&D discussion in the calls; technology-platform references are operating capability, not an R&D programme with measurable output.
The Bank made no acquisitions in the window — the only transaction was SMBC buying into YES Bank, i.e. the Bank as target, not acquirer.
scores.quote: The SMBC transaction was closed during the quarter... the combined stake for SMBC now stands at 24.2%

scores.rationale: No dividend, buyback or distribution policy is articulated anywhere in four calls; capital action ran the other way, with fresh equity issuance to SMBC diluting existing holders.
scores.quote: the combined stake for SMBC now stands at 24.2%

scores.rationale: Structurally asset-heavy with sub-par asset productivity — ROA still only 0.9% and NIM 2.7% against a self-admitted cost-of-funds disadvantage, with ~6% of assets stuck in low-yielding RIDF.
scores.quote: despite disadvantage of the Cost of Funds (CoFs), vis-a-vis the Government Banks as well as bigger Private Banking peers

scores.rationale: Small base with runway and recent evidence of capture — deposits/CASA outperforming industry and advances accelerating to 18.3% Y-o-Y (15-16% on average balances) — though management concedes headline credit growth lagged the system for most of the year.
scores.quote: Total Advances grew 18.3% year-on-year to INR 2.85 lakh crores... Though our headline credit growth currently lacks the system growth

scores.rationale: Expansion is domestic branch build-out plus early cross-border leverage through SMBC, credible but incremental rather than a premium brand travelling abroad.
scores.quote: our ongoing collaboration with SMBC provides helpful strategic support, particularly in Corporate and cross-border banking

scores.rationale: Pricing power is absent — spreads under intense pressure and deposit rates competed away — but mix is genuinely improving (CASA, RIDF rundown, exit from low-yield home/car/gold loans), leaving the two forces roughly offsetting.
scores.quote: we continue to see intense pressure on loan spreads, particularly within the wholesale segments

scores.rationale: Positioned off a cyclical trough with identifiable upturn: management calls NIM bottomed, the rate-cut cycle paused, RIDF drag rolling off and slippages at multi-quarter lows.
scores.quote: Sans, any further rate cuts by the RBI, we believe that NIMs have bottomed in this quarter

scores.rationale: Indian credit is a secularly expanding end market, corroborated in-call by resilient demand, 37 months of manufacturing expansion and rising system loan growth.
scores.quote: Manufacturing has now been in expansion mode for 37 straight months... reflected in the uptick in the system-level loan growth

scores.rationale: Organic-only, cost-disciplined and willing to forgo volume where returns are poor (home, new car and gold loans), with comfortable capital at 14% CET-1 and no M&A.
scores.quote: the Bank has strategically chosen not to pursue aggressive growth in two major product categories, that is the Home Loans and new Car Loans, as these product sub-segments currently do not generate attractive risk-adjusted returns

scores.rationale: Multi-year targets were set and hit — 1% ROA in the FY26 exit quarter, PSL compliance and RIDF cut from ~11% to ~6% — though the franchise's independence is qualified by its reliance on RBI/SBI/SMBC sponsorship.
scores.quote: In line with our guidance, Bank reported an ROA for the quarter of 1%

scores.rationale: Commentary is workmanlike and metric-led with no personality-building, but YES Bank remains an unusually high-profile, heavily-covered name, so the evidence cuts both ways.
scores.quote: Hence, I would keep my remarks brief and touch only on few of the strategic and thematic trends

scores.rationale: People investment and a workplace award are cited, but the CEO succession was filled externally (Tonse, ex-SBI) rather than from an internal pipeline.
scores.quote: recognized also among the top 25 India's Best Workplaces in BFSI for the year 2026

scores.rationale: Consistently strips out its own flattering items — gratuity charge, tax-refund interest, SR and treasury gains — and openly admits growth lagging the system and part of corporate growth being transitional.
scores.quote: The part of the Corporate growth is transitional and shorter tenure in nature

scores.rationale: Headline profit growth (44.5% FY26) is substantially helped by non-repeatable RIDF rundown, SR recoveries and tax refunds rather than pure operating skill, though management's own normalisation makes the separation possible.
scores.quote: moderation of some of our non-core income streams such as gains from our Security Receipts (SRs) portfolio, which was significantly lower at INR 86 crores this quarter against INR 338 crores

scores.rationale: No monopoly-like position in any customer's mind — the Bank is a mid-tier price-taker competing against government and larger private banks on funding cost.
scores.quote: despite disadvantage of the Cost of Funds (CoFs), vis-a-vis the Government Banks as well as bigger Private Banking peers

scores.rationale: Only modest switching-cost lock-in via transaction banking/API flows; the core deposit and lending book is repriced and contested continuously.
scores.quote: While the competitive intensity continues to remain high in deposits

scores.rationale: Indian banking as described is fragmented and hyper-competitive with customers holding pricing power on both deposits and loans, not a stable oligopoly.
scores.quote: the elevated competitive intensity in the market

scores.rationale: Licensing creates genuine entry barriers and no new entrants are cited, but pricing behaviour is irrational at the margin, with spreads and deposit rates competed away.
scores.quote: Despite adverse interest rate environment and elevated competitive intensity in Deposits

scores.rationale: The evidence points the other way — YES Bank is the funding-cost disadvantaged player ceding low-yield segments to stronger rivals, not the one harvesting weak competitors.
scores.quote: the Bank has deliberately deprioritized this product for the time being

scores.rationale: Far from under the radar: a reconstruction-era name with heavy analyst coverage, four global/domestic rating actions in one quarter and a marquee foreign strategic investor.
scores.quote: this has also been a quarter of significant external validation

scores.rationale: Brand relevance is being rebuilt rather than monetised — the Bank pays up for deposits and earns a 2.7% NIM, evidence of little image-driven pricing power.
scores.quote: the YES Bank's brand remained relevant and trust was rebuilt gradually through steady execution

scores.rationale: Reliability is the improving part of the proposition — multiple rating upgrades, 81.7% PCR and 0.2% net NPA are explicitly linked to funding cost and brand benefit.
scores.quote: Moody's upgraded our issuer rating to Ba1... These upgrades also carry tangible benefits for our funding costs, our Wholesale and Financial Institutions relationships and our brand

scores.rationale: Branch network as a multi-product engine is measurably improving customer access, with internally sourced retail disbursements up from 37% to ~52% in two years alongside digital payments and embedded banking reach.
scores.quote: internal sourcing from our branches, now accounting for approximately 52% of our Retail Asset disbursements, a substantial increase from just 37% around two years ago

scores.rationale: Benefit types are reasonably matched — granular retail/branch-led deposits at ~60% for the mass segment, and reliability/product-suite lock-in (API, transaction banking, forex, trade, CMS) for corporates.
scores.quote: aided by our comprehensive product suite, which includes differentiated product offerings of Application Programming Interface (API) and Transaction Banking

scores.rationale: A credible but not deep technology edge is claimed in digital payments, embedded banking and APIs, with fee income scaling off digital engines; no R&D intensity disclosed to support more.
scores.quote: our modern technology platform, the leadership in digital payments ecosystem we have and collaborative embedded banking capabilities

scores.rationale: Payments-ecosystem participation gives volume scale but no self-reinforcing two-sided network is evidenced, as the rails and standards are industry-owned.
scores.quote: the leadership in digital payments ecosystem we have

scores.rationale: A 1,328-branch network is expanding usefully but is not a reach rivals cannot match, being a fraction of the larger private and public sector banks it competes with.
scores.quote: we have expanded our branch network to 1,328 branches

scores.rationale: Asset-light model with no hard capex disclosure, but explicit growth capital deployment — ₹100+ crore primary infusion into the retail card business targeting ₹500cr revenue, plus QIP proceeds earmarked for growth.
scores.quote: we have earmarked a primary capital infusion of about INR 100-plus crores

scores.rationale: The only A&P-like item is an equity-funded 'brand equity transaction' with Bennett Coleman for media access, with no evidence yet of durable brand equity or sales lift, and it dilutes shareholders rather than expensing spend.
scores.quote: the company has recently issued warrants at INR 567 per share to Bennett Coleman and Company Limited. This is a brand equity transaction

scores.rationale: R&D/AI investment is producing measurable output — development cycles cut from 75+ days to under 30, agentic workflows launching, and a steady stream of new products (GlobalPay FOREX card, Mastercard-NSDL prepaid, Tax AI copilot).

scores.rationale: Bolt-ons are complementary and post-deal economics improved sharply (86400 revenue ₹34cr→₹74cr with EBITDA ₹5.4cr→₹18cr; Greenedge ₹36.5cr→₹103.7cr with PAT 4x), and management walked away from EffiaSoft and renegotiated DICE from ₹123cr to ₹68cr — but the sheer serial-acquirer cadence tempers the score.
scores.quote: revenues grew from about INR34 crores in 2025 to INR74 crores in FY26, represented a remarkable year-on-year growth of 118%

scores.rationale: No buybacks or dividends anywhere in the window; the capital policy runs the other way — a ₹950cr board-approved raise, QIP proceeds to deploy, and warrant issuances.
scores.quote: we have taken approval from the Board of Directors for a fund raise up to INR950 crores

scores.rationale: Genuinely asset-light platform turning ₹1,908cr of consolidated revenue with no meaningful fixed-asset base, though much of that revenue is Propel points booked gross at 7-9% margins, so the turnover flatters a thinly-moated line.
scores.quote: The revenue recognition basis is on a gross basis for Propel Points, and the margins vary from 7% to 9%

scores.rationale: Growing 42-48% YoY against an Indian spend-management market expanding ~15.5%, with 3,600 customers and 3.5-3.7mn users, implying sustained share capture in a still-underpenetrated category.
scores.quote: the Indian market is estimated to expand at a CAGR of 15.5%

scores.rationale: Geographic expansion remains announcement-stage across all four calls — GIFT City subsidiary approved and a UAE entity 'in final stages', with the MENA office promised 'in the next few weeks' in November still unformed by February and zero international revenue disclosed.
scores.quote: we are in the final stages of forming an entity in UAE with a view to expand in the MENA region

scores.rationale: Growth is volume/throughput-led with an adverse mix — Propel points (gross, 7-9% margin) was ₹247cr of ₹431cr in Q2FY26 while high-margin SaaS platform fees were only ₹10.5cr, and no pricing actions are cited anywhere.
scores.quote: Our SaaS platform fees contributed to around INR 10.5 crores... our Propel points revenue contributed to around INR 247 crores

scores.rationale: No discussion of cyclical positioning or an identifiable trough/upturn in the excerpts.
End markets are in secular expansion — spend management growing 15.5% CAGR in India, UPI volumes rising, and new tax rules extending employee benefits to the new regime expand the addressable base.
scores.quote: employee tax benefits have been extended to the new tax regime, which is a huge kicker to us

scores.rationale: The opposite of organic focus and restraint — four acquisitions in flight or closed in FY26 plus 'high-impact M&A' ambitions, funded by a ₹950cr raise, a QIP and warrant issues, with new business lines added nearly every quarter.
scores.quote: we remain committed to identifying high-level, high-impact M&A opportunities across domestic and international markets

scores.rationale: Founder-led with explicit multi-year targets they keep restating and promoter money alongside at the same price, showing independence from short-term pressure — including refusing a large deal others wanted.
scores.quote: while there is pressure internally, externally to do some large acquisitions, we want to make sure that we do the right acquisition

scores.rationale: Management actively buys visibility and uses promotional language rather than staying low-profile, paying with equity for access to major media brands and describing plans in superlatives.
scores.quote: giving us access to marquee media brands such as Times of India, Economic Times

scores.rationale: Mixed: the CFO seat turned over inside the window with the Deputy CFO stepping up as Interim CFO (internal bench, but instability), while 100+ AI engineers were acquired rather than developed.
scores.quote: MR. RAJESH TUMMALAGANTI – INTERIM CHIEF FINANCIAL OFFICER

scores.rationale: Management names its disappointments and abandoned deals plainly, corrects its own transcript errors, and flags a missed round number rather than glossing it.
scores.quote: while we are not very stoked about the performance through the financial -- last financial year

scores.rationale: Headline results are impressive but hard to attribute to durable skill — revenue is inflated by gross-basis Propel points, growth is partly bought via serial acquisitions and equity raises, and commentary leans on superlatives, so the halo risk is high.
scores.quote: we look to leverage AI automation to capture market share and render traditional models absolutely obsolete

scores.rationale: A self-declared category leadership claim but no monopoly-like position — the space has active competitors and the company still needs bank co-brand partners to reach customers.
scores.quote: listing has helped us consolidate our position as the number one spend management company in India

scores.rationale: Deep embedding into client finance workflows (petty cash, TDS reconciliation, expense approvals) creates real switching costs, evidenced by successful cross-sell into existing accounts like HCL and Subway.
scores.quote: We have also strengthened our presence in HCL, one of our key accounts, by upselling our TDS reconciliation module

scores.rationale: The excerpts describe a fragmented, fast-evolving fintech market rather than a stable oligopoly, with competitors present but no evidence of a consolidated few-player structure.
scores.quote: The spend management space is evolving at a fast pace

scores.rationale: Low structural barriers in fintech — the company itself enters new lines (retail co-brand, FOREX, fleet, tax) within quarters — and thin ~10% EBITDA margins on a guidance held flat suggest limited pricing rationality.
scores.quote: Our EBITDA guidance continues to remain in the range of 10 % to 11%

scores.rationale: Explicit weak competitors to take share from — peers facing headwinds in the core market and offline-bound incumbents in tax filing.
scores.quote: While competitors remain tethered to outdated offline workflows, we look to leverage AI automation to capture market share

scores.rationale: Deliberately the opposite of under-the-radar: a listed company actively courting media exposure, upgrading guidance publicly, and announcing global ambitions.
scores.quote: the breadth of our global ambition are driving us towards the next phase of transformation

scores.rationale: No image- or taste-driven pricing power; blended economics are thin because the largest revenue line carries 7-9% margins and demand is driven by compliance utility, not brand.
scores.quote: Requirements for efficiency, transparency, better compliance and regulation, which are the underlying thesis behind our products

scores.rationale: Customers buy compliance certainty and reliability, reflected in a marquee enterprise roster (HCL, Accenture, Bosch, Novo Nordisk, Adani Total Gas) that chooses a trusted partner over the cheapest option.
scores.quote: combining cutting -edge technology with unparalleled customer service makes us a trusted partner for business across industries

scores.rationale: Breadth of an integrated suite plus demonstrated account intimacy lets them solve adjacent problems inside existing clients rather than compete on standalone products.
scores.quote: our focus on building a strong ecosystem rather than standalone products and platforms

scores.rationale: Benefit type is well matched — corporates get integration-driven lock-in and compliance TCO, while the newly captive 3.7mn salaried retail base is being monetised with consumer credit products.
scores.quote: ZAG.money establishes our 4th monetization pillar, a captive high-intent base of 3.7 million salaried users

scores.rationale: A genuine multi-product stack with real AI throughput gains and newly acquired high-margin AI SaaS IP, though the sharpest capability was bought rather than built.
scores.quote: we have secured the complete spend management product suite and intellectual property... approximately INR 68 crores

scores.rationale: Some self-reinforcing structure across corporates, banks/networks, merchants and now a captive user base, but the effect is described as ecosystem cross-sell rather than a demonstrated two-sided flywheel.
scores.quote: Historically, our growth has been fuelled by 3 distinct pillars: enterprise clients, banking and network partners along with the merchant ecosystem

scores.rationale: Distribution reach is the clearest moat — 3,600 corporates, 3.5mn users and bank/network relationships that measurably re-rated acquired businesses, with Greenedge revenue going from ₹36cr in FY25 to ₹104cr in FY26 on Zaggle's network alone.
scores.quote: Greenedge has been able to leverage the Zaggle's network extremely well in scaling up their revenues

scores.rationale: Investment is deliberate and growth-oriented (content slate, digital, new segments) and did lift share and digital EBITDA, but content inventory is being run down and core ad revenue still fell all year, so incremental returns are unproven.
scores.quote: The judicious investment in content is a conscious choice taken by the company to invest for the future after a careful evaluation of the balance sheet.

scores.rationale: A&P rose only marginally alongside new show launches and a brand refresh, with no evidence yet of durable brand equity translating into revenue (ad revenue still declined YoY).
scores.quote: The launch of new shows across languages also resulted in a marginal rise in the advertising and promotional spend during the quarter.

scores.rationale: No R&D spend, pipeline or efficiency disclosure in any of the four calls; technology is referenced only as positioning language.
Deals in the window are small and complementary (Bullet micro-drama, Ideabaaz, Phantom Digital Effects VFX) but all are nascent with no post-deal margin evidence.
scores.quote: we announced a strategic investment in global VFX company, Phantom Digital Effects Limited

scores.rationale: The calls disclose a ₹21.8bn cash and treasury pile but are entirely silent on dividends, buybacks or any distribution policy.
scores.quote: Cash and treasury investments as of December 2025 stood at INR 21.8 billion

scores.rationale: The business is content-asset heavy — ₹69.3bn of content inventory/advances against falling advertising revenue — the opposite of asset-light with a protecting moat.
scores.quote: Overall, our content inventory advances and deposits stood at INR 69.3 billion

scores.rationale: Consistent, measured viewership share capture through the year (16.8% → exiting March above 18%), with regional leadership regained, and Zee is #2 so runway remains.
scores.quote: we exited the month of March with a network share of more than 18%, while for the quarter, it stood at 17.4%, a gain of 80 basis points

scores.rationale: Expansion is across Indian language markets rather than new geographies; international operations are not discussed in the window.
scores.quote: we have gained 100 bps Q-o-Q, taking our network share to 17.8%

scores.rationale: Digital growth is genuinely pricing/mix-led (language packs, revised pricing, telco repricing), but the much larger linear ad business showed no pricing power with revenue down 4–11% YoY.
scores.quote: revised pricing strategy on our digital entertainment platform, ZEE5, has resulted in a 73% year-on-year increase in our digital revenue

scores.rationale: The advertising cycle is clearly near a trough — four quarters of FMCG-led softness with sequential improvement and GST-cut/festive catalysts identified — though management's recovery calls have repeatedly slipped.
scores.quote: we are yet to see the full benefits of GST cut and a sustained pickup in FMCG advertising spend towards brand building

scores.rationale: The core linear TV end market is described as merely stable/flat (impressions and reach unchanged all year) while advertising shrinks; only the smaller digital segment is expanding.
scores.quote: the overall linear TV landscape continues to remain stable with weekly impressions of above 28 billion

scores.rationale: In the window management stayed organic, kept a net-cash balance sheet, avoided big M&A, and invested counter-cyclically in content while cutting digital losses to breakeven.
scores.quote: we continue to maintain sharp fiscal discipline and strengthening our balance sheet to fuel our future growth ambitions

scores.rationale: They set a ZEE5 breakeven goal and delivered it within the year, which is real tenacity, but the CEO skipped the Q3 call at short notice and the long-term narrative leans heavily on framing.
scores.quote: achieving the guidance which we had given at the start of the year

scores.rationale: Management is promotional rather than low-profile — a rebranded 'brand universe', an NSE launch event and anniversary framing dominate the opening remarks.
scores.quote: unveiling our sharp new brand universe... I'm certain all of you have experienced the new Zee

scores.rationale: Only two board additions and a strengthened ad sales team are mentioned; nothing systematic on talent development or an internal leadership pipeline.
scores.quote: The strengthened advertising revenue team enhances our ability to unlock emerging revenue streams

scores.rationale: They do own margin dilution from content spend and hit their stated ZEE5 breakeven target, but repeat 'cautiously optimistic' recovery language across four quarters of ad declines and lean on external blame (Middle East conflict).
scores.quote: the strategic approach undertaken to enhance the content offering has impacted our profitability during the quarter

scores.rationale: The headline digital turnaround is partly attributable to one-off syndication revenue and a renegotiated telco contract rather than repeatable operating skill, so results should not be read as proof of capability.
scores.quote: The revenue growth was aided by syndication revenues and revised pricing agreement with a telco player during this quarter

scores.rationale: No monopoly position nationally; the closest thing is dominant mindshare in specific language markets such as Marathi and Bangla.
scores.quote: For Zee Marathi... enabling us to achieve a market share of 33.6%

scores.rationale: Regional strongholds exist, but viewers face zero switching cost and carriage depends on periodic DPO contract renewals rather than lock-in.
scores.quote: successful renewals of contracts with BPOs in the Broadcast segment

scores.rationale: Broadcasting is a concentrated few-player market where Zee is a firm number two, but the paying customer (the advertiser) clearly holds the negotiating power given sustained ad-rate weakness.
scores.quote: We continue to maintain our position as India's strong Number 2, TV entertainment network.

scores.rationale: The company is chasing cheap Free Dish reach and entering crowded new formats while advertisers withhold spend — signs of contested, low-barrier competition rather than rational pricing.
scores.quote: in order to address the new set of audiences, we took the required steps to reach their households through Free Dish

scores.rationale: Share is visibly being taken from weaker rivals across regions — leadership regained in Bangla, seven channels at number one, fastest growth in the South.
scores.quote: 7 channels from Zee achieved leadership in their respective markets

scores.quote: Ideabaaz, which was launched at an event held at the National Stock Exchange recently

scores.rationale: Strong cultural brand affinity in language markets translated into engagement but not into pricing power, since ad revenue fell every quarter of the year.
scores.quote: Strong character-led storytelling, coupled with culturally rooted narratives enabled the channel to garner peak engagement

scores.rationale: Despite improved reach and share, advertisers cut or held back spend, showing price and budget cycles dominate rather than any trust or certainty premium.
scores.quote: March was severely impacted with the ongoing Middle East conflict where advertisers have held back their spends

scores.rationale: Genuine accessibility advantage — omnichannel monthly unique reach above 800 million plus a strengthened direct advertising sales organisation.
scores.quote: ZEE's monthly unique reach has crossed 800 million across platforms

scores.rationale: The company does tailor to both customer types (language subscription packs for retail, a rebuilt sales team for advertisers) but achieves neither an intangible premium nor corporate switching-cost lock-in.
scores.quote: ZEE5 introduced tailored subscription plan in 7 languages

scores.rationale: Technology is positioning language plus a minority VFX stake; there is no disclosed R&D intensity or proprietary multi-product tech edge.
scores.quote: ongoing strategic transformation into a content and technology powerhouse

scores.rationale: No two-sided network exists — subscriber and viewer growth is bought with content spend, not self-reinforcing scale.
scores.quote: aided by enhanced content offering across 7 languages and the revised pricing strategy driving our subscriber growth

scores.quote: weekly impressions of above 28 billion and a weekly reach exceeding 740 million during the year

scores.rationale: The only growth investments disclosed are a new Belgrade nearshore delivery centre and ongoing AI/sales capability spend, with no capex quantum or incremental-ROIC evidence given.
scores.quote: We opened a delivery centre in Belgrade, Serbia... while we have expanded our margins, we continue to invest in augmenting capabilities, specifically around AI and sales

scores.rationale: No brand-building A&P is discussed in any of the four calls; sales-and-marketing spend is mentioned only as a margin line item, not as brand investment.

scores.quote: We launched ZenseAI, our GenAI accelerator platform... 20% of this year's order book is AI influenced

scores.rationale: No acquisitions, integrations or deal pipeline are mentioned anywhere in the last-12-months calls.

scores.rationale: Genuinely asset-light with high utilization (84.3%), improving DSO of 71 days and a large net cash position, but the moat that should protect those returns is weak given renewal and pricing pressure.

scores.rationale: The only geographic move in the window is a Serbian delivery centre opened for talent and nearshore cost benefit; there is no evidence of a brand entering and winning new client geographies.

scores.rationale: Growth is explicitly volume- and offshore-led with an adverse mix shift, while AI is repurposing existing spend and pressuring renewal pricing — the opposite of price/mix-led growth.
scores.quote: a majority of AI spend is being repurposed from existing engagements such as application development and testing, creating pressure on renewals and pricing

scores.rationale: Conditions look trough-like (paused discretionary spend, furloughs, tariff/visa noise) while the record order book and 1.12 book-to-bill hint at an upturn, though management itself will not commit to consistent growth.

The balance sheet has become materially heavier — roughly INR3,300 crores of added intangibles and goodwill plus debt funding — against domestic sales that grew only 2.4%, so asset intensity has risen rather than fallen.
scores.quote: we have increased our intangibles by roughly INR2,500 crores, and we have increased our goodwill by roughly around INR800 crores

scores.rationale: Share is being gained in the brands with runway (Everyuth scrubs +262bps, facial cleansing +89bps, sweetener +80bps, Complan 5th to 4th), but the largest franchises are already near-saturated (Sugar Free 96.1%, Glucon D 58.9%), limiting further headroom.
scores.quote: EverYuth leads key sub-segments with a 48.7% share in scrubs, which is a positive of 262.3 basis points year-on-year

scores.rationale: Geographic expansion is broad and executing — RiteBite in 9 countries within its first year, WeightWorld into Poland/Finland/Portugal, Boots.com UK listing and Amazon UAE — with international like-to-like growth of 29.5% for FY26.
scores.quote: The international business, including Comfort Click business, delivered a like-to-like growth of 29.5%

scores.rationale: Ex-seasonal domestic growth was high-teens on mid-teen volumes, i.e. predominantly volume-led with only modest price/mix; the visible margin mix lift came from consolidating a higher-margin acquired business rather than domestic pricing power.
scores.quote: recorded strong growth of double-digit, in the high teens range, supported by mid-teen volume growth

scores.rationale: The seasonal portfolio (Glucon D, Nycil) is at a weather-driven cyclical trough — down 18.8% for FY26 on an already weak base — with management pointing to recovery, a genuine identifiable upturn if weather normalises.
scores.quote: the seasonal brands declined by 18.8%... So we see recovery from May onwards

scores.rationale: Core end-markets — VMS/preventive healthcare, protein snacking, sugar substitutes, better-for-you foods — plus the quick-commerce channel shift are in secular expansion, and management repeatedly frames these as structural.
scores.quote: well positioned to benefit from rising health awareness and the growing focus on preventive health care

scores.rationale: Against the 'organic focus, prudent leverage, no big M&A' test, management went the other way this year: a large debt-funded overseas acquisition taken on via a bridge loan, driving reported net losses and a 43.2% fall in full-year net profit.
scores.quote: The acquisition has been funded through a low-cost bridge loan at an interest rate of 5%

scores.rationale: Evidence of patient, persistent brand building — Sugar Free Green's 20th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth and a multi-year Nutralite CAGR — alongside a deliberate long-horizon reframing of Complan.
scores.quote: Sugar Free Green delivered 20th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth

scores.rationale: Calls are consistently operational and understated, led by the CEO and CFO with no promotional posturing, and management repeatedly declines to dramatise numbers.
scores.quote: We don't give separate numbers

scores.rationale: Sustained, externally validated people investment — Great Place to Work certification for the fourth consecutive year explicitly tied to talent development — though no detail on the internal leadership pipeline.
scores.quote: certified as a Great Place to Work for the fourth consecutive year, reflecting its continued commitment to talent development

scores.rationale: Management does disclose losses, exceptional items and seasonal misses plainly, but habitually reframes headline growth by excluding seasonal brands and the acquisition, and refuses like-for-like splits when analysts press for them.
scores.quote: excluding seasonal brands, the company delivered a strong double-digit growth

scores.rationale: Headline optics flatter the underlying business — 46.4% FY26 sales growth is acquisition-driven while domestic sales grew just 2.4% and net profit fell 43.2% — so results should not be read as evidence of superior operating skill.
scores.quote: net sales registered growth of 46.4%... while the domestic business grew by 2.4%

scores.rationale: Sugar Free holds a near-absolute 96.1% share of the sugar-substitute category and Everyuth 77.2% of peel-off masks, with Cuticolor the number-one doctor-prescribed hair colour — monopoly-like positions in the consumer's mind.
scores.quote: holding a commanding 96.1% market share in the sugar substitute category

scores.rationale: No evidence of switching costs or a captive aftermarket — these are repeat-purchase FMCG categories where the consumer can switch freely; the only lock-in-adjacent asset mentioned is B2B foodservice relationships for Nutralite Professional.
scores.quote: robust execution from focused B2B and B2C teams, enabling deeper market penetration

scores.rationale: Its core niches are concentrated with the company at or near number one (sweeteners 96.1%, Nycil 33.3%, glucose powder 58.9%) and fragmented retail buyers with no negotiating power, though the growing quick-commerce channel is a countervailing force.
scores.quote: maintained its number one position with a market share of 33.3%

scores.rationale: Pricing is described as disciplined with no mention of discount wars and promoter ownership is stable, but the newer growth arenas — protein snacking and VMS — are open, low-barrier categories the company itself has just entered by acquisition.
scores.quote: disciplined pricing actions, despite the challenging inflationary backdrop

scores.rationale: Complan is climbing ranks (fifth to fourth) inside a category that is shrinking, and Everyuth is gaining facial-cleansing share — both consistent with weaker players donating share.
scores.quote: Complan has maintained its market share and improved its position from fifth to fourth place

scores.rationale: The most profitable franchises sit in small, unglamorous niches — sugar substitutes, peel-off masks, prickly-heat powder, doctor-prescribed hair colour — that large FMCG players have largely left alone.
scores.quote: 77.2% in peel-off masks

scores.rationale: Consolidated gross margin guided at 66-67% annualised with most brands expanding gross margin, indicating real brand-derived pricing power, though seasonal categories showed demand is not fully weather-proof.
scores.quote: on an annualized basis, you can assume it about 66%, 67% on a consolidated basis

scores.rationale: Several franchises sell trust rather than price — Cuticolor is the number-one doctor-prescribed hair colour, Complan is being pushed through clinical and expert-led channels, and Comfort Click carries 4.6+ Amazon ratings across Europe.
scores.quote: The brand is Number 1 doctor prescribed in the hair coloring space

scores.rationale: Accessibility is improving on both ends — the acquired RiteBite brand plugged into the parent's distribution, organised-trade saliency up from 24% to 30%, strong quick-commerce expansion, and dedicated B2B/B2C field teams for Nutralite.
scores.quote: Robust growth on quick commerce underpinned by a continued expansion and distribution footprint

scores.rationale: The benefit type is well matched to customer type — image/taste intangibles and brand trust for retail consumers, and reliability-plus-service for the B2B foodservice channel served by a dedicated Nutralite Professional team.
scores.quote: Nutralite Professional expanded its offering with the launch of Cheesy Delight and Slim Mayonnaise variants... across all food service channels

scores.rationale: Innovation is formulation- and marketing-level rather than a deep technology edge; the only technology claims are AI applied to creatives and media buying, which is a widely available capability, not a proprietary moat.
scores.quote: leveraging AI-powered creatives and data-driven decision-making

scores.rationale: No evidence of any two-sided or self-reinforcing network in the last-12-month calls.

Distribution reach is a genuine asset — demonstrated by the ability to absorb RiteBite into the network and double its legacy performance, plus rural general trade, organised trade and quick commerce — but it is not shown to be unmatched versus larger Indian FMCG peers.
scores.quote: The RiteBite Max Protein business has been integrated into company's broader distribution network
